Cardinals Add Star Defender to Week 5 Injury Report vs Lions
full_text:
The Arizona Cardinals added defensive lineman Walter Nolen III to their Week 5 injury report against the Detroit Lions today.
Nolen, after practicing fully yesterday with no issues, was added to Thursday's report due to a calf injury. He was limited.
This would be a massive loss if the Cardinals aren't able to have Nolen available on Sunday, as Arizona's season is on the verge of slipping away after a 1-3 start.
Full breakdown for each side:
Sharar was the other new addition for the Cardinals' Thursday injury report.
Baker, Sweat and Seumalo all returned from veteran rest days on Wednesday in full capacity, which is a good sign.
Adams was previously ruled out by Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur while Wingard and Burch have now missed consecutive days, potentially putting their spot in doubt for this Sunday.
Nolen's gotten off to a slow start this season, though LaFleur was shared some words of encouragement.
“Yes, he just needs to keep going at it. I love Walt and he wants it really, really, really bad. And that's what I respect," he said.
"I look at people's intentions, and I know his intentions are that he wants to help this team and he wants to be productive. He just needs to keep going."
Williams was the only change on Detroit's side of things, going from DNP to limited on Thursday.
The Lions, statistically with one of the NFL's best offenses, move into the weekend with offensive coordinator Drew Petzing's familiarity as a potential bonus as prepration for his former team continues.
"People are going to have their narratives probably about it, including us. Drew definitely has his spin on that offense, but it’s the Detroit Lions offense," LaFleur told Cardinals media this week.
"They’re doing a lot of the stuff that they’ve done in the run game. They’re doing a lot of stuff that (Lions QB) Jared’s (Goff) has been really, really successful at — almost at MVP caliber levels and stuff. With all the same basically skill that they’ve had there for four years now or so. Then the bookend tackle and all those kinds of things. A lot of the same, but he’s definitely put his little flavor on it for sure.”
Final practice reports for both sides will emerge on Friday.

title: Cardinals Are Falling Apart: 2 Changes Could Still Save the Season
full_text:
ARIZONA — The Arizona Cardinals are staring the reality of a losing season directly in the face.
Arizona's 1-3 start isn't quite a lost cause, though losses have quickly piled up in the desert, and it's up to head coach Mike LaFleur to make changes before 2026 gets away from him.
“Our focus is (being) 1-0 each and every week so the word change doesn’t — we’re trying to do what we think is best for the week to win a football game. That’s the approach that I take, that (General Manager) Monti (Ossenfort) takes and that this organization takes — the coaches and the players," LaFleur told reporters this week.
"That’s all we’re focused on. I know people want big-picture analysis, but in the world that we try to live in and within our walls where it’s just us and the NFL, it’s week to week and (we) work to be 1-0 each week.”
There's ample opportunity for both sides of the ball to improve ahead of Week 5 . After a quarter of the season, here's one change the Cardinals need to make on each side of the line of scrimmage:
The Cardinals' usage of 13 (one RB, three TE) sets is third in the NFL through four weeks of play, which isn't a surprise given LaFleur's prior experience with the Rams and Sean McVay's love for the hefty packages.
However, Arizona's personnel groupings mostly reside in 11 (three receivers) personnel with that package used on 63% of offensive plays.
LaFleur's usage of 2+TE sets (34%) ranks 16th in the NFL, though that number has to jump for a few reasons.
The Cardinals' offensive line is getting no push upfront. Arizona's run stuff rate (17.8%) ranks in the bottom ten of NFL teams while their 1.1 average yards before contact is in the bottom third of teams. Pass-protection wise, Arizona's 2.6 second average time to throw is third-fastest in the NFL while their ESPN pass-block win rate of just 30% ranks second-worst in the league.
Simply put, the Cardinals are relying far too heavily on running backs making plays of their own accord while they're afforded little time to let passing plays develop.
There's no magic wand to fix these issues, but with two starting offensive linemen out for Week 5 and the next few weeks staring down a gauntlet of a schedule, the Cardinals need to adjust their attack.
Arizona's facing light defensive boxes just 27.9% of the time, which is the third-least in the NFL. Translation: defenses are mostly playing base against the Cardinals and are having success while doing it.
That's where the integration of multi-TE sets comes into play. More heavy bodies will potentially offset some of the losses suffered upfront while giving Arizona more advantageous looks in the run game. Tight ends such as Trey McBride and Elijah Higgins are more than equipped to handle those dual duties.
It's time Arizona embraces going heavier.
It feels like a lifetime ago when Cardinals defensive coordinator Nick Rallis was in future head coaching conversations thanks to the job done with an undermanned Arizona defense, getting creative with pressure packages and being aggressive towards offenses.
That's changed, drastically, and Rallis now finds himself on the hot seat entering Week 5.
Arizona's defense has allowed 30+ points in three consecutive games. They're bottom ten in yards allowed per contest (351.3) and fourth-worst in points allowed per game (29.3) through four weeks.
The Cardinals opted to fill holes in their defense left by departing starters as opposed to making serious upgrades — which includes their pass rush. Arizona's eight team sacks rank near the middle of the table while their pressure rate (21.1%) ranks in the bottom third.
Their explosive play rate allowed of 7% is also sixth-worst out of all NFL defenses.
Rallis' defenses have typically been at their best when he's sending pressure. That hasn't been the case in 2026, as Arizona's just one of six NFL teams to have a defensive blitz rate of less than 20%.
Half of the Cardinals' sacks have come on blitzes or pressures with five players. Arizona's defense is not nearly talented enough in either the front or backend to rush four and drop seven into coverage.
It feels like Arizona's defense has been more reactionary than aggressive. Yes, there's a talent disparity. No, Rallis doesn't need to turn into an evil genius such as Brian Flores when it comes to dialing up pressure.
The reality is the Cardinals' defense is undermanned. With that, you have two options: Sit back and play exotic coverages and hope offenses will make mistakes — or be the aggressor and force opposing teams to beat you with low percentage/probability plays on a consistent basis.
To Rallis' credit, the Cardinals are sixth in turnovers generated at seven. However, their bend but don't break defense has largely seen too many open receivers and holes afforded for teams to have extensive success on the field.
It's time for Arizona to be more aggressive in their defensive play-calling. Rallis' job may depend on it.

title: Cardinals Hot Seat Rankings: Who’s Under The Most Pressure After a 1-3 Start?
full_text:
We're a quarter of the way through the season, and the Arizona Cardinals have been an unfortunate underperformer with a 1-3 record.
It's not as if the Cardinals have been out-classed through their first four games. A win in Los Angeles started the season off on a positive note while Seattle's blowout loss was a humbling reset for first-year head coach Mike LaFleur. Back-to-back tough losses to San Francisco and New York bring us to present day.
What the rest of the season looks like largely remains to be seen. However, a number of figures within the organization find themselves in discussions daily from the fan base.
Whose seat is hot, and whose is not?
Ossenfort, in his fourth season, has yet to build anything close to a playoff contender. Coaches have come and gone, franchise players have departed, and his draft/free agency classes have yielded a heavy bag of mixed results.
Ossenfort — almost surprisingly — was retained while Jonathan Gannon was fired this past offseason. Injuries again appear to be stalling progress in the desert, though the Cardinals failed to upgrade key positions at edge rusher and right tackle. Those weaknesses are still glaring after four weeks of football.
Patience has run thin on Ossenfort, and if the Cardinals can't turn things around in the final three quarters of the season, it would be a very hard sell to the fan base for him to return for a fifth season.
LaFleur hasn't been without his issues as a rookie head coach. The offense hasn't been able to find explosive plays or counter whatever defenses are doing to stop them on a consistent basis while the defensive side of the ball still remains lackluster — a unit LaFleur doesn't directly oversee but still ultimately is in charge of as a head coach.
Yet we're only four games into LaFleur's tenure, and it's evident the potential he carries as an offensive play-caller once continuity and experience can eventually marry on his side of the ball. Arizona's offense has moved the ball well and quite frankly is a play or two away from being a 3-1 team.
The moral scoreboard doesn't mean anything, but LaFleur's been far from a failure in the infant stages of his career in the desert. His seat isn't anywhere close to warm.
Rallis' leash entering 2026 was already short. The Cardinals interviewed multiple defensive coordinators before being turned down and eventually settled for a fourth season under the play-caller.
There was hope the defense would be different with Gannon's fingerprints removed. That's yet to be the case, as Arizona's allowed 30+ points in three consecutive games. The Cardinals still aren't able to rush the passer and struggle to eliminate a team's top passing weapon on a weekly basis.
Veteran defensive coach Teryl Austin is very much looming as a potential replacement for Rallis, which could happen much sooner than some on the outside anticipate. Unless the Cardinals can turn things around, Rallis being relieved of his duties feels more like when — not if.
The Cardinals engaged in a lengthy contract dispute with Brissett this summer before reaching a number. It was a win for the veteran quarterback — who got one last payday as a starter — while Arizona kept their locker room happy and got a capable veteran passer to run LaFleur's offense.
Thus far, Brissett's been relegated to checking the ball down often and has struggled to find the aforementioned explosive plays. The time missed during his holdout very much impacted his timing/grasp of LaFleur's system and it shows.
Brissett, despite online pitchforks, hasn't been the biggest roadblock for Cardinals success. However, he's proven he isn't capable of taking Arizona's offense to new heights — and as losses pile and patience wears thinner — Brissett is very much on the verge of losing his starting job.

title: Cardinals-Lions Official Week 5 Injury Report
full_text:
ARIZONA — The first injury report for Week 5's tilt between the Arizona Cardinals and Detroit Lions has been revealed.
Both teams hit the practice field Wednesday for the first time in prep for their clash at State Farm Stadium:
Jeremiyah Love's ankle injury should keep him healthy and ready to go for this week despite his appearance on the report, according to head coach Mike LaFleur.
"No, it shouldn't impact [him]. But again, the best I can just tell you guys is maintenance. Just maintenance throughout the day, and then when we get to Sunday," LaFleur told reporters on Wednesday.
Earlier today, Lions head coach Dan Campbell spoke on trying to get Branch back into the mix.
"Look, we know there’s going to be a little bit of kicking the rust off just to get back into all of those, back to the player that he was. It’ll take a minute," said Campbell (h/t Lions On SI ).
"However, he’s an instinctive, aware player and he is a violent player. And so he’s got a knack for the football and his production, even if it’s not what it was in the immediate, as he grows back to that will have an impact, I believe."
The Lions and Cardinals will practice twice more this week (Thursday and Friday) before revealing game statuses such as questionable, out or doubtful after Friday's practice.
On Saturday, the two sides will have the opportunity to make up to two standard practice squad elevations. These could be key in revealing who teams believe will be healthy or unavailable for Sunday.
On game day, a final inactives report is due 90 minutes ahead of game time at State Farm Stadium. With a 1:25 PM kickoff, this report will be due at 11:55 AM on Sunday.

title: Cardinals Update Jeremiyah Love Injury Before Lions Game
full_text:
TEMPE — The Arizona Cardinals are expecting running back Jeremiyah Love to be available for their Week 5 matchup against the Detroit Lions after suffering an ankle injury in their Week 4 loss to the New York Giants.
"No, it shouldn't impact [him]. But again, the best I can just tell you guys is maintenance. Just maintenance throughout the day, and then when we get to Sunday," Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur told reporters on Wednesday.
Love was seen on the sideline having his ankle worked on and did not appear on the Cardinals' final drive to potentially win the game in Week 4. He was out-snapped 36-30 by fellow running back Tyler Allgeier.
This ankle injury is different than the one he suffered during preseason play, which kept him out for multiple weeks. He has yet to miss a regular season game.
“He’s been dealing with it for a little bit, but it’s just a management-type thing,” LaFleur said earlier in the week on Monday. “It’s like he tweaks it and then he feels fine, so we’re just trying to manage that. He’s doing a good job with it, too.”
Arizona will reveal their first practice injury report of Week 5 later today. The Cardinals will practice three times this week before designating players as either out, questionable or doubtful on Friday.
Love, just four games in his rookie season, addressed the grueling physicality of playing in the NFL as a rookie after the loss in New York.
"My body sometimes is down, sometimes tired. So it's just managing those things. And coaches know that. This is probably gonna be the longest year of my life," Love said after Week 4.
"I just want to manage that workload. So today just obviously making sure to keep an eye on managing me. But I didn't go out there hurt anything or anything like that. They're doing what they need to do to keep me up so that I can finish the season."
The Cardinals have been insistent on splitting touches between Love and Allgeier to steady the workload of the former number three overall pick .
Love thus far has 55 carries for 223 yards (4.1 YPC) and one touchdown on the ground. As a pass-catcher he has 11 receptions for 36 yards and one receiving touchdown.
The Cardinals are 1-3 on the season and are hoping to avoid a fourth consecutive loss after winning their season-opener against the Los Angeles Chargers.
If he's able to go, the Lions' defense has allowed the most yards and second-most points per game thus far, which opens the door for a big day for Love.

title: Cardinals Surprisingly Stagnant Across Week 5 NFL Power Rankings
full_text:
ARIZONA — The Arizona Cardinals are 1-3 through four weeks of play, placing them in a precarious spot across NFL power rankings ahead of Week 5.
Conor Orr: "Mike LaFleur was immediate in his response to a question about a quarterback change, which is totally fair. But with a developmental passer on the roster, I do wonder what the 'gotta see him' threshold is for a team that, according to ESPN’s draft slot projector, has a 55% chance of a top-five pick."
Josh Weinfuss described the season in four words: "too many self-inflicted mistakes" which actually might be five words now that we spell them out here.
"The Cardinals are still figuring out life under new coach Mike LaFleur. Following a convincing loss to the Seahawks in Week 2, Arizona has been close in its past two games but couldn't overcome a litany of self-inflicted mistakes," he said.
"Sunday's matchup ended up with a pick-six thrown by QB Jacoby Brissett on fourth-and-goal. The hope in the locker room is that if the Cardinals can minimize those types of mistakes, they can fix the season."
Nick Shook : "I thought I could count on Arizona’s offense to produce at a competitive rate on a weekly basis. The unit did so in two of its first three games and continued to do so on the first two drives against the Giants. Unfortunately, the rut the Cardinals entered (and their failure to find the end zone late) has shaken my confidence in this team.
"For once, the defense did its part to give Arizona a chance -- at least early -- and the offense failed to capitalize. Perhaps this is what I should have expected from the Cardinals all along."
The Cardinals are surprisingly moved up here despite their loss by Frank Schwab, who dove into Jeremiyah Love's usage:
"Love was the third overall pick of the NFL Draft and has looked good (4.1 yards per carry) even though his snaps have been limited. The Cardinals shouldn't be running the third pick into the ground when it's clear they're not a playoff contender, but it's still unusual to hear Love talking about how it has already been a long year when the Cardinals still have 13 games to go."
Staff : "Like the Jets, the Cardinals offered some hope for this season with a Week 1 win. But that victory over the 0-4 Los Angeles Chargers looks less impressive each week, and Jacoby Brissett’s three interceptions Sunday weren’t very inspiring."

title: 5 Big Gambles the Cardinals Made This Offseason: Have They Paid Off?
full_text:
The Arizona Cardinals are 1-3 through the first four weeks of 2026.
It's been an overall mixed bag for head coach Mike LaFleur, as the Cardinals have been far more competitive than initially imagined — sitting just a play here or there from a 3-1 record — though Arizona hasn't found the ability to win games.
It's still very early in the season, though the Cardinals' offseason is slowly beginning to reveal results.
Here are Arizona's five biggest gambles this offseason, and why they haven't paid off early in 2026:
The Cardinals opted to bypass opportunities to upgrade their 2025 pass rush that ranked in the bottom of the league last season in terms of sacks and pressure numbers, hoping for improvement from a handful of players in the OLB room led by Josh Sweat.
Sweat's clearly not healthy at this moment in time while the rest of Arizona's outside linebacker corps simply doesn't have a high ceiling. BJ Ojulari was unfortunately cut this summer after not being able to return to his rookie-year form due to injury while all of Baron Browning, Jordan Burch and Zaven Collins haven't been overly impressive, either.
Arizona's ability to get to the quarterback has been average to begin 2026, totaling eight sacks and a 21% pressure rate against opposing offenses. The Cardinals' defense relied on their pass rush improving internally, and they've been inconsistent at best to begin the year.
Wilkinson had a less than impressive season with the Atlanta Falcons in 2025 despite starting every game at right tackle, making his reunion in the desert a bit surprising. Arizona hadn't received strong tackle play from Jonah Williams previously, leaving ample room for improvement — though Wilkinson has been a liability this season.
According to Pro Football Focus, Wilkinson has graded out as the seventh-worst qualified tackle (63/69) to begin 2026. He's particularly struggled in run-blocking, as the Cardinals have the lowest EPA when running to his inside gap at -0.41.
You can't upgrade every position during the offseason, though Arizona was hoping for Wilkinson to be serviceable — he simply hasn't been thus far.
The Cardinals interviewed multiple defensive coordinators for a role in LaFleur's staff this offseason. Each said no, and Arizona pivoted back to Nick Rallis for a fourth season in hopes of things being different without Jonathan Gannon in the picture.
That hasn't been the case, as the Cardinals' defense has again been abysmal to start 2026. After a stellar Week 1 outing, Arizona's allowed three consecutive 30-point games and seemingly can't stop the run or pass.
In fairness, the Cardinals' defense received only stopgaps for players departing in free agency rather than upgrades with hopes of health being on their side. However, Rallis' fingerprints are entirely on this unit, and they haven't performed to expectations.
There's a very real possibility seasoned defensive coach Teryl Austin takes over his duties in the next few weeks.
The Cardinals took another big swing by hiring the first-time LaFleur as a head coach, though he arrived to the desert with a sparkly resume and promise to turn Arizona into a well-oiled machine.
In complete fairness, that transformation was never going to happen four games into his first season. However, LaFleur hasn't had a strong counter-punch to how defenses are attacking Arizona. The Cardinals' offense is being blitzed, heavily, with two-high shells — which has limited their ability to generate explosive plays and/or threaten to push the ball down the field.
The Cardinals' offense ranks dead-last in explosive plays, which if you talk to any coach across any level of football, they'll highlight as a winning stat next to turnover differential.
Fans should still be very optimistic about LaFleur and his tenure in Arizona, though he's yet to find a way to counter what defenses are doing to limit their attack.
With other pressing needs across the roster, the Cardinals shocked everybody by making a running back the third overall pick of the 2026 NFL Draft. When you put on the tape, Jeremiyah Love's presence as a top pick is warranted thanks to his ability to do just about everything at a high level.
However, the Cardinals haven't quite utilized Love how people outside of the building envisioned. He's rarely been featured in the passing attack while a mix of injuries and intent to spread touches across the RB room has prevented Love from handling a heavy workload early in his rookie season.
Drafting a weapon like Love as high as he went typically means you're committing to making him a prominent feature of the offense. Love has played well when given opportunities, though his touches have been sporadic through the first four weeks of the season — which is a bit surprising.

title: Cardinals Made 9 Roster Moves After Week 4; Here's What They Mean
full_text:
ARIZONA — The Arizona Cardinals have made a slew of roster moves following their Week 4 loss to the New York Giants.
It's still early in the season, though Arizona's just 1-3 and are quickly falling out of the NFC West race. Some would say as expected, though games have been winnable for the Cardinals — they just haven't converted.
Breaking down every roster move and what it means:
Johnson was confirmed to miss the rest of the 2026 season after suffering a biceps injury on the team's final drive.
"I feel for him, obviously. ... It sucks for him first and foremost. Sucks obviously for the Arizona Cardinals, our offense, this team. But you know, [this is] NFL football. Here we are in October. Show goes on," Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur told reporters Monday.
Long suffered a knee injury in Week 4. It's not currently known if his injury is considered season-ending like Johnson's was.
What these mean: The Cardinals may be forced to play seventh-round pick Jayden Williams at left tackle this week against a Lions pass rush that ranks second in the NFL in terms of sacks. Arizona likes Williams , though losing Johnson for the season is massive. However, the Cardinals made another move today, which we'll get to here in a moment.
In terms of Long, he was acquired via trade and was utilized primarily as a blocking tight end. The Cardinals are still waiting on Tip Reiman to get healthy.
Quitoriano gets the call-up from the practice squad after spending training camp with the Cardinals. He was stashed away on the practice squad after final roster cuts and is familiar with what LaFleur and co. want to do offensively. Now, he gets his shot to land on the roster and serve as a depth piece behind Trey McBride and Elijah Higgins.
What this means : The Cardinals love to run 13 personnel, meaning a third tight end (Quitoriano now) will be utilized in the run game often. The good news? He's a capable blocker and there shouldn't be any hiccups in his integration to meaningful playing time. Quitoriano's now on a standard NFL deal, so he gets a pay raise and can skip waivers if eventually released due to being a vested veteran.
Wills, a former top-ten pick, didn't play at all in 2025 as he rehabbed a knee injury and was plucked off the Buffalo Bills' practice squad to help fill in for Johnson. Wills has nearly 60 starts under his belt and is just 27 years old.
Wills, per NFL rules, must be on the Cardinals' active roster for a minimum of three weeks since he came from another team's practice squad.
What this means: It's unknown if Wills will be game-ready to start in Week 5, though the Cardinals obviously believe in Wills enough to snatch him and have him on the active roster. Arizona may not have loved the idea of starting a seventh-round rookie at left tackle this early in the season. Whether Wills is prepared with less than a week's notice remains to be seen, though the Cardinals obviously wanted a veteran in the mix.
Yeboah was a tight end who spent time with the Cardinals this summer as a camp body but was placed on injured reserve with a hamstring. He reached a settlement with Arizona and was cut in August and now makes his way back to the desert.
What it means: With Quitoriano now on the active roster, Arizona restores their tight end depth on the practice squad. He'll serve only as an emergency player in case of injuries ahead of him, though similar to Quitoriano — he at least knows the offense.
Jamison was signed to the Cardinals' practice squad on Sept. 3 as Arizona dealt with some injuries in the secondary. Even in spite of losing Will Johnson, Jamison is released with Art Green now the only cornerback on the team's practice squad.
Lee was signed to Arizona's practice squad on Sept. 1. With injuries to both Johnson and Adams along the line, Lee's dismissal is surprising, though Arizona now opts for more exterior depth as opposed to interior play.
Bios on each from the team's press release:
"Deculus (6-5, 330) has appeared in 26 games (six starts) in his NFL career with the Chargers (2025) and Texans (2022-24). He played 13 games (five starts) with Los Angeles last season after being acquired in a trade from Houston. The 27-year old Deculus entered the league with the Texans as a sixth-round pick (205th overall) in the 2022 NFL Draft out of LSU and spent his first three seasons in the league with Houston. He spent the preseason with the Titans.
"Perry (6-0, 211) spent the preseason with Green Bay and has previously been on the practice squads of the Texans, Patriots and Packers in his NFL career. He entered the league with Miami in 2024 as an undrafted rookie free agent from TCU. While at TCU, Perry played five seasons and appeared in 52 games, collecting 233 tackles (166 solo), 15.5 tackles for loss, 2.0 sacks, three interceptions, 13 passes defensed, one forced fumble and one fumble recovery."
Deculus is a player who simply bolsters the team's depth at tackle while Perry arrives to a Cardinals team that has multiple safeties down, including Andrew Wingard, Dadrion Taylor-Demerson and Kitan Crawford.

title: Cardinals Sign Big-Name OT After Paris Johnson Jr. Injury
full_text:
ARIZONA — The Arizona Cardinals were initially thought to be counting on depth as a result of Paris Johnson Jr.'s season-ending bicep injury.
On Tuesday, they flipped the script.
The Cardinals, per reports, are signing Buffalo Bills offensive tackle Jedrick Wills Jr. to their active roster.
From NFL insider Mike Garafolo on X:
"The #AZCardinals are signing OT Jedrick Wills off the #Bills practice squad, sources tell me and @RapSheet. The 10th overall pick in 2020 heads to Arizona after the team lost LT Paris Johnson Jr. for the season."
The #AZCardinals are signing OT Jedrick Wills off the #Bills practice squad, sources tell me and @RapSheet . The 10th overall pick in 2020 heads to Arizona after the team lost LT Paris Johnson Jr. for the season. @SalSports reported Wills was signing elsewhere. AZ it is. pic.twitter.com/SvoKGl9tDg
Johnson was just placed on injured reserve today. The Cardinals are 1-3 entering Week 5.
Wills has played five total seasons in the NFL and is 27-years-old. He was initially drafted by the Cleveland Browns as the tenth overall pick in the 2020 NFL Draft. He played his first few seasons in Cleveland before not playing at all in 2025 due to rehabbing his knee injury, which was an MCL sprain:
“I injured a couple of ligaments, but usually when people like when they get fell on or something in their knee, they mess up all their ligaments and people can just go in and repair it and they get healthy," Wills said earlier this offseason after signing with the Chicago Bears before being released ahead of final roster cuts.
"I had minimal damage to my ligaments. It was more of an alignment issue from where I got fell on. So they had to actually – it wasn't my knee, they had to go into my femur and do what was called an osteotomy to kind of correct my alignment. So my knee is healthy.”
He previously met with the New England Patriots and Detroit Lions this offseason before signing with Chicago and eventually Buffalo.
Wills signed with the Bills' practice squad ahead of the 2026 regular season. Since the Cardinals signed him directly off another team's practice squad, Wills is guaranteed to be on the 53-man roster for three weeks at minimum per NFL rules.
Wills has played in 58 games with 57 starts under his belt at left tackle. He's played in just 17 games once in his NFL career but when healthy, he's shown that he belongs.
As for the Cardinals, Arizona has seventh-round pick Jayden Williams behind him at left tackle and Josh Fryar on the right side of the offensive line at tackle.
Wills is generally viewed as a strong pass-blocker but struggles in run-blocking.

title: All of a Sudden, Cardinals' Offensive Line Looks Drastically Different
full_text:
ARIZONA — The Arizona Cardinals ' offensive line will look drastically different in Week 5.
The injury bug continues to rattle Arizona, as the Cardinals are losing left tackle Paris Johnson Jr. to a bicep injury that will keep him out for the rest of the season while right guard Isaiah Adams isn't likely to play this week according to head coach Mike LaFleur.
The Cardinals, almost overnight, are down two starters along the offensive line.
Injuries derailed the Cardinals way before the season started. Second-round pick Chase Bisontis suffered a torn MCL during preseason play, and now backup Jon Gaines appears to be prepared for action if Adams can't go.
Gaines is a player the Cardinals internally like. He's had a few years to develop, has spot-started recently for Arizona and has versatility to play any of their three interior spots along the offensive line.
Meanwhile, at left tackle, training camp darling and seventh-round pick Jayden Williams is set to take over for Johnson.
"Really, really impressed with Jayden. I think I’ve said that in here if I haven’t, but he’s wise beyond his years. He played big-time college football, so we have a lot of confidence in him," LaFleur said yesterday.
The Cardinals are down two starters entering Week 5's contest against the Detroit Lions. Running back Jeremiyah Love is also dealing with an ankle injury, but that's another story.
Yet no matter how you slice it, things have changed for Arizona — quickly.
According to ESPN's metrics, the Cardinals' offensive line ranks 31st in pass-block win rate and 21st in run-block win rate. Losing two starters along a unit that needs continuity more than any other isn't exactly a step in the right direction.
It's not as if other starters are playing well, either.
Isaac Seumalo hasn't been the presence many hoped he'd be after signing in free agency. Hjalte Froholdt is strong in pass protection but has struggled in the run while Elijah Wilkinson is very much the liability he was thought to be in free agency.
Arizona's offensive line ranks in the bottom third of average yards before contact on rushing plays at a mere 1.0.
Now, the Cardinals approach Week 5 and a Lions team that ranks second in team sacks (15) with an even more depleted unit and questions around their ability to win in the trenches.
"Each week can be a little bit different in terms of who you’re trying to ‘protect’ a little bit more and who’s going to have a little bit more of a stressful down," LaFleur said when asked how a game-plan changes due to injuries along the OL.
"You try to move that stress around a little bit so that it’s not just 60-plus plays of stress for those said players. There are a lot of factors.”

title: Falcons RB Brian Robinson Jr. Ready for More as Ravens Loom
full_text:
The Atlanta Falcons are riding the momentum of their best offensive stretch in a decade, and running back Brian Robinson Jr. played a major role in getting them there.
For the first time since the 2016 Divisional and NFCCG, the Falcons have put up 80 points (40 ppg) across two weeks. pic.twitter.com/qEqddMvitH
Robinson scored three rushing touchdowns in Atlanta’s victory over the New Orleans Saints, finishing with 62 rushing yards on 14 carries. His three touchdowns helped the Falcons establish control early and never look back as the offense continued its impressive turnaround.
Together, Robinson and Bijan Robinson helped Atlanta dominate on the ground. The duo combined for 207 rushing yards and five touchdowns, giving New Orleans few answers for the Falcons’ rushing attack.
“Just staying ahead of the sticks, being super efficient with the run game, and around it,” Robinson said. “I feel like me and B have just been doing a great job of just keeping the run game very efficient, and that obviously helps everything else around it.”
The Falcons have now won consecutive games after a difficult start to the season, and Robinson has been an important part of that turnaround. He has scored four touchdowns over Atlanta’s last two games while helping provide balance alongside Bijan.
Michael Penix Jr.’s recent play has also made the offense more difficult to defend. Penix completed 15 of 20 passes for 223 yards and a touchdown against New Orleans, forcing opposing defenses to respect both sides of Atlanta’s offense.
“Definitely,” Robinson said when asked if the passing game has opened things up on the ground. “I feel like they know they got to respect us. They gotta respect our run game. They got to respect our pass game. So, to leave them guessing, they don’t really know what to expect.”
Despite the offensive explosion, Robinson knows the Falcons cannot spend much time celebrating. The focus has already shifted toward the next challenge.
“We never want to get complacent, man,” Robinson said. “Regardless of what we did last week, after 24 hours, we flush it, and we got a new week ahead of us.”
That mentality will be critical as Atlanta moves forward, Robinson believes.
“Sky’s the limit, man,” Robinson boldly stated. “We can be as good as we want to be, long as guys continue to come in week in or week out and improve.”
The Saints game showed what Atlanta’s offense can look like when the rushing attack and passing game are working together. Now, Robinson and the Falcons have to prove they can carry that momentum into the next game vs Baltimore and continue building on what has been an impressive two week stretch.

title: Falcons QB Michael Penix Jr. Scouts Ravens Defense Ahead of Week 5 Showdown
full_text:
Michael Penix Jr. has helped transform the Atlanta Falcons offense since returning to the starting lineup, and his latest challenge will come against a Baltimore Ravens defense he believes has talent at every level.
The Falcons will host the Ravens on Sunday Night Football, with Penix preparing to face a Ravens team ranked 10th in the NFL in total defense, allowing 315.2 yards per game over four weeks.
Penix has been one of the biggest catalysts behind Atlanta's turnaround over the last two weeks. In his two starts, Penix has completed 33 of 45 passes for 479 yards, two touchdowns and one interception while posting a 113.1 passer rating.
The difference has been significant for Atlanta. The Falcons scored just 16 total points and produced 524 yards during the first two games of the season before Penix returned. In the two games since his return, Atlanta has scored 80 points and generated 918 total yards.
Now, Penix will have to keep that momentum going against Baltimore.
“They got some players. They got some ballplayers,” Penix said. “They're a really good team all around, but just talking defensively, I feel like they have guys everywhere.”
Penix believes the Ravens present a difficult matchup because of their depth across the defense.
“Their front is good, and they have backers that are good,” Penix said. “Their defensive backs are as good as, it's hard to find a weak point in their defense.”
Rather than focusing on one individual matchup, Penix emphasized the importance of Atlanta executing its game plan.
“But we’ve got to just lock into our scheme and trust our scheme,” Penix said. “And I know that the coaches, they'll make sure we have all the right things prepared for us so that we can come out and be successful again.”
One player who immediately stands out to Penix is Ravens linebacker Roquan Smith.
“He's a leader. He's the one that makes that whole defense go,” Penix said. “He has a lot of experience, played a lot of football, and he's definitely somebody that keeps them going,”
Then there is Kyle Hamilton, another versatile defender Penix knows will be a major factor.
Hamilton is frequently moved around Baltimore's defense, creating uncertainty for opposing quarterbacks before the snap.
“Yeah, for sure. He's a ball player, as well,” Penix said. “He's going to make plays. We're going to make plays, but we're excited for the challenge.”
The Falcons have gone from struggling to consistently move the football to averaging 40 points per game over their last two contests. Penix has provided stability, efficiency and explosive plays while allowing Atlanta's collection of offensive weapons to operate within Kevin Stefanski's system.
The Ravens will provide a much different test, but Penix appears ready for it.
After two impressive performances to begin his comeback, the Falcons quarterback will now have an opportunity to prove that his resurgence can continue against Baltimore's talented defense.

title: Falcons Get Major National Respect From Colin Cowherd
full_text:
The Atlanta Falcons have finally entered the national conversation across the NFL, and Colin Cowherd is buying what he's seen from the team through the first four weeks of the season.
In the latest edition of his Week 5 Herd Hierarchy, Cowherd ranked the Falcons No. 8 among the NFL's top teams, a significant sign of respect for a team that has won consecutive games after opening the season 0-2.
Cowherd's biggest reason for believing in Atlanta is the development of quarterback Michael Penix Jr. The third-year quarterback has looked increasingly comfortable under head coach Kevin Stefanski, particularly during the Falcons' last two games.
"What you're watching with Atlanta is not a mirage," Cowherd said.
Penix has started the Falcons' last two games and has delivered some of his best football since entering the NFL. In those two starts, he has completed 73 percent of his passes while posting a 113 passer rating.
Cowherd believes the coaching change has played a major role in Penix's emergence.
"Michael Penix broke into this league with a defensive coach," Cowherd said. "Then he gets Kevin Stefanski, who, when Cleveland fired him, interviewed for five jobs in about 45 minutes. He lands in Atlanta with all these weapons."
The results have been clear: the Falcons have scored 80 points in the two games since Penix returned to the lineup.
The Falcons' quarterback completed 15 of 20 passes for 223 yards and a touchdown in Atlanta's 45-24 Monday Night Football victory over the New Orleans Saints. The performance came one week after he helped lead the Falcons to a convincing victory over the Green Bay Packers.
For Cowherd, the most important part is that Penix is beginning to resemble the quarterback Atlanta believed it was getting when it selected him eighth overall in the 2024 NFL Draft.
"He always threw a beautiful ball, but he didn't have his guy," Cowherd said. "Michael Penix Jr. looked like he did last night and last week, like he did in college."
Penix's emergence has also coincided with the Falcons' offense finding its rhythm. Bijan Robinson has been one of the league's most productive running backs, while Drake London and Kyle Pitts give Penix multiple playmakers in the passing game.
After losing their first two games, the Falcons have responded with consecutive dominant victories. Now, they've entered the national conversation.
Cowherd's No. 8 ranking does not mean Atlanta has proven itself as one of the NFL's elite teams yet. However, it shows the Falcons are beginning to earn legitimate respect.
Atlanta seems to have found what it has been searching for: a confident quarterback and an offense that can make the Falcons a legitimate threat.
Cowherd's No. 8 ranking doesn't mean the Falcons have proven they're one of the NFL's elite teams, but they will have a chance to prove it Sunday night. The Baltimore Ravens come to Atlanta as one of the league's most well-regarded teams, giving Penix and the Falcons their biggest test yet.

title: Falcons No. 1 Rush Defense to Face New Challenge after Big Ravens Trade
full_text:
The Atlanta Falcons set out in the offseason to improve their run defense. They overhauled their defensive front in the offseason, partly out of a desire to improve the personnel and partly out of necessity due to players being out.
The results after the first month have been wildly spectacular. New general manager Ian Cunningham traded for two interior linemen in Gervon Dexter and Maason Smith, and the team got bigger at edge after losing Jalen Walker to injury and James Pearce Jr. to suspension.
After the first month of the season, the Falcons not only have the No. 1 rushing defense at 48.3 yards per game, but they'd have to give up 54% more yards per game to even fall to No. 2. They have by far the best run defense.
Atlanta's defensive front is scheduled to take on its toughest test of the season against Derrick Henry and the Baltimore Ravens. Quarterback Lamar Jackson is questionable for Sunday night , but the Ravens' rushing offense is still formidable. They're ranked No. 4 in the NFL at 153.5 yards per game (most of which had Jackson at the helm).
They accomplished the stellar rushing numbers despite being in a jam at center. Baltimore started the season with former Falcons practice squad member Jovaugn Gwyn for the first three games, and then turned to first-round pick Olaivavega Ioane last week against the Titans.
The Ravens were able to manage a 3-1 record against the Colts, Saints, Cowboys, and Titans, but the Falcons' defensive front poses a significantly bigger challenge. The Ravens weren't willing to risk their season on a question mark at center and pulled off a big trade with the Eagles for Pro Bowler Cam Jurgens.
The Ravens sent a fifth and a 2028 second-round pick to the Eagles for Jurgens and a seventh in a rare in-season trade that involves an offensive line starter.
We have agreed to trade C Cam Jurgens and a 2027 7th-round pick to Baltimore in exchange for a 2027 5th-round pick and a 2028 2nd-round pick. pic.twitter.com/8BtXXXtl2K
Jurgens started all four games for the Eagles this year. He was originally a second-round pick out of Nebraska in 2022 by Philadelphia. He's made the Pro Bowl in each of the last two seasons.
Even if he's not 100% familiar with the Ravens' offense by Sunday, he's still a plug-and-play center who will improve the quality of their line play when they take on the Falcons.
The Panthers' Chuba Hubbard rushed for 53 yards against the Falcons in Week 2. That's the most Atlanta has given up to a running back so far this season. The Ravens will lean heavily on Henry, especially if Jackson is out.
And they just got a big-time player on the offensive line.
The biggest challenge for the Falcons' defensive line just got a little bigger.

title: Falcons Waive Former UGA RB, Sign Former Patriots Draft Pick as Replacement
full_text:
The Atlanta Falcons are coming off back-to-back weeks of imposing their will on opposing defenses with their running game. Atlanta has the No. 2 rushing offense in the league, powered by Bijan Robinson and Brian Robinson Jr.
There hasn't been a lot of room for a third running back through the first four games of the year, but that hasn't stopped them from trying to improve the room with changes.
On Monday, the team announced they had placed popular undrafted free agent running back Cash Jones on waivers and signed former Jam Miller as a replacement.
Miller was selected by the New England Patriots in the seventh round of April's NFL Draft. He rushed 25 times for 92 yards in the preseason for the Patriots, but he didn't make their 53-man roster out of camp.
Miller was a key contributor for the Alabama Crimson Tide across a four-year career. His best season was 2024 when he had 668 yards rushing and seven touchdowns. He also added 16 catches for 155 yards and a touchdown.
Jones was considered to have an outside shot at making the Falcons' 53-man roster out of training camp. He was used at running back, wide receiver and on special teams after signing with the Falcons as an undrafted free agent out of Georgia in the spring.
He shined in the Falcon's preseason win over the Indianapolis Colts with seven carries for 41 yards, and he added four catches for 62 yards and a touchdown.
His versatility made him a possibility to make the team. However, the Falcons surprised everyone by keeping just two running backs on the active roster and releasing both Jones and Tyler Goodson. They both re-signed with the team as practice squad players, but Goodson was poached by the Cowboys and signed to their roster.
There's a strong possibility that Jones' time in Atlanta isn't done, and he could rejoin the practice squad in the near future. However, for now, the Falcons are still carrying just three running backs on the team.
The timing of the move is a little ironic for the former SEC stars, as the No. 2 Georgia Bulldogs travel to Tuscaloosa on Saturday night to take on the No. 6 Alabama Crimson Tide.
The Falcons will take on the Baltimore Ravens on Sunday Night Football. It will be their third-straight nationally televised game, and they're hoping to make it a third-straight win.

title: Homecoming or Breakout Party? Inside Falcons LB Harold Perkins Jr.'s Big Night
full_text:
Monday Night Football was a happy homecoming for Atlanta Falcons rookie linebacker Harold Perkins Jr.
It came at the expense of a sad “Domecoming” for the New Orleans Saints (1-3), as Atlanta (2-2) thrashed the NFC South arch rival 45-24 to spoil the 20th anniversary of the Caesars Superdome reopening after Hurricane Katrina .
“It was a surreal feeling,” said the New Orleans-born Perkins. “I was just trying to do my part and not let my teammates down. I was taking it all in.”
Perkins finished the primetime game tied with cornerback CJ Henderson for a team-high and career-high 10 tackles on the night. He notched his first career sack by getting half credit with safety Xavier Watts as they brought down Saints quarterback Tyler Shough in the backfield. Perkins added a quarterback hit.
Harold Perkins Jr. was everywhere last night, posting 7 tackles, 1 sack, 1 PBU, and 3 stops pic.twitter.com/0Oz3Ykh997
The highly versatile six-round NFL Draft pick out of LSU was also active in pass coverage, breaking up a pass.
“I thought Perk was outstanding,” Falcons head coach Kevin Stefanski said of the 6-foot-1, 223-pounder. “Really excited for Perk coming home. I thought he was really good.”
Perkins was just 11 months old when Hurricane Katrina tragically destroyed the city of New Orleans in August 2005. It forced his family to uproot and move to the greater Houston area, settling in Cypress, Texas, where he became a football star at Cypress High School.
Twenty-one years after disaster struck, a “beaucoup” number of Perkins family members watched him play his fourth career NFL game, and first in the Superdome. The Falcons linebacker said that around 30 family members, including his grandmother, were in the building to watch his standout performance.
Some were draped in Falcons gear, while some stayed loyal to their Saints fandom.
“It means a lot, just coming out there, coming back home,” Perkins, 22, said. “Not even just playing the Saints – be able to just be around my family, and they get to see me ball.”
With Perkins leading the way, Atlanta’s defense beleaguered the Saints all night.
New Orleans was held to 320 total yards: 270 passing and 50 rushing.
Shough was sacked twice, but spent the entirety of the game getting chased out of the pocket by the Falcons.
“We were out our top,” Perkins said. That means the Falcons unit was rabid and fierce.
“We played like some savages,” he added.
Per ESPN, Atlanta ranks eighth among the 32 NFL teams in total defense after Monday’s game.
Led by defensive coordinator Jeff Ulbrich , the Falcons have the league’s top run defense, as was evident in New Orleans.
“Credit our defense as a whole, our coaches for setting us up and putting us in the right positions to win,” Perkins said. “We just went out there and executed.”
The Falcons have a short, six-day turnaround before their next game.
They will finish their three-game primetime run at home against the Baltimore Ravens (3-1) on the Oct. 11 edition of Sunday Night Football.
Baltimore’s two-time NFL MVP quarterback Lamar Jackson has an outside chance of playing after spraining his left ankle in the second quarter of the Ravens’ Week 4 win against the Tennessee Titans. Jackson was in a protective walking boot and may miss extra games.
Tyler ‘Snoop’ Huntley will likely start against Atlanta if Jackson isn’t good to go.
Falcons-Ravens is set for an 8:20 p.m. kickoff from Mercedes-Benz Stadium. NBC will televise the game.

title: Falcons Power Rankings: The National Media Can't Agree on Atlanta
full_text:
The Atlanta Falcons dominated in a prime-time road game for the second week in a row , launching themselves from worst to first in the eyes of many in the national media. Yet, somehow, national power rankings still don't agree on the Falcons. Some list them in the top 15, while others rank them among the seven worst teams in the NFL.
The Falcons' next game can settle some of this debate.
Atlanta’s upcoming opponent, the Baltimore Ravens , are ranked as high as the No. 4 team in the NFL by some publications. The Falcons could see a serious rise next week if their offensive exploits continue on Sunday night.
The divisional beatdown elevated the Falcons in the NFL’s weekly power rankings across several platforms. Falcons OnSI pulled the results from those sites and put them all in one place for fans. Take a look below to see where the Falcons land compared with their division rivals.
After the Falcons dropped to No. 31 just two weeks ago, SI now lists them in the top 24 after their “ruination” of the Saints. It seems Conor Orr is starting to buy some of the hype, and he joked that we should all have prayer candles for Michael Penix Jr.'s continued health.
Elsewhere in the South, SI ranks the Panthers No. 14 (up nine spots), the Saints No. 25 (down five spots), and the Buccaneers No. 30 (idle).
Pete Prisco has more faith in the Falcons, lifting them into the league's top 20. He believes their season has turned around with Michael Penix Jr., and that is probably understating it -- Atlanta scored just 16 points in its first two games before putting up 35 against Green Bay and 45 against New Orleans.
Elsewhere in the South, CBS ranks the Panthers No. 18 (up eight spots), the Saints No. 23 (down five spots), and the Buccaneers No. 30 (down one spot).
Nick Shook is bullish on the Falcons after their consecutive weeks of domination. After having them as low as No. 31 after Week 2, he has Atlanta all the way up to No. 15 after Monday night. He said there should be “cautious” optimism about this team, but the next three weeks will determine how real this team could be – they have home games against Baltimore, Chicago, and San Francisco.
Elsewhere in the South, NFL.com ranks the Panthers No. 14 (up eight spots), the Saints No. 20 (down four spots), and the Buccaneers No. 30 (down 1 spot).
Despite describing the Falcons as “worst to first,” ESPN ranks them oddly low in its power rankings. Atlanta is somehow slotted behind the 0-4 Texans, the Packers (whom they just demolished in Week 3), and the Saints (whom they just demolished in Week 4).
Marc Raimondi highlighted the instant offensive turnaround since swapping Cooper Rush for Michael Penix Jr., but somehow that isn't enough to put them ahead of the teams they just embarrassed on national television? Strange.
Elsewhere in the South, ESPN ranks the Panthers No. 18 (up four spots), the Saints No. 21 (down three spots), and the Buccaneers No. 30 (idle).

title: Atlanta Falcons May Catch a Break With Baltimore Ravens Star Questionable
full_text:
The Atlanta Falcons could be facing the Baltimore Ravens without Lamar Jackson when the two teams meet on Sunday Night Football.
Jackson is dealing with a sprained ankle that gives him only an outside chance of playing against Atlanta, according to NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport .
Jackson could potentially miss multiple games depending on how his rehabilitation progresses, although the injury is not considered long-term and is not expected to require surgery.
The potential absence would be a significant blow to Baltimore. Jackson has been one of the NFL’s most productive quarterbacks this season, throwing for 967 yards with six touchdowns and one interception while completing 66.3 percent of his passes. He has also added 144 rushing yards and a touchdown on the ground.
Jackson was playing well before suffering the injury Sunday against the Tennessee Titans. He completed 15 of 20 passes for 222 yards and two touchdowns while adding 20 rushing yards in the first half as Baltimore built a 24 to 7 lead.
The injury occurred on a sack late in the first half, and Jackson did not return after halftime. He was seen leaving the stadium in a protective walking boot, adding to the concern surrounding his availability for Sunday’s matchup with Atlanta.
With Jackson sidelined, Tyler Huntley took over at quarterback to begin the second half. Huntley completed 8 of 9 passes for 63 yards and added 16 rushing yards on four carries. Although Baltimore was unable to score in the second half, the Ravens held on for a 24 to 18 victory.
Huntley’s performance could prove important if Jackson is unable to recover in time for Sunday. He is familiar with Baltimore’s offense and has previous starting experience with the Ravens, giving the team an experienced option behind Jackson.
Still, replacing Jackson would be a major challenge. His ability to make plays as both a passer and runner forces defenses to account for him on every snap. His mobility also creates opportunities for Baltimore’s rushing attack and play-action passing game.
Making it even more difficult for Hundley, the Falcons have the NFL's No. 1-ranked rushing defense . If they can focus on Derrick Henry without the threat of Jackson running, it will be hard to move the ball on the ground against Atlanta.
The Falcons will have to prepare as if Jackson could play until Baltimore makes an official decision. However, if he is ruled out, Atlanta would instead face Huntley and a Ravens offense that already gained experience playing without Jackson this season.
Jackson’s status will remain one of the biggest storylines throughout the week as Baltimore monitors his recovery.

title: Former Jaguars Top 10 Pick Finally Seeing His Work Pay Off with Atlanta Falcons
full_text:
C.J. Henderson has spent the past few seasons trying to find the consistency that made him a top-10 pick in the NFL Draft. On Monday night, he showed the Atlanta Falcons why they believed he could provide it.
With A.J. Terrell on injured reserve, Henderson has stepped into a starting role at cornerback. Rather than simply filling a void, he delivered one of his most productive performances in recent memory during Atlanta’s dominant win over the New Orleans Saints.
Henderson led the Falcons with 10 total tackles while adding a pass deflection and forcing a fumble that he also recovered.
It was the type of performance defensive coordinator Jeff Ulbrich envisioned when discussing Henderson earlier in the week.
“CJ is a tremendous luxury. In my opinion, he’s a one (cornerback). He’s a guy that would start on a lot of teams,” Ulbrich said.
Ulbrich also believes Henderson gives Atlanta security at cornerback while Terrell is sidelined and was excited to see him “show this league exactly who he is now.”
Henderson did just that against New Orleans.
His strip of Saints running back Kendre Miller created the only turnover in the game when the Falcons needed it most, up 7-0 early. Henderson looked ready for the moment and said as much.
“I had confidence. I’ve been working on my craft, you know, and letting my work come to life,” Henderson said.
That opportunity became even more important once Terrell went on injured reserve. Atlanta suddenly needed Henderson to take on a larger role in the secondary, and the former No. 9 overall pick responded.
“I’m out there attacking the ball, making plays,” Henderson said. “I feel like I can help this team.”
Henderson’s road to Atlanta has not been straightforward. Jacksonville selected him ninth overall in 2020 with the expectation that he could become a cornerstone of its secondary. Injuries and inconsistent play limited his time with the Jaguars, however, and Jacksonville eventually traded him to Carolina during the 2021 season.
Henderson spent three years with the Panthers as a part-time starter, and spent 2024 on the Texans' and Steelers' practice squads without making an appearance.
Atlanta provided a new opportunity for Henderson last season, and he's elevated his game in 2026.
The Falcons secondary played with confidence throughout Monday night’s victory, and Henderson credited preparation and trust for the unit’s performance.
“Just by doing our job, trusting our keys, trusting our training,” Henderson said. “That’s what we harp on during the week.”
Henderson acknowledged there are still plays the secondary needs to clean up, but his performance provided Atlanta with an encouraging development while Terrell remains unavailable.
10 tackles, a forced fumble and recovery, and a pass breakup made Henderson one of the Falcons’ most productive defenders Monday night.
Now, the challenge is turning that performance into consistency.
“I feel good,” Henderson said. “When you have a lot of confidence coming in, I mean, I’m still in there. We’ve got to finish on it.”
For Henderson, Monday night was an opportunity to show that the work he has continued to put in is translating when his number is called.
For the Falcons, it may have shown they have more depth at cornerback than they realized.

title: Falcons RB Bijan Robinson Making History in Prime Time
full_text:
Atlanta Falcons running back Bijan Robinson continues to prove that the bigger the stage, the better he plays.
Robinson delivered another dominant primetime performance Monday night against the New Orleans Saints, rushing for 145 yards and two touchdowns on 19 carries in Atlanta’s 45-24 victory. The performance continued an incredible stretch for Robinson, who performs best when the lights are brightest.
The numbers go beyond that streak. Since the 1970 NFL/AFL merger, Robinson currently owns the highest scrimmage yards per game average in primetime history, with 145.4 yards per game across his first 11 primetime appearances.
At this point, it is becoming more than a trend.
Robinson has established himself as one of the NFL’s most dangerous players when the lights are brightest, and Monday night provided another reminder of why.
The Falcons wasted no time getting him involved. On Atlanta’s third play from scrimmage, Robinson broke loose for a 59-yard touchdown that immediately quieted the Superdome crowd.
BIJAN ROBINSON. TO. THE. HOUSE. ESPN | ANF pic.twitter.com/MwZu66Ji8p
Robinson credited his offensive line for creating the opportunity.
“They made the hole right there on that backside, and I just took it,” Robinson said.
Once he found open space, Robinson had one goal.
“I was just like, ‘Can’t get caught.’”
The explosive run set the tone for a Falcons offense that scored 45 points and has now put up 80 points over its last two games. Robinson has been at the center of that offensive turnaround, but he was quick to give credit to everyone around him.
The @AtlantaFalcons are the only team in NFL history to have a 2-game span with: 80+ points 800+ total yards 8+ rushing TDs no more than 1 turnover no more than 1 sack allowed pic.twitter.com/C70yfZYCFs
“It’s fun to see just the O line and just how they bring so much energy to this offense,” Robinson said. “Without those guys, we don’t have what we have.”
Robinson also credited offensive coordinator Tommy Rees for having them ready.
“It’s all in the preparation, and we saw that look,” Robinson said.
That preparation allowed Atlanta to establish the run early while also opening opportunities for quarterback Michael Penix Jr. Robinson believes Penix’s ability to threaten defenses through the air has made the entire offense more dangerous.
“He helps out with the run game,” Robinson said. “You can’t just stack the box because you have to respect that he can get the ball anywhere on the field.”
The combination has made Robinson increasingly difficult to contain, particularly in primetime.
Still, Robinson is not interested in letting the recent success create complacency.
“This is a great win, but you gotta keep on getting better. Gotta keep on getting better,” Robinson said.
That mindset may be just as important as his production.
Robinson understands the attention surrounding the Falcons will continue to grow if they keep winning, but he wants the team focused.
“As a leader of the team, I try to make sure that the guys don’t get complacent,” Robinson said. “We’re always just trying to stay alive, stay humble, and stay focused on the task at hand.”
For now, though, there is no denying what Robinson has become.
When the lights come on, the Falcons keep handing him the football.
And Robinson keeps delivering.

title: The Ravens Must Emphasize These 3 Things To Upset The Falcons
full_text:
The Ravens are underdogs for the first time under rookie head coach Jesse Minter, and rightfully so.
The Falcons board the second-best run game in the NFL – and at 477 yards the last two weeks since Michael Penix Jr. took over at quarterback, it’s really the best (Bijan Robinson is averaging a cool 7.4/carry running outside zone). They are allowing an NFL-best 2.7 yards per carry – a half yard better than the rest of the NFL – and also have the number one pass rush in the league. And they are at home on a Sunday night.
The Ravens’ injury report continues to look quite imposing, from quarterback Lamar Jackson (ankle) not practicing all week, on down ( there are going to be quite a few absences ) and rookie offensive coordinator Declan Doyle must also navigate a makeshift offensive line for at least another week until new trade acquisition Cam Jurgens is out of the concussion protocol ( a lot about that risky trade is odd ).
It’s a lot to digest and the team is also in its second week back from traveling to another continent to play a football game in Brazil and some around the game believe the impact of that can take hold more acutely in the second week back. Baltimore’s run game is going nowhere with this offensive line right now no matter what Derrick Henry tries, which could spell big problems with backup QB Snoop Huntley not nearly as adept pushing the ball downfield as Jackson is (Lamar is leading the NFL at 10.1 yards/attempt and Huntley is at 5.9/attempt in his career.
Still, the Falcons have not yet proven to be a juggernaut under new coach Kevin Stefanski, the Ravens have a strong understanding of how he likes to operating facing him for years in Cleveland and Ravens offensive line coach Dwayne Ledford came over from Atlanta so he should have as good a read on Bijan Robinson as anyone, not that it will matter.
There is a path to win, and it will take the Ravens adhering to these principles:
The Ravens have played just five snaps in a 4-3 look all season. They should double that in the first half Sunday night. They’ve played just 24 snaps in a 3-4. Being in nickel or dime 90% of the time won’t fly against these Dirty Birds, and Minter has to know that .
“I think it is an exciting challenge for us, when you pride yourself on stopping the run,” middle linebacker Roquan Smith said. “Lot of respect for [Bijan Robinson] as a runner, their offensive line, their receivers, with their willingness to block. I think it is a great challenge for us. I look at this as a front-seven game. It is about showing up, and obviously the whole world's watching, so showing up and showing out."
Um, maybe a front-eight game. Could line up with Zion Young and Tavius Robinson on the edge, Calais Campbell (a former Falcon) and Nnamdi Madubuike inside (or even a Broderick Washington type), with hybrid defensive back Kyle Hamilton mugging the line of scrimmage as a de-facto LB, along with linebackers Smith, Trenton Simpson and Teddye Buchanan on the field.
We should see some personnel deployments Sunday that we have not seen prior. This difficult of this assignment dictates it.
So the line is still shaky and do-it-all-blocking tight end Durham Smythe was lost for the season, and we are asking more of a rookie tight ends that was expected. But, it appears both starting tackles – Ronnie Stanley and Roger Rosengarten are good to go. Running behind them has been one of the few things to work for the Ravens lately on the ground, and the perimeter attack will be huge all around Sunday , and extra tackle Carson Vinson should see plenty of the field.
The Falcons are mauling people at the line of scrimmage (72% success rate against the run is nuts) and not devoted a ton of manpower to do so. Ravens have to find a way to swing the math at least a little more in their favor and unbalanced lines and tackle-eligible plays can make that happen.
“For you to be No. 1 in the run game,” Henry explained of the Falcons, “you have to have guys that are willing to go tackle by any means. And it means something to them, from what we see on tape."
Doyle kept going on and on Thursday morning about nothing changing in terms of his overarching offensive goals if he has to play Huntley (he will). Um, that best just be lip service.
“Absolutely, when we put the game plan together, the mindset is still the same,” Doyle opined on Thursday. "We are still trying to stress and attack rules. We are still trying to go after a defense and see if we can pry out bigger plays and be able to move the ball down the field."
This needs to be a scaled -down approach loaded with high-percentage routes and checkdowns everywhere against a team getting a 47% pressure rate without having to blitz (20%, 29th in NFL). Short routes to the outside and trying to crate situations for big YAC is what is required here. Huntley is erratic throwing downfield and doesn't have Jackson's arm; the approach must reflect that.
Henry is already on pace to shatter his 15 receptions last season (seven through four games) and he should get fed some in the air by design – again, to the outside. More bubble screens and passes behind the line of scrimmage might be in order.

title: What The Ravens Thursday Injury Report Reveals About Sunday's Game
full_text:
Ravens coaches continue to claim two-time MVP Lamar Jackson could face the Falcons Sunday, while execs around the NFL wonder if he will even face the Browns in Week 6.
The superstar quarterback did not practice again Thursday with an ankle injury that kept him out of the second-half last week, had him in a walking boot and required an MRI test. Head coach Jesse Minter and offensive coordinator Declan Doyle certainly want Atlanta to wonder who will be at quarterback Sunday night, but trust me, the Falcons are expecting back-up Snoop Huntley for myriad and obvious reasons.
Minter claims the Ravens could take it right up until game time, but having Jackson play this early in the season on an injury like this would run counter to how they have already handled similar situations with star receiver Zay Flowers and left tackle Ronnie Stanley and $30M pass rusher Trey Hendrickson. Jackson, who is essentially in a walk year with no guarantees beyond this season , has traditionally required a week or two to be able to trust his body fully enough to play with lower-grade injuries in the past, and the Ravens offensive line remains under duress (we’ll see if just-acquired center Cam Jurgens can return from a concussion in Week 6 ) and the Falcons have the NFL’s premier pass rush right now.
So, yeah, it will be Huntley at QB, and the Ravens will also almost certainly be without Humphrey (calf) – in a career tailspin for years and injury-prone but carrying the top cap hit of any corner in the NFL and making $19.3M – as well. Hendrickson, also with a significant injury history, has yet to practice since getting a procedure on his finger last week that Minter said would get him back on the field quickly.  Hendrickson was signed to a $30M/year deal after Ravens general manager hid behind Maxx Crosby’s alleged medical issues ( he’s only playing about 95% of the reps for the Raiders ) to bail out of that trade.
Thursday is the last heavy practice day of the week and the participation generally is a strong indicator about Sunday.
Flowers has been limited with an ongoing hamstring injury but he is playing barring some unforeseen setback. The Ravens are trying to navigate left tackle Ronnie Stanley through a painful toe injury and limiting his practice reps but he practiced in full Thursday. Hybrid defensive back Kyle Hamilton has been nursing a groin injury and was limited Wednesday but practiced full on Thursday and also is in line to play.
Guards John Simpson (groin) and Andrew Vorhees (foot) did not practice Wednesday but returned in a limited capacity on Thursday. Simpson has been playing through this situation all season and started every game. The Ravens would be foolish to move rookie guard Vega Ioane from center . He should remain deployed between those two (on youngster Emery Jones Jr. if he has to fill in) for one more week until Jurgens can likely return.

title: Ravens Trade For Eagles Center Cam Jurgens Deserves Two Grades: We Explain Both
full_text:
The Ravens have known they needed a legitimate starting center option since the February scouting combine when star Tyler Linderbaum had a market far beyond where they wanted to go.
They also had exclusive negotiating rights to Linderbaum for the duration of his rookie contract and failed to get him extended before the 2025 season, when both he and two-time MVP quarterback Lamar Jackson required contract extensions and neither got close. So any window into the Ravens dealing two picks, a fifth in 2027 and a second-round selection in 2028, to take on Eagles lineman Cam Jurgens , who had major back/nerve surgery in February 2025 and has not been the same since, and move him back to his natural position of center has to start there.
Any evaluation of an in-season trade with a general manager as accomplished as the Eagles GM Howie Roseman must factor in the health and current status of the player, and the situation into which Jurgens is being parachuted – bleak with Baltimore’s interior offensive as bad as any in football and getting exploited in the pass rush and unable to sustain any interior rushing presence even for the great and powerful Derrick Henry. It’s a complicated transaction that merits two evaluating grades in real-time given the player’s highly-unusual injury history.
And after having time to speak to two outside general managers about this trade and some former general managers and salary cap guy and some other current NFL personnel executives, it became clear the spectrum to use for setting a standard of what this transaction could realistically offer the Ravens.
There is no way around the fact the Ravens dug themselves an ugly hole here by mismanaging this critical situation – while installing a new offense with a rookie offensive coordinator and with issues across the offensive line beyond just center. Their 30-year-old first-time play caller, Declan Doyle, always needed a proven veteran leader at this position – his mentor Sean Payton told us so this offseason – and the fact they didn’t take their pick of any available in the second round of the draft – before the run on interior OL begun that everyone in the league knew was about to begin – they probably solve this problem far more cheaply than what it’s come to now.
They weren’t fooling anyone pretty budget signings Danny Pinter and Jovaughn Gwyn were anything close to starting-caliber players (“They don’t have an NFL center on their roster, they just don’t,” longtime lineman and NFL analyst Brian Baldinger told me this summer), and when those guys got hurt (along with late signing Ethan Pocic who never looked right coming off Achilles surgery) the huge problem became suffocating .
The Ravens’ history is to draft and develop centers and they truly value them, because a lot of people thought Linderbaum went too high in the first place when they took him in the first round. They have resisted paying them top dollar going all the way back to Jason Brown . Holding 11 picks and not addressing this in a draft with myriad options was always odd and taking a hope-and-prayer pass rusher in Zion Young (yes, he can set the edge) struck us as ridiculously odd at the time and plenty of execs around the league agreed.
“You only make this move if you are desperate,” one GM told me, who also noted: "Those guys aren't exactly quick to trade picks that high (second round).
Jurgens has traveled to South America to get treatment for ongoing nerve issues and he gutted through 14 games last season but was in extreme pain and was not good on the field. The issue spread up and down his legs. The Eagles know his medicals better than anyone and were willing to unload him at a time their All-Pro guard, Landon Dickerson, is on IR and all-world tackle, Lane Johnson, just basically retired for mental health reasons. So when they do this, it raises major red flags about the medicals for a player who has a high pain threshold but carries big risks, or “serious medical red flags” as another GM put it:
“Jurgens is still a good player, he is, we have good grades on his film. And it’s a major upgrade to anything Baltimore had there. But … Howie isn’t mailing it in. He’s not tanking. No way Howie does this if he’s convinced this is a starter for him - at center or guard or anywhere - for the rest of that contract.”
Jurgens makes $16.5M this season and is essentially guaranteed $15M of his $17.5M salary for 2027 and carries that same figure for 2028, without such current guarantees.
“What are the Ravens thinking?” said one longtime NFL exec who watches the Eagles closely. “The good, but not really great, Cam, left once he had the back surgery. You don’t see trades like this for interior offensive linemen and this one had back surgery and the tape since then is not the same, including at center.”
Jurgens is a two-time Pro Bowl player and replaced a Hall of Fame center in Jason Kelce and learned from him before taking over. He anchored a dominating, Lombardi-trophy winning, offensive line loaded with Alphas. He is a warrior and brings a different profile and resume into that offensive line than anyone else’s, even decorated left tackle Ronnie Stanley.
"At the center position, you really are the voice of the offense out there," offensive line coach Dwayne Ledford said Thursday, hinting strongly at how much having a true vet center matters, as we've said all along.
Jurgens says he feels great this season, it was an ugly situation in Philly (although the one he’s walking into has issues, too), and the Ravens get to move stud rookie Vega Ioane back to guard, where he can maul, and perhaps they will be able to improve in pass protection and run blocking in the interior. Given the price they paid, they must.
Teams were blitzing the A Gap with abandon before Ioane stabilized things Week 4, stunts and twists were gutting them, and there seemed to be very little connective tissue between the center and guards no matter which combination Baltimore tried. Jurgens’s presence and intangibles change that, and they Ravens made big additions to their medical team this offseason and they have to hope they can keep Jurgens as healthy and pain-free as possible but he plays a car-crash position and some wonder if all the years of the Eagles running the “Tush Push” into the ground, literally, has taken years off those linemen.
“They may have just solved their biggest problem,” said one NFL personnel executive. “And if this isn’t their starting center the next three years, they just made it worse.”
But by Week 6, if indeed Jurgens is out of concussion protocol, the Ravens should have a better foundation in the middle of their line than at any point since Linderbaum left and they have to do whatever they can to maintain that as long as possible.
"He isn't a guard, strictly a center,” Baldinger suggested to me after the trade. “It allows Ioane to stay at guard where he can be the next (potential future Hall of Famer Marshal) Yanda."
