title: Ravens Georgia Natives Look Forward To Homecomings vs. Falcons
full_text:
Although the Baltimore Ravens will be the visiting team at Mercedes-Benz Stadium on Sunday night when they take on the red-hot Atlanta Falcons in primetime, two of their core leaders and best players on the defensive side of the ball will not only feel right at home but will also have a large contingent of supporters in attendance.
Both three-time All Pro safety Kyle Hamilton and four-time Pro Bowl inside linebacker Roquan Smith grew up in Georgia and are looking forward to business trip that will double as homecoming for them.
Hamilton hails from Atlanta and attended Marist School, a private Catholic school located in Brookhaven, Georgia. This interconference Battle of the Birds will be a true "full-circle moment" for him, given that his first opportunity to play at the Falcons' home stadium was supposed to be while he was in high school for a state championship game. But Mother Nature had other plans that fateful day.
"That got snowed out, and they moved it to my home stadium my junior year of high school," Hamilton said. "We actually lost that game. It still bugs me. But, yes, it will be cool to play in front of a ton of people that I know, grew up with and have people from Mobile, Alabama — where my dad's side is from — coming up. So, it will be really cool to just see everybody. My family does not have to travel, so that will be easy for them, and hopefully [we will] leave with a win."
Smith is a country boy from Macon County, Ga., which is about a two-hour drive from Atlanta. Unlike Hamilton, who starred at Notre Dame, when it came time to choose where to play at the collegiate level, he opted to stay closer to home and play for the University of Georgia.
While he got to play in some big games on the Falcons' home turf in front of fans as a Bulldog, he has yet to do so as a pro since he got traded to the Ravens during the 2022 season, prior to the Chicago Bears road game in Atlanta in Week 11 of that season. He plans on making the most of this opportunity not only for himself but for the small community that raised him.
"I have my high school football team coming up. I have the rec department coming up. I have like countless family members, countless friends and stuff showing up," Smith said. "It will be pretty sweet, man. [It's] obviously a quick little drive, about two hours, two hours and 20 minutes, and guys [are] coming from the country.
"There will be a heavy 'Macon County Roquan Tribe' out there. I am excited about that, but obviously the mission stays the same. With all the people coming to support, [I] definitely have to show up in a big-time way. That is just going to take me just doing my job, play in and play out, and playing violent."
As two of the central players in the spine of head coach and defensive play-caller Jesse Minter's unit that has underwhelmed and struggled with consistency through the first four weeks, both Hamilton and Smith are determined to take advantage of the opportunity to right the ship under a national spotlight.
The whole world will be watching, and we will be doing what it takes to get the job done," Smith said. "We know that it will be a challenge, but we are all excited for it.
"We are just excited to continue to showcase who we are and just keep building off our positives week in and week out, and building off the negatives as well and not having self-inflicted things.
They both serve as physical tone-setters for the team on that side of the ball and are well aware that any hopes they have of cooling or at least slowing down a 2-2 Falcons team that has looked like a juggernaut and averaged 40 points a game over the past two weeks begin and end with how well they defend First Team All Pro running back Bijan Robinson .
"I think [Robinson] is super talented in everything that he does," Hamilton said. "He is very sudden, very strong, explosive. Obviously, he has the stats to back it up and, you know, there is not a lot like him. So, it is up to us to be where we are supposed to be. I think that is the big thing first and foremost, especially in the run game. Do not get out of your gap, trust guys to come and do their job and I think we will be fine."
The Ravens have particularly struggled when it comes to tackling in space and run defense when it comes to yards given up before contact. They can't afford for either tendency to persist or rear its ugly head against the Falcons because they get steamrolled by one of the hottest and best-balanced teams in the league in primetime.
"I think it is an exciting challenge for us, when you pride yourself on stopping the run," Smith said. "[I have] a lot of respect for [Bijan Robinson] as a runner, their offensive line, their receivers, with their willingness to block. I think it is a great challenge for us. I look at this as a front-seven game. It is about showing up, and obviously the whole world's watching, so showing up and showing out."

title: Ravens Week 4 Rookie Report: Vega Ioane Aces Major Test With Flying Colors
full_text:
Several members of the Baltimore Ravens' 2026 rookie class saw extended action in Sunday's grind of a 24-18 long-awaited home win over the Tennessee Titans in Week 4. They are in an AFC North division in which every team's record is .500 or better, and they are tied with the Cleveland Browns atop the standings heading into next week.
Drafted and undrafted first-year players saw extensive playing time in all three phases. The only rookie who was a healthy scratch was undrafted quarterback Joe Fagnano, who still suited up as an emergency No. 3 option. Fifth-round running back Adam Randall is eligible to return from short-term injured reserve after this game, while third-round wide receiver Ja'Kobi Lane will remain on it for at least one more week after getting hurt in Week 1. Seventh-round defensive tackle Rayshaun Benny is on the practice squad and has yet to be elevated.
Here’s an overview of how these rookies performed in their late taste of NFL regular-season action.
The first-round interior offensive lineman made his fourth career start but played his first full game at center after he first slid over from his right guard spot to help close out last week's dramatic win. Not only was Ioane playing out of position, but he was going up against one of the best interior defensive linemen in the league, the Titans' star Jeffery Simmons. He kept Lamar Jackson clean by not allowing a sack, a quarterback hit or even a single pressure on Simmons' 32 pass-rush snaps and held the four-time Pro Bowler without a tackle for loss as well. His overall grade of 75.1 from Pro Football Focus was the fourth-highest mark on the team.
A sampling of Vega Ioane's first game at center. 💪 pic.twitter.com/ZNeBJ8MtGM
"It was pretty solid. I would say, [there were] a lot of mistakes on my end," Ioane said. "I take full responsibility for that. There were a lot of plays where I did not snap the ball at the right time [or] right cadence, things like that. But we have a lot of time to fix that. [I want to just give a] big shoutout to the guys around me, the whole [offensive] line, the receivers, the quarterbacks. They had full trust in me going out there. They have been helping me out throughout the entire game, so big shoutout to them."
Now that the Ravens have traded for two-time Pro Bowl center Cam Jurgens , they can slide Ioane back over to his natural spot, where he's been the most dominant. However, knowing that the youngster is capable of moving over and playing at a high level is a testament to his versatility and could serve them well if they ever find themselves in a similar pinch in the future.
The second-rounder played nearly 40% of the Ravens' total defensive snaps and had another solid game against the run, where he consistently set a strong edge on early downs and finished with a pair of assisted tackles.
classic zion young pic.twitter.com/a7FgiIX0zh
The fourth-rounder was active for the second time this season, but unlike his uneventful debut, where he didn't log a snap on offense or special teams, he logged 23 snaps and his first career catch and targets. Both of the passes that came his way were from Jackson during the last drive of the first half on back-to-back plays. The first resulted in a 13-yard reception that moved the ball just inside the range of second-year kicker Tyler Loop and the second target was just off the mark on a shallow route.
I don’t know about you guys, but I was starting to get worried about Elijah Sarratt. I’m glad the Ravens finally got him on the field! pic.twitter.com/WKCcXuLkWu
As key as the yardage he picked up on that drive was to set up an M&T Bank Stadium record 64-yard field goal, he committed one of several back-breaking penalties for the offense. Sarratt was flagged for holding while attempting to make a block downfield that negated an impressive 29 yard scramble by Jackson late in the second quarter that would've moved the ball near midfield.
The fourth-rounder recorded multiple new season highs for the second week in a row, playing 37 offensive snaps and hauling in both of his targets for the second week in a row for a career-high 34 receiving yards. His first catch went for a career-long 25-yard catch-and-run that was the result of a masterful play call by offensive coordinator Declan Doyle that got him streaking wide open down the field. His second catch almost went for a first down, as he picked up nine yards to jump-start an early fourth-quarter drive that looked like it was going to end with points had it not stalled out at midfield.
More good scheme by Declan Doyle. Fake screen setup gets the Titans' LB to bite and leave Matt Hibner wide open for a 25 yarder. pic.twitter.com/weIUHZ6AnC
"He is a smart dude, but he's continued just to work and learn and get better in blocking, [and] with anything he's asked to do, he does it, and he does it at a high level," Mark Andrews said. "So, [there's] just a lot of upside with him, and he's going to continue to make big plays and help this team win games."
The fifth-rounder played over 40% of the Ravens' total defensive snaps for the second week in a row, as he has clearly carved out a role in their defense. He recorded a career-high five total, all of which were solos, and he recorded his second career tackle for a loss on a third-down checkdown to a running back one yard behind the line of scrimmage to force a punt. Rivers was also responsible for allowing the touchdown completion to Titans' wide receiver Wan'Dale Robinson late in the fourth quarter that made the final score look closer than it actually was and felt for most of the second
The fifth-rounder saw his most extensive playing time of the season thus far for the second week in a row, with 27 combined between offense and special teams, including a season-high 18 on offense and nine on special teams, getting more reps with blocking tight end Durham Smythe lost for the season. He wasn't targeted but recorded his first career tackle on special teams when he ran Titans wide receiver Chimere Dike out of bounds after punt return of 10 yards in the third quarter.
The sixth-round specialist had another strong performance in a game that saw him attempt a career-high six punts and record a career-high 284 punt yards. He was a field-flipping weapon once again, helping the Ravens win the battle of field position by pinning the Titans' offense inside their 20-yard line four times and recording one touchback. He averaged 47.3 yards per punt and a long of 56.
With four-time Pro Bowl veteran edge rusher out recovering from finger surgery, the undrafted free agent got to play his first regular-season snaps on defense after playing exclusively on special teams through the first three weeks. He checked into the game on the Titans' second drive, played 16 snaps and made the most of his first extended opportunity in the fourth quarter on Tennessee's final possession when he recorded his first career sack. After the guard failed to pick him up on a stunt, Burke used his length to dive at the legs of Ward. His 14 snaps on special teams were the most among all rookies and tied for fourth-most on the team.

title: 3 Changes Ravens Must Make To Slow Down Bijan Robinson Sunday
full_text:
There is a very real chance the Falcons run all over the Ravens Sunday night in Atlanta.
In what is a homecoming game for two of the faces of the Baltimore defense – linebacker Roquan Smith and hybrid defensive back Kyle Hamilton – the challenge could not be steeper, with the Falcons rolling since young quarterback Michael Penix Jr. returned from injury and running back Bijan Robinson looking like an MVP candidate as a running back/overall offensive weapon and powerful back Brian Robinson forming a potent tandem with him.
Atlanta has legit weapons in the pass game too, with Drake London and Kyle Pitts, so this is a unique challenge. But if the Ravens, who have struggled against the run playing lighter boxes and a lot of dime coverage this season (six defensive backs), cannot mitigate rushing disaster on first and second down, they will be hard-pressed to tamp down the scoring on a fast track in a dome in a game in which is it almost certain back-up quarterback Snoop Huntley will be playing over two-time MVP Lamar Jackson .
“I think it’s a great challenge for us,” said Smith, who played at Georgia and is from a small town a few hours outside Atlanta. “And I look at this as a front-seven game … I’m focused on Atlanta, stopping this running attack, and getting all 11 hats to the ball and being our best selves.”
All 11 defenders – corners and everyone else included – being attuned to the run game, and the ability for this legit offensive line (though dealing with an injury to tackle Jake Matthews from last week) to turn a one-cut outside zone look into an 85-yard TD run, is required all the time.
“It’s a necessity against guys like Bijan,” said Hamilton, an Atlanta native. “All 11 is needed because he can make 10 miss; that 11th guy might make a touchdown-saving tackle.”
Here’s how the Falcons rank running the football through for weeks:
Rush Att: 139 (2nd)      Yds/Carry: 5.2 (2nd)     Rush TD: 8 (2nd)           1stDown%: 31.7 (2nd)
Expected Points Added: 13.4 (2nd)
However, they played with Cooper Rush at quarterback the first two weeks and as Ravens fans saw last season that means playing without a QB, and since Penix stepped in Week 3, Atlanta has 477 yards rushing in two games (Chicago is second at 360), averaging 5.9/carry (1st) with an unfathomable 22.1 EPA (Jacksonville is second at 7.9).
It’s going to take a village and here’s what rookie coach Jesse Minter is likely to try:
Second-year LB Teddye Buchanan has only played a few games since returning from a late-season ACL tear as a rookie. But he gets better each week and the Ravens are going to have to adjust markedly to how they approach this game.
Minter’s usual desire to get six DBs on the field as much as possible is out the window, and he played a 3-4 look nearly a third of the time against the Titans last week and he can’t avoid this reality Sunday night. Some looks like Buchanan and Smith and ascending linebacker Trenton Simpson and with Hamilton in a LB role or mugging the line of scrimmage is going to be what’s in order here.
The Ravens shouldn’t still be ranking second in the NFL in use of dime after this game. Can’t happen.
“It is figuring out who your best 11 are for specific situations, specific personnel sets that the offense is in,” Minter said Monday. “You can have three linebackers out there and they can have three receivers on the field, and you can end up in a mismatch in a hurry. So, it is always weighing the best personnel against what they have. We had all three out there a few snaps yesterday against some 12 personnel, kind of mixed in some different groupings with those guys. But I think as Teddye has come back and proven to be now capable of playing some more snaps, that we will certainly try to find ways to get use out of both him and Trenton.”
The Ravens want to get their money’s worth out of $30M edge rusher Trey Hendrickson . But he just had a finger surgery, he was not the same the last few weeks dealing with that injury and he is not good against the run. He will be a target to attack in that regard on early downs with the sinister outside zone these guys run.
I’m not saying you don’t dress him if he is cleared, but I am being careful about how I use him, I am leaning into big bodies and they took Zion Young in the second-round - over basically any center in the draft - because he can anchor. He and Tavius Robinson might need to be the duo on the edge in base looks when they are feigning 4-3 front. And the Ravens are going to need run stuffers like Broderick Washington to make a real impact here and show more impact than they have to this point, and former Falcon Calais Campbell returning to Atlanta should bring out the best in him.
This is the bread and butter; it gets Bijan Robinson in space, stretches the defense horizontally and this back is a genius at finding the right gap to attack and is an athletic marvel who can make two guys miss and cut it back the other way, anyway, if he is “blocked.” This will be pounded into the defense’s head all week, but they have to be so sound to understand their assignment and fill their lane.
“The outside zone scheme and stretch and things of that nature truly forces you to be gap sound,” Smith said. “That’s what it’s about - striking guys and being gap sound … Knowing that (Bijan Robinson) puts stress on the entire field at all times.”
The Falcons have run outside zone 77 times this season, second most in the NFL, and they average a ridiculous 6.9/carry when they do and have already scored four touchdowns doing it. Bijan Robinson averages 7.4/carry when he runs outside zone. Buckle up and be aware.
If this springs something early the Falcons will be relentless with running it.

title: NFL GMs Explain 3 Pros And 2 Cons Of Ravens Trade For Eagles Center Cam Jurgens
full_text:
The Ravens are taking a significant risk that new center Cam Jurgens, who has a deep history of back and nerve problems, is able to anchor their offensive line for years to come.
They are making that risk at a time when the person who understands Jurgens’s medicals and quality of play and what he looks like in practice better than anyone else, Eagles general manager Howie Roseman, one of the best in the game, has an offensive line is in disarray. Yet he still moved the two-time Pro Bowler in a year in which he was trying to build another Lombardi Trophy winner, after previously moving Jurgens from center to left guard.
That alone should give Ravens pause. Roseman doesn’t lose a lot of trades, he is always in win-now mode, and landing a fifth-round pick in the next draft and a second-round pick in 2028 for a player with this medical history at this moment in time, is unquestionably a strong haul for a lineman who to this point has not been the same since requiring surgery to repair a snapped disc that ensnared a nerve following the Eagles Super Bowl win in February of 2025.
“Howie doesn’t give up on a season for October,” said one longtime NFL executive who has done deals with Roseman in the past. “It’s a lot to give up for a player with that history. Yeah, that would scare me a little bit.
“The Ravens see an opportunity to win the division, and they’ve got a major issue with the interior offensive line, but this is going out on a limb. And Howie is clearing anything he would have owed (Jurgens) next year too. So he doesn’t have that injury risk hanging over him anymore, either … Look, the Ravens have a lot of guys who are near the end or won’t be back there next year. They have the situation with the quarterback (Lamar Jackson in final guaranteed year of deal ). That stuff will push you to do something like this.”
One NFL GM said: “Jurgens is still a good player, he is, we have good grades on his film. And it’s a major upgrade to anything Baltimore had there. But no way Howie is trading his center after his Hall of Fame tackle just retired (Lane Johnson) and his top guard is on IR (Landon Dickerson) if there isn’t a serious medical red flag. Howie isn’t mailing it in. He’s not tanking. No way Howie does this if he’s convinced this is a starter for him - at center or guard or anywhere - for the rest of that contract.”
Here are the biggest Pros and Cons to the trade, with Jurgens, 27, likely out until at least Week 6 after entering concussion protocol Sunday:
Desperate For Veteran Center Presence: Rookie offensive coordinator Declan Doyle was taking on water early. His mentor, Sean Payton, explained in detail the import of having a proven veteran center as a young coach in New Orleans (making a bold trade for a vet to address it) and Doyle’s run game was being swallowed up by a brutal interior line . And he was just forced to move a raw guard to center against one of the best defensive tackles on the planet. “You only make this move if you are desperate,” another GM said.
NFL analyst Brian Baldinger, a longtime former NFL lineman and expert on line play said of Jurgens recent film: "He isn't a guard, strickly a center. It allows Ioane to stay at guard where he can be the next (potential future Hall of Famer Marshal) Yanda."
There was way too much being asked of too many this early in the offensive operation, penalties were a major problem, and having someone you know can handle everything that comes with this vital position (medical permitting) is big. Desperate times call for desperate measures and this is a tough leader with an elite football IQ, but as we will explain there are serious risks involved too. “They may have just solved their biggest problem,” said one NFL personnel executive. “And if this isn’t their starting center the next three years, they just made it worse.”
Ioane Stops Moving: They can keep 14th overall pick Vega Ioane back at guard now and take a ton off his plate mentally and physically. Having his huge frame back at guard next to a proven center – and not whatever the Ravens were hoping to prove with Jovaughn Gwyn there – is a massive upgrade across the board, and if Jurgens breaks down, Ioane has already shown he can hold it down at center.
Fixed Cost : The Ravens were comfortable paying elite center Tyler Linderbaum in Jurgens’s salary range, but were not willing to go as high as the Raiders went, so he left. Jurgens has two years left on his deal beyond this season with very manageable cap numbers. And the guaranteed do not extend beyond 2027, at least, with $14.75 of his $17.5M salary guaranteed and with a salary of $17.5M in 2028. If he plays at his pre-surgery levels, that’s a win. That’s also a big if.
The Injury Risk Is Real: Jurgens was not right through the entire 2025 season, he gutted through 14 games but he was not the same guy. He was flying to South America for treatments at one point and has spoken about the incredible pain he was in and the nerve damage he experienced as part of the brutal back injury. He says he feels much better now, but man.
“What are the Ravens thinking?” said one longtime NFL exec who watches the Eagles closely. “The good, but not really great, Cam, left once he had the back surgery. You don’t see trades like this for interior offensive linemen and this one had back surgery and the tape since then is not the same, including at center.”
They Made This Mess: The Ravens let the highest-paid center in the league walk as a free agent, when they didn’t have to and are running a $365M payroll, and put their offseason resources almost exclusively into the defense. They gave a meh guard $10M (John Simpson) in free agency rather than address center.
They had 11 draft picks and drafted no one who snaps the football after letting Linderbaum leave and had their pick in the second round at basically every center in the draft with the run on them not yet beginning and chose project edge defender Zion Young, at the very tail end of the wave of those players, instead.  And if this season doesn’t go as well as planned, and a lot of this core are gone or no longer as effective – Derrick Henry, Ronnie Stanley, Roquan Smith, Marlon Humphrey, Calais Campbell, Mark Andrews – that second-round pick is going to feel like quite a price.

title: Ravens Acquire Pro Bowl Center Cam Jurgens In Trade With Eagles
full_text:
The Baltimore Ravens said goodbye to one of the best centers in the game this past March after they got outbid in their attempt to retain homegrown three-time Pro Bowler Tyler Linderbaum, who reset the top of the market by signing a massive deal with the Las Vegas Raiders.
After injuries decimated their top three contingency plans at the position and forced them to slide over first-round rookie guard Olaivavega Ioane , general manager Eric DeCosta decided to swing for the fences and not wait until the midseason trade deadline to find a permanent fix.
Shortly after ESPN's Adam Schefter reported that they are acquiring two-time Pro Bowl center Cam Jurgens from the Philadelphia Eagles via trade, the team officially announced the move from their own social media account.
We have acquired Pro Bowl center Cam Jurgens in a trade with the Philadelphia Eagles! pic.twitter.com/WveOQzYJZO
"Cam is a player we have long admired going all the way back to the draft process," DeCosta said in a statement. "He’s a young foundational piece along our offensive line – a great scheme and cultural fit who will contribute quickly in Baltimore."
According to Schefter's report, the Ravens are receiving Jurgens and a 2027 seventh-round pick in exchange for a 2027 fifth-round pick and a 2028 second-round pick. After reportedly being in concussion protocol, Jurgens has already passed his physical to finalize the trade and is expected to make his debut as the new anchor in the middle of the Ravens' offensive line next week when they play the Cleveland Browns in their first division game of the season, per Schefter.
Jurgens and Linderbaum were the top two center prospects in the 2022 NFL Draft and came off the board one round apart. The Ravens used the first-round pick they acquired after trading Marquise 'Hollywood' Brown to take Linderbaum at No. 25 overall out of Iowa, and the Eagles waited patiently for Jurgens to fall into their lap at No. 51 overall out of Nebraska.
Linderbaum was a plug-and-play starter from Day 1 while Jurgens sat behind future Hall of Fame center Jason Kelce as a rookie, started next to him at guard for 11 games in 2023 and was voted to each of the last two Pro Bowls as a center, including his breakout 2024 season that saw him hoist the Vince Lombardi Trophy at the end of the season.
This move has the potential to be the most impactful in-season trade DeCosta has made since he acquired four-time Pro Bowl inside linebacker Roquan Smith at the 2022 deadline from the Chicago Bears in exchange for 2023 second- and fifth-round picks and veteran linebacker A.J. Klein.
That aggressive swing took the defense from good to truly elite that year and the next under former defensive coordinator Mike MacDonald. This one for Jurgens can do the same for this year's offense under first-time play-caller Declan Doyle, as his unit has already shown flashes of being explosively elite.
To go from losing initial front-runner Danny Pinter (Petalla) in a joint practice in late August to both Jovaughn Gywn (ankle) and Ethan Pocic (knee) within a few plays of each other in the same game to landing a massive upgrade over all the above is a great place to be. Now they go from having a solid interior offensive line through four games to having what could be one of the league's elite moving forward as other established starters like two-time Pro Bowler Ronnie Stanley and John Simpson get healthier, and youngsters like Ioane and right tackle Roger Rosengarten gain more experience.
Acquiring Jurgens wasn't the only roster transaction the team made on Wednesday to improve their ability to block in the run game and pass protection. Just before news of the big trade broke, they announced the signing of veteran tight end Nick Vannett to the 53-man roster and second-year fullback Lucas Scott to the practice squad.
These two moves are in direct response to the confirmation of the season-ending torn Achellies suffered by veteran tight end blocking specialist Durham Smythe , who went down in the team's Week 4 win over the Tennessee Titans and was quickly ruled out after being taken to the locker room.
Vannett is in his 11th season and is well-traveled, having played for nine different teams in his first 10 years in the league. He was recently with the Seattle Seahawks during the summer before signing to the Ravens' practice squad last month. Scott originally signed with the team as an undrafted free agent out of Army and spent his rookie season on their practice squad. One or both could be part of the solution to the issues the offense has been having in short-yardage situations, in particular.

title: The Ravens Need A More Potent Pass Rush, Starting This Sunday
full_text:
The Ravens continue to strive to become a drastically better defense than they were a year ago.
The need to get more pressure on the quarterback. Physically impacting the QB more than they have in years remains an area of aspiration and perspiration, but is still lacking production. It’s something that may come naturally with $30M edge signing Trey Hendrickson and $20M defensive tackle Nnamdi Madubuikke getting to play meaningful reps together – injuries have precluded that to this point – and perhaps it’s just a matter of time.
But it’s something that must emerge as they face better quarterbacks with more regularity, with a dynamic Falcons offense awaiting them in Atlanta Sunday night. Rookie head coach Jesse Minter is already being somewhat defensive and defiant about what’s transpired thus far . The reality of what’s to come is probably somewhere between the picture he paints and where the team ranks in key pass rush metrics.
The Ravens were not able to get hands on young and vulnerable QB Cam Ward nearly as much as expected on Sunday, though he did often resort to chucking the ball out of bounds.
“They were very protection conscious, I would say,” Minter said of the Titans. “If you go back and watch all the third downs, they are in split-back [formations], chipping both edges. When you rush four against seven, it is going to look like what it looks like, so I thought the guys rushed pretty well overall.
“We can be a little bit more coordinated, and then I thought four or five times where we had opportunities to sack the quarterback, we are either leaving our feet too early or not taking that extra step. So again, I think our defensive line — especially some of the interior guys that we missed a lot during camp — working toward that, and I expect us to have really good days rushing the passer going forward."
The Ravens have a 4.9% sack rate for the season, which is 23rd in the NFL. It was 4.6% last season. So, no one is going to be pumped about that . Pressure is more important, and there has been an uptick there. Baltimore has a 35.1% pressure rate this season, 19th in the NFL; it was at 31.7% last season.
Madubuike is their best interior rusher and it’s not close, and he’s only played two games in over a year. He’s still knocking rust off but can take games over week after week at the top of his powers. Hendrickson was probably more impacted by the finger injury than the team let on, we’ll see how quickly he can return from the procedure he had last week, but his resume is legit.
Hendrickson is generating a 17.5% pressure rate, which is bigtime and far superior than anything we’ve seen in this locker room for a long time. One sack on 80 pass-rush reps isn’t ideal, but the best should be to come (though he will suffer against the run). He also leads the team with 10 hurries.
Tavius Robinson, the chief beneficiary opposite Hendrickson when he is going, leads Baltimore with two sacks and six QB hits. He has a motor and sets the edge the way the Ravens demand. What has been lacking is hybrid defender Kyle Hamilton impacting the QB as much as many expected; Minter barely blitzed last week, so not much opportunity there, and Hamilton has just three pressures on 25 pass rushes this season.
Getting more pressure on Michael Penix Jr. will be vital on Sunday. He is still feeling his way back from a third ACL repair and has a tendency to throw off his back foot some and deliver some turnover worthy throws when under duress. Given that the Falcons are the best run stopping team in the NFL, and the most dominant team running the ball, the Ravens are going to need some turnovers.

title: Zay Flowers Is Doing Things No Ravens WR Has Done Before. Here's Why:
full_text:
Let’s take a moment to celebrate what an audacious and stupendous start Ravens receiver Zay Flowers is having to his season – more explosive than any in franchise history – before we allow for the fact that things are about to change.
Flowers has been as impactful as any skill player in the NFL, he has been a total menace to defenses in the three games he has played while hampered with a hamstring injury, and we must also recognize that he only played one half in Week 1, missed Week 2, was on a tight pitch count Week 3 and then lost starting quarterback Lamar Jackson at halftime of Week 4 and the Ravens took the air out of the ball.
It makes what Flowers, signed to a long-term deal before the season , is doing all the more outlandish. But, with Jackson almost certain to miss a week or two (at least) with an ankle injury and the Ravens’ offensive line/blockers beset by injuries , and the run game going backwards and the schedule ramping up, and Flowers the only cog showing up regularly downfield, his pace is about to diminish.
Maintaining his level of explosion over a full season even with Jackson would be pretty remarkable, and the Ravens are going to have to get more creative with him out in space and in the run game and doing things behind the line of scrimmage with back-up QB Snoop Huntley unable to push the ball downfield like Jackson . Rookie coordinator Declan Doyle has done his best work totally unlocking Flowers and making him a threat in every quadrant of the field in ways like never before., and his usage in the slot has been particularly impactful.
“In our offense, he is going to line up at five different positions,” head coach Jesse Minter said Monday. “So, you can have a game plan for him when he is the outside receiver to maybe take him away, or maybe when he is the slot receiver, but then he is ending up as No. 3 a lot.
“He is ending up on linebackers in zone coverages. He is ending up out of the backfield a few times as we have seen this year. So, I think that is just a credit to Zay to be able to do all that and sort of understand the concepts that he can move around to different spots, and then to Declan, obviously, moving him around.”
Here’s how he’s done it, and where Flowers ranks among the top receivers in the NFL a month into the season (and, again, he’s only truly completed two contests thus far):
Flowers is second in the NFL, averaging 19.6 yards per reception. He is fourth in the NFL at 117.3 yards per game. He is fifth in Yards After the Catch (165) and would be tops had he not missed so much time and been limited to just 56 routes run this far (less than half of teammate Rashod Bateman, for instance, and well off the volume of other top 10 NFL receivers.
Flowers is third in the NFL catching 78% of his passes for a first down or touchdown and he is in truly rarified air in some of the advanced stats that speak to the downfield impact he is making:
Yards Per Route Run: 6.29 – 1st in NFL (1.41 is NFL avg).
Jaxson Smith-Njigba (SEA) is second among qualified receivers at 4.15, a massive chasm
Yards Per Target: 16.00 – 1st in NFL
Tyquan Thornton (KC) is second at 14.1 yards per target, again, well off this pace
The fact Flowers has twice as many receiving yards as any Raven , and everyone knows where the ball is going if it’s going more than eight yards downfield, and starting receiver Ja’Kobi Lane has barely played due to injury, and no one can intervene, is pretty special.
The most significant change in Flowers’s usage is something we told you was coming in the spring: he is a real dervish when he has a two-way go from the slot and he’s always done his best work in the middle of the field and being deployed more often from the slot plays even more into it.
Flowers has been in the slot 60% of the time this season; it was 37% last season. This has meant everything.
He has 14 catches on 16 targets for 282 yards (20.1/rec!) and a touchdown in the slot this season.
Doyle has also put him motion more than ever (27%, not a huge difference from 23% a year ago) and has already put Flowers in the backfield for four snaps this season; he was positioned there just twice all of last season. Everything about this offense is going to be stripped down without Jackson for however long they are without him, but Flowers is already doing things Ravens receivers simply have not done.

title: Josh Allen Week 5 Health Update After Only Four Rush Yards in Bills' First Loss
full_text:
Buffalo Bills ' quarterback Josh Allen took a hit on his left knee against the Los Angeles Chargers on September 27, but he subsequently avoided a trip to the official Week 4 injury report .
Now, with the Bills preparing for a Week 5 appearance on Monday Night Football, Allen strongly dismissed any idea that the knee is an issue that's ultimately limiting his rushing attempts.
"There's no truth to that. Feeling great," said Allen following Thursday's practice in Orchard Park.
There was some speculation that Allen chose to cut back on his running in the October 4 loss to the New England Patriots as a means of protecting an injured knee . The elite dual threat did not take off to run when the pocket broke down against New England despite multiple opportunities to do so.
Allen carried five times for only four total yards in the 29-26 setback, but the fact that the Bills did not hesitate to call his number in multiple short yardage situations suggests that they weren't concerned about his knee.
It's also worth noting that after being hit on a fourth-quarter carry against the Chargers, Allen proceeded to rush twice more down the stretch in the Week 3 victory. After a one-yard touchdown rush, the quarterback ran for seven yards up the middle out of shotgun formation on his final carry in the 24-16 win.
"I'm not concerned with Josh," said Bills' head coach Joe Brady in the wake of the September 27 incident. "I'd love for him to not take some of the hits. He's a competitor, and I have to take that into consideration with some play calling as well."
We wrote about Brady potentially deciding to dial back Allen in the running game for now.
Although unlikely, one has to wonder if Allen has felt any effects from the offseason foot surgery that had him on crutches for Brady's introductory press conference.
Attempting to avoid the Cleveland Browns' pass rush, Allen broke a bone in his foot in Week 16 last December. He played through the injury the rest of the way, opting for minor surgery not until after the Bills were eliminated.
Including playoffs, Allen has made 141 consecutive starts for the Bills.

title: Four Buffalo Bills With Most to Prove Entering Week 5 Road Game
full_text:
The Buffalo Bills suffered their first loss of the season in Week 4, falling 29-26 to the New England Patriots. It was a tough outing, and this week isn't going to be any easier.
Buffalo will hit the road in Week 5 and has to travel across the country for a showdown with the Los Angeles Rams on Monday Night Football. The Rams are 2-2 and have not looked like the contender everyone knows they can be, but they did seem to find a higher gear in their fourth-quarter win over the Philadelphia Eagles.
The Bills entered the season as a favorite to win the Super Bowl and knocking off the Rams would go a long way toward reminding us all why they're considered elite contenders. For that to happen, they need the following four players, who have a lot to prove, to step up their performance.
Dee Alford recorded an interception in the Week 4 loss to the Patriots, but he managed to put himself in the dog house after the game. Alford made a comment about the defense struggling to communicate due to crowd noise . He was trying to discuss the way sound travels in the stadium and while his words might have been innocent, it led to criticism.
The comment was seen as a complaint and the ordeal made enough noise that defensive coordinator Jim Leonhard decided to call out players who complain about crowd noise, and had some choice words. In addition to the bad PR he recently received, Alford is entering Week 5 with a PFF grade of 42.6 and needs to perform much better as they travel to L.A.
It's worth watching Alford's injury status as the week unfolds. He was absent from Thursday's practice due to an ankle issue.
Bills On SI's Ralph Ventre recently handed out grades for every position group and gave the inside linebackers a C-. He said they both have struggled against the pass and run, while claiming Bernard looks slow and Williams appears confused .
Those aren't flattering descriptions, and even with the coaching staff praising their performance, both need to be at their best against the Rams. If not, Matthew Stafford and Kyren Williams could both have plenty of success.
There's no player on the Bills' roster going into Week 5 with more to prove than second-year cornerback Maxwell Hairston. He's struggled through the first four games, earning a PFF grade of 45.6 . Week 4 was easily his worst performance , and Hairston was so frustrated afterward that he avoided the media.
Hairston apologized afterward , which was the right call. Still, he has a huge spotlight on him now and will be out there against an elite Los Angeles passing attack on Monday night. That can be a huge opportunity for him to prove this past game was a fluke, but it could be devastating for his stock if he struggles.

title: Bills' First Week 5 Injury Update: Status for DJ Moore, Christian Benford, Ed Oliver
full_text:
The Buffalo Bills were missing a few key pieces when they began practicing for the October 12 primetime road game against the Los Angeles Rams.
Most notably, wide receiver DJ Moore, who is dealing with an AC joint issue , was a non-participant in the week's first practice.
Meanwhile, defensive tackle Ed Oliver and slot cornerback Dee Alford, who were both banged up last time out against the Patriots, were not seen during the media-viewing portion of practice on Thursday ( h/t WGR's Sal Capaccio ).
"Our guys are gonna prepare. There's gonna be guys that might not practice, but you guys know how I am with that," said first-year head coach Joe Brady prior to Thursday's practice . "We're gonna do everything we can. We also have the luxury of having a full day, an extra day with that. We're gonna give some guys [the chance] all the way through to game day. Knowing that if they give us the best opportunity to win, we're gonna roll with it."
Despite banging up his shoulder in Week 2, Moore has maintained his consecutive starts streak that dates back to December 2020. The WR1 reaggravated that injury while hitting the ground against the New England Patriots on October 4.
Moore was limited all last week for practice. The Bills will seemingly handle him with care in an effort to get him ready for game day.
"DJ's a competitor. You see the difference with us with DJ out on the football field. I think that that's natural and that's real. He is always going to do, literally, everything he can to be out there, not just for himself, but for his teammates," said Brady, who coached Moore with the Carolina Panthers in 2020 and 2021.
Benford's presence at Thursday's practice is certainly a positive development considering the starting cornerback did not practice at all during New England Patriots week.
Forced out in the third quarter on September 27, Benford suffered a non-contact toe injury. He was spotted wearing a walking boot in the immediate hours following the Week 3 win. On the sideline in Week 4, he was not wearing anything around the injured area.
With Benford inactive against the Patriots , Maxwell Hairston and second-round rookie Davison Igbinosun were the starters at outside cornerback. It's worth noting that Benford injured a toe last December, and returned after missing one game.
Oliver was ruled questionable to return after tweaking his knee during the third quarter in Week 4, but he never re-entered the game. tweaked his knee came back to the sideline in uniform but sans helmet.
Alford suffered a second-half ankle injury. He was also tabbed questionable to return. Following the 29-26 loss, Alford spoke to reporters in the locker room .
"I'm feeling pretty good. Gotta get an MRI, see how things go. I don't really know too much right now, but I feel good. I'm a warrior, so I'm ready for whatever," said Alford.
According to Brady, neither injury is expected to result in a long-term absence.
Defensive end Landon Jackson injured his knee, but returned to the game for one play wearing a brace. In a positive sign for his Week 5 availability, Jackson was seen participating with the brace on Thursday in Orchard Park.

title: Bills WR Khalil Shakir Surprisingly Leads NFL in Critical Stat
full_text:
Year after year, there’s conversation about the Buffalo Bills’ need for wide receiver help. Despite still looking for a true WR1 they can rely on, the Bills continue to put up elite offensive numbers and one of the key pieces for the past couple of seasons has also been one of the more overlooked players.
Khalil Shakir has led Buffalo in receptions and receiving yardage the past two seasons, but still doesn’t get the credit he deserves. In 2024, Shakir had 76 receptions for 821 yards and in 2025, he had 72 catches for 719 yards.
This season, he’s again being overlooked due to the addition of DJ Moore , as well as the performance of Keon Coleman . Even Dalton Kincaid is getting plenty of attention, while Shakir just quietly goes about his job.
Despite being overshadowed, Shakir enters Week 5 tied for the team lead with 15 catches . He hasn’t made the flashy plays, which is why he’s fourth in yardage, behind Kincaid, Coleman, and Moore, but Shakir is still serving as one of Josh Allen’s most trusted targets.
Shakir is also the one creating the most separation. In fact, he’s not just creating more space than any Buffalo wideout, but through four games, Shakir surprisingly leads the NFL in yards of separation.
According to Gridiron Stats and Info , Shakir is getting roughly 4.5 yards of separation per route. That’s slightly above Jaylen Waddle and Kalif Raymond, who are tied for second with 4.2 yards of separation.
As a slot receiver, Shakir is given a healthy cushion, which Gridiron has at around 7.1 yards. While that seems like a lot, he’s still given less space to operate than both Waddle and Raymond, and is still making the most of his routes.
At this point, the only question is why Shakir isn’t seeing more targets. He does lead the team with 23 targets, but that comes with a caveat. Moore has missed portions of two of their games with a shoulder injury and Coleman is often the WR3, except for when Moore is out.
Shakir hasn’t typically been a red zone weapon and he doesn’t stretch the field, but he’s averaging 11.6 yards per reception. There’s nothing at all wrong with that average, and with him creating plenty of space, it seems he should be featured more often than he has been. Perhaps leaning on him in Week 5 against the Los Angeles Rams will be key, especially since the offense has been in a slump the past two weeks.

title: Three Roster Moves Bills Must Make Before MNF Road Matchup vs. Rams
full_text:
The past few days haven’t been very pleasant for the Buffalo Bills .
After falling short to quarterback Drake Maye and the New England Patriots on Sunday at Highmark Stadium, the Bills now have several questions surrounding the team despite still holding a 3-1 record.
Whether it be injured players that need replacements, schematic tweaks that seemingly must be made, or continuous miscues that need to be cleaned up , the to-do list for Buffalo is anything but small heading into Week 5.
First-year head coach Joe Brady’s players let a grand opportunity slip through their fingertips against New England, but there’s no time for sulking.
The Bills can’t let one loss compound into two, and the upcoming road matchup against the Los Angeles Rams at SoFi Stadium under the primetime lights of Monday Night Football will be anything but easy at the start of next week.
With that in mind, something must change. So, here are three roster shakeups that need to be made by Buffalo in order to make the most of the next opportunity against the Rams.
Both rookie wide receiver Skyler Bell and veteran wideout Joshua Palmer have had rough starts to their Bills’ careers.
However, it’s been for different reasons.
While one has been given seemingly every opportunity to shine, the other has been kept in the dark on the sidelines .
Palmer, who signed a three-year deal worth up to $36 million last March, struggled with injuries for most of the season last year before eventually winding up on injured reserve prior to the playoffs in January, but that didn’t seem to matter this spring and summer as Palmer continuously saw time with the first-team offense and top reserves all training camp.
And, that trend has continued for the veteran through the first four weeks of the season this fall. Meanwhile, Bell—who dealt with a bit of a groin ailment in August—has been reserved to waiting in the wings despite a stellar performance in the preseason finale against the Pittsburgh Steelers on August 27 at Highmark Stadium.
In the game, the former University of Connecticut standout hauled in seven of 10 targets from third-string quarterback Shane Buechele for 49 yards while also adding one carry for 28 yards and a touchdown.
Needless to say, it was an impressive display from the 2026 fourth-round pick, who finished his collegiate career between Wisconsin and UCONN with 220 receptions for 2,893 yards and 24 touchdowns, which included a senior campaign with the Huskies where he tallied 101 receptions for 1,278 yards and 13 touchdowns.
Simply put, considering Palmer has only ever produced one season of more than 584 receiving yards between either college or the NFL since he was a freshman at the University of Tennessee, the former Volunteer and Los Angeles Charger just doesn’t seem to be that much of a playmaker.
And, keeping that in mind, the potential that Bell possesses seems to be too intriguing to pass up at this point given that Palmer has just three receptions on nine targets in 2026. The veteran does have two touchdown catches to his name, but they were mostly due to blown coverages from the opposing defense than anything he actually did to get open.
Following a terrible performance against New England last Sunday, Pro Football Focus currently ranks Bills’ fourth-year linebacker Dorian Williams as just the 39th-best linebacker out of 74 players at his position, which means more than half of the qualifying inside linebackers currently rank higher than Williams according to PFF ’s grading system.
And, although Williams currently leads Buffalo’s defense in tackles with a total of 32, the impact of those takedowns have been miniscule.
With just three tackles for loss through four games, Williams hasn’t been firing downhill in the run game like he should be given the solid play of interior linemen like DeWayne Carter , Greg Gaines, and Deone Walker up front , and he’s been a downright liability in coverage, which is evidenced by his measly PFF pass-coverage grade of 54.4 (45th-best).
The Tulane product managed to fend off pesky rookie linebacker Kaleb Elarms-Orr during the offseason in order to earn the starting job out of training camp, but that appears to be more so because of Elarms-Orr’s inability to fully take the job away from him.
Despite shining in training camp , the rookie faded quite quickly once the pads came on in the preseason, and he’s done little to earn more playing time so far in the regular season when given opportunities on defense.
For that reason, Buffalo should think long and hard about elevating veteran linebacker Shaq Thompson from the practice squad moving forward, and possibly even bringing him up to the active roster after his three-game limit of promotions from the practice squad is up.
After joining Buffalo’s roster on June 10, 2025, Thompson went on to start eight of 14 games during the 2025-2026 campaign for the team between the regular season and playoffs, and he finished with 69 total tackles, eight tackles for loss, three pass deflections, one forced fumble, one sack, and one interception, which came in the Bills’ 27-24 victory over the Jacksonville Jaguars in the AFC wild-card round at EverBank Field in January. Thompson also received a pass-coverage grade of 69.2 for his efforts last year, which ranked 14th out of 88 total qualifying linebackers per PFF ’s database in 2025.
Furthermore, in addition to his solid statistics, the now 12-year veteran provided noticeable juice for former Sean McDermott’s defense when on the field, and that’s something that new coordinator Jim Leonhard could use for his incredibly youthful unit right now, which is surrendering an average of 26 points per game through the first four weeks of the season.
It’d seem prudent for Leonhard to get Thompson into the fold on defense sooner rather than later at this point.
After struggling with personal loss and battling through and undisclosed injury this summer, eight-year veteran defensive lineman Ed Oliver started the 2026 season off on a high note in his hometown of Houston, Texas, with a five-tackle performance that included one tackle for loss, one quarterback hit, and one critical fumble recovery against the Houston Texans at Reliant Stadium in Week 1, which rightfully earned him a game ball from head coach Joe Brady .
However, since that time, the past three games haven’t gone as well for the one-time 2019 first-round pick, and now he finds himself ailing once again after a flukey inadvertent hit on the sideline from Patriots’ fullback Reggie Gilliam—a former Bills’ teammate—caused Oliver to exit Sunday’s game early in Orchard Park, and his status moving forward is questionable at best as he failed to return to the game with an apparent left knee injury.
And, with fellow defensive lineman T.J. Sanders seemingly still recovering from appendectomy surgery he had on September 22, the Bills are going to need some reinforcements for the foreseeable future up front on defense until either player returns to the lineup.
Enter fifth-year defensive lineman Phidarian Mathis, who just returned to Buffalo’s practice squad on September 30 after serving a three-game suspension to start the 2026 season for violating the NFL’s substance abuse policy.
A former 2022 second-round pick of the Washington Commanders, the 6-foot-4, 312-pounder appeared to be on track to earn a final roster spot in Western New York prior to his suspension being handed down by the league at the end of August, and now would seem like the perfect time to get him reacclimated to being a serviceable member of Buffalo’s defensive line moving forward.
The Bills are going to need someone added to the rotation this week against the Los Angeles Rams, and Mathis appears to be the perfect candidate to fill the role.
Last year, the one-time University of Alabama defender appeared in seven games for the Bills between the regular season and playoff, finishing with 13 total tackles.

title: Buffalo Bills' WR Draft 'Bust' Finding Success in New Role
full_text:
It's no secret that Keon Coleman hasn't lived up to expectations after being drafted 33rd overall back in 2024.
The Buffalo Bills were in need of a new number one wide receiver after trading DJ Moore, and Coleman appeared to be an intruiging weapon on the boundary with solid contested catch ability.
Issues on and off the field have hindered Coleman's development, but the third-year receiver's strong start to his 2026 campaign illustrates he's finally settling into a dependable role within the offense.
It wouldn't be easy replacing Stefon Diggs, the man responsible for the greatest four-year stretch of any WR in franchise history. A four-time Pro Bowler and two-time All Pro, expecting a rookie to immediately fill his shoes was unfair from the beginning.
Coleman suffered a wrist sprain in November of his rookie season, causing him to miss four games. As a rookie, he recorded 29 receptions,  556 yards and four touchdowns.
His sophomore season saw him miss opening drives and even entire games for tardiness to team meetings and other off-field immaturity issues.  While his number of receptions increased from 29 to 38, is yards per reception drastically fell from 19.2 to 10.6, leading to only 404 yards in his second season.
While it may have been unfair to expect him to replace Diggs, Coleman wasn't showing enough consistency to prove he was even a top three wide receiver on the roster.
Buffalo finally decided to trade for an experienced WR1 this offseason, adding DJ Moore to the offense. Now, between Moore and a healthy Dalton Kincaid , Coleman can slot into a supporting role in the offense.
Coleman has already logged 217 receiving yards and a touchdown, setting a pace to shatter his previous season-highs. The advanced metrics illustrate just how consequential his production has been for the Bills.
According to Ryan Pagnetti , Coleman had the third-highest EPA per target entering Week 4's Monday Night Football matchup. His +1.13 EPA per target trails only Tyquan Thornton (+1.29) and Jakobi Meyers (+1.17).
With Coleman's 16 targets and 14 catches, he has the volume to be one of the leaders in total EPA among WRs, ranking ninth among 77 that qualify. His +18.2 total EPA currently ranks him ahead of players like Ja'Marr Chase (+14.4), Justin Jefferson (+13.2) and Garrett Wilson (+11.5).
Bills reporter Sal Capaccio found that Coleman also ranks second to Nico Collins with a +27.2% catch rate over expected.
At this point, the Bills recognize that Coleman isn't a wide receiver one, but they aren't relying on him to fill that role given the current personnel at both WR and TE.
Instead, he'll be a guy that Josh Allen can now rely on to move the chains (considering he's already accounted for 10 first downs this year), and someone who can step up mid-game if there's an injury, like Joe Brady mentioned in his press conference on Monday.
He's currently on pace for 60 receptions, 922 receiving yards, and four touchdowns, which would be by far the best year of his young career. Aside from the raw numbers, the previously cited advanced metrics show that Coleman is actually adding more value to the team by excelling as a role player rather than struggling as a top receiving option.

title: Bills' Grades for Every Position Group Through Season's First Quarter Show Weaknesses
full_text:
The Buffalo Bills are 3-1 through the first four regular season games of head coach Joe Brady's tenure.
Despite a disappointing result last time out against the New England Patriots, the Bills occupy first place in the AFC East division after one-quarter of the schedule. For reference, they started 4-0 each of the past two years under Sean McDermott.
Although there's been a lot of good, there is plenty that the Bills must fix moving forward. Here's how we see each position group's performance thus far. The grade scale ranges from A+ to F.
Josh Allen was sensational through the first two weeks, but did not meet his MVP standard in Weeks 3 and 4. His poor decision produced a late interception that essentially cost the Bills the chance to beat the Patriots. He also failed to take what the defense was giving him on too many occasions.
Reigning NFL rushing champion James Cook ranks in third in the league and second overall amongst yards per carry (6.0) leaders. Ty Johnson is back from injury, and practice squad running back Frank Gore Jr. filled in admirably while he was out. Backup Ray Davis has not yet been needed.
It looked a lot better when DJ Moore was healthy, but there have been bright spots in the receiving corps including Keon Coleman 's encouraging Week 4 performance. Josh Palmer has been boom or bust while Moore, who has been slowed by an AC joint sprain, is a clear difference maker when on the field.
Each of the three core members of the position group complement each other well. Allowing the Bills to frequently deploy 13 personnel, Dawson Knox, Dalton Kincaid and Jackson Hawes all are essential to success in run game and pose legit threats as pass-catchers.
Age appears to be catching up to Dion Dawkins, at least that was the case against the Patriots. Alec Anderson has been less than impressive at left guard, and the unit as a whole can be better in pass protection.
Bass has answered the bell after missing the entire 2025 campaign. He is a perfect 6-for-6 on field goals and he's missed only one PAT in 14 attempts.
Seventh-round rookie Tommy Doman has been an upgrade over Mitch Wishnowsky thus far. He's averaging 45.0 net yards per punt and has placed four of nine kicks inside the opponent's 20.
Greg Dortch quickly proved worthy of a 53-man roster spot, moving up after two weeks. He's averaging 8.8 yards per punt return and 26.3 yards per kick return. Most importantly, he's protecting the football.
Nose tackle Deone Walker has been an absolute monster and late-summer addition Greg Gaines has been serviceable in the middle. Ed Oliver has yet to get his feet under him this season, but young Landon Jackson has noticeably improved from his rookie season.
NFL sacks leader Greg Rousseau and Bradley Chubb have already proven to be a formidable starting duo, providing a noticeable boost to the Bills' pass rush. They could use more from the backups, but the two starters have been exactly what Buffalo needed on the edge.
Terrel Bernard and Dorian Williams have stumbled out of the gate against both the pass and the run. Bernard has looked slow while Williams appears confused at times. Whether it's fourth-round rookie Kaleb Elarms-Orr, Buffalo Joe Andreessen or practice squad veteran Shaq Thompson, the Bills would be smart to shake it up.
Cole Bishop and Chauncey Gardner-Johnson haven't exactly been a reincarnation of Micah Hyde and Jordan Poyer. Neither appears to take the proper angles, and each has had his share of missed tackles.
Second-round rookie Davison Igbinosun has been a lone bright spot for a group that has struggled to cover. Prior to his toe injury , Christian Benford was ineffective in man coverage situations. Maxwell Hairston and slot cornerback Dee Alford have been exploited regularly , too.

title: NFL Insider Names Bills as Top Suitor for Tyreek Hill
full_text:
It was Week 4 of the 2025 season when Tyreek Hill suffered a severe knee dislocation and multiple torn ligaments in his left knee. That sent him to the IR and the Miami Dolphins wound up releasing him this offseason. Now, Hill is eyeing a comeback and the Buffalo Bills continue to be seen as a logical destination .
One reason for this is the fact that Hill posted a cryptic tweet saying he was ready for some cold weather football. That had fans thinking he was looking north to Buffalo, and NFL insider Albert Breer agrees that the Bills could be a destination for Hill.
Breer was a guest on the Dan Patrick Show and said if he had to guess, he would say either Buffalo or the Kansas City Chiefs would be Hill's next team.
"If I had to guess right now, I'd say Kansas City or Buffalo. I think he's motivated to continue his career. Now, I don't know what percentage of him we're getting because it's not just coming back from the injury. And the injuries are really difficult one to come back from, right? And it's not just the injury. It's also his age, you know, and your ability to recuperate at that age."
Breer said that while it's colder in Buffalo than Kansas City, the Chiefs do still have plenty of cold weather games, so his post could have been referencing them as well. He also said that Hill could seamlessly transition to Kansas City since he has a relationship with Patrick Mahomes and has worked with offensive coordinator Eric Bieniemy in the past as well.
Throw in injuries suffered by Tyquan Thornton and Rashee Rice, and a reunion makes sense. According to Breer, however, Buffalo makes sense as well. He admits they have more weapons right now than the Chiefs, but adds that Hill brings them the one thing they don't have, a burner.
"But he makes sense for Buffalo, too. I mean, if you look at the Bills receiver group, right, you've got Keon Coleman, who's really come on in his third year. I think surprised a lot of people. DJ Moore is banged up now. But he's more of like the ball in your hands, run after catch guy," Breer said.
"And then you've got Khalil Shakir, who's your classic slot, right? What's the one thing they're missing? The one thing they're missing is a burner, right? And if you think Tyreek Hill can be that, he could add an element to Buffalo that they don't have right now and maybe unlock a little bit more downfield for Josh Allen."
Of course, Hill being the burner Buffalo needs depends heavily on how well he recovers from his knee injury. The Bills, or any other team interested, would need to see just how much he has left in the tank before deciding to make the move.
If he is anywhere close to the player he was during his tenure with Kansas City or the Miami Dolphins, Hill would truly bring a new element to the Bills' offense.

title: Buffalo Bills Named Logical Trade Suitor For Future Hall of Fame Edge Rusher
full_text:
Buffalo Bills edge rusher Greg Rousseau has been electric through four games of the 2026 season.
Rousseau is off to a red-hot start after notching six sacks so far and he is well on his way to a career-best season that shows the Bills made the right call in extending him last offseason.
However, the Bills could use more pass-rush juice, as they have 10 sacks in total and only 2.5 of those have come from edge rushers not named Greg Rousseau.
Bleacher Report's Kristopher Knox listed Los Angeles Chargers edge rusher Khalil Mack as a potential trade candidate , and he believes the Bills could come calling if he's on the block.
"The Chargers won't be eager to move Mack as long as they believe they can rebound," Knox said. "If they believe their season is lost, however, they could save $8 million in cap space by moving him."
"Potential Suitors: Buffalo Bills, San Francisco 49ers," Knox added.
Off to an 0-4 start, history is against the Chargers rebounding and making the playoffs, as the 1992 San Diego Chargers are the only team in league history to accomplish that feat.
Mack has already flirted with retirement before , and chances are his odds of hanging up his cleats will increase with another NFL season under his belt.
Knowing that, the Chargers would be silly not to consider trading Mack and getting something for him before he departs Los Angeles for nothing in 2027.
The Bills don't have a dire situation at edge rusher, but that may change if Rousseau can't keep up what we have to believe is an unsustainable pace.
Maybe Bradley Chubb, Michael Hoecht and T.J. Parker can pick up the slack if Rousseau falls off, but we can't say they will be able to for sure.
Mack is long in the tooth but he's still got plenty of gas left in the tank. Through four games this season, Mack has posted three sacks, which would rank second on the Bills. Last season, the future Hall of Famer had 5.5 in just 12 games.
Putting Mack opposite Rousseau would give the Bills one of the more potent edge rusher duos in the NFL and would also put Buffalo in better position to compete for a Super Bowl.
In terms of cost, Mack shouldn't be too expensive with the entire league knowing he may only be a half-year rental because of the fact that he could very well retire in 2027.
Knowing that, it may only cost a fourth-round pick to acquire him, or maybe a third in a deal that features a pick swap. The Bills have their third- and fourth-round picks the next two years, so that's a price general manager Brandon Beane can afford.

title: Bills Well Behind Rest of NFL in Critical Offensive Stat That Was Costly vs. Patriots
full_text:
Despite their current record, the Buffalo Bills have had several miscues over the course of the first four weeks of the 2026 NFL regular season.
And, while some observers overlooked those mishaps in September, maybe they shouldn’t have: everything hasn’t been hunky-dory.
Plays that nearly cost the Bills on the road in Week 1 against the Houston Texans at Reliant Stadium, as well as at home in Week 3 against the Los Angeles Chargers at Highmark Stadium, caught up to first-year head coach Joe Brady’s squad this past Sunday against the New England Patriots in Orchard Park, resulting in a critical loss in the AFC East.
Even if some fans may not want to admit to the fact, it was a game that had massive playoff implications written all over it for Buffalo in spite of the calendar only reading October . . . and the players let it slip through their fingertips, which is awfully similar to last fall when the team fell short to New England at home in primetime on NBC ’s Sunday Night Football in Week 5.
The parallels between the two contests and subsequent results are uncanny.
However, instead of entering this October’s game against the Patriots on a four-game winning streak that included outscoring their opponents by a total count of 133-90, this time around the Bills were heading into the matchup on a three-game run after outscoring their opponents 101-78 through the month of September.
And, although it might not seem like much to some, the National Football League is a game of inches, so going from an average margin of victory of 10.8 points in 2025 prior to the first Patriots’ matchup down to an average of 7.7 points per contest in 2026 is undeniably notable.
With Jim Leonhard’s young defensive unit still adjusting to a new scheme on the other side of the operation, the room for error is seemingly smaller this year for quarterback Josh Allen and his teammates this season, and that proved to be the case once again on Sunday against New England.
This time, though, the “smoke detectors” that Brady had been referring to since the preseason finally sounded the alarms over the weekend, and it’s something that needs to be fixed in a hurry.
One such area that appears to be in need of some serious change?
The team’s two-point conversion efficiency, which wound up costing Buffalo late in the fourth quarter following a go-ahead, 34-yard touchdown pass from Allen to third-year wide receiver Keon Coleman with 4:27 remaining in the game.
After the trip across the goal line, Buffalo led 26-21 and chose to try a two-point attempt in order to make it a seven-point affair, which could’ve made things a bit more difficult for the Patriots on the other side.
The result, though, was an incomplete pass from Allen to wide receiver Joshua Palmer, which really had no chance of completion at all. And, what’s even more frustrating is the fact that film review shows Buffalo’s gunslinger missed tight end Dalton Kincaid on the play, who was wide open right in front of his quarterback’s eyes after the playmaker initially stayed in to block.
Instead of the simple toss for a completion to Kincaid, however, Allen chose to try and fit a ball in between two defenders in the back of the end zone to Palmer, and  . . .  it was a bit of a frustrating head-scratcher for fans, to say the least.
“You study what you expect to get from the defense, kind of what their two-point situations (have previously) presented defensively, (and) you hope to put together a play that you feel is going to be successful against that,” Bills’ offensive coordinator Pete Carmichael Jr. said Monday at One Bills Drive .
“There’s also times where, as a coaching staff, you’re studying the two-point plays that are being run around the league and see if they fit with your personnel. But, obviously, we’ve got to do a better job there.”
With that said, should it have really been that much of a surprise to anyone invested in the critical moment that Buffalo failed to convert?
Although Carmichael Jr. is in his first season as offensive coordinator in Western New York in conjunction with first-year head coach Joe Brady, when looking at the recent stats from the Bills, maybe the failure shouldn’t have been much of a shocker to anyone at all, even in spite of the addition of Brady’s new offensive counterpart.
Although all 32 teams in the NFL collectively had the lowest two-point conversion success rate in the last 15 years heading into the 2025 season at just 41%, Buffalo was well below that rate last year.
According to the TeamRankings’ database , the Bills were just 28th in the league one season ago when it came to successful two-point conversions at a rate of just 22.22%, which was down from a success rate of 75% in 2023 and 50% in 2024.
Furthermore, what’s even more concerning?
Well, since Buffalo has now failed on both of its two-point attempts so far this season after Sunday’s screwup against New England , the team’s now just 2-of-11 on two-point tries since September 2025, and one of those successful tries occurred when former backup quarterback Mitchell Trubisky was in the game against the New York Jets in Week 18 last season.
Needless to say, the Bills are trending in a terrible direction when it comes to the backpocket play, and it’s not something to take lightly.
Who knows when the team might need to convert in such a critical moment later on this year?
It might even happen in the playoffs . . . if Buffalo can reach that point of the season.
And, although it’s unclear exactly what needs to happen in order to correct the issue moving forward, utilizing players like the previously mentioned Coleman, as well as Kincaid, who were both drafted in part due to their supposed red-zone skills, might be a good start.
Using Allen’s trusty legs and overwhelming brute strength would be helpful, too.
For some reason, seemingly none of those players have been utilized as much as they should be in that area of the field throughout their careers, though, at least not when it pertains to the two-point attempts, anyway.
With that in mind, something’s got to give. Points are precious in the NFL, and Buffalo simply can’t continue its struggles in this area going forward.

title: 4 Problems the Panthers Can't Ignore During Their Week 5 Bye
full_text:
I complained about this Week 5 bye as soon as the schedule came out. Four games and then a week off just seemed way too early, especially knowing Carolina would have to play the rest of the season without another break.
I'm starting to look at it a little differently now.
The Panthers are 2-2 and just beat Detroit in a game I didn't think they were going to win. They've also looked a whole lot better over the last three weeks than they did when Chicago put 59 points on them in the opener. But that doesn't mean I've forgotten about some of the things we've seen through four games.
There are still a few things I'd like Carolina to figure out before going to Philadelphia.
I'm not really sure what Carolina can do here because Jaycee Horn and Mike Jackson aren't walking through the door after the bye. Both are on injured reserve, and the Panthers are going to have to make this work without them for a while.
That wasn't exactly easy against Detroit.
Jared Goff threw for 412 yards, and there were times when it felt like Detroit could get whatever it wanted through the air. I know we're talking about a really good Lions offense, and Carolina was asking guys like Will Lee III to do a lot more than anybody probably expected this early.
The good part is they made enough plays when they had to. Lee and Lathan Ransom were there on the fourth-down stop that ended Detroit's final possession, and Carolina found a way to win despite everything going on back there.
But I can't just ignore 412 passing yards because the Panthers won.
Maybe Ejiro Evero changes some things until Horn and Jackson get back. Maybe Carolina uses one of its open roster spots on another corner. Whatever they decide, I don't think they can keep asking this secondary to survive every week and hope it works out.
I feel like every week I'm writing about another Panthers offensive lineman getting hurt.
Taylor Moton has been out. Damien Lewis missed the Detroit game, Monroe Freeling has dealt with an injury, and Corey Bullock had to step in at left guard Sunday night. Bullock settled in, and Carolina still managed to run the ball pretty well, so I'm not complaining about what the backups have done.
I'd just like to stop finding out how many backups they have.
Moton could be getting closer to returning after the bye, and this would be a pretty good time to get him back. Young has thrown for 1,268 yards and nine touchdowns, while Carolina has been moving guys around in front of him.
I've already liked what I've seen from this offense.
Now I'd like to see it with a healthy offensive line.
This is probably the one that bothers me the most.
Carolina gave up 59 points and 552 yards against Chicago, and I came out of that game wondering if the defense was going to be terrible. Then the Panthers held Atlanta to three points and Cleveland to 21, and I started thinking maybe I overreacted.
Then Detroit put up 452 yards.
I don't know what to make of that yet.
I'm not expecting Carolina to hold everybody to three points. I also don't think giving up 452 yards to Detroit is the same as what happened against Chicago because the Lions have a really good offense, and Carolina was missing a bunch of guys.
But at some point, I need to know what this defense is.
Maybe the answer is somewhere in the middle. If that's the case, fine. I just don't want to spend the next three months wondering which version is showing up every Sunday.
I know I've talked about Chuba Hubbard enough already, but I'm going to do it again.
Hubbard ran for 122 yards against Detroit, and Carolina finally had the running game I've been waiting to see. Young still threw for 329 yards and two touchdowns, so it's not like getting Hubbard involved took anything away from him.
I think it actually made things easier.
That's what I don't want Carolina to forget during the bye. Young is playing really good football right now, but that doesn't mean he needs to throw it 40 or 50 times every week. If Hubbard is running the ball like he did Sunday night, give it to him.
I'm probably making this too simple, but I don't think I am.
Make teams worry about Hubbard. Then let Young work off of it.
I'm still not going to say I love having a bye after four games. Ask me again in December, when Carolina hasn't had a week off in two months, and I'll probably be complaining about it again.
But right now, I can see how it helps.
The Panthers aren't 1-3 and trying to figure out how to save their season. They're 2-2, Young is playing the best football of his career, and they just beat a Detroit team I thought was going to come into Charlotte and beat them.
I feel a whole lot different about Carolina than I did after Week 1.
That doesn't mean the Panthers don't have problems. They do, and four games have been enough to show us what some of them are.
Now they have a week to do something about them.
