title: Panthers' NFC South Odds Just Took a Turn Nobody Saw Coming
full_text:
If you had told me after Week 1 that the Panthers would have the best odds to win the NFC South a few weeks later, I probably would've asked what you were watching. Carolina had just given up 59 points to Chicago, the defense looked terrible, and the Panthers turned the ball over three times.
I wasn't thinking about winning the division after that game. I was wondering how bad this season might get.
Carolina is now +160 at DraftKings to win the NFC South. The Panthers were +250 at the previous update after opening the season at +350. Atlanta is at +194, New Orleans is +260 and Tampa Bay is all the way down at +1100.
I'm not going to lie, I had to look at those numbers again. We're talking about the same Panthers team that looked completely lost defensively against Chicago, and now they're 2-2, already have a 34-3 win at Atlanta, and just beat Detroit 32-26 on Sunday Night Football.
I've spent the last few weeks trying to figure out what this team is. I'm still not completely sure, but apparently the oddsmakers are starting to believe Carolina might be pretty good.
I know how ridiculous that would've sounded after the Chicago game. I wouldn't have bought it then, either. But look around the NFC South right now and tell me who is running away with this thing.
Carolina and Atlanta are both 2-2, and the Panthers already went to Atlanta and beat the Falcons by 31 points. New Orleans is 1-3, and Tampa Bay is 0-4. Four games isn't much, but it's enough for me to look at this division and think, why not Carolina?
Then there's Bryce Young . I've written enough about how well he's playing, so I'm not going to do the whole thing again here. But 1,268 passing yards and nine touchdowns through four games isn't something I can just ignore, especially after he threw for 329 yards and two touchdowns against Detroit.
And it's not just DraftKings that has started looking at Carolina differently. ESPN's Football Power Index gives the Panthers a 48% chance to win the NFC South, with Atlanta next at 31%.
That's where I started looking at this a little differently myself. One sportsbook moving Carolina after a Sunday night win is one thing. When you start seeing numbers like that in other places, maybe there's actually something here.
Here's what keeps stopping me from going all the way with this. I've changed my mind about the Panthers about three times already, and somehow we're only four games into the season.
They were awful against Chicago. Then they went to Atlanta and won 34-3, and I started thinking maybe Week 1 was just one of those games. Then Carolina lost at Cleveland, and I was right back to wondering what this team was.
So, of course, the Panthers turned around and beat Detroit in a game I picked them to lose.
That's been this season so far. Every time I think I've figured Carolina out, they give me something else to think about.
There are still things I don't trust. The defense has had its moments, but Jared Goff just threw for 412 yards against this secondary. The injuries have also gotten ridiculous, and we don't know exactly who Carolina is getting back after the bye.
But maybe I've been holding that Chicago game against them too much. Since then, Carolina has won two of three, nearly won the Cleveland game, and already has a road win over Atlanta. If this division is still close later in the season, that Atlanta win could end up meaning a whole lot.
Now the Panthers get the bye, and I don't think anybody in that building is complaining about having it this early anymore. After that, we'll get Philadelphia, Tampa Bay, and Green Bay. Ask me what I think about Carolina's chances after those three, and I might have a much better answer.
I'm still not ready to say the Panthers are definitely winning the NFC South. There's too much football left, and this team has already fooled me more than once.
After Week 1, I would've thought that was crazy.
I'm not laughing at it anymore.

title: Bryce Young Just Revealed What's Really Changed for Him in Carolina
full_text:
I've been trying to figure out what's different about Bryce Young this season. I know part of the answer is pretty simple. He's in his fourth year, he's gotten better, and we're finally starting to see some of the things Carolina thought it was getting when it drafted him No. 1 overall.
But I don't think that's all of it.
Young has thrown for 1,268 yards and nine touchdowns through four games, including 329 yards and two touchdowns against Detroit. As good as those numbers are, it's the way he's playing that has stood out to me. He looks comfortable, and I don't know how many times I could've said that during his first few years in Carolina.
Then I listened to Young's interview with Pat McAfee this week, and something he said about offensive coordinator Brad Idzik got my attention.
“He wants my input. He wants all of our input,” Young said.
The more Young talked about Idzik, the more I started wondering if we've been overlooking something pretty important.
Idzik isn't some new coach who came in this year and changed everything. He's been around Young for three years and has already had a big hand in the offense behind the scenes. What's different now is that Dave Canales handed Idzik the play-calling duties.
I think that matters because of the way Young described their relationship. He said they spend the week talking about the game plan, what he likes, and what he feels comfortable with. If Young wants something added or doesn't like something they're working on, they talk about it before Sunday.
Maybe I'm making this too simple, but that sounds like a pretty good way to make your quarterback comfortable.
We've spent years talking about everything Young needed to do better. Get the ball out quicker. Be more aggressive. Handle pressure better. Push the ball downfield. Some of that was absolutely fair, especially for a quarterback Carolina took with the first pick in the draft.
But maybe the Panthers had some figuring out to do, too.
Young said before the season that he had “all the confidence in the world in Brad.” He also called Idzik a big reason for what the offense had already built. I probably wouldn't have thought much about those comments in August, because what else is a quarterback going to say about his offensive coordinator?
Four games into the season, I'm paying a little more attention to them.
This was the part of Young's interview that really got me.
McAfee asked how much information Young wants from his play-caller once he's on the field. I figured Young would talk about wanting as much information as possible before the headset cuts off, but his answer was about as simple as it gets.
“Just give me the play,” Young said.
At first, I kind of laughed at it. Then Young explained why, and it made a lot of sense.
He and Idzik have already talked through everything during the week. Young knows why certain plays are being called and what Idzik is looking for in different situations. Maybe it's third-and-1, and Carolina knows it could go for it on fourth down, or maybe they absolutely need to pick up the first down right there.
Young also talked about knowing when Idzik wants to speed things up or slow them down. Those aren't conversations you can have while the play clock is ticking, and that's where the work they do during the week comes in.
By the time Sunday gets here, Young doesn't need all of that explained again. Idzik gives him the play, and Young already knows what he's looking for.
I don't know if freedom is the right word for it. Trust probably makes more sense.
I'm definitely not saying Idzik took over the play-calling and magically fixed Young. That's not fair to Young, and I don't think it's really what we're seeing anyway.
Young deserves a lot of the credit for this. He's in Year 4 now, and he's been through more than most young quarterbacks have to deal with. There have been coaching changes, bad offensive line play, injuries around him, and even a benching along the way.
The rest of the offense matters, too. Tetairoa McMillan has given Young a legitimate weapon, Chuba Hubbard just ran for 122 yards against Detroit, and Carolina has somehow kept things together up front despite all the injuries. There isn't one thing you can point to and say that's why Young is playing better.
But I keep going back to what Young said about Idzik.
For most of his career, the conversation has been about what Young needed to change. What if Carolina finally figured out that it needed to listen to him a little more, too?
Maybe that's why Young looks so comfortable right now. He has a play-caller who wants to know what he likes, spends the week making sure they're seeing things the same way, and then doesn't try to overload him once the game starts.
I'm not giving Brad Idzik all the credit for what we're seeing from Bryce Young.
But I'm starting to think he deserves a whole lot more than we've been giving him.

title: Bryce Young’s Impressive Start Earns Much-Deserved Praise
full_text:
The brief professional history of the Carolina Panthers’ current starting quarterback has been well-documented. Bryce Young was the first overall pick in the 2023 NFL draft. He suffered through a miserable rookie campaign in which he totaled more turnovers (16) than touchdown passes (11) and was sacked 62 times in 16 games.
Enter new Panthers’ head coach Dave Canales in 2024. After two weeks and a pair of rough outings, the former offensive coordinator of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers benched Young. He would eventually return, started Carolina’s final 10 games and showed that the time off was a bit beneficial.
This past season proved to be somewhat of a breakthrough year for the young quarterback, but it certainly was not without its flaws. Young threw for a career-high 3,011 yards, and his 23 TD passes were also a personal best. However, he did show a knack for late-game heroics.
Still, there were also 15 turnovers in 16 regular-season outings. Young was picked off in the first quarter of the Panthers’ playoff loss to the Rams, but finished the game with 264 yards through the air and one score, plus rushed for a touchdown.
Now it is 2026 and after four games, the reigning NFC South champions own a 2-2 record are coming off an impressive 32-26 prime time triumph over the visiting Detroit Lions. They are tied with the Atlanta Falcons for the best record in the division. Canales’s club is off this week.
🚨 Bryce Young went from being benched in 2024 to leading his team and making ELITE throws like these. He’s getting PAID this offseason. pic.twitter.com/l5C3K1WRgj
NFL writer Mike Jones of The Athletic came up with his “quarter-season superlatives” for the 2026 season. When it came to a player or a team making what he referred to as the “biggest leap,” he singled out Carolina’s rising signal-caller.
“After a rocky first two seasons, Bryce Young displayed promise down the stretch of last season and helped Carolina end its playoff drought. He ranked No. 21 in passing (3,011 yards) and No. 27 in passer rating (87.8), but comfort in coach Dave Canales’s offense has translated into strong results this season.”
It’s been quite the start for the 25-year-old performer. He leads the NFL with 1,268 yards through the air, and currently ranks 10th in the league in passer rating (100.0). Young has hit on 62.3 percent of his throws, connecting for nine scores compared to only two interceptions. He has not fumbled this season, despite being sacked 10 times, and does have one rushing touchdown.
Josh Sweat unblocked gotta be terrifying for Bryce Young pic.twitter.com/lcFhewvdwy
For comparison, let’s take a look at how the 2025 season started out for the 2021 Heisman Trophy winner. The team lost its first two games and actually got off to a 1-3 start. Young was connecting on just 60.4 of his attempts for only 753 yards. There were 5 touchdown passes, three interceptions, and a pair of lost fumbles (1 retuned for a touchdown). He was sacked just six times, and his 77.1 passer rating ranked a dismal 27th in the league.
Talk about improvement? Instead of leap, it’s more like leaps and bounds for the Panthers’ quarterback. He and his teammates return to action on October 18. It will be fascinating to see if Canales’s club can build off that impressive win over the Lions, and Young can pick up where he left off after a strong four-game performance.

title: The Carolina Panthers' 2-2 Record Might Be Lying to Us
full_text:
I don't know what to make of this Panthers team, and I thought I did after Week 1. Carolina gave up 59 points and 552 yards to Chicago, including 291 on the ground. There wasn't much about that game that made me think we were going to be having a much different conversation four weeks later.
Then Carolina went to Atlanta and won 34-3, and suddenly I wasn't so sure. Was Chicago just one really bad game, or was Atlanta the one we shouldn't read too much into? I wanted to see it again before changing my mind about anything.
Four games in, the Panthers are 2-2, and I still don't completely know what they are. But after watching the last three games, I'm starting to wonder if that record is underselling them a little bit.
I've probably spent too much time thinking about that Chicago game. I know it was only Week 1, but when you give up 59 points and let a team run for almost 300 yards, that's going to stick with me for a while.
That's why I wasn't ready to make too much out of what happened in Atlanta. Carolina looked like a completely different team, especially defensively, but I needed to see more than one good Sunday before I was ready to believe Week 1 was just a bad day.
Then came Cleveland, and that game might bother me even more now than it did when it happened. Carolina had 360 yards, held the Browns to 259, and had the lead with less than five minutes left. The Panthers had every opportunity to leave Cleveland 2-1, and somehow they came home with a 21-18 loss.
I know you can't go back and turn a loss into a win because you think a team should've won. Carolina didn't finish the game, and that's on them. But when I'm trying to figure out whether this team is really just an average 2-2 team, I can't completely ignore what happened that afternoon, either.
Then Detroit came to Charlotte, and I picked the Lions 31-27. I thought Detroit was the better team, and with all the injuries Carolina was dealing with, especially in the secondary, I wasn't sure the Panthers had enough to keep up for four quarters.
This is probably the biggest thing keeping me from going all in on Carolina right now. Detroit had 452 yards Sunday night, Jared Goff threw for 412, and there were definitely times when I thought the Lions were going to keep moving the ball and eventually take control.
And yeah, I still remember Chicago. Maybe I've brought that game up too much over the last few weeks, but 59 points is hard for me to just forget.
At the same time, maybe I need to start letting it go a little bit. Carolina has played three games since then, and Atlanta scored three points while Cleveland managed only 259 yards. Detroit moved the ball all night, but when the Lions needed one more conversion to stay alive, Carolina's defense got the stop.
I'm not telling you this is suddenly a great defense because I don't think it is. There are still things that bother me, and all the injuries in the secondary aren't going to make me feel any better about it.
But maybe Week 1 isn't who they are, either.
This is probably where I've changed my mind the most through four games. I've kept saying I wanted to see Bryce Young do it again, and every week he keeps giving me another reason to stop asking.
Young threw for 329 yards and two touchdowns against Detroit. T etairoa McMillan had 14 catches for 192 yards and two touchdowns, and Chuba Hubbard finally gave Carolina the running game I've been asking for with 122 yards.
That's starting to look like a pretty good offense to me.
Obviously, McMillan isn't going to catch 14 passes every week, and Hubbard isn't going to run for 122 every Sunday. Young is going to have bad throws and probably a bad game somewhere along the way. That's football.
What I'm not going to keep doing is treating every good performance like something that needs to be proven again the following week. We're four games into the season now, and Young keeps playing well. McMillan looks like a legitimate No. 1 receiver, and we just saw what this offense can look like when Hubbard gets going, too.
At some point, I have to judge what I'm actually watching.
This is where I keep coming back to Cleveland. If Carolina finishes that game, we're talking about a 3-1 team right now that has won three straight and just knocked off Detroit on Sunday Night Football.
I know that's not how this works. A loss is a loss, and nobody is giving the Panthers that game back. But I also think we'd be having a completely different conversation about this team right now if they had finished it.
Maybe 2-2 really is exactly what Carolina is. There are still enough problems on defense and enough injuries that I'm not ready to start talking about the playoffs four games into the season. I want to see what this team looks like coming out of the bye, especially with Philadelphia waiting on the other side.
But I know I'm looking at the Panthers differently than I was after Week 1. Back then, I was wondering how bad this season might get.
Now I'm starting to wonder how good they might actually be.

title: Panthers Make Huge Leap in Latest NFL Power Rankings, But There’s Bad News
full_text:
NFL power rankings are what they are. There are numerous versions from thousands of writers and media members. They can be a good gauge of how a team is faring during the season, and are certainly highly subjective.
Let’s go back to the start of the 2026 season. All four teams in the NFC South failed to win their first game. Hence, Nick Shook of NFL.com came out with the following rankings when it came to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers (14th), New Orleans Saints (21st), Carolina Panthers (27th), and Atlanta Falcons (28th).
Obviously, things have changed quite a bit since then. The Panthers and Falcons own 2-2 records, the Saints are off to a 1-3 start, and the 0-4 Bucs are the only winless team in the NFC.
Prior to last week's action, Dave Canales’s team sat at the No. 22 spot. Then came the club’s rousing 32-26 Sunday night victory over the visiting Detroit Lions. It elevated the Panthers to 14th on Shook’s list.
“After a rough Week 3 showing, Bryce Young returned to top form , carving up Detroit’s defense for 329 passing yards and two touchdowns. Chuba Hubbard did his part, too, finishing with 122 rushing yards and two TDs, while Tetairoa McMillan produced a career night, catching 14 passes for 192 yards and two scores. That’s an explosive offense, folks.”
That it is. Only three teams in the league have amassed more total yards than the Panthers, who lead the league in passing yards per game. Carolina’s 121 points scored in four games ranks fourth in the league. And while the club’s record sits at 2-2, it’s the franchise’s best start since opening 3-1 in 201.
The Panthers notched their most impressive win of the season despite missing several key players,” added Shook, “including WR2 Jalen Coker, which makes their latest triumph even more notable.
BIJAN GETS THINGS STARTED EARLY @ATLvsNO on ESPN⁰Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/2WkWScWreu
The only team in the league to make a bigger jump in Shook’s power rankings from Week 4 to Week 5 were the New England Patriots. That 29-26 victory over the rival Bills at Buffalo elevated Mike Vrabel’s team from 31st to 18th, an impressive 13-spot jump. Of course, there was also another club that moved up eight notches as did the Panthers, and that would be Kevin Stefanski’s Falcons.
Atlanta has been rejuvenated by the return of quarterback Michael Penix Jr., the team has won evened its record after a 0-2 start. The Falcons have scored a combined 80 points in road wins over the Packers (35-14) and Saints (45-24) since that ugly 34-4 home loss to Canales’s team in Week 2.
It will be interesting to see where the Panthers land on Shook’s updated rankings. Along with the Kansas City Chiefs, Canales’s club will sit out Week 6.

title: Time to Highlight the Ridiculous Nature of Bryce Young's Panthers Turnaround
full_text:
The results are in and the signs are very positive. Brent Sobleski of Bleacher Report handed out his quarterback grades for Week 4. He deservedly gave the Carolina Panthers’ field general an “A,” and also spoke of just how far the former University of Alabama quarterback has come in a relatively short time.
“Bryce Young leads the NFL with 1,268 passing yards through four weeks of play, and the Carolina Panthers feature the league’s top-ranked aerial attack. “Think about those facts for a few seconds,” added Sobleski. “Let them marinate. Now, understand Young is two years removed from being benched by head coach Dave Canales despite being the No. 1 overall pick from the 2023 class. He only got the job back in 2024 because Andy Dalton suffered an injury from a car wreck. "
Canales’s club, with new play-caller Brad Idzik, leads the NFL in passing yards per game (301.3), and only three teams have averaged more total yards per game (104.5) after four weeks than the defending NFC South champions. Led by their passing game, only the Buffalo Bills (127), Dallas Cowboys (122), and San Francisco 49ers (122) have scored more points than the Panthers (121).
“Now, Young is cooking and looks every bit the part of a franchise quarterback ,” said Sobleski. “He shredded the Detroit Lions’ porous secondary during Sunday Night Football despite wide receivers Jalen Coker and Xavier Legette being on injured reserve.”
Bryce Young to Tetairoa McMillan on 3rd-and-14. WOW. pic.twitter.com/KUuPNU49oS
Of course, Young did have 2025 NFL Offensive Rookie of the Year Tetairoa McMillan, and the duo put on a show. The Panthers’ signal-caller connected on 29 of his 41 throws for 329 yards and a pair of scores. McMillan was targeted 16 times and hauled in 14 passes for 192 yards and both of those touchdown tosses.
After four weeks of action, the four-year quarterback is the league’s 10th-ranked passer. Those aforementioned league-high 1,268 yards have come in Young completing 101-of-162 passes (62.3 percent). There have been nine touchdown passes compared to only a pair of interceptions. He’s thrown for at least 300 yards twice in four weeks, quite the jump considering he reached that mark just three times in his first three NFL campaigns.
Here’s one more morsel to gnaw on. Those two picks are the only two miscues by Young this season, who has not fumbled in four games this season. A year ago, the emerging performer turned over the football five times in the club’s first five quarters of action. He finished with 11 interceptions and four lost fumbles in 16 regular-season contests, and also served up one pick in the playoff loss to the Los Angeles Rams.
The 2-2 Panthers are off this week, and return to action on October 18 with a clash with the Eagles at Philadelphia. There’s an awfully long way to go this season, but there are certainly a lot of encouraging signs when it comes to the Carolina’s 25-year-old hurler.

title: Panthers Stock Report: Who Soared and Who Slipped After Huge Lions Win
full_text:
I really didn't think the Panthers were going to beat Detroit. I picked the Lions 31-27, and with Carolina missing guys all over the place, I figured eventually it was going to catch up with them.
Carolina beat one of the better teams in the NFC, Bryce Young was really good again, and Tetairoa McMillan had one of those games where you almost run out of things to say about him. The Panthers also finally got Chuba Hubbard going, which I've only been asking them to do pretty much every week.
So yeah, there's plenty of Stock Up this week. Stock Down was a little harder to find after a win like that, but there are still a couple of things that bother me.
I know I've talked about this enough already, but give Hubbard the ball.
Carolina finally did that against Detroit, and he gave them 122 rushing yards. This looked a lot more like the running game I thought we were going to see this season, and it also meant Young didn't have to do everything himself.
That's the part I've never really understood. Young has been really good, but why make him throw it all over the field if you don't have to? We already watched him throw it 48 times against Cleveland, and I don't need to see that every week.
I'm not saying Hubbard needs 25 or 30 carries every Sunday. But after what we just watched against Detroit, I don't think I should have to keep asking Carolina to get him the ball, either.
I was worried about Jahmyr Gibbs in this game. After watching Chicago run for 291 yards in Week 1, how could I not be?
Detroit finished with 46 rushing yards. I definitely didn't see that coming, especially against this Panthers defense.
Devin Lloyd came back and played every defensive snap, and having him back in the middle sure didn't hurt. I don't think it's a coincidence that one of Carolina's best games against the run came with Lloyd back out there.
Now, I'm not ready to say the run defense is fixed. I've already gone down that road once this season, and I'm not doing it again after one game. But 46 yards against Detroit? I'll take that every single time.
Corey Bullock was one of the guys I was worried about going into this game. Damien Lewis was out, Bullock was starting at left guard, and Detroit was about the last team I wanted to see him thrown in there against.
Then he had a rough moment early, and I thought, here we go.
After that, though, I really didn't notice him much. Normally, saying I didn't notice somebody wouldn't be much of a compliment, but for an offensive lineman filling in for a starter, that's pretty much what I'm looking for.
Bullock played every offensive snap, Hubbard ran for 122 yards, and Young threw for 329. I'm not saying Bullock needs to take Lewis' job or anything crazy like that, but I was worried about him before the game. By the time it ended, I really wasn't.
That's good enough for me.
This one is a little tough because I actually thought some of the guys back there did a pretty good job with what they were being asked to do. Will Lee III was playing a much bigger role than anybody probably expected this early, and he helped make the fourth-down stop that finally ended Detroit's last possession.
But Jared Goff still threw for 412 yards.
Yeah, he threw it 52 times. Carolina was also missing Jaycee Horn and Mike Jackson, so I'm not going to sit here and act like the secondary was at full strength and just got torched all night.
Still, 412 yards is a lot. Philadelphia is waiting after the bye, and that's probably the biggest thing on this defense that still worries me.
Seriously, who else can Carolina afford to lose?
The Panthers went into Sunday night without Horn, Jackson, Xavier Legette, Jalen Coker and Lewis. Then Monroe Freeling went down during the game, because apparently the injury list wasn't long enough already.
Somehow, Carolina keeps finding guys to throw out there, and somehow, they're still finding ways to win games. That's great, but I really don't want to find out how many more injuries this team can take before it finally becomes too much.
I hated this Week 5 bye when the schedule came out. Now I'm looking at this team four games into the season and thinking maybe whoever made the schedule did Carolina a favor.

title: Bryce Young Was Pressed About the MVP Chants. His Response Says Everything
Overreaction? Panthers Saved Their Season With Primetime Win Over Lions
full_text:
The Carolina Panthers season is alive and well after a primetime win over the Detroit Lions . Carolina beats Detroit 32-26 as Bryce Young and Tetairoa McMillan show out with their connection and elite-level plays.
This is the Panthers' first Sunday Night Football win in almost 11 years, with their last coming on October 25th, 2015, with a home victory over the Philadelphia Eagles. That team went on to play in the Super Bowl.
This isn't to say that Bryce Young and Co. are making a Super Bowl run, but winning on primetime still matters and can catapult a team toward a successful season.
With the win, the Panthers sit at first place in the NFC South, having a 2-2 record and a win over the Atanta Falcons, who just demolished the New Orleans Saints on Monday Night Football.
Obviously, Carolina's win was huge for morale, overall momentum, and the standings. What if the Panthers lost though?
Despite obliterating the Atlanta Falcons in Week 2, Carolina would be tied for the second-worst record in the NFC South. The Falcons took care of business against the New Orleans Saints on Monday night, improving to 2-2 and looking elite on offense since Michael Penix Jr. came back.
Had Carolina lost, that would've been 0-2 at home, with two of its next three games on the road against teams that made the playoffs last season, the Eagles and the Packers.
Maybe the rest of the division struggles just as much as Carolina could, but thats why the win on Sunday night was so important, Carolina stays above the rest of the queue for another week, and can't make any mistakes this weekend with the bye.
No one expected the Buccaneers to be this bad for four weeks, so that gives Carolina some room, but even so, if Carolina lost, they'd be only one game above Tampa Bay. It's a world of difference for the rest-of-the-year outlook.
So no, it's not an overreaction. The NFC South will likely remain a tight race through the rest of the season, so the week-to-week outlook can fluctuate throughout the year.
Carolina's next four weeks are as follows.
Sunday, 10/18, 1:00 PM ET, at Philadelphia Eagles
Sunday, 10/25, 1:00 PM ET, vs. Tampa Bay Buccaneers
Thursday, 10/29, 8:15 PM ET, at Green Bay Packers
Sunday, 11/8, 1:00 PM ET, vs. Denver Broncos
2-2 in that four-week stretch is a must. If Carolina can somehow go 3-1, then there's something real going on in Charlotte.
Obviously, the Tampa game is a must-win for division purposes, but there's even a chance that the Bucs' are still winless by that point. Losing to a potential 0-6 Tampa Bay team would be as demoralizing a loss as any loss in the NFL.

title: Bears 1st Quarter Report Card: Caleb Williams' Injury Can't Slow This Offense Down
full_text:
Most Chicago Bears fans optimistically expected a 3-1 start to the 2026 NFL season, but probably not in the way that it's happened. With Caleb Williams' hamstring injury sidelining him for the last two games, the Bears have been forced to turn both Case Keenum and Tyson Bagent as starters. Against all odds, both quarterbacks delivered a win to keep the Bears' season on track through the first quarter.
With that in mind, let's take a look at the offense through the first quarter of the season and hand out some grades. Which position groups have overachieved, and which groups remain somewhat uncertain? Let's take a look, starting with the quarterbacks.
This one is a no-brainer. All three of the quarterbacks that have started a game for the Bears this year have played lights-out football, and Bears fans can rest easy knowing that winning the division is still very much on the table, even with Ben Johnson ruling Caleb Williams out again for Week 5 .
Another easy A+ grade goes to the running backs. The Bears lead the league in rushing yards by a healthy margin, racking up 196.3 rushing yards per game. D'Andre Swift started the season with an explosive three-touchdown performance but got himself benched in Week 4 for an egregious fumble . Kyle Monangai, on the other hand, has been an absolute juggernaut. If he keeps up his current pace, the Bears may have a running back controversy on their hands.
After two easy grades, we come finally to some tough ones. Through four games, no one has seized the WR1 job that was left vacant after the Bears traded DJ Moore to the Buffalo Bills this offseason. Rome Odunze leads all receivers with 233 yards, but a surprising No. 2 is Kalif Raymond with 220 yards while Luther Burden III is just one yard behind Raymond. Additionally, no receiver has more than one touchdown.
That said, Ben Johnson's offense may not need a dominant WR1 to find success. Almost every week we've seen a different receiver step up to make plays and pace the team, and as long as the Bears continue to win, I see no problem with a WR1-by-committee approach. That earns this group a straight 'B'.
If any offensive position group has disappointed so far this season, it's been the tight ends. Colston Loveland's confusing disappearance after a red-hot end to his rookie year has been especially disappointing. He has barely more receiving yards than running back D'Andre Swift at this point and is still looking for his first touchdown of the year.
Cole Kmet has just four receptions all year, though one was a gorgeous touchdown catch in Week 1. Meanwhile, the rookie Sam Roush is struggling to start the season. Altogether, I can't give this group a grade any higher than a D+, mostly due to how far below expectations their first quarter performance fell.
This unit may not be quite as dominant as they were a year ago, but that's a high bar to clear. They're still playing at an elite level, especially Darnell Wright, who may very well be the NFL's best right tackle . Both Joe Thuney and Jonah Jackson are playing at an All-Pro level, as well. The only question marks are at the center and left tackle positions.
Garrett Bradbury has recovered well from a catastrophic Week 2 performance , one that included five penalties. But it still feels like it's only a matter of time before we see the rookie Logan Jones take over. As for left tackle, Braxton Jones was holding it down well until a knee injury forced the Bears to place him on IR last week. Theo Benedet started in his stead, but there's a reason why he's the third-string left tackle.
Despite these issues, this offensive line has still done a commendable job in keeping Ben Johnson's high-octane offense going. They've earned a B+ for the first quarter and could see that grade improve should Ozzy Trapilo return from injury in the next week or two.

title: Kyle Monangai Injury Update Puts Roschon Johnson Under Fantasy Football Microscope
full_text:
The Chicago Bears have a concern when it comes to running back Kyle Monangai ahead of the Week 5 game against the Green Bay Packers, and his injury could open the door for some work for fellow running back Roschon Johnson.
Monangai is dealing with toe and thumb injuries that have kept him out of practice over the first two days of the week.
But it appears the toe is the bigger issue currently , with ESPN's Jeremy Fowler reporting that Monangai's status for this and the following week is in question as he battles a turf toe issue .
Fowler notes that Monangai is hoping to play through it.
"Bears RB Kyle Monangai is dealing with a turf toe injury, placing uncertainty around his availability over the next 1-2 weeks, per sources, though he’s hoping to play through it and the team/player are still managing the situation," Fowler said.
With Monangai in danger of missing time with his turf toe, fantasy football owners want to know if the Bears' RB3, Johnson, is worth adding in fantasy football. Here's what we think.
Johnson is worth a speculative add for now, but don't go falling all over yourself to add him. By that we mean don't drop a player with any semblance of value for him, and we say that for a few reasons.
The most simple reason is we still don't know if Monangai is going to miss time. We suspect the Bears will hold him out because it's so early in the season, but then again, Chicago has a divisional matchup against the Packers , so he could push to play.
Even if Monangai misses time, D'Andre Swift is still the lead back and is going to handle the vast majority of touches, both on the ground and through the air.
Swift is also on the injury report this week , but unlike Monangai, he was able to log a limited practice on Thursday, so he's trending in the right direction. There has been nothing to suggest he's in danger of sitting out. If Swift does get ruled out for Sunday, Johnson becomes a much more attractive option because Chicago would likely give him a ton of work in that scenario.
Another reason we don't love Johnson has to do with the fact that he has been mostly ineffective during his career, with the former fourth-round pick averaging 3.8 yards per carry. He has stuck in Chicago strictly for his special teams work.
Another thing to note is that the Bears have two running backs on their practice squad in Zavier Scott and Salvon Ahmed, and one of them will get elevated if Monangai sits.
Ahmed is the favorite to get the nod, as he has been with the Bears since the offseason, and he was far and away the superior runner over Johnson in training camp and the preseason. The only reason he didn't beat Johnson out for a roster spot is because of Johnson's special teams value.
The only reason we could see Johnson getting more work over Ahmed behind Swift is because he fits the profile of the kind of back head coach Ben Johnson wants in a one-two punch at the position. Johnson likes a power runner, like Monangai, and a more agile, explosive runner like Swift. Johnson fits the former type.
The bottom line is this: Johnson is worth an add off the waiver wire, but don't go out of your way to get him.
If you've got an open spot on your roster and have a precarious situation at running back, it makes sense to add Johnson, but we would only start him if both Swift and Monangai are ruled out.

title: When Was the Last Time the Chicago Bears Have Been Favored at Lambeau Field?
full_text:
The great Billy Joel once said, ' the times they are a-changin '. That sentiment can easily be applied to the Chicago Bears and Green Bay Packers since Ben Johnson landed at O'Hare in the 2025 offseason.
Former Packers QB Aaron Rodgers owned a 25-5 record against the Bears, and it initially looked like Jordan Love would pick up right where he left off. One of the league's most storied rivalries also turned into one of the most one-sided battles from 2008 through 2024. Then Johnson arrived and reinvigorated the Bears organization.
Conversely, he also seems to have knocked the Packers down a peg (a record-breaking come-from-behind playoff win will do that) in the process. Johnson hasn't hidden his disdain towards their neighbor to the north, which was clear in their three matchups last season.
At this point, it's become clear which side the consensus is on heading into Sunday's game. The Bears are favored at Lambeau Field (by 2.5 points, according to DraftKings Sportsbook ) for the first time since the 2006 season opener.
How did that game go for Chicago?
The Bears were coming off an impressive 11-5 campaign in 2005, and vibes were high heading into the 2026 season. Their first matchup was against their hated division rivals in Green Bay, and Chicago was favored by 3.5 points on the road.
Bears signal-caller Rex Grossman and Co. had no issue beating the spread. They came away with an impressive 26-0 win on Green Bay's own turf. A surprising rookie contributor put the final nail in the Packers' coffin early in the fourth quarter.
𝐒𝐞𝐩𝐭𝐞𝐦𝐛𝐞𝐫 𝟏𝟎, 𝟐𝟎𝟎𝟔 Devin Hester has his first career punt return TD as the Bears beat the Packers in Week 1! 🐻⬇️ pic.twitter.com/20svZ3k1wz
Bears rookie third-round selection Zavion Thomas hopefully took notes on Hester's performance. He hasn't made much of an impact through the first month , but his abilities in the return game are the main reason the team pulled the trigger on him when they did. Here's to hoping they start utilizing him in the punt return game on top of his normal kickoff duties.
What did the Bears do after the impressive season opener? They became the team we all thought they would be ( if you know, you know ). They went on to represent the NFC in the Super Bowl before ultimately falling short to the Peyton Manning-led Indianapolis Colts.
The Bears and Packers are seemingly two teams heading in polar opposite directions.
Johnson turned the Bears into a legit contender as soon as he arrived in Chicago. He helped a team that won only five games the previous year more than double their win total last season. They went 11-6 and were a play away from being a game away from a Super Bowl appearance.
Meanwhile, the Packers were the team Chicago beat to put themselves in that situation . The first half of their Wild Card matchup looked much like virtually every game the two teams have played over the past 20 years. Green Bay owned a 21-3 lead and looked utterly dominant. Then the fourth quarter happened, and the Bears mounted a furious comeback to send their rivals packing with a 31-27 win.
Green Bay seemingly hasn't recovered from that loss (and the loss of Micah Parsons on defense a few weeks earlier). Their two wins this season have come in games where they've barely squeaked out wins against the 1-3 Jets and winless Buccaneers (who were starting an undrafted rookie at QB). Their two losses have been blowouts.
While the Bears would be hard-pressed to repeat their 26-0 drubbing with backup quarterback Tyson Bagent under center , they do stand a good chance of coming out on top on Sunday. The Packers seem rudderless right now, and Ben Johnson and Co. probably smell blood in the water.
From there, they'll take it one game at a time. There's little doubt that they firmly have their sights set on another Super Bowl run. They'd hopefully have much better luck this time around.

title: Injury Update Casts Doubt on Kyle Monangai's Status for Week 5 vs Packers
full_text:
The Chicago Bears may be without one of their top offensive playmakers for their Week 5 division showdown with the Green Bay Packers. Despite a positive injury update from head coach Ben Johnson on Wednesday, Kyle Monangai was once again listed as a 'Did Not Participate' o n Thursday's injury report , and now we know why.
According to a report from ESPN's Jeremy Fowler , Monangai is dealing with a turf toe injury, which shrouds his status for at least this upcoming game in doubt. If Monangai is unable to play on Sunday, the Bears will likely have to turn to third-string running back and four-year veteran Roschon Johnson. Johnson has just four rushing attempts all season, and all four of those came in last week's game.
Week 5 is a critical opportunity for the Bears, and they're already going into that game with a severe handicap. Caleb Williams still isn't practicing as he recovers from his hamstring injury, and Ben Johnson already named Tyson Bagent as the starting quarterback. Bagent showed last week that he can be relied on to deliver wins, but the offense's ceiling is much, much lower with him under center than it is with Williams.
That's what makes Monangai's availability so important. Without him, the Bears' rushing attack becomes one-dimensional behind D'Andre Swift. I mean that without any disrespect towards Swift, who has proven that he can take over games just like Monangai does. His explosive performance in the season opener powered the Bears to their historic 59-point Week 1 debut.
But the Bears' offense functions best when their rushing attack is a two-headed monster. When either Swift or Monangai are out, it becomes far more difficult for Ben Johnson to attack defenses the way he wants to. Roschon Johnson can handle a few rushing attempts, but the Bears would have to lean heavily on Swift if Monangai is unable to go.
The Green Bay Packers may be circling the drain, but they're still a dangerous opponent, and they'll be playing like their entire season is on the line (in many ways, it is). Every divisional game can go sideways in a New York minute, and if the Bears don't have both of their starting running backs available, even a short-handed Packers defense may be able to derail the Bears' offense, especially with the crowd of Lambeau Field at their backs.
Bears fans will just have to hold onto hope and wait for the Friday injury report to be released. At this point, seeing Monangai listed as 'Questionable' is probably the best-case scenario.

title: One of Dennis Allen's 'Window Washers' Closer to Losing Starting Job
full_text:
One of the greatest dangers for the Bears defense facing Green Bay is getting burned for big plays from receivers, particularly speedy Christian Watson or
 Matthew Golden.
In that case, one cornerback in particular is a potential problem . Of course, this is Tyrique Stevenson.
In the final year of his contract, Stevenson has a rather peculiar mix of statistics but it's not much different than last year. He has allowed 60% completions, which isn't bad for a cornerback. However, he has allowed more yards per completion than all but two other starting cornerbacks at 21.3 yards a catch. He also is fourth-worst among all starting cornerbacks in passer rating against when targeted at 143.8.
The obvious problem is Stevenson allowing few plays, but the ones he does allow are for big yardage. Last week was an example with a 58-yard bomb to Isaiah Williams as Stevenson trailed the play.  He also got beat on a similar play by Jalen Coker for a TD in the opener.
🐻 #Bears DC Dennis Allen on Tyrique Stevenson’s early-season struggles: Stevenson has battled a hamstring injury and allowed 5 catches for 96 yards and a TD against the Jets. Allen emphasized that mistakes are inevitable at cornerback, but what matters most is bouncing back,… pic.twitter.com/jk1JqQMxZn
"Well listen, the No. 1 thing I would tell all of you in this scheme it's like being a window washer on a high-rise building," Bears defensive coordinator Dennis Allen said of his cornerbacks. "You can't make mistakes or you can't have a bad day because bad things really happen. So, that's part of the business in this.
"You know, we put those guys out there and give them a tough job. All of the great ones, OK, every one of them have been beaten at some point in time. And really it's about go on to the next play, line up again, play with the same confidence, aggression, and it's just, I mean, it's a part of the business."
The problem for Stevenson is this weakness could mean his starting job. Kyler Gordon continues going through practices, and his return could be this week or next week. When that happens, rookie Malik Muhammad becomes a cornerback who can move to the outside.
A 58-yard TD strike from Geno Smith to Isaiah Williams for the @nyjets ! 📺: FOX/FOX One pic.twitter.com/sQze3bjxOI
It would then be up to Allen to move his window washer, er, starting cornerback to the bench or to move Muhammad there.
Muhammad has allowed a spectacular passer rating against of 43.5 playing both the slot cornerback position and, at times, outside at Stevenson's spot. He has allowed 44.4% completions. Considering this, and Stevenson's contract expiring after this year, it's not difficult to ascertain who is going to sit — or maybe Allen has a plan for all of them to play in some type of rotation.
Ultimately, none of this will happen until Gordon is deemed ready to return from physically unable to perform. He is practicing, but not necessarily ready to play a full game if he does get activated.  Johnson revealed how this return could look for Gordon.
Tyrique has been expelled from Al Harris university
"Yeah, look, I think with any of these guys that are coming off the PUP list, to think that any of them would be ready to go in there and play 50, 60, 70 plays in a game, I think that would be unrealistic to think," Allen said, referring to Gordon, defensive end Shemar Turner and linebacker Noah Sewell. "With all of these guys, as we begin to get some of them back, I think the prudent action would be start to incorporate them in and yet don’t expect them to be full-time players initially on."
Allen can't discount what he's seen from Gordon, who has been a focal point of controversy since his calf injury in the offseason and his subsequent decision to rehab it on his own.
TOUCHDOWN JALEN COKER! WHAT A THROW AND CATCH #NFL #Bears #DaBears #Panthers #KeepPounding pic.twitter.com/Tgk1lEFoq5
"I think he’s working hard," Allen said. "I think he’s competing out there on the practice field and that’s good to see. I’m excited about all these guys that are coming off the PUP list and what I think they can help and what I think they can bring to the table."
They're going to need someone to cope with all of the speed the Packers have at receiver.
This week would be as good of a time as any for an injection of new blood and to sit players who haven't been hitting the standard, or for that matter getting the windows cleaned.

title: Bears' Thursday Injury Report: Kyle Monangai, D'Andre Swift Trending in Opposite Directions
full_text:

The Bears started off the week with quite the lengthy injury report that had seven players not practicing, with six of those players sitting out for injury-related purposes.
However, Thursday brought some good news, as five of those players were upgraded. Among those players was D'Andre Swift, but we can't say the same for his backfield mate, Kyle Monangai.
On the Caleb Williams front, there was no change in his practice participation on the injury report, but there was a report earlier Thursday that offered some optimism for him.
Now, a look at the full injury report for Chicago and much more.
UPDATE: After this article was published, ESPN's Jeremy Fowler reported that Monangai is dealing with turf toe and his status is uncertain for the next one to two weeks.
Fowler adds that Monangai is going to try and play through the injury, but it isn't clear if he'll actually be able to.
"Bears RB Kyle Monangai is dealing with a turf toe injury, placing uncertainty around his availability over the next 1-2 weeks, per sources, though he’s hoping to play through it and the team/player are still managing the situation," Fowler reported.
With Monangai not practicing for a second straight day, that leaves his status even more up in the air.
Head coach Ben Johnson said Monangai's thumb is "not an issue" on Wednesday, but he did not address the toe issue, which was something we didn't know about initially.
Johnson did say that Monangai was feeling the wear and tear of his 30-carry game on Sunday, so perhaps this is just the Bears giving him a little extra rest.
But, since we don't know that for sure, we'll say Monangai is trending toward a questionable tag, at best, for now.
With Swift, Jackson, Thuney and Wright all being upgraded, all four players are now on track to suit up. That said, with a limited practice for each, they will still be worth monitoring on Friday.
The PUP guys, Gordon, Sewell and Turner, are all trending toward being ready to return, although they still have to be activated first, which will also mean roster moves will be in order to make room for them. That said, their status for this week has not yet been confirmed, so they aren't locked in yet.
Speaking of possible returns, Lewis remains on track to make his return after sitting out last week's game with a hip issue.
Again, Williams did not take part in practice on Thursday, but he does appear to be ramping up a bit in his recovery , according to Dan Wiederer of The Athletic .
"Williams is progressing notably with his on-field recovery steps. Per those in the know, he has looked spry and comfortable taking drops, planting, slinging it around," Wiederer wrote.
Wiederer then went on to say that the Bears' upcoming schedule could complicate Williams' return with the short week between Week 6 and 7.
"The Bears do have a scheduling quirk that could factor into Williams’ clearance. After a Week 6 Sunday game in Atlanta, Bears face quick Thursday night turnaround before home v NE. (Then an extra-long turnaround before 11/1 MNF game in Seattle.)," he said.
Wiederer seems to think it's possible we won't see Williams until all the way in Week 8. If that's the case, it's a bit odd the Bears didn't put him on injured reserve, but that could also just be because they assumed he'd heal faster than he did.
Whatever the case may be, Williams' return date won't be a concern until the Bears start losing. As of right now, they're undefeated with Williams on the shelf.

title: 3 Bears Whose Roster Spots Could be in Jeopardy With Players Returning From IR
full_text:
The Chicago Bears a few tough decisions to make over the next two weeks.
They opened up the 21-day practice windows for linebacker Noah Sewell and defensive lineman Shemar Turner on September 23. That means they would have to be activated to the 53-man roster by next Wednesday in order to play this season.
They're in a similar position with cornerback Kyler Gordon. They opened his 21-day practice window on September 30. That would give him one more week to join the active roster before he suffered a similar fate.
With Turner and Sewell both providing quality depth, and Gordon being one of their best players in the secondary ( on the rare occasion when he's healthy ), all three seem like safe bets to return to the lineup. Three players would need to get cut in corresponding moves, though.
Which unlucky few stand out as potential roster casualties?
Some might find this one surprising. We went back and forth between James Lynch and Jayden Loving (they'll likely need to cut ties with a defensive tackle, since they're not really in a great position to release a corner).
The Bears previously cut Lynch over Loving when cultivating their 53-man roster. They didn't want to risk losing the promising undrafted rookie to waivers. It's probably less of a fear with him being a healthy scratch over the first month, but we could see a scenario where they don't want to risk it.
The coaching staff has to like what they've seen from Lynch when he's been out there, though. The 27-year-old played over 30% of the snaps in each of the first three games (before being a healthy scratch last week) and has been one of their better run defenders when he's been on the field. Lynch would be a lock to rejoin the practice squad if he clears waivers.
We just saw Marcus Davenport play 12 snaps against the Jets after being called up to the active roster. They'd probably have a similar plan for Lynch later this season.
Edge rusher Jamree Kromah is in nearly the exact situation as Lynch. However, he's actually in a more similar spot to Loving. The Bears didn't want to risk losing either player after they both showed major flashes throughout the preseason. Neither player has cracked the gameday roster yet, though.
Shemar Turner will probably play a similar hybrid role to Dayo Odeyingbo . That fact could see Kromah losing a numbers game he presumably barely survived on roster cutdown day.
Daniel Hardy's role is safe due to the value he brings on special teams. Kromah doesn't bring that same impact, which is why he hasn't seen the field over the first month of the season. He's another player they'd love to bring back to the practice squad.
Skyler Thomas' job feels like the safest of the three players listed here. However, we struggle to see a scenario where they cut ties with Clark Phillips III after acquiring him in the trade for Gervon Dexter Sr. last month (even if he hasn't played a defensive snap). We also gave Jack Sanborn a slight edge thanks to his special teams value.
Thomas' job definitely won't be safe once Coby Bryant returns from IR in (hopefully) December. Nevertheless, with Gordon's return on the horizon, he might not stick around that long.
The Bears would only have three pure safeties on the roster if they cut ties with Thomas, but Cam Lewis is a hybrid player with a ton of experience on the back end. They wouldn't need him to provide depth at nickelback anymore, either.
Stop me if you've heard this one before, but Thomas would also be brought back to the practice squad. The fact that it's difficult to find cut-worthy players is a testament to the team's depth. This one would've been a lot easier to write in the pre-Ben Johnson era.

title: What Ben Johnson Wants to See More of from Tyson Bagent Against Packers
full_text:
While the Packers are still worrying about Ben Johnson's comments from last year, they have apparently missed the respect t he Bears coach and quarterback Tyson Bagent have been giving them this week.
When you're yapping , it's easy to miss what's being said  — even the compliments.
Johnson has been nothing but respectful to the Packers so far this week but beyond that he is especially wary of two players he also identified last year as real problems.
"It's a good team, as we all know," Johnson said of the 2-2 Packers. "Some changes from a year ago, just special teams wise and defensively. More so schematics than personnel per se, but it's a good special teams unit. They're playing really well. They have a lot of big bodies.
When looking at Tyson Bagent performance context matters. This guy hadn’t started in 1059 days (longer than Keenum) was coming off a concussion and half the fans wanted Keenum to start. Great operation. Efficient on 3rd down. Good downfield. Excellent first start. #DaBesrs pic.twitter.com/Dt5nRRumT1
"I think they're really well coached. Defensively, a lot of speed. I have a ton of respect for these safeties, nickel, these guys fly around. The guys up front, they're playing really well. Also, new addition in (Packers LB Zaire Franklin) 44 at the Mike linebacker. He's all over the place. Instinctive player, so really good unit and (Packers) (defensive coordinator Jonathan) Gannon does a great job with them. Then, their offense; obviously Jordan Love’s one of the better quarterbacks in this league. He is as accurate as anybody. I think they have got great speed on the outside and they've given us issues in the past. It will be a really big challenge for us on the road.”
Obviously Johnson isn't about to chant "Green Bay (inhales vigorously)" like Bears fans have all offseason. Matt LaFleur hasn't been insulted by Johnson this week in the least, and both of the guys who had the cheese grater hats last year — Caleb Williams and DJ Moore — won't be a part of Sunday's game.
It's the Packers safeties who really concern Johnson, Xavier McKinney and Evan Williams. Ironically enough, it was Williams who was doing some of the yapping in Green Bay, today. It doesn't matter. The Bears still have a job to do and it's avoid the safeties.
Evan Williams ahead of Packers-Bears: "It's easy to have a camera in front of you and say whatever you want. That's not going to stop you from getting hit in the mouth on any given Sunday ... it's great for the news articles and all that, but at the end of the day, it's not…
"They fly around and they make things muddy back there," Johnson said. "I think they've got a good mix of coverages. (Gannon is) doing a little bit of stuff that they did in Arizona, just in terms of showing a blanket back there and then rotating on the snap and it can be challenging for the quarterbacks.
"We got to be very disciplined and having our eyes in the right spots and our route runners have got to be in the right spots as well, we're coaching up here this week."
McKinney was a second-team All-Pro last year. The Packers didn't have Williams in the first game at Soldier Field last year, won 22-16 on Caleb Williams' bomb to Moore. They did have him in the playoff loss to the Bears, though.
Real unbiased list, Packers vs Jets matchup breakdown: Where did I miss? QB - Packers RBs - Jets WRs - Packers TEs - Packers OL - Jets DL - Jets (it’s close) LBs - Packers CBs - Packers Safeties - Packers ST-Packers HC - Packers pic.twitter.com/m3ZNDsTPUZ
These two players can be particularly troublesome if quarterback Tyson Bagent is to take the advice he received from Johnson after Sunday's win and film review. It was to take his shots. Johnson said he wanted to see Bagent be a little slower to checkdown on some passes and he gave up on chances to make big, deeper throws against the Jets.
“There's a handful of them and I mean when the moments present themselves obviously I've got to take it," Bagent said. "I was a little quick to get to the checkdown but that can't be the case going forward. I've got to be better in that sense, especially going into this week.”
Johnson doesn't want his backup QB playing like a backup, which is something any backup QB would want to hear.
The #Bears are now -1.5 favorites against the #Packers in Green Bay next week. They were +2.5 underdogs on the lookahead line when the day started.
"I think that he falls into the to the category of people that I felt rallied behind me," Bagent said. "He said he's giving me the keys and I appreciate that and look to be better going forward.”
One play in particular is eating at Bagent after last week. It was how he missed a potential big gainer. “Luther Burden over the middle, that was certainly one that really sticks out egregiously, is the one to Luther across in the middle," Bagent said.
2 jets players ran into each other luther burden wide open for a TD tyson Bagent missed #dabears awful screen call for roush pic.twitter.com/DLRoaFKMKm
It happened in the third quarter.
To avoid being too cautious, Bagent knows it's going to mean attacking those highly respected Packers safeties.
“I think you just have an understanding that they're playing at a high level back there, they've been together for a long time, they communicate really well," Bagent said. "They get everybody on track with what they're doing in the back end and I have a lot of respect for those guys back there and really just have to be clued into each play and understanding that they could make a splash play at any time, just being cautious around those guys.”
Maybe the better word than caution is respectful.
The Bears have been nothing but respectful of the Packers this week.

title: Caleb Williams Injury Update Confirms Bears QB's Progress in Recovery
full_text:
The Chicago Bears may be 2-0 since losing Caleb Williams to a hamstring injury , but that doesn't mean that the fans aren't itching to see No. 18 return under center. For those fans, the latest report on Williams' rehab should be music to their ears. According to Dan Wiederer of The Athletic , Williams is "progressing notably with his on-field recovery steps" and has looked "spry and comfortable taking drops, planting, slinging it around."
Williams is still not practicing with the team, but the fact that he's moving around with that much confidence leads one to believe that his return is near. In fact, notable NFL insider Ian Rapoport gave his own update from the Caleb Williams front on Wednesday, and he suggested that Williams could return to practice next week ahead of the Bears' Week 6 game against the Atlanta Falcons.
These updates from Rapoport and Wiederer are tremendous news for Bears fans, but Wiederer adds a cautionary note regarding the Bears' schedule "that could factor into Williams' clearance". In Week 6, the Bears travel to Atlanta to take on the Falcons, then face a quick turnaround at home against the New England Patriots on Thursday Night Football.
Williams could potentially return in Week 6, but the Bears may choose to play it safe and hold him out for one more game, especially if they keep winning. However, bringing Williams back after a month on the sidelines and asking him to lead the Bears to victory on a short week doesn't sound like the wisest of plans.
Wiederer did not elaborate on his point about this scheduling quirk, but the fact that he even brought it up makes it something worth considering. The Bears may face a situation where they either bring Williams back in Week 6, which could be too soon, or wait until Week 8, during which time they may lose one or two more games.
The positive injury updates for Williams continue to roll in, and it sure sounds like he'll be ready to play in Week 6, or at the very least start practicing again. Should he return at that point, he would have missed only three games, and the Bears have already won two of those three. In fact, with the Bears favored to beat the Green Bay Packers in Lambeau Field for the first time in 20 years, there's a very good chance the Bears will be undefeated in Williams' absence.
The Bears were lucky that Williams' injury was not a significant one, and they've been lucky since then that both of their backup quarterbacks have delivered signature wins. If their luck continues to hold, they may very well prove to be a legit Super Bowl contender , after all.

title: Bengals Safety 'Very Hopeful' to Play Sunday at Dolphins
full_text:
The Bengals' secondary could get back one of its most important players on Sunday against the Dolphins. Bryan Cook practiced in a limited capacity Thursday, an improvement from Wednesday, when he did not practice at all.
Cook confirmed after practice that, while recovering from his ankle injury has been frustrating, he is very hopeful he will be back on the field against the Dolphins this week.
"Kind of frustrating, but I'm trying to figure it out," Cook said at his locker. "Very hopeful, I'm trying to do everything I can to be out there."
Cook followed this up by emphasizing how much the defense depends on him in certain areas. He also said that he could have corrected mistakes before they happened.
"They depend on me in certain aspects, some things that on the field like 'this person made a mistake' but I feel like me not being out there can hurt," Cook said. "I can help to a certain extent like certain plays that may have been a mistake, I feel like I could have been out there and said something to correct it before that play even happened."
Cook emphasized that while he badly wants to get back on the field, he will make sure he is healthy first to avoid hurting his teammates and harming the defense's performance.
“You know how much I love my teammates, and I want to be playing but I can’t be selfish in that aspect, But at the same time, I feel if I'm not being who they need me to be on the team, on the field, I'm hurting my teammates," Cook said. "So I never let that happen. It's always team first at the end of the day. So if I can be what I need to be for my team, I'll be out there, and if I feel like I'm giving them less than myself, I’ll never let that happen. It’s always team-first at the end of the day.”
Last week, the team elevated Russ Yeast from the practice squad to rotate with PJ Jules at safety, opposite Jordan Battle.
Both played admirably, and we could see them again this week. Cook practicing is a great sign for his immediate availability; however, with the bye week looming, Zac Taylor and the coaches could choose to let him continue healing this week.

title: Bengals Safety Jordan Battle Knows Actions, Not Words Will Answer Questions About His Tackling
full_text:
Cincinnati Bengals safety Jordan Battle heard the comments, and he doesn’t fully agree.
Not the shipload of comments on social media about his missed tackle Sunday against the Jacksonville Jaguars.
“No,” Battle said. “I almost cussed. But no, I don’t pay attention to none of that on social media.”
The comments Battle was challenging were the ones made by defensive coordinator Al Golden on Wednesday when he was asked about Battle’s missed tackle of Jaguars tight end Brenton Strange on third and 18.
Strange added 12 more yards after the miss for a 23-yard gain that gave the Jaguars a first down, eventually leading to a field goal in the first quarter of the Bengals’ 22-17 loss.
“If I'm being completely honest, I don't think the criticism on that one – we've always got to make a tackle; we understand that – but he needs friends on that one,” Golden said. “We've got to gang-tackle that. We have to have our cleats in the ground, vision, we've got to know the down and distance, we've got to know the sticks.
“There should be guys breaking on either side of Jordan,” Golden added. “It shouldn’t be just a one-man show. He knows he's got to be better on that play. I know I have to coach everybody else better to get them where they need to be when that ball is thrown on third and 18.”
Battle appreciated Golden defending him but said regardless of what else was happening on the field, he needs to make that tackle.
“I hold myself to a high pedestal, and my expectation for myself is very high,” he said. “If I’m one on one with the guys, I expect to make the tackle. Yeah, we want more guys around the ball, but if I happen to be the only guy around the ball, I for sure have to make the tackle.”
Missed tackles has been an ongoing theme since Golden took over as defensive coordinator last year.
SportRadar had Battle with 21 missed tackles last season, third most in the league behind then-teammate Geno Stone (26) and Colts linebacker Zaire Franklin (23).
To show how subjective a stat such as missed tackles can be, ProFootballFocus had Battle with 17 missed tackles last year, which was tied for 23rd in the league.
This season, the two stat sites are more aligned, as both show Battle with five. That ranks tied for ninth on SportRadar and 18th on PFF.
Battle offered his theory on why he has struggled with missed tackles.
“I feel like sometimes I just tend to just go full speed,  don't break down, just try to run through a guy,” he said. “Later on that drive, I did a better job of coming to, gathering and then getting them on the ground.
“So I gotta work on controlling my speed and just work on getting to a gather and just finish a guy and try to be chest to chest,” he added.
Bengals head coach Zac Taylor also came to Battle’s defense earlier in week.
Taylor wasn’t taking issue with the validity of the missed tackle numbers. He just said he feels as though Battle is making a lot of good plays that are overshadowed because the glare is so bright on the misses.
“I think there’s a lot of great examples of Jordan Battle tackling,” he said. “The (third-and-18) one coming out of the post is the one we got to get on the ground. There are a bunch of other examples where he does come out of the post and get people down with some tough tackles on the sidelines.
“He has to be a standard setter for us in that way,” Taylor added. “It’s a disappointing one for us, the one that got out. But there are some great examples of him doing an excellent job of it.”
Battle suffered a hamstring injury in the Week 3 game at Pittsburgh and has fighting through it given the state of the safety room with fellow safety Bryan Cook dealing with an ankle injury that forced him to miss the Jacksonville game and might keep him out Sunday against Miami as well.
“It was fine,” Battle said of his hamstring. “The second half got a little tight, but it was nothing I couldn’t play through.
“I feel much better right now,” he added. “It’s definitely loosened up, and I feel ready to go.”
The Bengals listed Battle as limited on Wednesday’s injury report, but he was a full participant Thursday.
While Battle doesn’t read the social media comments about his tackling, he does get hear repeated questions about from reporters. And he said he’s fine with that.
“I'm not gonna say it gets annoying because it's what we expect,” he said. “Playing the game of football, we gotta give you guys the answer. You guys are gonna ask the questions, and that’s fine with us. We signed up for this.
“Go out there and be better on the field and make tackles, and we can avoid those questions.”

title: Key Bengals Pieces Return to Practice on Thursday Ahead of Dolphins Road Matchup
full_text:
The Bengals got two huge pieces back on the practice field Thursday afternoon as they keep tuning up for the road action against Miami this weekend.
Multiple local media members shot footage of wide receiver Ja'Marr Chase (concussion) and safety Bryan Cook (ankle) in full pads headed out to practice.
The two can be expected limiteds at practice today; their statuses will be released around 4:15 p.m. ET. Cook is fighting through a lower-body issue, while Chase's injury is much more fickle.
It's very rare to see a player suffer a concussion in a Sunday game and play the following Sunday, but if he passes all the tests, he is good to go.
This is the first concussion Chase has ever suffered in the NFL. He has to meet the guidelines laid out below to return to the field.
"Every NFL player diagnosed with a concussion must follow a five-step process before being cleared to fully practice or participate in an NFL game," The NFL rule states. "This process, developed from internationally accepted guidelines, ensures that each player receives consistent treatment.
"Each player and each concussion is unique, and there is no set time frame for return to participation. Team medical staff consider the player's current concussive injury, as well as past exposures and medical history, family history, and future risk in managing a player's care. After a player has progressed through the five-step process and is cleared for full participation by his club physician, he must be seen and separately cleared by an Independent Neurological Consultant (INC), jointly approved by the NFL and NFLPA, who is not affiliated with any NFL club. Until cleared by this independent physician, a player may not return to contact practice or play in an NFL game."
Cincinnati has a few more injured names who did not suit up fully for practice, including Tee Higgins, who looks like a very long shot to play on Sunday as of now, but the positive signs are there for at least a couple of Cincinnati stars getting healthier.
Higgins was on the rehab field but did not work out in full pads.

title: Referee Report: Sunday's White Hat for Bengals vs. Dolphins Holding Down NFL Average
full_text:
While NFL referees are throwing flags at a record pace through the first four weeks of the 2026 season, the white hat on the call for the Cincinnati Bengals vs. Miami Dolphins games on Sunday has one of the lowest counts.
Brad Rogers is in his 10th season as an NFL official and eighth as a head referee.
His first game as a referee also was Zac Taylor’s first as Cincinnati head coach, the 2019 season opener in Seattle, a 21-20 Bengals loss.
The Bengals are 3-3 with Rogers as the referee, with his most recent assignment coming in Week 14 last year in Buffalo, where the Bills won 39-34.
Rogers’ first Bengals game was the wild 37-36 win in Atlanta in 2018 when he was a field judge.
The Dolphins are 1-3 with Rogers.
Brad Rogers and his crew average 12.5 per game. Only Ron Torbert (11.5) and Alex Kemp (12.0) are averaging fewer.
Rogers averaged 13.3 last year, which was the sixth most. He also ranked sixth in 2024 (13.8) and was third in 2023 (12.4).
The league did not reward Rogers with a postseason assignment in either of the last two seasons.
His last postseason game was an AFC Wild-Card contest between the Chiefs and Dolphins in the 2023 season. That was the last time he worked a Miami game.
Rogers’ only other postseason assignment was as a field judge for an AFC Wild-Card game between the Chargers and Patriots in the 2018 season.
Here is a closer look at the other Cincinnati games Rogers has called:
Week 14, 2025: Bills 39, Bengals 34

title: Celebrating Bengals TE Drew Sample’s 100th Game and 5 Memorable TDs
full_text:
Cincinnati Bengals tight end Drew Sample will reach a milestone Sunday when he appears in his 100th game.
“Halfway to Huber,” Sample quipped earlier this week, referring to former punter Kevin Huber’s franchise record of 216.
A 2019 second-round pick, Sample will become the 82nd player in franchise history to hit the 100-game mark, tying Pacman Jones and David Fulcher at exactly 100.
The longest tenured Bengals, Sample was the second draft pick in Zac Taylor’s tenure as head coach. Wednesday, Taylor spent some time reflecting on what he has appreciated most about Sample in his eight seasons.
“Consistency. Dependability,” Taylor said. “His first combine interview with us was a 10 out of 10. You could really see what kind of person you were getting in the room. Especially early on, we wanted to build it with really smart guys that could do a lot of different things for you, and Drew has held up that part of it.
“Consistent special teams player for us over all eight years,” Taylor continued. “He’s played a really valuable role for us on offense. If you just look at the percentage of snaps he’s taken over the years it’s a high, high amount. He’s done a lot of different jobs for us whether it is play tight end, play running back, been a focal point on the punt team over eight years.”
Sample has played 1,095 special teams snaps. Since the the NFL started tracking snap counts in 2013, that ranks eighth among Bengals players behind Shawn Williams (1,673), Clayton Fejedelem (1,454), Vincent Rey (1,394), Kevin Huber (1,370), Akeem Davis-Gaither (1,341), Clark Harris (1,295) and Jordan Evans (1,182).
Offensively, Sample’s statistics are sparse, with 119 receptions for 855 yards and five touchdowns.
The longest reception of Sample’s career came last year in Miami, a 27-yarder.
His longest touchdown was a 22-yarder against Buffalo on Sunday Night Football in 2023, which Taylor referenced in an impressive display of recall after being asked about Sample.
“You look back over 100 games, his touchdown receptions, there’s the story for you,” Taylor said. “What have his touchdown receptions been? None of them we ever thought we would score a touchdown on.
“One was against Buffalo in a seven-man protection where he leaked out and scored on a Sunday night,” Taylor added.
Drew Sample was +1200 to score a touchdown tonight 👀 pic.twitter.com/rw00TTK0RR
That pass from Joe Burrow, who has only thrown two of Sample’s five touchdowns.
Burrow referenced that Buffalo play as well during his Wednesday news conference.
“He was in the protection, a full slide seven-man protection and catching the ball somehow on a scramble drill,” Burrow said. “I think that’s really a microcosm of the evolution of Drew. That’s what we’re going to ask him to do, and everybody knows it. We’re going to put him in to be really good in protection, but when things break down, I think he’s gotten so much better at the second part of a play, understanding spaces and where I’m expecting guys to be in those scramble drills and making himself available.”
Sample’s first career touchdown came in 2020 at Houston, on a pass from Brandon Allen.
“His first one was on lizard against Houston in 2020,” Taylor said. “I think that was the last time we ever ran that play, he ran a flat route for a touchdown. There is your story, 100 games, all the different ways he’s touched the ball for us in the passing game.”
Sample’s most recent score came in last year’s blowout loss at Minnesota, on a pass from Jake Browning.
“One when he was in full-time protection, in 58 protection, home game (against the Raiders),” Taylor said.
What a tremendous touchdown pass from Joe Burrow to Drew Sample. It’s the 3rd of the day for Burrow and 1st of the season for Sample. Burrow has been tremendous today playing outside of the pocket and making the most of what the Raiders allow. pic.twitter.com/i9FyooOe9o
The other was in 2023, a home loss to the Steelers.
JAKE FIESTY TO DREW SAMPLE FOR THE TOUCHDOWN 🔥 #WHODEY pic.twitter.com/5PeMP4hcnl
“You can count on him, man,” Burrow said. “As reliable as it gets. He’s going to understand his job as well as everybody else’s job and will work to coordinate and try to get everybody on the same page. He’s a very valuable piece for us.”
