title: 'Perform On His Level' - Bengals Pass-Catching Depth Aiming to Fill Star WR Absence Against Dolphins
full_text:
The Bengals have nearly a dozen key players dealing with injuries right now, including Ja'Marr Chase (concussion) and Tee Higgins (groin). It means potentially bigger roles for guys like Mike Gesicki and Colbie Young this week in a hot road contest against the Dolphins.
Young dealt with an injury last week (missed the Jaguars game) and fought through a projected longer recovery timeline to practice on Wednesday. He could be WR2 or WR3 on the depth chart depending on how Higgins progresses.
It would be stunning to see Chase get out of the concussion protocol within a week of taking the hit.
"We came off of two losses, and we really need to get that rebound. If we don't have those big guys out there, we still need to be able to perform. So, being out there, having one of the best quarterbacks, we need to be able to perform on his level," Young said to FOX 19 about the standard before highlighting his impact so far. "That's what I was hoping when I was coming into this league. I know that we got guys. It's a long season, so there was always going to be a possibility there. So I'm happy that it's coming sooner rather than later."
Gesicki has already seen his role increase, going from 21 snaps each in the opening two games, to 29 against Pittsburgh and 47 against Jacksonville.
He hasn't logged a Pro Football Focus grade higher than 63 since exploding for a 90.1 grade in Week 1 (seven catches, 78 yards, one score).
"We got a ton of talent," Gesicki noted to FOX 19. "Obviously, those two guys are two of the best in the world at what they do. So hoping that that we can get them out there. If not, we got a bunch of guys that are extremely talented and have made plays in this league, whether this is their first year and they've been rolling now, or whether it's been for a couple years and the opportunities just don't come as much. So whatever it is, whether it's the running back room, receiver room, tight ends, we got guys that are ready to have that next man up mentality if need be."
Cincinnati may not need both players to perform well to pull out a win against the 0-4 Dolphins, but it's hard to picture a loss if Young and Gesicki pop in this one.
Two very important Bengals offensive players this week as Cincinnati prepares to hit the road for a 1 p.m. ET kickoff on Sunday.
"We need to get right." 90 locker room seconds with Mike Gesicki on ending the losing and finding the right pieces if Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins can't play. pic.twitter.com/Aak7CqFnlM
"Having one of the best quarterbacks, we need to be able to perform on his level." Colbie Young on what could potentially be a big week for him. #Bengals @FOX19 pic.twitter.com/ZJMT0FOfwr

title: 'Close To Figuring Something Out' - Joe Burrow Putting In Extra Work, Evaluates 2026 Opening Quarter Performance
full_text:
Joe Burrow got his weekly press conference started about 20 minutes late today for a good reason. Cincinnati's most important player is turning over every stone he can to keep the Bengals' losing streak from continuing this weekend.
He discussed what he tries "to find" in those post-practice sessions with the media and touched on how he judges his four-game 2026 season performance so far.
"Just me trying to get better. A couple other guys stayed after as well, but I was just trying to work on my mechanics today," Burrow said before revealing a bit more through extra questions. "I felt like I was close to figuring something out, so I wanted to get a little more reps with it ... It's all feel. It's all feel. It's a results-driven business, and how the football comes out is my result."
On the self-evaluation side, Burrow noted his turnovers so far this season. He sports the 11th-most interceptions in the league, with three given to the other team.
His Pro Football Focus turnover-worth play rate is the highest it's been since his rookie year (2.2% this season, 3.2% as a rookie). He now has the third-most fourth-quarter turnovers since 2020 (25).
"Yeah, some ups and downs," Burrow said about his 2026 performance so far. "More turnovers than I would like at this point. Other than that, I think I played really good football, but obviously turnovers are a big part of the game, so I got to limit that."
Still, he's playing pretty strong football all around, ranking ninth in the league with a 69.1 QBR. That could go up even higher against Sunday's opponent.
Burrow and his teammates are not taking the 0-4 Dolphins lightly this week. Cincinnati has every reason to try and get to 3-2. According to RotoWire , no 2-3 team has reached the Super Bowl in the past 10 seasons, let alone won it.
"We certainly have a lot of respect for these guys," Burrow declared. "Your record doesn't mean too much. Four weeks into the season, there are still 13 games left to play. Know a lot can happen in those 13 games, and we have a lot of respect for their coaching staff and how they play football. So we're gonna have our work cut out for us."
Burrow now tied with Lawrence for second most 4Q turnovers since 2020. pic.twitter.com/vNnH95n758

title: Joe Burrow Clarifies Postgame Comment, Opens Up About Bengals' Under-Center Offense
full_text:
After a few days to think on it, Cincinnati Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow walked back his “we should throw it more” comment in the aftermath of Sunday’s 22-17 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars.
“I might have been a little emotional after the game,” Burrow said with a smirk.
Following the loss in which he threw 54 passes for 428 yards and the running game accounted for just 23 yards on 15 carries, Burrow was asked if the team needed to be more balanced.
“My response to that would be, ‘Let’s throw it more,’” Burrow replied.
Wednesday, Bengals play-by-play announced Dan Hoard asked Burrow to clarify whether he meant they should throw it more in that situation when the run game is struggling or throw it more in general.
“Obviously you want to have balance as an offense, and the run game wasn't good enough on Sunday, and I feel confident in myself that you put it in my hands and I'm going to make it work,” Burrow said. “Like you said, it’s very situational. When you get into a game like Sunday, and they're a really good defense, really good front seven, I felt like we were we were moving the ball pretty well in the pass game.
“I could have been better in spots to help our guys and not put our defense in bad positions with the turnovers,” he added. “But yeah, we’ve got to be more balanced going forward, and a big part of that is the run game.”
The Bengals rank 31st in rushing attempts per game with 20.8. Only Green Bay (18.3) has fewer.
They rank 31st in rushing yards per game with 74.3. Only Green Bay (58) has fewer.
And they rank 27th in yards per attempt with 3.58.
All three numbers, if they hold, will be the worst in the Zac Taylor era. The previous lows were 22.4 attempts (2024), 89.8 yards (2023) and 3.83 yards per attempt (2022).
The Bengals spent a big chunk of the offseason installing more under-center and play-action plays in an attempt to balance their pass-run differential, but thus far it has not proven to be a key to unlock a more explosive offense.
“We obviously have to be better at it,” Burrow said. “We’re still going to stick with it and keep getting reps invested in that. I think it’s very valuable, so we have to be able to do it. But we need to be better.”
A big reason why the Bengals haven’t gone under center much is that Burrow prefers to not turn his back to the defense and instead read the pre- and post-snap alignment from his position in shotgun.
That increased usage seems to be testing him as a passer as well in addition to finding footing in the run game.
But Burrow said it hasn’t been the technique as much as the ineffective run game that has affected him a passer.
“It starts with running the football,” he said. “Under-center play-actions are built off the run game. Teams have to respect the run first and foremost, so you don’t just get jet rushers off the edge.
“That just puts your offensive linemen in a bad spot when they’re trying to sell run, but the defense isn’t respecting the run and just rushing the passer,” he added. “That’s not a recipe for success, so that starts with the run.”
Given that it’s just four weeks into the new scheme, comfort level could be an issue as well.
But Burrow shot down that idea.
“I’m comfortable doing whatever is needed,” he said.

full_text:
The Bengals hit the practice field on a gorgeous Wednesday in October across Cincinnati.
All eyes are on names like Ja'Marr Chase (concussion), Tee Higgins (groin), Bryan Cook (ankle), and more as Cincinnati tries to work through a bunch of minor injuries that've hit the WR room and secondary in recent weeks.
A bunch of names went limited, a good sign that they could play on the road against one of the league's worst teams in Miami. A bunch of names also missed practice, a not-so great sign.
Check out all of the Wednesday practice statuses below:

LIMITED: Jordan Battle (hamstring), Barrett Carter (ankle), Dexter Lawrence II (wrist), Dalton Risner (knee), Colbie Young
FULL: B.J. Hill (Achilles)
Joe Burrow has been off the injury report for a few weeks now after dealing with back soreness to start the season.
He's fighting through this adversity with the team.
"Yeah, that's part of what leaders do," Burrow said about driving the mood of the team forward this week. "But at the same time, we're still very confident, and we have guys in that locker room that feel real good about who we are, where we are, and what we're going to do. Obviously the last two weeks haven't gone the way that we wanted. I was proud of us fighting back in that fourth quarter. Obviously, I'd like to get it done. We're not here for moral victories — this is the NFL. No excuses, but we've got a lot ahead of us."
Zac Taylor had a similar sentiment following another tough loss to an AFC foe.
Cincinnati can't keep dropping games in the conference if they want to achieve all of their goals this season.
"Yeah, I believe in these guys. I mean, it sucks. We had opportunities there," Taylor said about his message after the Jaguars' loss. All week, I knew that, on all three phases, this is a really well-coached team. They have talent. They're a good team. But it's disappointing that we came up short, because we had our opportunities and we didn't fully take advantage of them. And so now, we're 2-2. We've got to own that and bounce back next week."

title: Andre Szmyt Shares the Reason the Browns Special Teams Unit Has Found So Much Success
full_text:
For the past decade or so, the Cleveland Browns have been searching for a kicker to fill the shoes, literally, of legendary kicker Phil Dawson.
The 20-year-career finished his career with 215 games, 441 field goals made and 518 extra points . He also kicked over 1,200 kickoffs, marking an incredibly long and reliable career in the NFL.
Fortunately, after years of searching for the next guy to take his spot as a long-term leg in The Land, the front office may have accidentally stumbled into finding one.
In late December 2024, Andre Szmyt was signed to the Browns' practice squad. He was then signed to a future contract in early 2024, before landing on the 53-man roster for the 2025 season.
And since then, he has been the starting kicker for Cleveland , beating out Dustin Hopkins along the way.
Across the last two seasons, Szmyt has locked down a long-term spot as the Browns' go-to leg when needed. While he hasn't yet landed a big contract, mainly because the NFL isn't willing to invest in kickers, he has been incredibly reliable and consistent.
The 28-year-old is knocking through 91.4% of his field goals and 97% of his extra points, with seven makes on kicks over 50 yards.
This season , he is a perfect 100% on both marks. He also made a game-winning 56-yarder against the Pittsburgh Steelers on Thursday Night Football, marking yet another memorable moment in his young career.
When asked about what has made him so successful, he shared that the camaraderie with the special teams unit has led to him being so comfortable on the field.
"We're so close. I think that kind of camaraderie we have shows on the field. I mean, I trust those guys with everything," he said when asked about his ability to be confident when out on the field. "I know they're going to do their jobs to the absolute best, and then it kind of allows me to just go out there and play free and not just football, you know, like I know they got me outside the building, too.
"So I love those guys honestly, and I wouldn't be in the position I am without them."
Andre Szmyt opens up about his close relationship with Rex Sunahara and Corey Bojorquez, crediting their trust and camaraderie for helping him play with confidence. "We're so close. I think that kind of camaraderie we have shows on the field. I mean, I trust those guys with… pic.twitter.com/Z7L7KI3gjS
Szmy, Corey Bojorquez and Rex Sunahara have been a trio that has stood out the last few seasons, mainly due to just how consistent they have been.
Sunahara is always right on the money with his snaps, Bojorquez has averaged 40.4 yards per punt across the last five seasons, and Szmyt has done his job with the ball on the turf. That chemistry Smyt mentioned goes a long way, and it has been on full display in each of their productive roles.
While the defense and offense have both undergone plenty of changes, the unit remaining together shows just how important it is to build up a group that is so heavily bonded.
Looking to keep this momentum going and find win No. 4 on the campaign, they and the rest of the squad will return to the gridiron on Sunday, Oct. 11, for a matchup against the New York Jets. The two sides will clash at 1:00 p.m. EST.

title: Why It Works for the Browns to Trade for This Pro-Bowl Running Back
full_text:
The Cleveland Browns' fast start to the season puts them in a position to be able to add to the team at the trade deadline.
They have just over one month until the November 10 deadline to decide which areas of the team to address. The favorable schedule in the meantime may increase their urgency to improve the roster.
The Browns’ weakest area on offense has been running the football. Quinshon Judkins has received the bulk of the carries and is averaging just three yards per rush. The running attack will need to improve for the Browns to compete when the weather turns cold and games get meaningful in December.
Tony Pollard would be an intriguing option for the Browns. He currently plays for the 0-4 Tennessee Titans and is on an expiring contract. Pollard is in his age-29 season and has amassed 221 yards with 4.1 yards per carry.
The Browns would upgrade their running back room with the addition of Pollard. They are able to absorb his contract and can get him for mid-round draft picks. The Browns have four fourth-round picks in next year's draft. One of those, plus their fifth-round pick, can be intriguing for a thin Titans team.
Cleveland’s roster no longer needs to rely on mid-to-late-round picks to contribute right away and can afford to lose one of their fourth-round picks. Pollard would come in as a rental player, and if he performs well, then he can be re-signed for cheap as he would be in his age-30 season.
Splitting the carriers with Judkins would make sure each of them are fresh down the stretch. Judkins has struggled to show his burst after a season-ending surgery last year. Pollard has rushed 1,000 yards the past four seasons and is currently on pace to just be shy of the benchmark .
The addition of Pollard can help the running game get going to relieve some pressure off of Deshaun Watson. If the Browns can add a facet to their offense, then maybe they will not need to rely on game-winning drives.
Judkins is a second-year player and should get stronger as the season moves along. He showed flashes in his rookie season that he can be the main guy in the backfield to do all the heavy lifting.
Backup running back Raheim Sanders has shown that he can run the ball hard and is averaging 5.2 yards per carry in limited action. The duo bring a physicality that will not be easy to bring down in cold weather
The Browns have recently signed Jaleel McLaughlin as the team’s third running back. He played one offensive snap and took the ball 28 yards to the end zone. Reinforcements may also be on the way without giving up draft picks.
Dylan Sampson was injured in the first game on a kickoff return. The injury was deemed “significant”, but the Browns have not ruled him out for the season. Sampson could return for the Browns down the stretch and provide a speedy alternative to the power of Judkins.
Andrew Berry values mid-round picks, and now that most of the starters have shown that they deserve to start in the NFL, he can use those picks to build depth to really make the team a contender. Pollard will get a lot of interest from contending teams to bolster the backfield, and the pot could get too big for Berry to want to make the move.
Should they be active or not at the deadline, the Browns have played themselves in a position to seriously consider improving the team for this season.

title: It's Time For the Browns to Move On from This Player
full_text:
Ever since the end of his career-best 2024 season, Jerry Jeudy has not lived up to the Browns hopes.
After finishing with 90 catches, 1,299 yards, and four touchdowns, Jeudy had Browns fans believing he was the team's real number one wide receiver.
However, in the 2025 season, Jeudy's production was basically cut in half. 90 receptions went to 50, 1,229 yards dropped to 602, and four touchdowns dropped to two.
After last season, Jeudy finished second in the entire NFL in drops with 10.
Then came the 2026 NFL Draft . Cleveland used one of their two first-round picks on KC Concepcion, a receiver out of Texas.
Then, they doubled down and used their first second-round pick on Denzel Boston, another receiver out of Washington.
With two additions to the wide receiver room in the draft, it was already being hinted at by the organization that Jeudy was on his way out.
So far in the 2026 season, Jeudy's production on the field has once again decreased.
Through four games, Jeudy has only been targeted a total of eight times. Out of those, he has caught five passes for 62 yards.
As for the rookies, Boston and Concepcion have seen a combined 30 catches through 50 total targets, for 428 yards and two touchdowns.
Not only have the Browns clearly moved on from Jeudy on the depth chart, but also on the field schematically.
Let's say the Browns do actually want to move on. Who could be some teams that are interested?
The first team that comes to mind is in need of some help for their young quarterback trying to avoid "bust allegations"
Outside of Carnell Tate, the Tennessee Titans could use another receiver pretty badly.
As for a potential return, the Browns may want to look into adding a player like Tony Pollard. If not a player, they may do the deal for some late-round picks. As a reminder, the initial Jeudy trade with the Broncos only required the Browns to give up 2024 fifth- and sixth-rounders.
Would you trade Jerry Jeudy to the Titans for Tony Pollard? Bleacher Report’s Alex Kay proposed the two teams swap players to help bolster areas of weakness on each roster. "No other Browns back outside of starter Quinshon Judkins has garnered more than six carries or eclipsed… pic.twitter.com/aXaVm1VTie
In the scenario Jeudy wants to go to a contender, the Kansas City Chiefs are always looking to get more help for Patrick Mahomes.
If the Browns want Jeudy out of the AFC as a whole, a trade that has been talked about previously is a receiver swap with the Arizona Cardinals.
Marvin Harrison Jr. is having a similar 2026 season to Jeudy. With only 5 receptions for 85 yards and a touchdown, a change of scenery may be needed for the former number four overall pick.
Regardless of where the Browns receiver ends up, it's clearly time to move on.

title: Deshaun Watson Combats Any Sort of QB Room Drama with Latest Comments
full_text:
The Cleveland Browns quarterback room is facing an unfamiliar problem: they have too many players.
Dillon Gabriel was activated from the injured reserve list yesterday, giving the Browns the next 21 days to make a decision on what to do with their roster. The addition of Gabriel shakes up the room, but Deshaun Watson is not worried.
“Dillon, he’s been around this whole time. He’s been in every meeting. He’s been traveling with us. He’s been on the practice field with us. He’s been communicating, giving suggestions within the offense and different reads,” Watson said about Gabriel returning from injury.
“So DG, man, he’s a great teammate, a better person . It’s good to have him back on the field and see that he’s healthy. All of us in that room, we’re one big group, got one goal and that’s ultimately to win and be successful.”
Watson’s comments show that the team is bought into Todd Monken’s culture, and their main focus is winning. Gabriel returns as Watson is proving that he is the starting quarterback on the team. He is currently backed up by Shedeur Sanders, and Gabriel can challenge for the backup role should they put him on the roster.
Gabriel being with the team while on the injured list means that he has been involved in the installation of Monken’s offense each week. He has been praised for his ability to understand and operate the offense. If he cannot overtake Sanders for the backup role, then he can be listed as the team’s emergency third quarterback on game days.
Taylen Green has been that emergency quarterback and should Gabriel take his spot, then the Browns can activate Green to the roster and use his playmaking skills on gadget plays and short-yardage downs.
Watson has shown that he has the respect of the locker room, as the team has rallied behind him for three-straight game winning drives. They have won their three games as a complete team and the camaraderie has been palpable.
Gabriel has 21 days of practice before the Browns have to decide to promote him to the roster or keep on the injured list for the remainder of the season . Even if he is not on the roster, he has proven that he is a valuable member in the quarterback room and that he can provide positive results for the Browns without being on the field.

title: Ranking the Browns' 5 Biggest Needs Before the Trade Deadline
full_text:
The Cleveland Browns have been one of the biggest surprises of the 2026 NFL season.
Very few people imagined the Browns would be winners in three of their first four games. Even fewer expected to see Deshaun Watson play as well as he has.
With the success, the Browns can actually be buyers at the trade deadline for the first time in a number of years.
Here are five position groups that could use some help.
Over this past offseason, the Browns did a lot of work signing, trading, and drafting different players to improve the offensive line.
Despite all the effort, Cleveland still ranks near the bottom of the league in PFF offensive line rankings at 28th.
Even if the Browns don't want to spend a lot of assests to go get another starter, building the depth of the unit is always in play when Deshaun Watson is taking the snaps.
Would you trade Jerry Jeudy to the Titans for Tony Pollard? Bleacher Report’s Alex Kay proposed the two teams swap players to help bolster areas of weakness on each roster. "No other Browns back outside of starter Quinshon Judkins has garnered more than six carries or eclipsed… pic.twitter.com/aXaVm1VTie
The Browns used two top picks on KC Concepcion and Denzel Boston in the 2026 NFL Draft.
With that being said, they don't necessarily need another big name to come in. Rather, a better term to use would be a makeover.
Cleveland clearly has their next stars in Concepcion and Boston, so trading a guy like Jerry Jeudy makes too much sense.
As for additions following a Jeudy trade, they could look to sign a veteran receiver who helps develop the young talent.
So far this season, Carson Schwesinger and Quincy Williams have already proved to be a great duo on the Browns defense.
Outside of them, Easton Mascarenas-Arnold has proved he can hold his own, but behind him is where the depth gets very weak.
It does not need to be a star linebacker, but if Cleveland can get some depth for cheap, they should absolutely look into it
The only reason why the defensive line is so high on this list is due to the recent Mason Graham injury.
While the Browns were able to sack Aaron Rodgers five times against the Steelers without their sack leader, extra help would always be nice.
Very similarly to the linebackers, you do not need a star. However, adding someone to take the weight off Jared Verse's shoulders sounds very nice.
By far, the cornerback room is the biggest place of need for the Browns.
Outside of Denzel Ward and Tyson Campbell who has been fighting injury, the Browns have had to rely on Myles Harden a lot.
In week four, the Steelers made it a focal point to target Harden who at times got stuck covering DK Metcalf.
By the end of the game, Pittsburgh targeted Harden a total of seven times. In those attempts, the Steelers were able to generate 4 catches for 117 yards and a touchdown.
If there's a position where the Browns should potentially go after a star, it's the cornerback.

title: Browns Hit With Brutal Injury News as 3 Defensive Linemen Miss Practice
full_text:
The Cleveland Browns are trying to get healthy.
And unfortunately, it seems like week by week, more bodies continue to be added to the injury report.
On Wednesday, Oct. 7, the Browns' Week 5 injury report was released with a few days to go until the team travels to New York for an outing against the Jets. While there were many expected players on the injury report, including defensive tackle Mason Graham, others appeared on it that raised some eyebrows.
Here are the standouts from the most recent injury report from the Browns:
The Browns' 27-24 victory over the Pittsburgh Steelers on Thursday, Oct. 1, a good ol' fashioned TNF rivalry matchup, was hard-fought. Countless members of the defensive unit were banged up throughout the contest, with many of their injuries carrying into this week.
Hall Jr. went down after Graham did, suffering a lower-body injury that would eventually be classified as a right-ankle injury.
He sustained the injury in the first half, being blocked by a member of the Steelers' offensive line into teammate Jared Verse. With how the night was going, it was a miracle Verse didn't get rolled up on and injured.
Hall Jr. has not practiced since the injury, taking time to get himself back up to full health.
Alongside Hall Jr., Cleveland obviously was without Graham, who is currently working to get back up to speed from an MCL and ankle sprain in his left leg. He's not the other unexpected standout on the injury report; edge rusher Derek Barnett is.
#Browns @ #Jets Wednesday injury report pic.twitter.com/02yKd7T7Gz
He is reportedly dealing with an ankle injury as well.
All three did not practice Wednesday.
The Browns' depth at the position is already incredibly weak, and having three linemen out is going to be taxing for the rest of the squad.
The Browns have been lucky to have most of the offense healthy this season, minus the offensive line.
Once again, Elgton Jenkins and Teven Jenkins have ended up on the injury report. Elgton Jenkins, who was dealing with a concussion, is back and practicing, though, just a week after missing the Steelers game due to a concussion. Teven Jenkins, on the other hand, has missed the entire regular season due to a back injury.
He has still not returned and did not practice Wednesday.
Quarterback Dillon Gabriel is still on the injured list and is cleared to return; however, a roster spot has not been cleared just yet. He did participate in practice, while wideout Tylan Wallace did not due to a knee injury. He is in a difficult spot, especially since he is not really a must-have on the roster, as the front office continues to shuffle around the practice squad with more wideouts and special teamers.
Lastly, Cleveland's injury report featured two players who were limited.
Safety Grant Delpit, who has been dealing with a shoulder injury since practically the beginning of the season, was limited in practice, and defensive tackle Kalia Davis was as well. He was in the same boat as Gabriel, having just been activated from the injured list.
Davis will have to get a roster spot cleared for him before he can play, but Delpit should be good to go by Sunday.
The Browns and Jets collide from MetLife Stadium on Sunday, Oct. 11 , with kickoff slated for 1:00 p.m. EST.

title: 5 Browns Who Could Be Playing Their Way Onto the Trade Block
full_text:
As we enter week five of the NFL Season, the trade deadline is just about a month away.
The cutoff time for teams to make moves is November 10th, 2026, at 4 p.m. ET
Here are five names that could be on the move in the near future.
So far this season, Teven Jenkins has yet to see the field as he is dealing with a back injury.
In 2025, Jenkins finished as one of the NFL's best run-blocking guards. For the Browns, they made a plethora of moves on the offensive line this offseason in free agency and the NFL Draft, so they may want to focus on their young core.
While the injury makes trading him a bit trickier, there could be a team like the Green Bay Packers who want to improve their run game.
Since the Browns drafted "Big Thanos" in the fourth round of the 2023 NFL Draft, there has been one big problem with the former Ohio State Buckeye: injuries.
When Jones has actually seen the field, his gigantic frame has played a great benefit for the Browns' run game.
Similar to Jenkins, maybe there is a team that wants to send a late-round pick and take a flyer on the 6'8" 370lbs lineman.
"A contender could trade for Jerry Jeudy.. The Cleveland Browns have Denzel Boston and KC Concepcion" ~ @AdamSchefter #PMSLive pic.twitter.com/7rZW6E7rZy
After taking two receivers early in the 2026 NFL Draft, it has been very clear that Jerry Jeudy is nearing the end of his Browns tenure.
Since the 2024 season where Jeudy finished with over 1,200 yards, his production has simply fallen off a cliff.
So far in 2026, he has only five catches through four games.
While the trade value may not be incredibly high, the Browns only spent a 2024 fifth- and sixth-round pick to get the former first-rounder.
Maybe there's a team like the Tennessee Titans that could use another man in the receiver room.
This one is a bit of a hot take, but it actually may not be the most surprising trade the Browns could make.
Yes, Ronnie Hickman is only 24 years old, but he currently ranks near the bottom of all NFL safeties in the 2026 season according to PFF.
Especially with the addition of Emmanuel McNeil-Warren in this past year's draft, Hickman's starting job is on the line.
For the Browns organization, they brought Hickman in as an undrafted free agent in 2023. Therefore, any return you get is a positive gain.
While the fans may not want to see the former Buckeye leave, if a team wants to send valuable capital it will be hard for the Browns to say no.
Do the Browns NEED to get rid of a QB now that Dillon Gabriel has been activated from IR? pic.twitter.com/8c9vsQBcMQ
Potentially the biggest Brown who has flown under the radar this season is Dillon Gabriel.
In the final preseason game this year against the Patriots, Gabriel put on a clinic. In the game, he completed 12 out of 15 passes for 187 yards and 3 touchdowns.
After that game, Gabriel was placed on IR with a back injury but is expected to return soon. The big question now is whether the Browns roster four quarterbacks.
If they decide to only keep three, Gabriel stands out like a sore thumb as every other option has publicly received praise from head coach Todd Monken.
As more quarterback injuries occur around the league, there is a high chance a team makes a call for the former Heisman candidate.

title: Browns Rookie Receives High Praise from Superstar Receiver
full_text:
After the week four Thursday Night Football matchup where the Cleveland Browns defeated the Pittsburgh Steelers , one of Pittsburgh's best players highlighted a Browns rookie.
Denzel Boston grew up in South Hill, Washington, which is about an hour away from Seattle.
Naturally, Boston grew up supporting his hometown team, the Seattle Seahawks.
After Thursday Night's game, former Seahawk and now Pittsburgh Steeler DK Metcalf gave praise to the rookie.
Metcalf went on to tell Boston that he was "a fan of his game", to which Boston smiled as he grew up watching Metcalf torch defenses in Seattle.
Browns rookie WR Denzel Boston said Steelers WR DK Metcalf told him after their teams faced off that he was a fan of his game. It was a cool moment for Boston, who grew up a Seahawks fan. pic.twitter.com/LQ8wvLdtVo
Coming out of the University of Washington, Boston was scouted similarly to Metcalf.
Many analysts commented on the size comparison. For Boston, he stands at 6'4", 215 lbs. For Metcalf, he stands at the same height but weighs about 20 pounds more.
While Boston did not compete in the 40-yard dash at the NFL Combine or a Washington Pro Day before entering the league, he showed his playmaking ability and breakaway speed in week two against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.
On the field, Metcalf is looked at as a serious deep threat receiver, who will most likely win one on one coverages given a decent ball. Many defenses have grown to be scared of playing him.
For Boston, so far through four games of his career, he has been more of a safety net for Deshaun Watson. Despite this, he has still made some remarkable plays.
As of now, the sky is the limit for Denzel Boston. In his first four games, he has 13 receptions for 284 yards and two touchdowns.
In many people's eyes, he is being looked at as the favorite to win the 2026 offensive rookie of the year award.
But fans are also forgetting about another man.
With the emergence of Denzel Boston, some are forgetting that Cleveland also spent one of their first-round picks on KC Concepcion .
With Boston potentially becoming the team's deep threat, Concepcion gets to play the role of quick slant, shifty, and slot wide receiver.
By having both young receivers available, Boston and Concepcion are poised to make defenses crazy having to try and defend either guy.
Regardless, after years of bouncing between Jarvis Landry, Odell Beckham Jr, Amari Cooper, and Jerry Jeudy, it looks like the Browns are finally going to have some stability in the receiver room going forward.
The future is bright for the Cleveland Browns.

title: Predicting Where Browns QB Dillon Gabriel Ends Up By the End of the Season
full_text:
For the Cleveland Browns, the quarterback position has stayed level for the first four weeks of the season, as Deshaun Watson has led the team to a 3-1 record. Shedeur Sanders remains the backup, while rookie Taylen Green sits behind him.
Yesterday, the Browns designated second-year QB Dillon Gabriel to return to practice after he suffered a back injury in the final preseason game vs. the Patriots. Gabriel now has a 21-day practice window, during which Cleveland can activate him at any time.
Cleveland will most likely slide Gabriel into the QB3 spot behind Watson and Sanders, but if they don't activate him in those 21 days, he will either be cut or remain in the IR spot for the whole season.
Gabriel was the 94th overall pick in the 2025 Draft; many Browns fans questioned the pick at the time given when he was taken and the plan for him. In Gabriel’s defense, he started 10 games last year, playing solid football for a backup. His completion percentage being below 60% and yards per attempt at just 5.1 put him among the lowest in the league.
So what should the plan be for a player like Gabriel? We know he can be a solid backup at any place, but his ceiling as a player seems limited; his future will most likely be on another team.
We have unfortunately see n countless starting quarterbacks go down with injury in just the first four weeks of the NFL season (Jayden Daniels, Jaxson Dart, Sam Darnold, Caleb Williams, and Kyler Murray, to name a few), so there will always be a market for a backup in the modern NFL.
If Cleveland was able to get any draft compensation for Gabriel, I think they will take it; we have already seen the Vikings trade away former first-rounder JJ McCarthy for just a fifth-rounder. The Atlanta Falcons were the favorite pick for Gabriel to land, as they are coached by former Browns coach Kevin Stefanski and have kept their lefties (Penix & Tagovailoa) as their starter and backup.
The Falcons would be the most reasonable team for Gabriel, but other teams that do not have an established guy at backup could make a move for him. That includes teams like the Jets, Buccaneers, Jaguars, or Dolphins, who have either rookies or players with no experience starting in their backup position.
The future of Dillon Gabriel does not look to be in Cleveland, and the decision of keeping him or not may come sooner rather than later.

title: Browns Have 2 Under-the-Radar Trade Targets Who Could Transform Their Defensive Line
full_text:
The Cleveland Browns are a good football team. There's no questioning that.
Through the first four weeks of the 2026 NFL regular season, the Browns sit with an overall record of 3-1, placing them first in the AFC North.
But even with such success, there are improvements to be made, especially if the team wants to realistically make a run by the time the playoffs roll around.
With defensive tackle Mason Graham injured, young superstar Jared Verse still attempting to get his feet underneath himself and the rest of the line being relatively unknown in the long-term reliability department, making a move to land one more big man up front should be on the Browns' radar.
Here are two rushers the front office should target who can help boost the Browns' defensive unit:
A fifth-overall selection in the 2022 NFL Draft, Kayvon Thibodeaux's development path hasn't quite panned out the way the New York Giants had hoped it would.
While he isn't a bad player, not by any means, he hasn't replicated the success he found back in 2023, when he recorded a career-high 11.5 sacks. Since then, though, he has totaled just eight across the last three seasons.
And just last offseason, the team added a young, high-upside piece to the defensive line by taking edge rusher Abdul Carter with the No. 3 overall selection.
With the Giants continuing to struggle to find wins, all while the defense continues to get younger, moving Thibodeaux could be a good way for the team to land some extra draft capital and maybe a mid-level contributor.
When the Browns traded Za'Darius Smith back in 2024, they landed a fifth- and sixth-round pick. When the Steelers recently traded defensive back Joey Porter Jr., they received a sixth- and second-round pick.
That makes the market easier to understand for the Browns.
If they send New York a 2027 third-round pick and a 2027 fourth-round pick, which they have three of as of now , they could get the deal done. Not only does this give the Giants more opportunities to continue the youth movement this offseason, but it also lands them something for a player who will likely seek a new contract with a different team at the end of the season.
The only issue Cleveland will run into when discussing a move for Thibodeaux is the Giants' lack of starting potential at the position with Brian Burns out for the season.
So, to make this happen, the Browns will have to bring something convincing to the table, or toss in one of Sam Williams or Derek Barnett .
Back in the 2018 NFL Draft, Payne went 13th overall.
And since then, he has been quietly one of the league's best defensive tackles.
Across the last nine seasons, he has totaled 440 tackles, 37 sacks, 65 tackles for a loss, 84 quarterback hits and seven forced fumbles. Routinely forcing his way into the backfield, Payne is still a highly sought-after 29-year-old.
With the Washington Commanders at the bottom of the NFC East, holding a 1-3 record, changes are going to be made as the team prepares to retool at the deadline and into the offseason. Payne, who is an unrestricted free agent in 2027, is likely on the chopping block and looking for a long-term extension with a new squad.
Pairing Payne with second-year defensive tackle Mason Graham could be a perfect opportunity for the Browns, especially if they can give him an extension this offseason with Deshaun Watson's contract relatively off the books.
Payne could also slide into the No. 1 spot if Graham's injury is more long-term than the team initially thought. Fortunately, that isn't something you'd have to worry about with Payne, as he has only missed three games across the last nine years.
So, what about landing him ? What would that cost?
Again, the market is somewhat all over the place, but with what the Steelers got in return for Porter Jr., a player like Payne would warrant something similar.
If the Browns threw a 2027 fourth-rounder and a 2028 second-rounder the way of the Commanders, there should be no reason for them to pass on the offer.
The Browns should be buyers as the 2026 NFL Trade Deadline approaches, and if Payne ends up on an offer sheet, they should be willing to spend a bit to land him.

title: CeeDee Lamb, Tyler Guyton Injury Updates Highlight Cowboys Week 5 Roundup
full_text:
The Dallas Cowboys suffered a horrendous setback in Week 5 of the NFL season, falling to the previously winless Tampa Bay Buccaneers under the bright lights of Thursday Night Football.
It was a brutal all-around performance for Dallas, and it started hours before the game even began with the loss of Joey Porter Jr ., who was ruled out of Thursday night's game after showing up to AT&T Stadium and falling ill.
Porter was sent home from the stadium because of his illness , and then the team went on to put up their worst performance of the year. It was a failure in all three stages of the game, but the injuries also continued to pile up, which could have a longer-term impact on the Cowboys as they aim to bounce back.
Among the injured Cowboys on Thursday night were star wide receiver CeeDee Lamb and left tackle Tyler Guyton, while defensive backs Shevon Revel and Alijah Clark also went down.
The latest on what we know about the team's high-profile injuries can be seen below.
Lamb would be the biggest loss for the Cowboys, after his incredible start to the 2026-27 campaign. He entered the game leading the league in receptions and receiving yards, but finished the game with just two catches for nine yards.
According to ESPN's Todd Archer, Lamb suffered from tightness in his quadriceps for the second straight game, which led to the star pass catcher going in and out of the lineup during the crucial stretch of the game.
Hopefully the extra days of rest following Thursday night's game will allow him to get back to full strength.
Guyton, meanwhile, suffered a back injury that knocked him out of the game. He was replaced by the recently acquired Broderick Jones and will continue to undergo testing on Friday. While an X-ray on Thursday night showed positive news , he is not completely out of the woods yet.
It's unfortunate to see Guyton, who has struggled with injuries throughout his career, suffer another setback after a strong start to his season.
On the defensive side of the ball, Revel started the game but also suffered what appeared to be a leg injury late. There has been no official update on his status. Along with the injury, he struggled with inconsistencies in his play, including a brutal defensive pass interference that awarded Tampa Bay a first down on 3rd-and-13. Later in the game, he was called for illegal contact that again extended a Bucs drive.
Backup safety Alijah Clark also suffered an injury during the game, going down with a hamstring injury. We'll have to see how the players bounce back and what further testing reveals on Friday morning and afternoon, but for the sake of the Cowboys, let's hope there was nothing too severe that will further impact the team's depth moving forward.

title: Dak Prescott Stares Down Employee Who Calls Out 'Embarrassing' Cowboys Loss
full_text:
The Dallas Cowboys couldn't have picked a worse time to put up their worst performance of the season than on Thursday night, with the entire NFL world watching in primetime as the winless Tampa Bay Buccaneers stormed into town .
Everyone, including the oddsmakers, expected the Cowboys to make easy work of the Buccaneers , who were without star quarterback Baker Mayfield.
Instead, undrafted free agent rookie Jalon Daniels came in and dominated the Cowboys' defense, which reverted to its putrid form after showing some positive signs during the team's win in Week 4.
After the game, a video went viral of Dak Prescott walking back to Dallas' locker room following the loss. In the middle of the tunnel, Prescott can be seen stopping dead in his tracks and staring down someone off camera who could be heard yelling out "embarrassing" as the team left the field.
Here’s our angle of a worker — either stadium employee or valet car driver — calling out Dak Prescott and the Cowboys performance, with Dak’s reaction which he said was prompted by the man looking away after saying the criticisms. #dallascowboys #nfl pic.twitter.com/ffznCyahvv
Sam Gannon of KDFW-FOX 4 initially shared the video with the caption, "An employee inside AT&T Stadium said 'embarrassing' after that Cowboys loss. Dak looking back to see who it was."
She added, "Catastrophic loss for the Cowboys. Employees inside the stadium chiming in too."
Shortly after the video went viral, there was clarification about the off-camera person who shouted at the team. "I'm told the person that said 'embarrassing' to Dak was a car service driver , not a stadium employee," Gannon added.
Prescott addressed the confrontation after the game, saying: "When he said it, I just happened to look at him at that point and he looked away, and then I turned my head back, and he said something else. That’s the part, just as a man of a person, feel free to speak your mind. Just speak it. Don’t cower away from the reaction you’re going to get .”
Dak Prescott sounded frustrated that someone yelled “embarrassing” to him as he was walking back to the locker room. Some reporters said it was a stadium employee pic.twitter.com/JxgQGJSwuP
Whoever the person was, they were right. Everyone in the Cowboys organization, from top to bottom, was embarrassed by the team's effort, and there will need to be some major changes to get back on track. It was one thing to lose in heart-breaking fashion against the Baltimore Ravens in Brazil, but to not show up at home against a winless team is inexcusable.
Dallas continues to shoot itself in the foot, and the Cowboys' defense continues to be among the worse in the league. If Brian Schottenheimer, Christian Parker, and the entire coaching staff cannot get things in order, there is no amount of blockbuster trades that can help the team.
Let's just hope that the team can use the extra three days away from the field to do some real soul-searching and figure out what changes needs to be the immediate priority ahead of Week 6.

title: Biggest Takeaways From Cowboys' Pathetic Week 5 Loss to Buccaneers
full_text:
On Thursday, we warned of this being a classic trap game for the Dallas Cowboys and unfortunately it turned out to be just that, as the Cowboys lost to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers 24-16 in Week 5.
The Cowboys were heavily favored over the Bucs , who were 0-4 and starting an undrafted rookie quarterback. But the Cowboys looked like the winless team and failed in every way imaginable against Tampa Bay.
Dallas certainly looked the part of a team that was not only tired after three games in 12 days, but unprepared, too. But don't get it twisted: we're not letting Dallas off the hook because of that, There is just no excuse for how the Cowboys played.
With the Cowboys falling to 2-3 on the season after one of the more hideous performances you will ever see, here are the biggest takeaways.
The Cowboys needed to stop the run and force an undrafted rookie quarterback to beat them. Well, they failed at that.
Dallas was allergic to setting the edge, as we saw on the Emeka Egbuka touchdown run, and the defense wasn't much better up the middle, either.
A 72-yard Bucky Irving run that set up Tampa Bay's second score of the game should've never happened, but the Cowboys simply couldn't get off blocks and take the Bucs' running back down.
The Cowboys weren't much better in pass defense. DaRon Bland fell and allowed Tez Johnson to rip off a 64-yard catch that set up Tampa's third touchdown of the night, and he slipped again on a play later in the quarter and gave up a first down on a third-and-21, which led to Tampa eventually scoring on a field goal.
We saw more of the same issues in the pass-rush, also, which was able to get some pressure but again couldn't finish with sacks , the tackling was terrible and the Cowboys had multiple self-inflicted wounds with penalties to help Tampa Bay extend drives.
Talent is a problem, but Christian Parker has no answers to get this group back on track. This defense is completely lost in every aspect and there is no hope things are going to get better.
The Cowboys came out firing and made it look easy on the opening drive, but it was all downhill from there.
Dak Prescott was very off and the Cowboys had no answers for the heat Todd Bowles was bringing with the blitz and the offensive line didn't hold up good enough.
Running behind Tyler Smith worked early, but that eventually stopped and Dallas once again couldn't run the football.
Head coach Brian Schottenheimer admitted at halftime that he was not doing a good enough job calling the plays, especially when it comes to adjusting for the blitz, and he was right.
“I gotta call better plays, No. 1," Schotty said. "We’ll make some good adjustments right here, but it’s gotta start with me calling better plays.”
Schottenheimer should be out of a job at this point, but we won't hold our breath for that. It's definitely time to let Klayton Adams take over play-calling duties just to try something different because Schottenheimer has stunk all season long.
The Cowboys have been abysmal on special teams this season and that continued on Thursday night.
With very little margin for error with the Cowboys trailing by 11 in the third quarter, KaVontae Turpin coughed up the football on a kickoff return and the Bucs ended up turning it into points.
You just cannot make this up.
Jerry Jones said this week that he isn't as concerned about Bland as fans are. He and the Cowboys' coaching staff need to wake up and meet the concern level fans have.
We already went over the two egregious blunders he had to allow big completions in the third quarter, blunders this putrid defense can ill-afford with how poorly it is playing overall.
Bland had an opportunity to redeem himself with a gift-wrapped pick-six in the fourth quarter, but, of course, he dropped it.
The Cowboys simply cannot continue running Bland out there on a weekly basis because he is not a starting cornerback. Hopefully Cobie Durant comes back next week. Even if he doesn't, the Cowboys need to try someone else on the boundary.

title: CeeDee Lamb Injury Update: Latest on Cowboys WR After Leaving Week 5 Game
full_text:
CeeDee Lamb was on the verge of history entering the Dallas Cowboys' Week 5 game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers . He recorded 189 yards and a touchdown on 17 receptions against the Houston Texans and was close to becoming just the third player in team history to have 500 yards and five touchdowns in the first five games of the season.
It appears that won't happen as Lamb struggled mightily against the Bucs, recording two receptions for nine yards before being sidelined with a quad injury.
With Dallas trailing 24-10, the offense took the field, but Lamb was not out there. It was reported that he was questionable to return .
Lamb watched as the Cowboys moved the ball 99 yards, with George Pickens recording a 17-yard touchdown to make it 24-16. Dallas then attempted a two-point conversion and failed, which honestly sums up their night.
Injuries have been the theme for the Cowboys all season, and they suffered a loss right before this game began. Cornerback Joey Porter Jr., who was added in a trade last week, was sidelined due to an illness.
Other players to go down during this one include safety Alijah Clark, who has a hamstring injury and is questionable. Pickens was also banged up on the 99-yard drive, as he went to the sideline to have his shoulder checked out.
On the ensuing defensive drive, rookie linebacker Jaishawn Barham was banged up and had to head to the sideline to be checked out as well. Also out is Tyler Guyton, the starting left tackle, who has been dominant this season. Broderick Jones was brought in to replace Guyton as he deals with a back injury.
The Cowboys had some good news on the injury front before kickoff, as they were able to get Tyler Smith back. The All-Pro left guard had thumb surgery before Week 1 and missed the first four games of the season.
Smith was back in the starting lineup and was impressive on the opening drive, opening holes for Javonte Williams. Since that drive, however, the Cowboys have been forced to throw the ball as they Bucs have been putting the clamps on the ground game.

title: Cowboys Booed Off Field Amid Shameful Third-Quarter Performance vs Bucs
full_text:
The Dallas Cowboys are hitting a new low as a franchise.
Dallas entered the fourth quarter of Thursday night's matchup at home against the winless Tampa Bay Buccaneers trailing 24-10.
As a result, the boos started to rain down from the frustrated fans at AT&T Stadium.
And no one should blame them.
Halloween has come early in Arlington.
There doesn't need to be much analysis for why the Cowboys were an embarrassment in the second half. All you need to do is take a look at the third quarter drive chart.
- Bucs 2-play, 86-yard TD drive - Dak Prescott INT - Bucs 5-play, 85-yard TD drive - KaVontae Turpin fumbles on kickoff - Bucs field goal Aug. 30 - at Ohio State Buckeyes - Cowboys turnover on downs after Prescott misses Jake Ferguson
Jerry Jones' reaction from his suite says it all.
pic.twitter.com/aoa7UHyRy9
The Cowboys defense somehow looks worse than last season. Who would've thought?
Buccaneers undrafted rookie quarterback Jalon Daniels looks like a seasoned veteran against Christian Parker's "scheme." Daniels certainly deserves credit for playing well but it's hard to imagine him playing this well again as Tampa Bay continues through the season with Baker Mayfield still sidelined.
But if the defense isn't giving up a big play down the field or on the ground, they're giving up first downs via penalty.
After a disasterous third quarter, the penalty issues continued on the first play of the fourth quarter. Tampa Bay was faced with a 3rd and 13, a chance for Dallas to get its offense back on the field, but Cowboys cornerback Shavon Revel Jr. was called for pass interference to extend the drive.
Dallas fans have grown accustomed to watching the offense carry the load while the defense struggles, but Dak Prescott and the Cowboys offense were nearly as bad as the defense.
Despite falling behind to begin the second half, the Cowboys had a chance to get back into with an answer of their own, but Prescott continued to miss routine throws and looked shaken by the Tampa Bay defense.
Headed into the third quarter, he was 13 of 28 passing for 166 yards, no touchdowns and an interception. Despite all of Prescott's own miscues, he doesn't deserve much blame for the interception that happened after a pass bounced off Ryan Flournoy's hands and into the air.
Still, there's no question that Daniels was outplaying Prescott after three quarters.

title: Richard Sherman Recklessly Questions If Joey Porter Jr. Illness Is Contract Related
full_text:
Just ahead of the Dallas Cowboys Thursday Night Football showdown with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, they received some unfortunate news. Cornerback Joey Porter Jr., who was added in a trade with the Pittsburgh Steelers last week, was a late scratch .
Porter was sent home with the team, saying he was "very sick," but not everyone believes the illness is legitimate. Despite seeing Porter looking ill and walking with a staff member who was carrying a trash can for Porter, Richard Sherman said this could be contract-related.
While speaking on the Prime pregame show, Sherman was asked what type of player Porter would bring to the Dallas defense. He was complimentary of the defensive back, but couldn't help but dive into the contract situation, saying Porter might not be sick if the Cowboys gave him a new deal.
"Well, you can expect one of the best players in the National Football League. He played the corner position, hasn't given up a touchdown in man coverage since 2023. I think they can build a really cool defense around him. I think, you know, maybe if they would have gave him a new contract, maybe he would have been a little healthier today."
“I think if they gave him a new contract, maybe he would have been a little healthier today.” Richard Sherman implying Joey Porter isn't playing tonight because he hasn't received a new contract. pic.twitter.com/7zrKOtLb1L
Sherman's comments come with no basis other than pure speculation, and he admitted he was speculating. Still, it's rather reckless to just throw out an accusation. Sherman also couldn't help himself from continuing to bring up Porter's lack of an extension even after the panel reminded him not to speculate.
"Everything developed really quickly. It's unfortunate. I thought he played well last week in the 25 snaps that he played. He didn't get targeted. He's a good player. He will definitely elevate this defense and help them become better. But I think there's going to be some decisions made with the contract that helps him move forward."
Porter was added for a second-round pick in 2028 and a sixth-rounder in 2027. The former second-round pick has emerged as one of the top man-coverage corners in the NFL and did well in his debut with the Cowboys, despite limited practice time.
He was unhappy with his contract situation with the Steelers and sat out the first three weeks, citing back pain. That pain healed quickly once he was in Dallas , but Porter said he planned on playing this season without an extension.
Sherman isn't buying that, however.

title: Joey Porter Jr. 'Sent Home' By Cowboys Before Being Declared NFL Week 5 Inactive
full_text:
Joey Porter Jr. was set to make his debut at AT&T Stadium as a member of the Dallas Cowboys on Thursday Night Football against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers .
A few hours before kickoff, Porter pulled up to the stadium and appeared to be ready to go despite a short turnaround for Dallas.
Porter Jr. made his debut on Sunday night on a pitch count , but was expected to see a slightly increased role on Thursday. That's when some shocking news was announced, and Porter was among the Cowboys' list of inactives due to an "illness."
Now, NFL insider Jane Slater is revealing more details about Porter's health after the sudden change in status, after he did not appear on the injury report all week and did not enter Thursday night with a designation.
Joey Porter Jr. arrives for his home debut with the Dallas Cowboys pic.twitter.com/vuNtf9VQ5K
"So I talked to another #Cowboys team source who just told me Joey Porter Jr. was 'very sick' when he arrived to the facility and the team sent him home ," Slater shared on X.
It was a smart move by the Cowboys to avoid getting several players in the locker room ill, and also checks out with what was shown as Porter arrived.
In a video shared online, which you can see above, Porter can be seen holding his mouth and coughing as he entered the stadium. NFL insider Mike Garrofolo added, "I’m told Porter has been vomiting with a bad virus. Just not in a condition to play tonight for the Cowboys ."
it definitely appeared Joey Porter Jr. was trying to hold that in as he got off of the #Cowboys bus. he lost that battle. https://t.co/OfYimoCV5v
It's unfortunate that Porter will not be on the field on Thursday night, but allowing him to rest up and avoid a wider outbreak is the wise move for Dallas. And no one should be guarding Emeka Egbuka if a ride to the stadium made them sick.
During his debut, Porter Jr's Dallas career got off to a hot start, playing 19 snaps in covreage and allowing no receptions on one target. Once he is healthy enough to return to the field, the Cowboys appear to be taking a step in the right direction with their injury-ridden defensive backfield.

title: Cowboys, Lions Are Ideal Trade Partners Amid Detroit's Defensive Woes
full_text:
The Detroit Lions and Dallas Cowboys have one thing in common: their defenses stink.
Through three weeks, the Lions rank dead last in total yards and passing yards allowed per game. The Cowboys rank 30th in the former and 24th in the latter while also sporting the league's second-worst run defense.
The biggest need the Lions have on defense is at cornerback, where D.J. Reed has been disappointing and Detroit hasn't found anyone to replace Terrion Arnold, who was no great shakes to begin with before he was released amid legal troubles.
After acquiring Joey Porter Jr. in a trade with the Pittsburgh Steelers last week, the Cowboys might have an expendable cornerback they could send over to the Lions if Detroit is interested.
The Cowboys first need to get healthy at cornerback before they can unload anyone. But that should be happening in the next week or two when Cobie Durant comes back from his hamstring injury .
Durant should not be the one the Cowboys are willing to trade because we believe he's better than both Shavon Revel and DaRon Bland, and, of course, they aren't going to trade Porter, who the Lions were interested in before Dallas swiped him instead.
The two tradeable cornerbacks the Cowboys have are Bland and Revel, although Dallas would almost certainly be more willing to move Bland.
Bland once looked to be on a star trajectory earlier in his career, but he has taken a nosedive since, both because of injuries and ineffective play. Perhaps a change of scenery is what he needs.
Bland is healthy in 2026, but he is struggling once again over four games and the Cowboys might be willing to unload him, especially considering he's a likely cut candidate in 2027 . Dallas could then give more snaps to Durant and Revel once Bland is gone, which would instantly improve its coverage.
Bland has a big contract, but it not impossible to move at all, and the Cowboys can pick some of it up to make a deal work. From there, there is an out in Bland's deal in 2027, so the Lions aren't stuck with him if they don't want to be.
Because of Bland's struggles, the Lions would probably be more interested in Revel, who offers more upside given his small sample size of just 11 games played in the NFL after he was a third-round pick in 2025.
But Revel hasn't been that good thus far and remains unproven, so he's anything but guaranteed to solve the Lions' issue at cornerback.
Admittedly, neither one of these players are that attractive right now, but the Lions are also in a desperate situation, so they may view a trade for Revel or Bland more favorably than most teams. And, oftentimes teams feel like they can fix a player who has struggled elsewhere.
Because their stocks are low, neither player should cost much. The Lions would likely be looking at a Day 3 pick for either one.
Cowboys fans might scoff at the idea of any team wanting to trade for Revel or Bland, and especially Bland, but don't underestimate how desperate the Lions are right now.

The Chargers have several other key players whose Week 5 outlook isn't so good, like James, Jackson, and McConkey, among others. The Chargers are desperate, in more ways than one, so the Broncos will have to be ready to exploit the absence of these key players, and beware the cornered-animal effect of this division rival.
