title: Broncos' Biggest Winners & Losers of Sean Payton Taking Back Play-Calling
full_text:
Sean Payton has taken back the play-calling duties at Denver Broncos HQ.
First-year offensive coordinator Davis Webb had been under heavy scrutiny as the play-caller amid the Broncos' struggles out of the gate. On Wednesday, rumors lit up the NFL that Payton's patience was wearing thin, but he didn't even wait until after this week's road matchup with the Los Angeles Chargers to make the decision.
Payton made the decision to take back the play-calling on Monday. So the ESPN rumors were well-founded after all. On Thursdays, we're supposed to hear from the Broncos' coordinator trio, but instead it was Payton who stepped up to the podium and announced he's taken back the play-calling duties.
"We’ll make a change offensively," Payton said. "I’ll call the plays."
Payton did the best he could to tip his hat at Webb and preserve a semblance of dignity on behalf of his young protege. But it's not just Webb dealing with a dinged PR profile; Payton has plenty of egg on his face, too.
"I want to say this first, and I said it to Davis the other day talking to him. I’ve done this long enough where I know when I have a future head coach, and he’s going to be one," Payton said. "All the things that it’s hard to find will happen. In fact, the same thing to some degree—a little bit different—happened to myself early in my career."
And by the way, if you ever doubted Payton's confidence in his play-calling acumen, after relinquishing them to Webb in the offseason, the veteran coach disabused you that notion when he was asked about the NFL's growing ranks of talented play-callers.
“I think I’m still one of them," Payton said.
With Payton taking back the play sheet, there are some big winners and losers at Broncos HQ. Let's examine.
Amid Nix's early-season struggles, it's easy to forget he's the only quarterback in NFL history to pass for 7,500-plus yards, 50-plus touchdowns, and win 20-plus games through his first two years as a pro. It was unprecedented success, as there have been quarterbacks, like Justin Herbert, who had crazy statistical production out of the gate, but not the wins.
Nix had both. And who was the guy calling the plays and putting the young quarterback in position to achieve such individual success, leading to the Broncos' immense collective success? Payton.
Nobody is perfect. We've critiqued Payton's play-calling at times with Nix as his quarterback. Overall, though, Payton's resume speaks for itself.
Payton's play-calling helped bring the city of New Orleans its one and only World Championship and vaulted Drew Brees into the Pro Football Hall of Fame. Payton placed Nix on a similar path to start his career, and although the veteran coach genuinely thought giving Webb the play sheet was the best thing for his young quarterback and the team, the results simply haven't been there.
It's a tough setback for Webb, and I'm sure that Nix feels for his dear friend and coordinator. But he's got to be quietly excited by Payton taking back the play-calling, as Nix has been on pace to produce a career-low season statistically.
In all honesty, Webb is one of the few losers in this equation. But if he has the right mindset, he can take this as a learning experience, grow from it, and become a better coach and play-caller in the future.
I'm sure this was a tough decision for Payton for multiple reasons, not the least of which is how it'll affect Webb's NFL profile as a future head-coaching candidate. That's why Payton led with the head coach stuff in his initial statement.
If Payton's big decision leads to an offensive renaissance for the Broncos, and Nix looks like the quarterback of yore, it'll give owners and front offices around the league even more doubts about Webb's wherewithal as a head-coaching candidate.
But that's only an immediate setback for Webb, relative to the 2027 hiring cycle. If the Broncos go on to meet their playoff expectations, regardless of whether it results in a Super Bowl berth, Webb could still garner head-coaching interest, but more likely, he'll have to wait another year.
That's okay. He's only in Year 4 as an NFL coach, and he's still young at 31. Payton ultimately had to do what he believed was best for the Broncos, not what's best for Webb's NFL resume.
If one of the collateral effects is that this decision keeps Webb in Denver for another year, I'm sure it's a consequence Payton will accept happily, even if his protege isn't quite as thrilled.
Sutton has only caught nine passes for 86 yards through four games. He's on pace to finish the season with under 100 targets, which has never happened with Nix as his quarterback.
Under Payton's play-calling, Sutton produced a career-high 10 touchdowns in 2023 with Russell Wilson as his QB, followed by back-to-back 1,000-yard seasons and his second Pro Bowl selection with Nix.
Sutton would never say it publicly, but he knows his stock just went up.
I say 'loser,' but it could end up being a big win for Engram, too. With Webb as the play-caller, Engram's snap share has risen dramatically since last season because of the coordinator's prioritization of the multiple-tight-end sets.
Engram has been kept in to block at a much higher clip, which has also seen his usage in the passing game climb, too. Unfortunately, though, Nix and the Broncos haven't been able to exploit Engram's increase in playing time with producion on the field.
Last season, Engram finished third on the team in receiving, but he was overall frustrated by the amount of snaps he have up to Adam Trautman. We'll see if Payton chooses to continue the multi-tight-end thing, and I have a sneaking suspicion that he will.
If so, Engram will actually end up being a winner in this big decision. If Payton goes back to the 11 personnel/spread approach he favored last year, Engram might see his playing time decrease.
It's no coincidence that every winner I've mentioned so far is also on my ' Biggest Disappointments at the Quarter Pole ' list. That includes Dobbins, who is also on pace for a career-low-type season.
The Broncos' ground game just hasn't clicked yet, like, at all. The Broncos made the decision to re-sign Dobbins with a 4x raise, and so far, that investment has been squandered.
That's about to change, though, provided Dobbins can stay healthy (knock on wood). He and Payton made magic together last season before the veteran back suffered a foot injury that ended his campaign.
The Broncos returned the same starting five for the third straight year. So why has this offensive line looked orders of magnitude worse than it did the previous two years?
It's the same scheme, the same quarterback, and the same collection of backs. Even Zach Strief remains this team's run game coordinator and ultimate O-line czar.
The only new factor was that Payton wasn't calling the plays. It certainly hasn't helped that Denver has faced, literally, the NFL's four best teams in consecutive weeks to start this season.
That has something to do with the O-line situation, and why it's allowing a career-high level of pressure on Nix. Payton's play-calling should get this unit back on track.
Payton famously advised his wife, Skylene, to draft Waddle in fantasy. Outside of one game, though — Week 2 — Waddle hasn't been much of a fantasy factor, though he did score his first touchdown as a Bronco last week.
In two of Denver's four games, Waddle has totaled two or fewer receptions. That's obviously not what the Broncos had in mind when they relinquished a first- and third-round pick to acquire Waddle and his contract.
Payton now has all the weapons that he's coveted traditionally and that have been hallmarks of his offenses over the years. Sutton gives him the big-bodied X receiver; Engram is the athletic, pass-catching tight end; RJ Harvey is the explosive receiver out of the backfield; and Dobbins is the between-the-tackles grinder.
The only thing missing was the explosive downfield speed demon, and that's exactly what Waddle brings to the table. When we…

title: Broncos' Most Disappointing Players at the Quarter Pole of the Season
full_text:
When the NFL changed the regular-season schedule to 17 games, we lost the ability to perfectly break down the season by four-game quarters.
But as a rule of thumb, I still do it. The Denver Broncos stand at 2-2 at the quarter pole of the 2026 season.
We've seen some epic comebacks and some alarming developments . Overall, though, the Broncos are in exactly the same position they were in at this time last year.
However, a handful of players have been disappointments thus far. The quarter pole is the first pit stop to look back and get a feel for the trajectory the Broncos are on.
Today, we're doing that by looking at the Broncos' biggest disappointments thus far. Note how many of the names on this list are supposed to this team's best players.
That's disappointing, but it also illustrates how much room there is to improve. The Broncos have faced a tough initial schedule, playing the NFL's four best teams to start the season, and once they break through this guantlet, I expect these players to bounce back big through the resistance training they've received.
I don't want to be too hard on Nix because I'm a firm believer in him as a young quarterback, and I remain confident that he'll bounce back. That said, I'd be lying if I didn't say he's been a disappointment this season.
Like all Broncos fans, I expected to see a Year-3 step forward from Nix, but through four games, he's mostly looked like a hesitant rookie, fearful of pushing the ball downfield, and content to take the checkdowns.
It would seem that Sean Payton is equally concerned. Payton took action entering Week 5's road tilt against the Los Angeles Chargers, stepping back into the play-calling process on game day , though offensive coordinator Davis Webb will still be involved and will be the voice Nix hears in his helmet.
Make no mistake; this move is all about getting Nix out of his funk . Yeah, the Broncos' run game has been non-existent, and the offensive line is giving up an unprecedented pressure rate on Nix, but Payton knows that his team will only go so far as this young quarterback can lead them, and the veteran coach is taking a more hands-on approach to ensuring things get back on track.
Color me optimistic that Nix takes some big steps forward this week against the Chargers. He's never won at SoFi Stadium, and he's yet to defeat Justin Herbert head-to-head, which only means Nix is due.
Dobbins is averaging a career-low in yards per carry (3.5). He's been dinged up with a hip injury, though he hasn't missed a full game.
Whether it's the injury, the play-calling, or the offensive line, Dobbins hasn't looked like the confident, savvy runner we saw for 10 games last season. Payton remains adamant that Dobbins is "important" to what Denver is trying to achieve, but it's time for the veteran back to step it up a notch.
In four games, Dobbins has 46 carries for 161 yards. Six of his carries have moved the chains. Beyond that, though, he's been a dud — and after getting a 4x raise this past offseason, that's not good.
A good game for Sutton used to be nine receptions for 86 yards and maybe a touchdown. Alas, he's yet to score through four games and that stat line serves as his total production for the season thus far.
Suffice it to say, the Pro Bowl receiver has been a disappointment thus far. Sutton's effort has been questionable at times, and the typical my-ball mentality fans came to know and love has been absent from his game.
I attribute this to Nix's struggles and the play-calling issues, but with Payton stepping back in on game days, it's time for Sutton to step it up. I believe he will, as soon as this week .
All-Pro left tackle Garett Bolles and All-Pro right guard Quinn Meinerz haven't been enough to sustain the Broncos' offensive line as the NFL's top unit this season. Left guard Ben Powers has been okay, but center Luke Wattenberg and right tackle Mike McGlinchey have been downright bad.
This unit is allowing career-high pressure on Nix, and it's simply not moving opponents off the block in the run game. The Broncos ranked 29th in rushing for a reason. In just about every measurable way, the Broncos' offensive line has been bad this season.
Bolles isn't blameless, as his penalties have popped up as a consistent liability through four games. With Payton's increased involvement, though, this unit should take a big step forward in the second quarter of the season.
Bonitto has exactly one sack through four games. He's off to the slowest start of his career since becoming a starter in 2024.
Although Bonitto has still found ways to impact the game pressure-wise, he's not been able to get home. It's worth mentioning, though, that he had a big strip-sack erased in Week 2 by a Riley Moss penalty.
I don't know if it's the level of competition Bonitto has faced or the absence of John Franklin-Myers next to him on the defensive line, or Jonathon Cooper opposite him on the edge, but Denver's Pro Bowl rush linebacker needs to amp up his game moving into the next few weeks.
Speaking of disappointments, I have to list Cooper's replacement in the starting lineup. Elliss has been ineffectual as a pass rusher and not much better against the run.
Through four games, Elliss has been held without a sack. I'm sure a big part of the explanation is the tough offensive lines he's faced thus far, but the Broncos thought he was ready to be a starter; they were looking for ways to get him on the field more.
But Elliss has been a big disappointment thus far. If he doesn't improve, it wouldn't surprise me to see Que Robinson start eating into his snaps more, much like he did last week against the San Francisco 49ers.
Singleton has missed a lot of tackles, but he's also made a team-high 47. Early this season, he showed a troubling penchant for picking the wrong lanes to fill in run defense, and his overaggression led to missed tackles and big plays by opponents.
Throw in Singleton's scary-bad coverage, and he's been a disappointment thus far. I know most Broncos fans didn't have super high expectations for the soon-to-be 33-year-old linebacker, but I didn't expect him to look as lost as he has at times.
For what it's worth, though, Singleton turned in an encouraging performance last week agains the San Francisco 49ers, though he allowed all of his targets in coverage to be completed. Perhaps it's a sign that he's moving in the right direction, I don't know. But Denver needs him to pick it up.
I don't want to cast Surtain as a liability. He's been far from it. But he's not been great thus far.
In Week 3, Davante Adams burned Surtain up and down the field like he was a rookie again. Surtain seemed poised to bounce back last week before he suffered a lower-leg injury that saw him exit the game early.
Now, Surtain is expected to miss time and is week-to-week, but when he comes back, the Broncos need him to return to a semblance of his Defensive Player of the Year form.
The only impact Mims has made thus far has been a negative one. After getting injured in the season opener, he missed two straight games, and in his return last week, he lost a fumble, which ended up being the momentum-swinging turning point for the 49ers.
Granted, Mims has been held back by multiple injuries, starting in training camp, but when he's been on the field — which has admittedly been few and far between — we haven't seen the high-impact player we know.
With a little luck from the injury bug, though, hopefully Mims can get his groove back. The Broncos are going to need him with Pat Bryant injured and out for the next few weeks .

title: 5 Bold Broncos Predictions That Could Shock the Chargers
full_text:
The Los Angeles Chargers may be 0-4, but the Denver Broncos haven't fared well against them since Sean Payton became the head coach.
Entering this Week 5 matchup with the Chargers, the Broncos are struggling offensively , lacking explosive plays and failing to establish a run game. Sean Payton decided to step in and take on more of a play-calling role on game day, starting with this game against the Chargers.
Payton clearly understands that the Broncos can't afford to overlook the Chargers and lose their second divisional game of the season.
As we all know, fortune favors the bold. If I'm right about this week's bold predictions, the Broncos will walk out of SoFi Stadium at 3-2. Winning cures all.
At some point, Sutton has to make a major appearance. After four weeks of questionable effort, he has 86 yards on nine catches on 21 targets.
Bo Nix has trusted Sutton as his top target through his first two years. With Pat Bryant out, Sutton needs to find a way to get involved. Jaylen Waddle is getting a lot of attention and is still getting open, so Sutton's excuses are nearly out.
But this is the game for the Pro Bowler. Sutton reminds everyone exactly who he is, and produces 100-plus receiving yards.
Nix has been way too quick to hit the check-downs, especially against the San Francisco 49ers. If he keeps that up, Harvey could be poised for a big game, given the injuries the Chargers are dealing with.
Harvey is coming off his season-high 93 yards from scrimmage against the 49ers. Still, the 49ers were healthy last week, but the Chargers are dealing with multiple injuries to their linebackers and secondary.
Watch for Harvey to have a big game at SoFi.
With Patrick Surtain II likely out , Barron will face heavy pressure to perform. Many have already slapped a bust label on him because his play hasn't been great and he's only played sparingly, so this is a prime opportunity.
Against the Chargers' receivers, Barron doesn't have the best matchup, but he has shown a nose for the ball and can snag a pass and take it to the house, which is exactly what happens on Sunday.
Along with Barron's pick-six, the Broncos will snag another interception as their pass rush harasses Justin Herbert all game. The Chargers' offensive line is, once again, beat up, and Denver should be able to win consistently up front without having to blitz.
The Broncos get home at least four times, with Zach Allen picking up a strip-sack that Denver recovers. This defense is a prideful unit, and it has struggled to be consistent and force negative plays.
The Broncos look to this banged-up Chargers offense to correct the narrative.
The Broncos have typically played to their opponent's level, even against struggling teams. The Broncos have also struggled consistently against the Chargers during the Payton era.
But this year, with Denver at 2-2, the enthusiasm around this team has taken a hit. That's about to change.
The Broncos make a big statement before a short week against the Seattle Seahawks, beating the Chargers by at least 17 points.

title: Sean Payton Makes Major Change to Broncos' Offensive Play-Calling
full_text:
The Davis Webb experiment has officially concluded.
Coming off a concerning loss to the 49ers and with third-year quarterback Bo Nix undergoing early-season struggles , the Denver Broncos have made a decisive change to their offensive play-calling process.
According to ESPN's Adam Schefter , the Broncos are taking a more "collaborative" approach ahead of Sunday's game against the Chargers, with head coach Sean Payton assuming increased playsheet responsibility and effectively demoting embattled rookie offensive coordinator Davis Webb, who will maintain a "significant" role on staff.
The news was confirmed Thursday by 9NEWS insider Mike Klis.
"Sources confirm Broncos will feature more collaborative approach to game planning and play calling this week between HC Sean Payton and OC Davis Webb," Klis wrote on X. "Payton more involved in play calling although key will be whether he or Webb is communicating plays to Bo.  Chiefs do something similar between Andy Reid and Eric Bieniemy. Payton has already been heavily involved in putting together game planning in recent weeks."
Speculation has mounted in recent days that Payton could take back playcalling from Webb following Denver's second loss this season, in which they averaged just 4.6 yards per play, were held to only 82 total rushing yards, and finished 8-for-17 on third down.
Through four weeks, the Broncos' offense ranks 27th in both yards and points per game, 26th in rushing yards per game, 21st in passing yards per game, and 20th in EPA (Expected Points Added) per game.
"It's a fair question; I appreciate it," Payton said Sunday regarding a potential move away from Webb. "It's tough to discuss any of that right now. But I told those guys, ‘Hey, we’ve played some tough teams, and this is another good football team.’
"There were a lot of things we did well defensively for a good portion of the game. I felt like the time of possession began to affect us. We had the big turnover in the kicking game, and that flips the field and all of a sudden you're back out there on defense. To your original question, we always look at everything in each game and that's how we'll approach this one.”
The Broncos are facing a trap game of sorts, hitting the road to take on their winless division rivals in Los Angeles. At 2-2, they can either get back above .500 while proverbially driving a stake in the 2026 Chargers' hearts — or they can allow the home team to save their season with an upset.
The Chargers' defense is rife for exploitation, ranking 22nd against the run and 14th against the pass. Two of their starting defensive backs, safety Derwin James and cornerback Donte Jackson, are also banged-up.
With Payton at the controls, this could turn out to be a get-right matchup for the Broncos. But certainly not one they're taking for granted.
“I buy into the notion in the NFL each week, you’re going to see teams that week-in and week-out, when you watch them play a number of their games... For me, it’s the scheme study, the personnel study and not as much the end result," Payton said Wednesday.
"They had five takeaways in Buffalo, they’ve been ahead in a number of games, they’ve started actually really well. So the focus really becomes on the personnel of the opponent and how they’re playing their defense and offense and kicking game.”

title: Bo Nix Has a Message for His Critics Entering Week 5
full_text:
Publicly, Sean Payton continues to back offensive coordinator Davis Webb as the Denver Broncos' play-caller.
The scrutiny on Webb is at an all-time high. And local and national insiders report that Payton is running out of patience on the play-calling front.
Payton has not acknowledged any of that buzz publicly, and he's also been in no mood to throw third-year quarterback Bo Nix under the bus. However, with the Broncos sitting at 2-2 at the quarter pole, Payton knows that what he's seen is nowhere near good enough to meet the club's expectations.
His focus is figuring out how quickly these offensive issues can be fixed.
"I think that the most important job I have is really evaluating the whys," Payton said on Wednesday. "After a four-game sample size… All right, certainly this isn’t championship football or what we see; how quickly can we correct those things?”
The noise outside Broncos HQ is reaching levels that could drive this team to distraction. Winning heals all wounds, but Nix is doing his best to tune out the noise as he prepares to step into a stadium in which he's never won this weekend, as the Broncos travel to take on the Los Angeles Chargers.
“I think for me it’s very simple," Nix said on Wednesday. "For me, it’s all about who you’re giving your attention to. Who are you listening to? I think there’s something really valuable about tuning out the noise and not listening to all the noise and the distractions. If you’re not careful, that’s just what they become, just distractions.”
Nix chooses to listen to the people who are actively trying to make him better, like his coaches and teammates. They actually have the power to help him.
We have been critical of Nix this week because he left so many plays on the field in last Sunday's 24-14 loss to the San Francisco 49ers. 14 of his 25 completions went to running backs, and he seemed extremely hesitant to push the ball beyond 10 yards downfield.
Nix knows it, though. He knew he missed a few plays long before he ever turned on the Week 4 film.
“Yes, absolutely," Nix acknowledged that he missed some plays last Sunday. "There’s never been a game that I’ve played that I didn’t want to have a couple back... That’s just unfortunately what I’ve learned, is that you could play out of your mind, and I’d still go home thinking about one or two plays that are just driving me crazy."
No quarterback is perfect, but in the NFL, fans and media often hold them to unrealistic expectations. Nix pursues perfection, knowing that it's unattainable in the "never-satisfied game" that he plays professionally.
"So it’s sort of a never-satisfied game, and that’s one thing you have to be careful with this job, is working so hard and not ever being satisfied," Nix said. "For us, obviously it’s all about winning. It’s all about putting our team in the best situation possible. So for me, there are definitely several things that I want to change, and I want to get better at. That’s going to happen. It’s going to come over time.”
One of the challenges of being a quarterback is trying to walk the razor's edge of protecting the ball while also taking calculated risks to push it downfield at times. Since arriving as the Broncos' first-round pick in 2024, Nix has shown a penchant for walking that line, but this season, his balance, so to speak, has been off.
Mostly, we've seen a hesitant, almost unsure Nix where he seems quite reluctant to do anything but check the ball down to running backs. He's made some big-time throws, including a deep 49-yard near-touchdown strike to Jaylen Waddle in Week 2, but there's a reason Nix currently leads the league in passes behind the line of scrimmage.
“It’s the hardest thing, in my opinion, about playing the position because as soon as you make one throw and it’s picked, then you made a bad decision," Nix said. "As soon as you make one and you rip it and you’re like, ‘Well, I fit it in there, but it probably wasn’t smart.’ Then you’re considered lucky or you’re a gunslinger."
Nix has a point. But throwing the labels aside, that's the magical sweet spot the NFL's top-tier quarterbacks are trying to find. He has to figure out how to re-conjure some of that Mile High Magic without overthinking it.
Coming off a broken ankle and two offseason surgeries, Nix has faced some unique challenges entering his third year. On top of that, the Broncos drew the NFL's toughest initial schedule — their first four opponents have literally been the four best teams in the league — and he's rolling with the punches of trying to execute for a new play-caller.
Meanwhile, the Broncos' offensive line is allowing pressure on Nix at an unprecedented rate this season, and his unit continues to be plagued by painfully slow starts in each game. Fortunately, he's able to cultivate a tough mindset and keep his focus on the plays and the things he can control.
"To me, it’s not about the labels. It’s not even the overall outcome," Nix said. "It’s about, ‘What was this play asking for? Did I do my job? Did I not?’"
Nix doesn't view himself as some kind of home-run hitter; he's more of a point guard whose job is to distribute the ball to his playmakers.
"If there’s an accumulation of plays that turns into me throwing the ball 100 times in a game down the field, then I’ll do it," Nix said. "But at the same time, when you consistently watch and if you look at the most successful guys, over and over, they just take completions. They keep the ball moving. They have less footballs on the ground. When it’s there, yes you hit it, but at the same time, first-and-20, you’re not eager to just drop back and just force something out there."
It's a respectable mindset, but the easy completions can't always come at the expense of foregoing a shot at the big play. Nix knows that. And as he said, he believes it'll all come together for this offense in time.
Payton's concern is that it doesn't all come together too late. He knows exactly what Nix's film last week showed: a handful of missed opportunities.
"We've had some opportunities, but there are a handful of things that aren't clicking," Payton said . "And we gotta figure it out fast, because we're going into Week 5."
Payton and Webb are focused on helping the young quarterback and the players around Nix fine-tune "the little things" that will, ostensibly, lead to better results in the bigger picture.
"The thing that I saw in the film was, yes, are there certain throws that, from a timing standpoint, he wants back? Yes," Payton said of Nix. "But I think, collectively, when you’re playing well on offense, you’re doing a lot of little things well, and then that job for him becomes somewhat easier. So that’s really the focus this week is the little things, detailing the little things, and we’ll see that in the end product.”
The Broncos are working hard to tune out the noise. But if they go into SoFi Stadium and lose to the winless Chargers, that din will get cranked up to '11,' and might make it impossible to ignore.
For the sake of Payton, Webb, Nix, and the Broncos, they need to get a win on Sunday and not fall prey to the wild machinations of a wounded, cornered animal, as Jim Harbaugh's Chargers appear to be entering Week 5.
Nix has never beaten the Justin Herbert-led Chargers. Nix got a win in the finale last year, but Harbaugh rested Herbert and many of his starters.
I don't care that L.A. is 0-4; if Nix can go into SoFi and get a win head-to-head over Herbert and a divisional opponet that has foiled him for two-plus years, it could do wonders for his confidence and momentum going into Week 6's home game against the Seattle Seahawks.
Winning is the salve that heals all wounds, and it would certainly quiet the noise.

title: Broncos TE Adam Trautman Pops Up on Initial Week 5 Injury Report
full_text:
The Denver Broncos listed seven players on their initial Week 5 injury report as the team prepares for its divisional road showdown against the Los Angeles Chargers on Sunday.
As expected, cornerbacks Patrick Surtain II (ankle) and Riley Moss (ribs) and wide receiver Pat Bryant — all of whom were injured in Denver's Week 4 loss to the 49ers — did not practice on Wednesday.
Surtain reportedly is anticipated to miss anywhere from two to four weeks while Bryant and Moss could also be sidelined for a short period of time. Broncos head coach Sean Payton said he believes each of the players will avoid going on injured reserve, which would sideline them for at least four games.
“That’s jumping way ahead. I don’t think so, and if they were I wouldn’t say so, but I don’t think so," Payton told reporters Wednesday.
Elsewhere on the injury report, tight end Adam Trautman and outside linebacker Dondrea Tillman were limited with shoulder and hamstring issues, respectively. Defensive lineman Zach Allen was given a vet rest day, marked as limited.
Running back Tyler Badie (foot) was a full practice participant.
Wednesday's #DENvsLAC injury report: 📰 » https://t.co/vwWr7HUiVu pic.twitter.com/MXsp7oFNUk
On the Chargers' side, the list is almost comically extensive: 18 players marked down, eight of which were DNPs — including starting tackles Joe Alt and Rashawn Slater, safety Derwin James, outside linebacker Khalil Mack, and wide receiver Ladd McConkey.
Both teams will practice again on Thursday and Friday before releasing their final Week 5 game designations.
Just as they did last week, backup cornerbacks Jahdae Barron and Kris Abrams-Draine will fill in if/when Surtain and Moss are declared inactive against the Chargers. Both held their own despite unfavorable circumstances amid the 24-14 defeat in San Francisco.
“They’re savvy players, they both have good football instincts and IQ," Payton said of Barron and Abrams-Draine. "One of the reasons you draft at that position is because it’s hard to find in free agency. So both were ready when they needed to be and that’s encouraging.”
On the offensive side, Bryant's absence will mean a bump up the depth chart for the likes of Marvin Mims and Troy Franklin, and perhaps a further increase in targets for leading pass-catcher, running back RJ Harvey. The Broncos are also looking to get elder statesman WR Courtland Sutton involved following a slow start to the season .
“He know I’m doing my best to get him the football," quarterback Bo Nix said of Sutton on Wednesday. "I think in the same way as saying, ‘Nobody’s asking for the football,’ I think sometimes it’s tougher because you want to reward those guys and get them the football because they’re not asking for. You see their effort and you see them working really hard at it. You want to reward them by getting them the football. I just think right now there’s a lot out there on the field for a lot of these touches and a lot of guys getting the football."
If Trautman remains limited by his shoulder issue, reserve tight end/fullback Nate Adkins could see more work behind starter Evan Engram.

title: ESPN Insiders Predict Sean Payton Could Make Major Broncos Change
full_text:
After Sunday's loss to the San Francisco 49ers, Denver Broncos head coach Sean Payton said it's "way too early" to even countenance a change at offensive play-caller.
Four weeks into the 2026 season, the Denver Broncos sit at 2-2, having played the four best teams in the NFL consecutively . New offensive coordinator and play-caller Davis Webb has had his moments, but the scrutiny remains high as Bo Nix and the offense continue to struggle to find consistency.
Payton's message, again, is that it's too early . That's not necessarily what ESPN 's Jeremy Fowler and Dan Graziano are hearing, though.
Graziano is hearing from people inside the league that Payton's patience is not everlasting.
"A lot of people around the league seem to think Broncos coach Sean Payton won't wait too much longer to take playcalling back from Davis Webb, though I have to believe it won't be an impulse decision if it happens," Graziano wrote on Wednesday .
In Houston, Texans head coach DeMeco Ryans has taken the defensive play-calling back from coordinator Matt Burke amid the team's 0-4 start, so the precedent is there. Payton isn't the type to wait to see whether another head coach sticks his neck out to make such a move first, but I mention Ryans only to show that decisions like this are often made during the season.
The reality is, the Broncos don't have all the time in the world to turn the offensive ship around. Yes, there are 12 more regular-season games, but each one is crucial and plays a big part in the final divisional and playoff picture.
The question is, how much longer can Payton afford to wait? He's considered one of the best offensive play-callers of the modern era, and while Webb is his protégé and a coach on the rise, his performance has not met  expectations.
"In Denver, complicating matters is that its head coach happens to be one of the best playcallers of his generation -- that, and Bo Nix is not playing well. My sense is Webb will have more time, but at some point the product needs to match the expectations," Fowler wrote.
It would be one thing if Nix was playing well, but the Broncos were just struggling overall as a unit. But that hasn't been the case.
Instead of seeing the young quarterback make the expected Year-3 leap forward, fans are becoming increasingly fearful of a regression , fueled, in part, by Webb's inexperience as a play-caller.
Payton is there, looking over Webb's shoulder, but in each of the past two games, the Broncos' head coach has been seen more and more often with a play sheet in his hands, especially in the second half.
While Webb has yet to impress anyone with his play-calling, the Broncos haven't exactly executed well as a unit. That's true of Nix and every man on offense, but it triggers the classic chicken-or-the-egg quandry.
Is Nix struggling because of Webb's play-calling? Or is Webb's play-calling failing to launch because of Nix? We have far more reason to acquit Nix in that question, given his experience, than we do Webb, who has exactly four regular-season games under his belt as an NFL play-caller.
The other factors to consider is the stiff schedule Denver has faced. The Broncos won't always have to play the very best teams in the league each week, so it will be interesting to see how the offensive product looks on Sunday, for example, against the 0-4 Los Angeles Chargers.
The pressure allowed on Nix by the Broncos' offensive line is an all-time high. And the starting five, despite returning every starter for the third straight year, has played far from the top-rated unit it was last year. It makes me wonder how much that has affected Nix as a passer, given that he leads the league in passes behind the line of scrimmage this season.
The Broncos invested big into wide receiver Jaylen Waddle, giving up a first- and third-round pick to the Miami Dolphins and absorbing his big contract. Denver isn't seeing much of a return on that investment, and it's fair to wonder if Payton could do a better job of maximizing the talent around Nix.
We know that Payton contributes to the game plan each week, and he certainly signs off on it. But the Broncos have continued to be exceedingly slow starters, while struggling to stay on the field and finish drives with points.
At this point, Payton is likely keeping an open mind on Webb and the play-calling because of his belief in his protégé and the quality of opponents the Broncos have faced thus far. The Chargers will be a telling litmus test, though.
If Nix and the offense fail to launch against a winless Chargers team that features the NFL's 24th-ranked scoring defense, perhaps it would be enough to convince Payton to step in and take back the play-calling.
That puts a lot of pressure on Nix and Webb, but welcome to the NFL. That's the way the cookie crumbles.
If Fowler and Graziano are hearing rumblings inside the NFL, it's only a matter of time before Payton effectuates a change, even if it means he ends up with some egg on his face. The Broncos can't afford to let the season slip away — not with the Super Bowl expectations they've established.

title: Broncos Stock Report: 4 Risers, 3 Fallers Entering Week 5
full_text:
The Denver Broncos have started the season 2-2, going .500 against the NFL's four best teams at the quarter-pole.
Given how tough Denver's first four opponents have actually been, the 2-2 start is a moral victory of sorts. A look at the Broncos' next four opponents makes that even clearer.
The Los Angeles Chargers may be winless, but they're a division rival and Sean Payton has yet to win at SoFi Stadium as Broncos head coach. The Broncos are 1-3 against Jim Harbaugh's Chargers, so it would be unwise to sleep on their 0-4 AFC West rival.
After the Chargers, the Broncos return home on a short-week turnaround to host the Seattle Seahawks on Thursday Night Football . Then it's a mini-bye of sorts, as the Broncos will get 10 days to prepare for the Arizona Cardinals on the road, followed by their rematch with the Kansas City Chiefs at Mile High.
If the Broncos can get to Week 9 at 4-4 or better, they'll be in good position to capitalize on the softer stretch of their schedule, and potentially still be in position to win the AFC West. The 4-0 Chiefs have yet to play the toughest stretch of their schedule, nor have the 3-1 Las Vegas Raiders, both of whom still have to play the four teams of the NFC West, the Buffalo Bills, and the New England Patriots.
The Broncos are still very much in control of their destiny. With that said, though, the Broncos have to take care of business against the reeling Chargers, who will be desperate to get off the schneid at home.
Let's take a look at this week's stock report to get a feel for which Broncos are rising and falling entering this Chargers matchup on the road.
Barron led all Broncos cornerbacks in snaps last week, stepping in to relieve the injured Patrick Surtain II. Shortly after Surtain exited, Riley Moss followed with a rib injury, which put even more onus on Barron.
The second-year corner stepped up , allowing only one completion in coverage and tackling well. He looked like a starting-caliber corner, which is exactly what the Broncos hoped to see from their 2025 first-round pick.
Let's hope Barron can sustain the momentum against the Chargers.
Nix's numbers against the San Francisco 49ers weren't bad on the surface, but diving a little deeper, 14 of his 25 completions went to running backs. He leads the NFL in passes behind the line of scrimmage, and he seems hesitant to push the ball downfield.
Now, that could simply be a reflection of the tough defenses Nix has faced to start this season, but it's an obvious theme that the coaches have to figure out. Protecting the ball and avoiding negative plays is a mandate, but so is taking the calculated risks that lead to big plays.
Sean Payton and offensive coordinator Davis Webb have to get to the bottom of whatever is ailing Nix, and I'm confident they will. Nix needs a big bounce-back game against a Chargers defense ranked 16th in yards allowed and 24th in points (26.5 per game).
Harvey caught 10 passes last week against the 49ers. He was basically the Broncos' entire offensive attack, as Nix checked the ball down to him time after time.
The problem was, the 49ers tackle so well, so while Harvey was able to make a few guys miss, by and large, he was brought down within three or four yards, limiting his impact. As a runner, he didn't have it easy against San Francisco, carrying it seven times for 25 yards.
Since his return from a hamstring injury that cost him Week 2, Harvey has been the engine of this offense. The Broncos need to get more receivers involved, but the second-year back has built up a nice head of steam.
Sutton has become the disappearing man in Denver's offense. Nix has looked his way often (22 targets), but he's only been able to connect with Sutton on nine completions for 86 yards.
That used to be a solid single-game stat line for Sutton. Part of his lack of involvement stems from how opponents are playing the Broncos, and some of it has been on Nix, but Sutton himself needs to step it up.
We're not seeing the my-ball intensity that has been a hallmark of Sutton's decorated career. But it's not too late for the soon-to-be 31-year-old to return to form.
Allen was once again a major force in Week 4 , despite the loss. He made five tackles and although the Broncos were unable to sack Brock Purdy, Allen led the team with four hurries, all of which were hits on the 49ers' quarterback.
Allen's blocked field goal at the bottom of the second quarter helped keep the Broncos alive entering the half. He's been a whirling dervish and arguably the NFL's best interior defender through four weeks.
With a team-high three sacks, we may be witnessing Allen's best season as a pro.
Elliss has been starting opposite Nik Bonitto with Jonathon Cooper on the commissioner's exempt list. Alas, Elliss has been far from the impact player the Broncos expected him to be.
Against the 49ers, Elliss played 40 snaps , but finished with zero pressures on the quarterback. That's simply not good enough.
However, with zero sacks so far this season, Elliss is due for a big game. And so is Bonitto for that matter.
Credit to Badie; when the Broncos have given him touches, he's answered the bell. Against the 49ers, he rushed only twice for 10 yards, but caught two passes for 32 yards, helping to move the chains.
Tyler Badie and the Broncos needed 3 yards and they got 25 😤 DENvsSF on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/QdbJCTwtbJ
Badie also scored a two-point conversion, taking the direct snap and running behind All-Pro right guard Quinn Meinerz to pay-dirt. With Jonah Coleman on injured reserve and J.K. Dobbins still trying to find his groove, Badie's impact has been welcome.
I have a feeling that Dobbins is in for a big game this week against his former team. But the bang-for-buck that Badie is offering the Broncos puts him in position to have a good game, too.

title: One Advanced Metric Reveals Silver Lining to Broncos’ 2-2 Start
full_text:
Four games into the 2026 NFL season, the Denver Broncos sit at 2-2 , with slow starts in each game and a pathetic total of just 13 first-half points.
It's clear the Broncos have a lot of work to do to become a top contender.
However, it's worth noting the Broncos have played four teams that have all shown why they rank among the favorites for a deep playoff run, if not a trip to the Super Bowl. The Broncos' 2-2 start isn't something to dismiss outright, because they've found ways to beat two top teams, and in the other two games, they've had their chances.
As the advanced metric DVOA shows , the Broncos have faced the NFL's toughest schedule in the first four weeks. No other team has faced the gauntlet that Denver has.
Four weeks into the season, DVOA now accounts for opponent adjustments to the tune of 40%. The Broncos sit 14th overall in DVOA at 0.6%, ranked 15th in offense at -2.2%, 14th in defense at -0.7%, and 15th in special teams at 2.1%. Remember that DVOA is better for defense when it's negative.
But what about Denver's opponents thus far? As it turns out, the Broncos have already faced the top three teams in DVOA. In order of ranking, they are the San Francisco 49ers, Jacksonville Jaguars, and Kansas City Chiefs.
The 49ers rank first overall at 54.8%, first in offense at 44.6%, fifth in defense at -13.5 %, and 22nd in special teams at -3.4%.
The Jaguars rank second overall at 40.1%, fourth in offense at 21%, third in defense at 19.4%, and 18th in special teams at -0.2%.
The Chiefs rank third overall at 25.6%, fifth in offense at 20%, 10th in defense at -5%, and 16th in special teams at 0.6%.
While special teams isn't a strength for these three teams, they have top offenses and defenses — all three offenses in the top five and two defenses in the top five plus one in the top 10.
Add to this that the Los Angeles Rams rank seventh overall in DVOA at 18%, seventh in offense at 13.6%, fourth in defense at -18.9%, and 32nd in special teams at -14.5%. That means that every team the Broncos have faced is in the top 10 in overall DVOA, offensive DVOA, and defensive DVOA, with three in the top four in each category.
The Broncos have areas to improve, but the fact is, they've faced four teams that all have a legitimate case for the Super Bowl.
The question now is what happens with the Broncos in the next four games?
Denver will face the Seattle Seahawks on a short week in Week 6 on Thursday Night Football and the Chiefs again in Week 8. The Seahawks rank sixth overall in DVOA and have the top defensive DVOA.
In other words, while the schedule won't be as tough as it was the first four weeks, the Broncos still have to face two tough opponents in their next four. And they can't take the likes of the Los Angeles Chargers (this week's opponent) and the Arizona Cardinals lightly, even though they rank lower in DVOA. The Cardinals rank 19th overall, while the Chargers rank 31st.
Again, if there's a silver lining to the first four weeks, it's that the Broncos faced four tough teams and still found a way to win two of those games, both at home.
The Broncos would certainly like to get more than two wins in the next four games to secure a chance at the playoffs. But to do so, they need to win at least one of these two games against the Seahawks or Chiefs, while taking care of business versus the Chargers and Cardinals, both of which are on the road.

title: Detroit Lions Sign Former Washington Commanders DT to Practice Squad
full_text:
The Detroit Lions announced a practice squad roster decision that should help add depth to the defensive line.
According to multiple reports, former Washington Commanders defensive tackle Jeffrey M'Ba has been inked to Detroit's practice squad.
Since he was designated in the league's International Pathways Program, he is the 17th member of the practice squad.
M'Ba, 27, is a 6-foot-6 defensive tackle who played collegiately at Independence, Auburn, Purdue, and SMU.
He went undrafted in 2026, but was able to land with the Washington Commanders as an undrafted free agent. M'Ba did not make the Commanders initial 53-man roster coming out of training camp, but returned on their practice squad.
After being cut, M'Ba quickly found his way to Detroit. Tyleik Williams is currently dealing with a foot injury, so added depth could be warranted moving forward at practice.
A native of Libreville, Gabon, he recorded 42 tackles (16 solo), five sacks and 7.5 tackles for loss in his final season with the Mustangs.
Defensive coordinator Kelvin Sheppard acknowledged the solid play of the defensive line against the Carolina Panthers.
Detroit's defensive line was able to record three sacks and regularly pressured Panthers quarterback Bryce Young.
Unfortunately, the linebackers unit and secondary were not executing at a high level.
"I told them and I told the D-line, 'It's a disservice what we've been doing to you all.' I truly feel like this is the best D-line we've had in my six-year tenure here since I got here in 2021," said Sheppaed. "And we haven't been complementing it well enough on the backend to see the benefits of it and be outright beneficiaries is what they should be with what the D-line is doing, especially Sunday night . They assaulted the pocket all night. They generated pressure all night on the quarterback.
"But as you saw, the quarterback was able to get the ball out with the quick release and get it completed far too many times. So, there are things we've corrected, there are things we've talked about going into another tall task this week against Arizona and (Cardinals Head Coach Mike) LaFleur coming from the LA Rams."

title: Detroit Lions Week 5 Thursday Injury Report: DT Returns to Practice
full_text:
The Detroit Lions continued their preparation for the Arizona Cardinals with a Thursday afternoon practice at the teams Allen Park Performance Center.
Defensive tackle Tyleik Williams, who missed the first practice of the week with a foot injury, returned to the playing field. He was considered day-to-day with a foot injury suffered last week.
He expressed following practice that he suffered a bruised foot and feels he should be good to suit up on Sunday afternoon.
Those not spotted, during the period open to local reporters to observe, included offensive guard Ben Bartch and cornerback Rock Ya-Sin.
Defensive coordinator Kelvin Sheppard shared prior to practice that he did not just want to just provide lip service to address the key issues. The biggest issue facing the defense is the work being done at practice has not translated well to the field.
"So, I get up here and I recap the game before, and I'm going to do the same. But what I'm not going to do is get up here and read off a stat sheet, a stat column, tell you about how we've got to bridge communication, how we've got to do this and that," Sheppard said. "Because at this point, all of it's lip service. Until it starts to show on Sunday, until the evidence starts to show up at the game, it's lip service. What we do here, bridging it to the game, it sounds good, but it's lip service."
Additional Insider Analysis: Cardinals Have Talent, But Lions Can Exploit These Holes
The former NFL linebacker acknowledged the game against the Panthers did not meet the standards and there needed to evidence of change starting to be showcase out on the playing field.
"What I will say is we did not play well enough defensively to help this team win that football game Sunday night at Carolina," said Sheppard. "There were a lot of things in there that we absolutely didn't like that we turned on the tape as a unit on Monday, hashed out, talked about, and the same thing I told them, it's lip service. So there has to be real change. It has to be real evidence of change.
"Whether that's personnel driven, whether that's some things come out, whatever the case is, something has to change."

title: Detroit Lions Receivers Coach Calls Out Jameson Williams
full_text:
Detroit Lion s receivers coach Scottie Montgomery raised eyebrows this week, when he publicly called out Jameson Williams.
The former first-round pick had multiple drops against the Carolina Panthers, including a deep pass early in the game that he should have hauled in.
He was able to finish Week 4 with six receptions for 102 yards, including a 49-yard catch from Jared Goff.
Montgomery expressed Williams needs to refocus in order to become a player that can secure receptions when he is wide-open or in contested situations.
“Every target he had in that game should've been a catch. If it hits you, you gotta catch it," Montgomery told local reporters earlier this week. "You can’t be boom or bust in this league. That is average. We gotta get him completely refocused on making wide-open catches and contested catches."
In training camp this summer, Williams was able to demonstrate improved pass-catching, but it has not translated into the regular season. In the season-opener, Williams had numerous drops against the New Orleans Saints.
Against Carolina, Williams supposedly lost the football in the lights, which resulted in the early drop.
“Yeah, that's a tracking issue. You can lose it in the lights, but when it comes out of the lights, you've got to find it and catch it. Catch the dark spot. We have to make that play. It gives us the ability to go to the next level, and consistency, in every play, is what we really have to work on.”
Williams has regularly stated he wants to be considered among the best in the league, but has fallen short of that standard this season.
"We have to get him completely refocused on making wide-open catches, contested catches. He's doing great in the run game," Montgomery said. "He's doing some things that we really like to see , but we're talking about greatness. We're not just chasing, hey, man, he’s a good player in this league.
"I want him to be among the best, and I think that he has the opportunity to do that if we can clean up some of the things that you're talking about.”

title: What DC Kelvin Sheppard Feels Is 'Ultra Disrespectful' Narrative
full_text:
Detroit Lions defensive coordinator Kelvin Sheppard finds it "ultra disrespectful" the current narrative surrounding the 2026 team is the offense must carry the whole roster.
The former NFL linebacker still believes his unit can carry their weight, sharing with local reporters, ". "We're gonna do our one-third here, hell or high water. Point blank period."
Unfortunately, the defensive unit has completely lost the trust of supporters, due to coverage breakdowns, poor tackling against the Panthers and not being able to keep opponents out of the end zone in the first four games.
Sheppard is not going to make drastic changes to the defense. In fact, he defended the amount of blitzes called against the Panthers, indicating he believed they were the right calls.
Adjustments will be made, personnel groupings were be modified, especially when Brian Branch returns in the near future. The hope is the defense will rally together and right the ship quickly, as Sheppard is currently on the hot seat.
Head coach Dan Campbell was asked earlier this week about the perception he is holding the offense to a higher standard than the defense, based on comments he made during a recent radio interview.
“Well look, my message to the offense is, we came into this thing saying that we had our standards for the way we wanted this offense to run. That was my message to the offense," said Campbell. "So, if we're okay offensively with what we've done, then we're not looking at it the right way because it's not good enough. That was a message to the offense is what that was. Defensively, we just need to get in the right position. Let's get in the right position. Let's be where we're supposed to be.
"We'll make a couple little tweaks here personnel wise and get these guys in the proper places," Campbell added. "It won't be perfect, but at least if we know that we're fitting the right gaps where we're supposed to be in these zone drops, we give ourselves a better chance .”
Quarterback Jared Goff also does not believe the offense needs to carry thet team, indicating the goals remain especially high, including being the best offense in the National Football League.
“No, I think I feel like the offense is capable of a lot more and I think that we would all agree with that. Again, I think the sentiment is we have been good," said Goff. "We've done some good things, and we've scored and had some good drives, but we haven't been great. And we're very, very capable of being great and above that. We want to be the best offense in the League and we have to start playing like it.”

title: Detroit Lions Official Against Cardinals Presents Concerning Challenge
full_text:
The Detroit Lions have drawn Carl Cheffers as the head referee for their Week 5 game against the Arizona Cardinals.
In his career as a head referee, Cheffers has officiated 15 Lions games. Detroit is 6-9 in those games, with a loss in their most recent game in 2025. That game was the team's Week 16 contest against the Pittsburgh Steelers, and it featured a controversial ending.
The Lions drove late in the game with a chance to win, reaching the Steelers' 1-yard line with less than 30 seconds remaining. Quarterback Jared Goff connected with Amon-Ra St. Brown for what appeared to be the go-ahead touchdown, but it was nullified by an offensive pass interference penalty.
Later in the drive, the Lions snapped the ball with eight seconds remaining and Goff connected with Amon-Ra St. Brown. After being stood up, St. Brown lateraled to Goff who reached into the end zone. However, that play was also nullified as St. Brown was whistled for offensive pass interference for pushing off his defender.
Cheffers is one of the longest-tenured officials in the league, having served as a head official since 2008. He has presided over three Super Bowls, with the first being the New England Patriots' infamous rally from a 28-3 deficit to defeat the Atlanta Falcons.
Additionally, Cheffers officiated the Tampa Bay Buccaneers' Super Bowl win over the Kansas City Chiefs in the 2020 season and the Kansas City Chiefs' win over the Philadelphia Eagles in the 2022 season.
His four assignments up to this point this season include the Giants' win over Dallas in Week 1, the Steelers' loss to the Patriots in Week 2, Washington's win over Seattle in Week 3 and the Chicago Bears' defeat of the New York Jets last week.
Cheffers' crew ranks sixth in terms of flags thrown this season with 63. His highest total in a single game this year was 19, which came in Week 1 in the primetime matchup between Giants and Cowboys.
The veteran official's two highest counts of penalty flags thrown include false start and delay of game. He has thrown seven defensive pass interference flags, and six offensive holding flags.
Detroit will be looking to get to 3-2 on the season with a victory Sunday leading into their bye week in Week 6.

title: Pros and Cons of Lions Trading for Kansas City Chiefs Cornerback
full_text:
The Detroit Lions ' secondary needs answers.
Through four games, the Lions have unfortunately made a case for the title of the NFL's worst defenses. They rank near the bottom of the league in several categories, and have left more to be desired during their 2-2 start.
Because of the struggles in the secondary, as well as the depleted personnel, many believe the Lions would benefit from making an addition to their secondary via a trade ahead of the Nov. 11 deadline.
The safety group is set to get deeper with Brian Branch returning to practice this week, but the cornerback position has endured a plethora of struggles early in the season.
One possible option that the Lions could consider is veteran Kristian Fulton, who is currently in the final year of his contract with the Kansas City Chiefs. Fulton is still owed $5 million of his $9.75 million salary, but the Lions could have the space to add him onto the books.
Fulton was suggested as a potential trade target for the Lions by ESPN's Jeremy Fowler , who noted the team's need for secondary help.
"One potential option is Kansas City's Kristian Fulton, who is in and out of the Chiefs' lineup," Fowler wrote. "He is owed real money -- $5 million of his $9.75 million base salary is guaranteed -- but perhaps the Chiefs and Lions could split the bill to facilitate a deal. Is it worth calling Pittsburgh for Jalen Ramsey? Not sure he's available, but the Lions' defense seems far from settled."
Up to this point this year, Fulton has earned a 76.0 Pro Football Focus defensive grade on 115 defensive snaps. His role has diminished, including not playing a snap against the Dolphins in Week 3, throughout the last two weeks with rookie Mansoor Delane returning to the lineup after a Week 1 injury.
Fulton recorded an interception against the Indianapolis Colts in Week 2, and has notched seven total tackles this season. However, he is in the final year of a two-year pact he signed with the Chiefs, and with the team drafting Delane in the first-round of the draft this year could be viewed as expendable moving forward.
Meanwhile, the Lions are still looking to find reliable options at the cornerback position. D.J. Reed and Roger McCreary are the current starting options, with McCreary usurping Rock Ya-Sin. Ennis Rakestraw is also in the mix, and rookie Keith Abney II could get more work moving forward amidst the secondary's struggles.
If the Lions were to make a move for Fulton , it would likely require a Day 3 pick in return based on the market. This could be a worthwhile price for the Lions to pay, and even if Fulton is not an elite option he would at the very least give the team some depth and another reliable veteran presence.
Detroit seems to be intrigued with Rakestraw's performance in recent weeks, and as a result may not be as willing to crowd the depth chart and take opportunities away from him. However, acquiring Fulton could also put some pressure on Reed, as he has not lived up to expectations after signing a three-year deal last year.
Ultimately, adding another experienced option would be beneficial for the Lions. Even as a one-year rental, Fulton has some upside and could help Detroit's cornerback room recover from a tough start.

title: Burning Question: Can Brian Branch Save Detroit Lions Defense?
full_text:
The Detroit Lions welcomed back two players who could make an impact in the second quarter of the 2026 NFL season.
It is not expected that center Cade Mays and defensive back Brian Branch, two players who were limited in practice on Wednesday afternoon, to suit up before the bye week.
Branch is returning back from a torn Achilles suffered last season. Speaking to reporters, he expressed gratefulness for those that helped him to return and a readiness to get back to playing in Kelvin Sheppard's defense.
"It was very fun. I missed being back out there. It's been a long time coming. What 10 months? There's nothing like being back out there, especially with this group of guys," Branch explained to local reporters, following his first practice of the 2026 NFL season. "Just getting back in the groove of things. I just loved being back out there. I love this game and you can't take this game for granted.
"That's what this taught me during this time off. You can't take nothing for granted. I told Dan (Campbell) I'm starving since I got injured. Just day by day been working and grinding. I'm getting the rust off now in practice. I feel good. I'm ready to go. Since I got injured, just been day by day, been working, been grinding. Showing up at 7 a.m., Fisch, (strength and conditioning Josh) Schuler, everybody had their part in it with me and I want to thank all them for that.”
Branch has the ability, when healthy, to be a versatile defensive back who can make plays against opposing tight ends. With the team wanting to be stout against the run, Branch being around the line of scrimmage is an added benefit.
His positional flexibility can assist Sheppard to find the right mix of defensive backs to utilize in nickel formation.
Christian Izien did not have a good performance against the Carolina Panthers, as he struggled in both zone and man-to-man coverage and was among the many players who missed tackles on Sunday Night Football.
One of the areas the Lions must improve quickly is getting off the field on field third-down defensively. If Branch can be a physical presence and disrupt opposing offensive weapons running down the field, it will not be as easy as it has been for opponents to find their way into the end zone.
While Branch and any lone player cannot save the defense , as he steadily gains confidence and makes plays, Detroit's defense should improve.
Detroit also will adjust their personnel against the Arizona Cardinals this week. Rookie defensive back Keith Abney could have an expanded role along with veteran Jalen Mills.

title: Detroit Lions Week 5 Wednesday Injury Report: DT, CB, OL Out
full_text:
The Detroit Lions returned to the practice field for the first time, to begin their preparation for a Week 5 road contest against the Arizona Cardinals.
Those not spotted at the portion of practice open to the media included defensive tackle Tyleik Williams, guard Ben Bartch and cornerback Rock Ya-Sin.
Williams is considered day-to-day, while Ya-Sin is likely to miss some game action.
Prior to practice, head coach Dan Campbell confirmed that both safety Brian Branch and center Cade Mays would hit the practice field on Wednesday.
It is not expected that Branch will suit up against the Cardinals, especially since the team has their bye next week.
Additional Detroit Lions NFL Insider Analysis: After Six Years, Dan Campbell Has Officially Been "Lionized"
Campbell expressed it could take a minute for Branch to execute at peak capacity.
"Look, we know there’s going to be a little bit of kicking the rust off just to get back into all of those, back to the player that he was. It’ll take a minute," said Campbell. "However, he’s an instinctive, aware player and he is a violent player. And so he’s got a knack for the football and his production, even if it’s not what it was in the immediate, as he grows back to that will have an impact, I believe."
Branch has remained involved in meetings, but the defense will welcome back a player that is aggressive and has a knack for being around the football.
"We’ve been as smart as we can be with that, making sure that he is physically ready to practice. And I don’t want to say conservative, but yet let’s make sure, and make sure, and make sure," Campbell said. "That’s Step 1, and then look, he’s been in meetings, he’s able to watch walk-through , he can’t participate up until this point, so he’s stayed in it mentally but it’s not the same as taking reps.
"I think that’s the big thing is, yes, he’s been there mentally but so much of it has been let’s focus on the rehab, the rehabilitation, and making sure that we’re all in there," Campbell added. "Because if we don’t get that right, the rest of it doesn’t matter. And I feel really good about both of those guys. I feel like those guys are prepared."

title: 2 Defensive Changes Lions Must Make After First Quarter of Season
full_text:
The Detroit Lions defense has been facing plenty of scrutiny over the past several weeks.
After a first half shutout of the New Orleans Saints in the season opener, the Lions' defense has been picked apart over the course of their 2-2 start. In their two losses, the defense has been a big reason why the team hasn't been able to emerge victorious.
The group ranks near the bottom of the league in many categories defensively, which has led to defensive coordinator Kelvin Sheppard facing plenty of criticism. However, the team has a chance to get things right starting with their Week 5 matchup with the Arizona Cardinals.
Here are two defensive scheme changes Sheppard and the Lions could make that could be beneficial to their chances of performing at a higher level moving forward.
With all the concern about the team's affinity for man coverage, this is an argument that may seem confusing at first. After all, the Lions' secondary issues should them playing less man coverage as opposed to more.
However, the Lions have proven to stick to their ways throughout Dan Campbell's tenure as head coach, and as a result there's reason to believe the Lions won't be going completely away from it any time soon.
With Aidan Hutchinson , Alim McNeill and D.J. Wonnum all having multiple sacks early in the season, the team would likely benefit from bringing their corners down closer to the line of scrimmage to play more press coverage.
Detroit is middle of the pack in pressure rate, meaning they could have the ability to get after quarterbacks more if they are forced to hold onto the ball longer.
Throughout the first four games, the Lions have played plenty of off-man coverage. While this gives the cornerbacks more opportunity to stay back on opponents, it also allows wide receivers the opportunity to separate quicker.
By putting more pressure on opposing wide receivers, Detroit's defensive backfield could do their pass-rush a favor and force quarterbacks to hold the ball longer, which could lead to more sacks.
With the Lions' affinity for man coverage, most looks are with either no high safety or one. Scattered throughout Sunday's film are reps where the single safety is lined up 15 yards off the ball, which leads to some inefficiencies in the run game.
Having a presence in the run game from a safety is very important, especially with the struggles the Lions are having at the linebacker position. This is an area where Brian Branch's return could be very impactful, as he's proven to be a reliable tackler throughout his career.
Detroit having a deep safety so far from the play opens up the possibility for more big runs, as they are forced to take pristine angles or risk missing the tackle due to running backs beng shifty in the open field.
If Detroit elects to bring the safeties down closer to the line, say 10 yards instead of 15, they run the risk of not having deep coverage on vertical routes. However, they also allow themselves more insurance in the run game.

title: Why I Don't Trust Detroit Lions GM Brad Holmes To Sign Good Cornerbacks
full_text:
Detroit Lions general manager Brad Holmes actually did proclaim once that he loved sitting in the film room to watch defensive backs play.
"I love corner play," Holmes said at the 2024 NFL scouting combine. "I just love it. I could watch DB individuals all day every day. It’s poetry in motion. I love DB play. But yeah, we just want to get the right fit."
Holmes later added, "They’re not growing on trees. Although that’s arguably, them and wide receivers, probably the most volumous group, position group in the draft. But that doesn’t mean that they’re all going to be good, especially as high as you might have to pick them, because of their physical qualities. If you get wooed by the physical qualities too much but they don’t have the intangible qualities you can get yourself in trouble."
Unfortunately, after six years on the job, there is no other conclusion to draw other than he is not aware of what a good cornerback looks like.
Since his arrival, the former Los Angeles Rams Director of College Scouting has an abysmal cornerback track record, both in the draft and in free agency.
In 2024, he targeted Terrion Arnold and Ennis Rakestraw with the Lions first two picks. Unfortunately, the Philadelphia Eagles were able to land two better defensive backs (Quinyon Mitchell and Cooper DeJean) with their two early picks in that year.
Ifeatu Melifonwu could not stay healthy, as he was the Lions 2021 third-round draft choice. He is no longer with the team.
Free agency has also been horrid for Holmes.
Cam Sutton was cut after an arrest warrant became public. Holmes invested $33 million in the veteran in March of 2023.
Emmanuel Moseley also did not work out. Injuries derailed his chances to succeed in Motown.
Even when good defensive backs find their way to Detroit, Holmes has been too cheap to keep them around.
Darius Slay expressed the biggest mistake made by the Lions was letting Carlton Davis depart. After making the decision to trade for him, the team allowed him to depart in free agency to the New England Patriots, where he has excelled.
Commanders veteran Amik Roberston is certainly a better nickel cornerback than what the Lions feature presently.
Khalil Dorsey has found his niche on special teams, but he is not a starting caliber cornerback.
Kindle Vildor has bounced around the league, but Lions' fans are only going to remember him for the football bouncing off his head against the 49ers in the 2023 NFC Championship Game.
D.J. Reed has lost a step and is nowhere near worth his $16 million salary. He is having a slow start to the season and is coming off a bad game against the Carolina Panthers.
With how poor the defense is, with the secondary not able to execute in either zone or man-to-man coverage this season, is it not really conceivable that Holmes can fix the problem.
The front office reportedly tried to land Joey Porter Jr., but he is now with the Dallas Cowboys. All other options seem not as appealing at this point.
This writer is at the point that if Holmes targets a defensive back, something is likely wrong with that player, whether it be injury related or a lack of coverage skills needed to play at the NFL level.
Pundits are now floating many names that Holmes should target, but if the defensive coordinator also is in over his head, how can that formula actually be expected to work.
A poor cornerback evaluator with a poor defensive coordinator.
The math ain't mathin to make anyone feel better about improving the secondary that much this season.

title: With Chris Brooks Sidelined, Packers Add ‘Dawg’ to Running Backs
full_text:
GREEN BAY, Wis. – The Green Bay Packers took a 52-man roster (one less than the limit) and an 18-man practice squad (one over the limit) out to the practice field on Thursday.
The Packers on Thursday afternoon promoted running back Pierre Strong from the practice squad, where he will take the place of last week’s starter, Chris Brooks, on the roster against the Chicago Bears on Sunday. They also made official the signing of linebacker Jack Dingle to the practice squad.
With Kristian Welch taking Edgerrin Cooper's place on the roster, the Packers filled Welch's spot on the practice squad with a high-RAS linebacker. https://t.co/9HI2a5cg4A
Brooks suffered an ankle injury during last week’s win at Tampa Bay.
“We’re going to give him another day, see where he’s at tomorrow and then, obviously, make a decision after that,” coach Matt LaFleur said before practice .
As it turns out, the Packers moved quickly rather than waiting until Friday or even Saturday, when they usually make their final roster moves before gameday.
That Brooks presumably won’t be available against Chicago is no surprise. The Packers re-signed Damon Bankston to the practice squad earlier in the week, a sign that Strong would be needed in the game and someone would be needed for the scout team.
With a keen eye for cutback lanes and above-average acceleration, Strong was the team’s most productive running back during training camp.
“The cutback, pass pro, hands out the backfield, anything on special teams,” Strong said after the final preseason game. “I consider myself a dawg. I can do it all.”
It appeared he had put himself in position to make the roster through a combination of his performance and Josh Jacobs landing on the exempt list. Instead, during final roster cuts, the Packers acquired Kaleb Johnson from the Steelers and released Strong.
Strong was a fourth-round pick by the Patriots in 2022. After spending his rookie year with New England and the 2023 and 2024 seasons with Cleveland, he failed to make the Browns’ roster in 2025. The Packers signed him to the practice squad, and that’s where he spent the entire season without playing in a game.
“I’m hungry. I’m always going to be hungry,” he said. “Practice squad, 53-man roster. I’m still hungry, but I’m very hungry now. So, I want to get back to where I’ve been.”
He might get his chance against the Bears. The other healthy backs on the roster are MarShawn Lloyd and Johnson. Lloyd, a third-round pick in 2024, has carried the ball 30 times for a team-high 81 yards – a paltry 2.7-yard average. Johnson has carried the ball 20 times or 80 yards, a 4.0-yard average highlighted by a 31-yard run against the Bucs.
Both players fumbled in the game, though. LaFleur’s patience had worn thin, raising the possibility of benching players who put the ball on the ground.
Strong has carried the ball 99 times in three seasons with a 5.0-yard average. Plus, he contributed 17 tackles on special teams. This preseason, he carried the ball 15 times for 58 yards (3.9 average) and had a 68-yard kickoff return at Denver.
“Obviously he made some big plays not only in the kicking game but did a nice job running the ball,” offensive coordinator Adam Stenavich said a few days later. “We’ve got to get him going a little bit more in protections on third down, things like that, get him the ball in his hands in the passing game just to see how he does there, but he’s done a nice job so I’ve very encouraged by what I’ve seen from him so far.”
Strong hasn’t played in a game since the 2024 finale at Miami. Asked what it would mean to make the roster, Strong at the end of the preseason said, “The world, you know? It ain’t even about me no more. I just brought my little girl in the world, so everything I do is for her. So, it’s just like, I want her to grow up and watch her father play football. So, like I said, it’d mean the world to me. Where I’m at right now, millions of kids wish they were here. So, I’m just staying. I’m going to stay and grind.”
The Packers have tossed aside their usual roster-building philosophy by adding a bunch of veterans. So, with the running game struggling, this big, powerful veteran would be a potential fit. ⬇️ https://t.co/xNBgyd9wFN
