title: Texans Add New Trio to Practice Squad, Lose Noteworthy DB to Rival
full_text:
The Houston Texans have made a several roster changes following the events of their Week 4 loss to the Dallas Cowboys — all of which came from their practice squad.
Per KPRC2 's Aaron Wilson, the Texans hosted visits for cornerback Jaden Davis and running back Deuce Vaughn on Tuesday, and will be signing both to their practice squad.
Wilson notes that Houston hosted a visit with free agent linebacker Chad Muma, who CBS Sports ' Matt Zenitz also signed to the practice squad.
The #Texans are signing linebacker Chad Muma to their practice squad, sources tell @CBSSports . Former 2022 third-round draft pick with 103 career tackles. pic.twitter.com/xTPVH0uThn
In the process of the Texans' three signings, though, they also wound up losing out on one of their practice squad defensive backs, Alijah Huzzie, who has been signed to the Jacksonville Jaguars' roster.
It's a lot to take in as it relates to the Texans' practice squad movement. So to break things down a little easier, let's sort through each of Houston's new additions (and their single departure) one by one, and sort through why each move might matter heading into Week 5:
Vaughn, a 5-foot-6, 176-pound running back out of Kansas State, was selected in the sixth round of the 2023 NFL Draft by the Dallas Cowboys
Vaughn has played 16 career games throughout his two years in the league––both of which being with the Cowboys––where he recorded 40 rushing attempts for 110 yards, along with 10 catches for 58 yards.
Why the Texans Signed Him: The Texans' running back depth is pretty shallow right now. Outside of their regular contributors on offense, David Montgomery and Woody Marks, Houston has three backs between their roster and practice squad: Dare Ogunbowale, British Brooks (injured reserve) , and Jawhar Jordan. Adding Vaughn gives Houston another layer of security at the position with someone who hasn't played in an NFL game since 2024, yet has some appealing quickness and ability to work as a runner and pass-catcher that helps his stock.
Davis, a 5-foot-10, 182-pound defensive back out of Miami, was selected in the seventh round of the 2024 NFL Draft by the Arizona Cardinals.
He's played in three career games with the Cardinals, all of which came in 2025, where he recorded three tackles with a little over 60 total snaps played.
Why the Texans Signed Him: The Texans' cornerback depth saw a couple of changes on Tuesday. For one, they saw Jaylin Smith hit injured reserve with a hamstring injury. But Houston also lost Alijah Huzzie to the Jaguars in a move will discuss a bit more later. But with that in mind, it felt obvious the Texans were going to add some form of depth within their secondary, and Davis winds up being just that.
Muma, a 6-foot-3, 239-pound linebacker out of Wyoming, was selected in the third round by the Jaguars in the 2022 NFL Draft, and has gone on to turn into a five-year NFL veteran playing for Jacksonville, the Indianapolis Colts, and the Jacksonville Jaguars.
He's played in 58 career games, recording 103 tackles, three TFLs, 1.5 sacks, and three passes defended. He's also been listed as a starter for seven games.
Why the Texans Signed Him: The Texans have had to shuffle around their linebacker room in recent days because of the groin injury to sideline Azeez Al-Shaair for Week 4 against Dallas . That led to Kenneth Murray being elevated to the 53-man roster as the green-dot signal caller and starting linebacker on the defense, yet he would go down with a concussion at the end of the game.
So Murray might be sidelined for at least one game, and we don't know much about Al-Shaair's availability for Week 5 just yet. Adding a linebacker felt due, and it winds up being Muma.
Alijah Huzzie, a 5-foot-10, 195-pound defensive back who's been with Houston dating back to the 2025 season, has been a bit of a fixture on their practice squad as someone who could even be worthy of a 53-man roster spot.
Many projected Huzzie to make the 53-man roster before the start of the season as a depth corner and backup nickel to Jalen Pitre, yet he would wind up falling short of that nod. He wound up on the practice squad, and in short time, he's now on another AFC South team in Jacksonville less than five weeks into the new year.
It matters for the Texans in two ways: one, Houston loses a talented defender in Huzzie; someone who's been in the system for close to a year, and might've been worthy of a 53-man roster spot over one of the five tight ends or six linebackers the team decided to bring onto the roster, yet now heads elsewhere for nothing.
Two, Huzzie's departure comes at a time in which his services could be utilized by the Texans now that Jaylin Smith is going to miss some time. Whether it be as a backup nickel or a contributor on special teams, a role could've easily been there for Huzzie to make his mark on Houston’s roster for Week 5.
That fit for Huzzie, though, now resides in Jacksonville––a team that the Texans will coincidentally be facing up against as soon as Week 6 in London, so expect a bit of a reunion to take place for both sides.

title: Texans Should Be Concerned About Latest Injury to CB Jaylin Smith
full_text:
It looks like the Houston Texans will be without some depth in their secondary for at least the next four weeks.
That's because second-year cornerback Jaylin Smith has been placed on injured reserve.
According to KPRC2 's Aaron Wilson, Smith is reportedly dealing with a Grade 2 hamstring injury that'll effectively sideline him for multiple weeks, thus leading to the Texans placing him on injured reserve.
Smith had been receiving secondary opinions on the hamstring injury he had suffered this past week against the Dallas Cowboys. However, it won't prevent him from missing a bit of time in the Texans' lineup, which is seemingly becoming a bit of a trend for the young second-year corner.
With the newest absence now forcing Smith out of the mix for the next few weeks, this now marks the third time that the Texans have been forced to place him on injured reserve throughout his young career.
Smith has played in eight of his 23 available games between the regular season and playoffs with the Texans thus far, and will be slated to miss the next four, at the very least.
Smith was sidelined for four games just two weeks into the 2025 season with a similar hamstring injury before returning in Week 8 against the San Francisco 49ers . Just one game later, though, Smith would suffer a torn meniscus against the Denver Broncos to sit him out for the remainder of the year.
Wilson reporting that there is optimism for Smith's eventual return to the lineup is certainly encouraging that he won't be missing the entire season. Once those four weeks on injured reserve are up after Week 9 against the LA Chargers, then perhaps the team can re-evaluate.te.
However, seeing that this is now the third instance of Smith missing extended time, you can't help but be a little bit concerned about what his future looks like as a valuable piece in Houston.
Smith was brought in just a little over a year ago with a day two pick in the 2025 NFL Draft with hopes of being a valuable future asset in the secondary, largely because of his versatility and prowess in man-coverage.
Yet, nearly a season and a half into his career, Smith hasn't really had a chance to show off the appealing skills Houston initially brought him in for.
And for the next few weeks, it'll be the same case.
Smith has only recorded 38 defensive snaps through the eight games he's been active in thus far, with only seven of those coming this season. Instead, he's been a primary part of Houston's special teams game, as he's been on the field for 65% of their special teams snaps this season.
Since he arrived last spring, the Texans have liked what Smith brought to the table as a future CB3 behind Derek Stingley and Kamari Lassiter . However, without being able to stay consistently healthy, now approaching his third IR designation in a little over 20 games, it hurts his chances of being able to cling onto a bigger role in the secondary––both in the short and long term.
For the stretch that Smith is forced out of the mix, however long that may be, we can expect for Tremon Smith to claim those CB3 duties, and the primary backup to fill in on the boundary behind Stingley and Lassiter.
For the stretch that Jaylin Smith was out over the course of his rookie season, it was now-nine-year veteran Tremon Smith who stepped up to the occasion for his role and played relatively well throughout the season too.
Over the course of his 2025 campaign, Smith recorded 23 total tackles, two passes defended, and a forced fumble while also being available in all 17 games.
So considering the team was in this same spot last year, expect the Texans to lean on Tremon Smith a bit more while shorthanded in their cornerback room, both as a depth piece in their secondary and a contributor on special teams.

title: Colts-Steelers Thursday Injury Report: Colts Get Promising News as Steelers Lose Major Piece
full_text:
The injury reports for the Indianapolis Colts and Pittsburgh Steelers are starting to take shape.
Both Indianapolis and Pittsburgh released their initial injury reports on Wednesday , giving us a look at which players are in jeopardy of missing out on the Week 5 clash. But Thursday provided some more clarity as to who’s going to be available and who will be watching from the sidelines.
Let’s take a look at both teams’ reports with one more practice to go before Sunday’s game.
Indianapolis Colts Injury Report (As of 10/8)
Positive news for center Tanor Bortolini and linebacker Akeem Davis-Gaither. Bortolini practiced, albeit in a limited fashion, while wearing knee and elbow braces. Interestingly, the Colts only list the ankle as an issue, so definitely something worth monitoring. Getting Davis-Gaither back to full participation is huge, too, as Indy can’t afford another change at the green dot. Tight end Will Mallory had his second full practice in a row as well. Indy may elect to use caution with him coming off a thumb injury, but Mallory is certainly trending in the right direction and could play this weekend.
#Colts starting C Tanor Bortolini, who did not practice yesterday due to a right ankle injury, *is* practicing today. He has a brace on his right ankle as well as a brace on his left arm/elbow. pic.twitter.com/qg5TkM71nc
Only defensive tackle Grover Stewart is new to the injury report on his rest day, but Charvarius Ward is now listed with a groin issue after getting Wednesday off to rest. Another situation worth monitoring. No practice for Arden Key, as he’ll miss significant time with his hamstring injury . Jonathan Taylor was back to a regular workload after a rest day to start the week.
It could be another week with slim pickings at wide receiver for Indianapolis. Keenan Allen, a limited participant in back-to-back days, has not made any progress as he works back from a groin injury. Ashton Dulin remains week-to-week with his hamstring injury. Having not practiced at all Wednesday or Thursday, he’s trending towards another week on the sidelines. That could open the door for Darius Slayton to make his Colts debut. Slayton signed with the Colts on Sept. 22 but hasn’t dressed in the two games he’s been available for, so a chance to make a strong first impression for the 29-year-old.
Linebacker Jaylon Carlies is the third Colt with back-to-back days as a non-participant, putting his chances to play up in the air. Bryce Boettcher is the backup WILL linebacker if Carlies doesn’t suit up, but the Colts would be remiss if they didn’t give their top draft choice in CJ Allen a chance to make an impact. Allen, despite being drafted 53rd overall, has found snaps hard to come by thus far , logging just 11 across the first four games.
Overall, there’s definitely some positive news on the injury front for the Colts. Getting Mallory back to full health is a plus, and if Davis-Gaither and Bortolini are fit enough to play, both would go a long way towards maintaining continuity and chemistry on their respective sides of the ball. Ward and Carlies are the key ones to watch, as either one of them being unavailable changes the equation defensively. But there's plenty of reasons for optimism otherwise.
Pittsburgh Steelers Injury Report (As of 10/8)
The major news for Pittsburgh is that wide receiver Michael Pittman Jr. not only is trending in the wrong direction (was a limited participant on Wednesday), but he’s expected to miss several weeks after raggravating the foot injury that’s held him out of practice this week. So a hit to the top of their wide receiver depth chart. From a Colts perspective, they will have to wait to play against Pittman for the first time since trading him to the Steelers in March.
Steelers HC Mike McCarthy said WR Michael Pittman re-injured his foot and now is expected to miss multiple weeks. pic.twitter.com/4YEtQaKuCP
Cornerback Jalen Ramsey improved from not participating Wednesday to practicing in a limited capacity. Good news for the Steelers secondary, which also opened safety DeShon Elliott’s practice window as he’s been on injured reserve with a knee injury. However, Jamel Dean has missed two straight practices, suggesting he’s a longshot to play on Sunday.
No progress for Rico Dowdle, whose two straight days as a limited participant make him a coin toss for Sunday. Dowdle has missed the last two weeks and is yet to log a full practice, so he’s likely to miss his third consecutive game.
Cam Heyward was back to full participation after a rest day. The 37-year-old veteran remains one of Pittsburgh’s most valuable pieces.
Looking at how the week has gone thus far, Pittsburgh would’ve hoped to be in a better position by now. But instead, they’re down at least one offense skill player for several weeks, likely without their backup running back and are banged up in the secondary. Friday will be crucial for the team to figure out who they’ll be playing without as they look to maintain a home winning streak against Indianapolis that stretches back to 2008.

title: Colts Quarter-Season Report Card: Surprises, Disappointments Through Four Games
full_text:
Just like that, a quarter of the NFL season has come and gone.
It’s been an eventful first four weeks in Indianapolis. The Indianapolis Colts started out with back-to-back losses, but rebounded and now sit at 2-2, good for second place in the AFC South.
Some players have come out of nowhere to emerge as surprise contributors, while others haven’t lived up to their potential. Here’s a look at which Colts players have surprised, and who’s disappointed through four games.
DeForest Buckner’s play through this first quarter has been a pleasant surprise. Coming off a neck injury which caused him to miss seven games last season and undergo surgery, the expectations for what Buckner could provide coming off the operation were on the ground. Whatever he could produce would be a bonus.
But Buckner has roared out to a tremendous start. His three sacks and four tackles for loss in four games both lead the team. He’s been one of the few bright spots for a Colts pass rush which has been highly ineffective so far. With injuries continuing to pile up at defensive end, Buckner has remained a consistent source of disruption from the interior.
At 32 years old and coming off a major injury, Buckner wasn’t expected to be carrying the Colts’ pass rush, especially this early in the season. Instead, he has looked like the same disruptive force Indianapolis has relied on since his arrival in 2020.
Like Buckner, Spencer Shrader entered this season with questions to answer regarding an injury. His 2025 season was off to a great start, but ended abruptly due to a knee injury.
Shrader not only got back healthy, but barely beat Blake Grupe out for the kicking job in training camp and is now off to a tremendous start. Aside from missing his first PAT attempt of the season, Shrader’s been otherwise perfect. He’s made all 11 of his field goal tries, with 8 of the 11 coming from beyond 40 yards.
Shrader has quickly become a weapon for the Colts, and has been a lifesaver for an offense which has struggled to score touchdowns at the same high rate they did a season ago.
Akeem Davis-Gaither has been one of the biggest surprises for the Colts after signing as a free agent in March.
Davis-Gaither entered 2026 as a relatively unheralded addition to a linebacker room that had plenty of questions surrounding it. Instead, he has become an important piece of the Colts’ defense.
Davis-Gaither leads the team with 37 tackles through four games and has played nearly every defensive snap along the way. He has also taken on the green-dot responsibilities as the defense’s primary communicator.
His impact was particularly evident in Week 4, when Davis-Gaither recorded eight tackles and helped anchor a defense that allowed just 13 points to Washington. He was also named to PFF’s Week 4 Team of the Week .
Davis-Gaither was never expected to be a defensive focal point when he signed with Indianapolis, but four games in, anf it's difficult to imagine where the Colts’ defense may be without him.
Matt Goncalves has quietly become one of the Colts’ most valuable pieces through the first four games.
After playing tackle in college and as a rookie, Goncalves made the transition to right guard in 2025 and started all 16 games at the position. He was solid in his first season there, but the Colts needed him to take another step forward in 2026.
So far, he has done exactly that.
Goncalves has started all four games, earning a 81.6 PFF grade, which ranks ninth among 74 qualified guards. He's allowed just two pressures and one sack in pass protection and is yet to be penalized.
His play has helped make the interior of the Colts’ offensive line a strength, with PFF ranking Indy’s offensive line third in the NFL entering Week 5 and specifically highlighting Goncalves as one of the unit’s strongest performers.
Goncalves entered the season as a promising young player still establishing himself at guard. Four games in, he looks like another great find on the offensive line by the Colts scouting department.
The first four weeks of the season have been a sobering reminder of the quarterback that Daniel Jones has been most of his career.
While Jones played some of the best football of his career in his first 10 games with the Colts, leading the team to an NFL-best 8-2 record, he hasn’t been on the same level in 2026.
Jones finished his injury-shortened 2025 with 3,101 passing yards, 19 touchdowns, eight interceptions and a 100.2 passer rating. Through four games this season, he has 754 passing yards, three touchdowns, four interceptions and a 73.9 passer rating. His yards per attempt has also dropped from 8.1 to 5.7.
But the biggest concern has been his inability to protect the football. Jones has committed at least one turnover in every game this season and has already accounted for seven of the Colts’ eight total  turnovers.
That is a dramatic departure from the version of Jones the Colts saw last season, and it has made his uneven play one of the team's biggest issues through the first month of 2026.
One of the most confusing storylines of the season so far is the lack of involvement for CJ Allen. The Colts drafted Allen 53rd overall this past April as the first player in their draft class. With glaring holes at linebacker, the expectation was that Allen would have an impact right away.
Instead, Allen has hardly gotten an opportunity .
The rookie has only appeared in two of four games so far, managing one tackle in just 11 snaps. As a result, Allen is one of the most difficult Colts players to evaluate. But it’s clear that he hasn’t lived up to what was expected of him.
If there’s any chance for Allen to turn things around, it could be this week against Pittsburgh. Both Davis-Gaither and Jaylon Carlies appeared on Wednesday’s injury report , so there’s a window of opportunity for Allen. Should either one of them not be 100 percent on Sunday, then the rookie could see the most snaps of his young career to date.
But until that happens, the first quarter of Allen’s rookie season has been nothing short of a disaster.
Alec Pierce’s 2025 breakout season created plenty of excitement for what he could do in his second year with Daniel Jones. Instead, his 2026 season has been derailed by injury.
Pierce recorded 1,003 receiving yards and six touchdowns last season, establishing himself as one of the league’s biggest big-play threats and earning a massive four-year, $114 million contract extension. The expectation was that he would build on that success this season and remain one of the Colts’ most important weapons in the passing game.
That hasn’t happened. Pierce suffered a heel injury in Week 2 and was subsequently placed on injured reserve, with his availability for the remainder of the season unclear. His absence has left Indianapolis without its most dangerous downfield weapon at a time when the passing game has already struggled.
There’s still time for Pierce to return and make an impact, but his inability to stay on the field has prevented him from building on his breakout 2025 campaign. If he were at least able to stay on the field, then this could be a much different conversation.
Laiatu Latu entered his third NFL season with the expectation to take another step forward and emerging as a go-to pass rush maestro. Instead, the former first-round pick has gone backward.
Latu recorded 8.5 sacks and 45 tackles last season, establishing himself as one of the Colts’ most important pieces along the defensive line. This year, Latu has just one sack and 13 total pressures, with his 60.0 PFF pass-rush grade ranking 68th among 110 qualified edge defenders.
Latu's individual struggles are also a symptom of a horrific pass rush unit as a collective. Per Next Gen Stats, the Colts' 25.5% pressure rate through four games ranks dead last in the NFL.
There have been flashes, including a sack of Marcus Mariota last week, but Latu hasn’t consistently created the kind of pressure the Colts need from him. His lack of impact, plus injuries…

title: Sauce Gardner Takes Accountability After Ugly Week 4 Showing
full_text:
The Indianapolis Colts walked away from London with their second straight victory on Sunday, but it was a completely different storyline for star cornerback Sauce Gardner.
Gardner put together arguably the worst performance of his NFL career against the Washington Commanders, and he isn't making any excuses for it.
According to NFL Pro and Next Gen Stats, Gardner allowed four receptions on five targets for 117 yards and a touchdown, the most receiving yards he has surrendered in a single game throughout his career.
To make matters worse, much of that damage came against seventh-round rookie Athan Kaliakmanis, who was forced into action after Marcus Mariota suffered a knee injury in the first quarter.
Gardner also allowed a 156.3 passer rating when targeted, tied for the highest mark among cornerbacks in Week 4, via PFF.
But surprisingly, those coverage numbers weren't even Gardner's biggest concern when he went back and watched the film.
"I wasn't giving my best effort. I wasn't really giving my best effort in the run game," Gardner admitted Wednesday.
Gardner specifically pointed to multiple plays where he failed to pursue the ball with the effort he expects from himself, including an 87-yard catch-and-run that was eventually called back due to penalties.
"But it was definitely an embarrassing watch," Gardner said. "To just look back at that tape, it was like my effort when the ball is on the other side, it was like an embarrassing watch, an embarrassing feeling."
"That's not what I stand for. That's not the type of person I am. That's not the type of player I am, and that'll never happen again."
I think that response says quite a bit about the type of player Indianapolis has in its secondary.
There is a difference between having a bad game and allowing that performance to become your standard. Gardner clearly has no intention of letting that happen.
Naturally, Sunday's performance has brought back some criticism surrounding the massive price Indianapolis paid to acquire Gardner last November.
But I still believe you have to look at that trade through a much wider lens.
The Colts were 7-2 and sitting atop the AFC when Chris Ballard sent two first-round picks and Adonai Mitchell to New York. At that moment, Indianapolis looked like it could be one elite cornerback away from making a legitimate championship run.
It was exactly the type of aggressive move Colts fans had been begging Ballard to make for years.
And from my perspective, Gardner is still a future Hall of Fame-caliber cornerback. The chances of finding someone with his talent in either of those first rounds were never particularly high.
More importantly, Sunday's performance was a clear outlier compared to what we saw through the first three weeks.
Gardner had allowed just five completions on 10 targets entering the Washington matchup, making his struggles in London that much more surprising.
Even the best defensive backs in football have bad afternoons, and one performance isn't going to change my evaluation of Gardner.
What matters now is how he responds, and judging by his comments Wednesday, I would expect a completely different player the next time he takes the field.
"That performance –  I ain't got to worry about seeing that ever again," Gardner said.
For a player who has already established himself as one of the premier corners in football, I wouldn't bet against him.
Michael Greene is a graduate of Indiana University and the Scouting Academy. He's in his first year covering the Indianapolis Colts and NFL, with a unique focus on fantasy football.

title: Colts-Steelers First Injury Report: Multiple Starters Miss Practice
full_text:
The Indianapolis Colts and Pittsburgh Steelers have released their first practice reports ahead of their clash in Week 5.
Both teams are seeing injuries start to pile up now that the season is in full swing. Each defense is dealing with thin position groups at different levels and have several starters listed after the first practice of the week.
Let’s break down each team’s report and what it means going into the weekend.
Indianapolis Colts Injury Report (As of 10/7)
Tanor Bortolini and Akeem Davis-Gaither are new names to the injury report, as Arden Key, Jaylon Carlies and Ashton Dulin’s issues were all disclosed in head coach Shane Steichen’s postgame press conference. Key is expected to miss “some time,” leading the Colts to sign defensive end Carl Lawson to their practice squad . While Jaylahn Tuimoloau is the most likely option to start in Key’s place, Lawson is likely to be elevated and rotate in at some point.
Bortolini has been a revelation for the Colts this year, anchoring the center of their stout offensive line. Dulin played on Sunday after missing two games with the same hamstring issue, so seeing him pop up is a concern. Steichen had initially considered Dulin to be “week-to-week.” Davis-Gaither, who was not included in the postgame injury updates by Steichen, now has a knee injury, raising the question if he suffered something during practice. Both he and Carlies are coming off stellar performances in which they both posted PFF grades in the 90s .
No real concern over running back Jonathan Taylor, who gets the day off after becoming the NFL’s all-time leading rusher in international games last week. Wednesday is typically a veteran rest day, which explains wide receiver Keenan Allen and cornerback Charvarius Ward’s absences. That said, Allen did not play in London with a groin injury and needs to show progress the remainder of the week to feel more comfortable about his status going into Sunday.
Wednesday’s practice report for #INDvsPIT pic.twitter.com/H7qNmJBqaQ
The best news of the day for Indianapolis is tight end Will Mallory’s return to practice after starting the season on injured reserve. The team opened his 21-day practice window today and not surprisingly, Mallory was a full participant. Should the Colts deem he’s ready to go for Sunday, the Colts may look to get the 27-year-old involved in the offense.
The initial forecast projects another week with a thin group at wide receiver . Injuries were part of the reason Indianapolis brought Darius Slayton in and signed him directly to the roster, but he’s yet to play despite having two weeks to acclimate. The Colts also signed former Philadelphia Eagles receiver Quez Watkins to the practice squad, so he’s in play for an elevation, but the 28-year-old hasn’t taken an NFL snap since 2023.
If there’s a silver lining to double injuries at linebacker, it would be that the door is now open for the Colts’ top draft choice in CJ Allen to get the most playing time of his young career thus far. The second-round pick has only played in two of four games thus far, registering only 11 snaps.
Pittsburgh Steelers Injury Report (As of 10/7)
Pittsburgh has a slightly better looking report, though it’s quite top-heavy. Four of the five players listed are starters.
The immediate concern for Pittsburgh would be the secondary. Both starting nickel Jalen Ramsey and outside starter Jamel Dean did not practice. Should neither be able to go, the Steelers will turn to Brandin Echols in the slot and Daylen Everett on the perimeter, though the team did sign Sean Murphy-Bunting off the Buccaneers’ practice squad on Tuesday, so he could play a role if needed.
We have signed CB Sean Murphy-Bunting to the Active Roster off the Tampa Bay Practice Squad, signed LB Marte Mapu to the Practice Squad, waived DB Doneiko Slaughter and placed DT Derrick Harmon on the Reserve/Injured List. @BordasLaw 📝: https://t.co/VWvvwTwFi5 pic.twitter.com/WV7kVe6s3l
The 37-year-old Cameron Heyward gets a rest day, so his status for Sunday won’t become clearer until later this week.
If Indianapolis fans were looking forward to seeing former Colts receiver Michael Pittman Jr. for the first time since leaving the organization, they may have to wait a little longer. While Pittman is listed as a limited participant with a foot injury, local Pittsburgh media spotted Pittman wheeling around the facility on a scooter, so definitely one to watch. Running back Rico Dowdle has missed the last two games with his toe injury, so he seems to be trending in the right direction.
Michael Pittman Jr. was wheeling around the locker room after practice on a one-legged scooter. Something to monitor.
Broadly speaking for Pittsburgh, we’ll need to see how the week unfolds before coming to any sort of injury-related conclusions. But the pass game on both sides of the ball are the early areas to monitor.

title: Colts Add Former Lou Anarumo Edge Defender: But is it Enough?
full_text:
The Indianapolis Colts are in desperate need of pass rush help .
The defensive line in Indianapolis , specifically the edge room, is already banged up. Starter Arden Key is expected to miss some time with a hamstring injury and Micheal Clemons has been on injured reserve, leaving a depleted and inexperienced group.
Additionally, the unit has been severely disappointing in the opening four games. Per Next Gen Stats, the Colts have the lowest pass rush win-rate in the league (25.5%), nearly four points behind 2nd-lowest (29.2%).
To add some freshness and juice to the group, the Colts signed 31-year-old defensive end Carl Lawson to their practice squad, yet another player who has played for defensive coordinator Lou Anarumo at one point or another.
But, will bringing in Lawson on board be enough to give the pass rush new life? Let’s break it down.
For Anarumo, bringing in Lawson brings some familiarity and trust.
The two spent four seasons together in Cincinnati from 2017-20, when Anarumo was the Bengals' defensive backs coach and later defensive coordinator. Lawson emerged as one of the more disruptive players on Cincinnati's defense during that stretch, recording 20 sacks, 19 tackles for loss and 83 quarterback hits across 51 games.
Lawson's best season came back in 2017, posting 8.5 sacks and 8 tackles for loss as a rookie. He also registered 7.0 sacks with the New York Jets in 2022, showing that he has previously been capable of providing legitimate production off the edge.
That history doesn't guarantee anything about Lawson's potential production for the Colts, particularly at 31 years of age. But it does give the Colts a veteran who already has experience playing for Anarumo and understands the defensive scheme.
If Indianapolis needs to call on Lawson sooner rather than later, that familiarity could prove valuable.
The question, however, is how much Lawson has left in the tank.
The veteran defensive end hasn't played a full season since 2022 and appeared in just one game for the Baltimore Ravens last season. At 31 years old, the Colts can't reasonably expect the player who once lead the way in Cincinnati to suddenly reappear.
That doesn't mean Lawson won't contribute. Indy doesn't necessarily need him to become the main man, just to play his role. If elevated from the practice squad, Lawson could provide a veteran presence in a rotational role while the Colts navigate injuries along the edge.
But that's a much different proposition than asking Lawson to solve the team's pass-rush problems.
The Colts need consistent pressure from their defensive ends, and Lawson hasn't provided that at the NFL level in some time. His familiarity with Anarumo and his previous production make him an intriguing addition, but there is no guarantee he'll produce for the Colts.
For now, view Lawson as a low-risk, high-reward addition. He should bring experience in the short term that's currently lacking with veterans injured, and any production he adds on the field is a bonus.
The reality is that Lawson was never supposed to be the answer for Indianapolis. Had things gone its way this offseason, we'd be looking at a completely different pass rush.
The Colts pursued Trey Hendrickson with the hope that the veteran pass rusher could give the defense the proven production it lacked, but the two sides ultimately couldn't reach an agreement, and Baltimore scooped Hendrickson up.
Instead, Indianapolis gambled that Latu would take the next step up and become their No. 1 edge rusher, while Key and Clemons to provided veteran depth around him. That plan has unraveled quickly. Latu hasn't made the anticipated leap, while injuries to Key and Clemons have left the Colts scrambling for answers.
The injuries brought the Colts to Lawson, a player who wasn't on an NFL roster at the start of the week and is now being asked to potentially help stabilize the league's worst pass rush.
It's difficult to look at the situation without thinking about what could have been if the Colts had landed Hendrickson. Lawson may still provide useful snaps, but Indy needed a proven difference-maker at the position. Instead, the team is banking on a fading veteran to help right the ship.
Lawson is not the solution to the Colts' pass-rush problems. Even if they want him to be, Lawson is nothing more than a temporary filler for a position group that desperately needs reinforcements.
The veteran can provide experience while Key and Clemons are unavailable and could potentially give Indy some useful snaps if he's elevated from the practice squad. But expecting him to suddenly become a difference-maker would be unrealistic.
The Colts need a legitimate threat off the edge, and Lawson isn't that player anymore. His history with Anarumo makes the signing sensible, but it doesn't change the reality that Indianapolis is adding an aging player who barely played last season to a pass rush that ranks last in the NFL in win rate.
For now, Lawson gives the Colts another body and some veteran experience. That's useful. It just isn't enough to move the needle.

title: Colts' Wide Receiver Room Is Becoming a Problem
full_text:
The Indianapolis Colts are back to .500 after winning two straight, but there is still something missing from this offense.
Indianapolis simply does not have enough explosiveness at wide receiver right now.
Daniel Jones averaged a career-best 8.1 yards per attempt last season, helping create one of the most dangerous offenses in football before his Achilles injury. That number has dropped considerably through the first month of the season, and the absence of Alec Pierce has been impossible to ignore.
Pierce isn't just another receiver in this offense. He led the NFL in yards per catch in back-to-back seasons, averaging 22.3 in 2024 and 21.3 in 2025 before signing a four-year, $114 million extension this offseason.
He opened this season with four catches for 61 yards against Baltimore, but aggravated his surgically repaired left heel against Kansas City after just one catch for 11 yards.
Now he is on injured reserve and is not eligible to return until the Colts' October 25 matchup against Minnesota.
That has left Indianapolis searching for somebody to replace the vertical threat he brings.
The Colts signed Darius Slayton shortly after Pierce went down, and the move made perfect sense. Slayton has averaged 15.0 yards per catch throughout his career and spent six seasons playing alongside Jones in New York.
Slayton even said that he and Jones "see the field pretty similarly," which made him seem like about as close to a plug-and-play option as Indianapolis could find.
Yet he has been inactive in back-to-back games.
The first one was understandable. Slayton had just arrived and was still learning the offense.
But being a coach's-decision inactive again in London, especially with Pierce on injured reserve and Keenan Allen out with a groin injury, is much more concerning.
Ashton Dulin finally returned against Washington and caught three passes for 29 yards, including a 23-yard reception, but even he is now dealing with a hamstring injury.
The Colts did sign veteran wideout Quez Watkins to their practice squad on Tuesday, reuniting him with head coach Shane Steichen from their days together in Philadelphia, though he hasn't played in the NFL since 2023, so it's hard to imagine he'll surpass Slayton on the depth chart anytime soon.
Josh Downs remains the reliable volume option underneath, and guys like Keenan Allen and Laquon Treadwell certainly have their roles.
But none of them replace what Pierce does.
Indianapolis does not need another possession receiver. This offense needs somebody who can consistently threaten a defense vertically and create explosive plays.
Whether that means exploring free agency or attacking the trade market, the Colts at least need to be looking.
I understand the complicated part. Indianapolis just committed $114 million to Pierce, and once he returns, a room featuring Pierce, Downs, Allen, Slayton, Dulin, Treadwell and Burks suddenly looks crowded.
But crowded on paper doesn't mean much when the players expected to provide your explosiveness are either injured or not playing.
The Colts are 2-2 and still right in the middle of the AFC South race heading into Pittsburgh.
There is too much talent on this offense to allow one missing element to hold it back, and right now, the lack of a legitimate downfield threat is doing exactly that.
Michael Greene is a graduate of Indiana University and the Scouting Academy. He's in his first year covering the Indianapolis Colts and NFL, with a unique focus on fantasy football.

title: Week 5 Power Rankings: Jury Still Out on Indianapolis Colts
full_text:
The Indianapolis Colts are starting to turn things around, but are doing so very quietly.
After opening the season 0-2, Indianapolis has won back-to-back games and enters Week 5 at .500. Despite the improved record, there still isn't much consensus on what to make of this team.
Some see a team that could make a run at the playoffs. Others aren't convinced the Colts have done enough to prove they're ready to compete.
Here's where some of the biggest names in NFL media have the Colts ranked heading into Week 5.
The Colts dropped two spots in Connor Orr’s rankings, despite Indianapolis getting a win in Week 4, noting the team needs to continue improving its roster as the season progresses.
“I don’t really care what happens to this iteration of the Colts, but following the Sauce Gardner trade last year, literally the only sensible follow-up is to continue pouring resources into this team and trading for Colts legacy son Marvin Harrison Jr.,” he wrote.
Indianapolis jumped up just one spot to No. 22 in the power rankings voted on by ESPN’s team of beat reporters.
Stephen Holder is unconvinced that the first four weeks have given any answers as to who the Colts are. His four words to describe the start: Who are these guys?
The Colts have managed to get to .500 with consecutive wins, but there are so many questions about their viability as playoff contenders,” he wrote. “The defense has played better but hasn't faced a major test in the past two weeks…Sunday's win somehow produced 30 points despite QB Daniel Jones posting his lowest passing total in a full game since joining the Colts last season (143).
The Colts came in at No. 22 in Mike Florio’s power rankings , two spots better than last week.
Florio kept his analysis brief. He’s not sure Indianapolis is capable of winning the division, and questions its ability to win enough games to “steal a wildcard berth.”
No change from last week in Chad Graff and Josh Kendall’s updated rankings, but concern is growing, particularly over the quarterback play.
The Colts went to London and didn’t have to do much to beat up on the undermanned Washington Commanders,” they wrote. “But there’s rising concern about (Daniel) Jones, who completed 19 of 34 passes for just 143 yards with no touchdowns and an interception.”
Clearly, the duo is not moved.
Another one-place jump for the Colts . Ralph Vacchiano believes the team is a playoff contender, and are better than it gets credit for. At the same time, the quarterback remains a wildcard.
“They are an overtime FG away from being 3-1 this season. So they’re a playoff contender, but how much longer can they thrive if (Daniel) Jones keeps making big mistakes?”
Vacchiano also cites concerns over the pass defense, which has allowed the third-most yards so far this season (1,105).
Nick Shook dropped the Colts two places in his new rankings, arguing that Commanders’ quarterback Marcus Mariota’s injury gave Indianapolis a “favorable outcome.”
“You’ll take any and every win in this league, although this one doesn’t inspire a ton of confidence,” he wrote. Shook shares the same worry over Jones’ turnover problems that several have already pointed out.
Bleacher Report’s analysts collectively ranked Indianapolis at No. 23 , no change from the week prior.
Brent Sobleski writes that the Colts are a shell of the team they were a year ago, and a big reason why is the drop off from Daniel Jones.
“He's been part of the problem to start this season despite the two-game winning streak…As long as Jones does a better job with his ball security, the Colts could easily win their next two contests.”

title: The Indianapolis Colts Are Still Searching for a Pass-Rush Fix
full_text:
The Indianapolis Colts entered the offseason knowing they needed defensive end help.
Four weeks into the season, they're still looking for it.
Indianapolis had a glaring need coming out of last season and spent much of the offseason trying to boost its pass rush. There was no shortage of options, and the Colts came close on some.
But instead of landing the kind of addition that could change the position, things took a turn.
And now, with injuries piling up, the questions surrounding the position have only gotten louder.
To understand the Colts’ current predicament, we have to go back to the offseason. General manager Chris Ballard knew he needed to add some juice to the defensive line in order to elevate Indy’s pass rush.
“We’ve gotta address the front and make sure we have enough,” he said in his end-of-season press conference back in January. “You’ve got to find ways to be deep enough and have enough talent on the roster that you can still win games.”
The Colts saw plenty of turnover at the position, losing veterans Kwity Paye, Tyquan Lewis and Samson Ebukam to free agency. That left just Laiatu Latu and Jaylahn Tuimoloau from last year’s team still under contract.
Ballard knew what he had to do. And with former Bengals defensive end Trey Hendrickson, the 2024 sack leader under current Colts defensive coordinator Lou Anarumo, available, he became the obvious primary target.
The Colts got real close to inking Hendrickson to a deal that would’ve transformed the defensive front. But they missed out at the last second, with Baltimore swooping in to snatch Hendrickson up on a monster four-year, $112 million deal.
Ravens signing DE Trey Hendrickson to a 4-year, $112M deal. (via @rapsheet , @tompelissero ) pic.twitter.com/Tjaf7Sv0Ae
That left Ballard with a decision to make. Indianapolis still needed to address the issue, but the team wasn't going to find another Trey Hendrickson sitting around waiting to be signed.
Instead, they took a more boring approach.
Indianapolis added Arden Key as a low-end starter option opposite Latu and later brought in Micheal Clemons as a rotational depth piece. Neither move carried the same weight as the Hendrickson pursuit, nor were they as flashy of moves, but together they gave Indianapolis two experienced bodies to help fill out the depth chart.
Later in the offseason, Ballard took two late-round flyers on rookies George Gumbs Jr. and Caden Curry, but that was it for additions. Instead of adding the game-changer, the Colts went for role players, an intentional decision that forced the Colts to bet on Latu breaking out in his third year. Which, in theory, could work. Latu would lead the way, Key would complement and the rest of the unit would do the rest.
But four games into 2026, and that plan has been tested significantly.
The team placed Clemons on injured reserve Sept. 22. ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler announced Tuesday that Key, who suffered a hamstring injury in Indy’s 30-17 win over the Commanders , will miss around 3-4 weeks. So now, the Colts are right back where they started.
Colts pass rusher Arden Key is expected to miss about 3-4 weeks with a hamstring injury, per sources. Head coach Shane Steichen said Monday that Key, a starter, would miss ‘some time.’ pic.twitter.com/2qsGqC8dQQ
Assuming Key’s absence, Latu and Tuimoloau are Indy’s starting edge rushers, leaving Indianapolis in the same situation they were in a year ago: looking for a boost.
While the Colts pass rush is undermanned, the injuries also provide opportunity.
Curry and Tuimoloau, both of whom have played rotational roles this season, will be thrust into larger roles. Gumbs, who’s yet to make his NFL debut, will get the chance to suit up for the first time.
For Tuimoloau, his opportunity has finally arrived. After spending most of his rookie season on the bench, Indy’s second-round pick from 2024 has finally found his way into more playing time. But that comes with steep responsibility, and it’s unclear how ready he is.
And of course, there’s Latu.
While Latu hasn’t had a Hendrickson-like impact for the Colts through four games, the team is still banking on him establishing himself as the top dog. There have been flashes, as there have been throughout Latu’s career, but the final product hasn’t always been there. Now, there’s never been a better time for that to change for Latu than now.
The next few weeks will be crucial, not just for the pass rush, but for the team. As the defense adapts to life without Clemons and Key, the Colts will find out whether the bet they made on their young defensive ends can pay off, or if they’re better off exploring other options.

title: Is it Too Early for the Colts to Panic About Daniel Jones?
full_text:
Daniel Jones looked like a completely different quarterback once he entered Shane Steichen's system last season.
His legs paired with Jonathan Taylor's rushing ability and Alec Pierce's deep-threat presence created almost a perfect storm. For stretches, this offense looked unstoppable, and Jones was doing whatever he wanted with the football while still taking care of it.
Then came the Achilles tear.
Jones tore his right Achilles on Dec. 7 against Jacksonville, ending a career year in which he completed 68% of his passes for 3,101 yards, 19 touchdowns and eight interceptions.
Just 280 days later, he was back under center for Week 1 against Baltimore.
And four games into his return, I think it is fair to start asking the question: Should the Colts be worried about Daniel Jones?
Nothing about Jones physically screams that Achilles is still bothering him.
He moved well throughout training camp, has shown he can escape the pocket and even scored his first rushing touchdown since the injury Sunday against Washington.
But we still haven't seen the same Daniel Jones who made defenses account for his legs every single play last season.
Jones rushed for 164 yards and five touchdowns in 13 games last year. Through four games this season, he has just 21 yards and one score.
Maybe that matters more than we realize.
An Achilles injury is brutal, especially for a quarterback whose athleticism was such an important part of what made this offense dangerous. Jones may technically be healthy, but expecting him to immediately have the same burst and confidence only nine months removed from surgery might not be completely fair.
We saw a version of this with Kirk Cousins after his Achilles tear. Cousins returned for Atlanta in 2024 and threw 16 interceptions in 14 games before eventually losing the starting job.
Obviously, that isn't a perfect comparison. Cousins was older and never had Jones' mobility to begin with.
But it does make me wonder how much an injury like this can impact a quarterback mentally, not just physically.
This is where my true concerns begin.
Jones has already turned the ball over seven times through four games, throwing four interceptions and losing three fumbles. He had 11 total turnovers across 13 games last season.
That simply cannot continue, and against Washington, it wasn't only the turnovers.
Jones finished 19-of-34 for just 143 yards, and there were several opportunities where receivers were open and the throw simply wasn't accurate enough.
Could Jones be trying to compensate for some of those explosive plays he used to create with his legs by forcing more with his arm? Maybe.
That's impossible to know from the outside, but something is clearly different right now.
Still, I'm not ready to panic, Jones is four games removed from a long and grueling rehabilitation process. He deserves some time to rediscover the rhythm that made him so good in this offense last season.
I still believe Jones can play at an elite level in Indianapolis, but the ball security has to improve immediately.
And if we know anything about the quarterback Indianapolis saw last season, Jones is going to work relentlessly to get back to where he needs to be.
Michael Greene is a graduate of Indiana University and the Scouting Academy. He's in his first year covering the Indianapolis Colts and NFL, with a unique focus on fantasy football.

title: Colts Week 4 Snap Count Analysis: What’s Going on With CJ Allen?
full_text:
The Colts came home from London with a 30-13 win over Washington, but the Week 4 snap counts left behind a few questions worth digging into.
Some players are earning bigger roles. Others are somehow seeing theirs disappear.
Here are the three snap-count storylines that stood out most.
At this point, the situation is getting harder to ignore.
CJ Allen, the Colts' top pick in the 2026 NFL Draft at No. 53 overall, was active Sunday and did not play a single defensive snap. He has now played just 11 defensive snaps through four games, recording one assisted tackle.
That is strange enough for a second-round linebacker, but it gets even stranger when you consider how Indianapolis talked about Allen all offseason.
Lou Anarumo and his staff put the green dot on Allen almost immediately after he came off PUP during training camp. He wore it at Georgia, and Chris Ballard's scouting staff specifically highlighted his communication ability and green-dot potential.
Allen opened camp with a calf strain and later suffered a hamstring injury that Anarumo said set him back roughly a month. That explanation made sense early.
But we are now a month into the season, and Allen isn't just being eased in — he isn't playing.
Austin Ajiake had not logged a defensive snap entering Sunday and played 17 against Washington. Bryce Boettcher played 18, while Jaylon Carlies played 30.
There may also be a slight philosophical difference between Ballard's vision and Anarumo's.
Ballard's staff drafted Allen believing he could run the defense from the MIKE spot. Through four weeks, that vision has yet to materialize on Sundays.
Adebawore continues to make the most of every opportunity he gets.
He played 29 defensive snaps Sunday, or 45% of the defense, and split a third-down sack with Laiatu Latu.
More importantly, Adebawore currently leads Indianapolis in pressure rate despite still operating in a limited role.
He generated four pressures and 1.5 sacks against Houston in Week 3, then followed it up with another disruptive performance in London.
At some point, production has to earn more opportunity.
The Colts needed somebody to step up at receiver with Alec Pierce on injured reserve and Keenan Allen out with a groin injury.
Laquon Treadwell answered.
Treadwell played 56 offensive snaps, tied with Tyler Warren for the most among Colts skill-position players, and led Indianapolis with five catches for 42 yards on six targets.
He entered Sunday with four catches on five targets all season, but when his role expanded, his production followed.
Treadwell may not provide the same vertical element as Pierce, but he has done exactly what Indianapolis has needed from him.
Allen's continued absence is easily the biggest snap-count story to watch moving forward.
If Allen still cannot crack the rotation as the season moves deeper into October, the questions are only going to get louder. For a player the Colts once viewed as a potential green-dot linebacker from Day 1, 11 defensive snaps through four games is becoming harder to ignore.
Michael Greene is a graduate of Indiana University and the Scouting Academy. He's in his first year covering the Indianapolis Colts and NFL, with a unique focus on fantasy football.

title: How Foyesade Oluokun Continues to Drive the Jaguars' Defensive Success
full_text:
JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- Foyesade Oluokun just keeps getting better and better.
Week 4 was Oluokun's 132nd NFL game since joining the NFL as a sixth-round pick with the Atlanta Falcons in 2018. And like he did so many times in his first 131st games, he made his impact felt with a game-changing play. It was the perfect type of performance from the ninth-year veteran to sum up what he means to a defense that has played a big part in the Jaguars' 3-1 start
After Oluokun made one of the most important plays of the Jaguars' entire season with his fourth-quarter interception against the Bengals last week, he was given the nod for AFC Defensive Player of the Week for Week 4. It was a well-deserved honor, and one that helps put Oluokun's true value to the Jaguars on display.
Oluokun recorded seven tackles, an interception and a forced fumble in Jacksonville’s 22-17 win at Cincinnati. He is one of two players this season to record at least seven tackles, an interception and a forced fumble in a single game. The interception marked his 10th career interception. He became the fourth active NFL player with 10+ sacks, 10+ interceptions, and 10+ forced fumbles, joining S Harrison Smith, LB Fred Warner, and LB T.J. Watt. Oluokun’s two interceptions in 2026 are tied for the third most in the NFL this season.
But what truly makes Oluokun special is the fact that he has done it week after week, year after year. Oluokun is entering his fifth year with the Jaguars, and he is still as important today as he was when he signed in 2022. Oluokun has played 88% of the Jaguars' snaps this season, showing zero signs yet of slowing down.
“He's had a really good season so far," Jaguars defensive coordinator Anthony Campanile said on Thursday. "He might be, at that position, just one of the smartest guys I've ever been around ... He really is like having a coach on the field. He knows everything."
Oluokun is helping lead a Jaguars defense that ranks tied first in interceptions (six), second in points allowed (53) and run defense (74.3), and tied second in takeaways (eight) in 2026. He is doing so while helping lead a first-time full-time starter at the other linebacker spot in Ventrell Miller, and he has proven to once again be the heart of the Jaguars' defense as a whole.
"He's on it before he walks in the building in terms of what's going in new. He's totally prepared for that," Campanile said. "And the thing about that is a lot of times you have guys who are smart, they can process the whole thing, but maybe they don't have that element of violence when they play. And he gets so much out of his body in that regard. Like, he plays violent as hell. And he's still able to keep that kind of controlled rage about him and be a great communicator. Even some of our communication as he's the green dot, he's done a great job with.”
The numbers back it up when it comes to Olukun, too. According to NextGenStats, the Jaguars' defense has allowed 3.3 yards per carry on designed runs this season, the second-fewest in the NFL, despite using a light box on 46.8% of those carries (4th-highest) and contacting ball carriers at or behind the line of scrimmage on 36.7% of them (8th-lowest). This means Oluokun is having to do a lot of heavy lifting at times, and he has thrived while doing so.
Oluokun is also one of only two linebackers in the NFL who has two interceptions through the first month, joining former fellow Jaguars linebacker Devin Lloyd. By total coverage EPA, Oluokun has been the most valuable pass-defender at the linebacker position in football. He has simply been at his best for the Jaguars this year, defying any chance of him slowing down from the ever-reliable pace he has always set.

title: Jaguars Get Much-Needed Defensive Back News in Latest Week 5 Injury Report
full_text:
JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- While the Jacksonville Jaguars' injury report did not decrease in size on Thursday, they did get some good news.
The Jaguars had safety Eric Murray upgraded from non-participant in Wednesday's practice to limited participation on Thursday. That is a sign of progress as Murray goes through the NFL's concussion protocol, and it does now seem as if there is a chance the Jaguars could have the veteran safety on the field on Sunday vs. the Philadelphia Eagles.
Murray was injured in Week 4's win over the Cincinnati Bengals and missed a good chunk of the second-half, which led to the Jaguars needing to lean on second-year safety Rayuan Lane since Caleb Ransaw was also injured. With Murray's status improving Thursday, it appears the Jaguars might be able to see their secondary be a bit closer to full-strength against the Eagles.
“Eric means a lot to us. Eric is one of the guys you would kind of put him in a classification of he's a coach on the field," Jaguars defensive coordinator Anthony Campanile said on Thursday. "You guys probably know that from being at practice. He's just really good communicator, knows the ins and outs of the defense and can kind of see problems before they start on the field. He's been great that way all the way through, the entire season last season, the beginning of this season."
Murray is a critical part of the Jaguars' secondary considering he and Jourdan Lewis are amongst the unit's elder statesmen. If the Jaguars do not have Murray on the field, they will likely have to lean on Lane once again, in addition to third-round rookie Jalen Huskey. The Jaguars had Antonio Johnson step in when Murray missed time last year, but Johnson is now a starter.
"Other guys, if they have to step up and do that, I have total confidence that they will, because we've really got a good bunch of communicators back there," Campanile said. "And that's one of the things we're always looking for at that position. A guy who has position flexibility, one. And then two, smart guys,  guys that love to play, that love to learn and obviously, know the ins and outs of all the calls, learn football.”
The list of other limited Jaguars was the same as Wednesday's injury report: offensive tackle Cole Van Lanen (knee), cornerbacks Montaric Brown (hamstring), Jarrian Jones (foot), Jaylon Jones (hamstring), and Jourdan Lewis (hamstring), offensive tackle Anton Harrison (elbow), defensive tackle Davon Hamilton (foot), and defensive end Josh Hines-Allen (groin) were listed as limited.
The Jaguars had two players as full participants for the second day in a row after they had previously been limited throughout the season in running back LeQuint Allen (hip) and wide receiver Jakobi Meyers (thumb).
The Jaguars should have most of these players available in Week 5 against the Eagles in London, though Brown is one player whose status might not be known until much closer to game time on Sunday.

title: 3 Key Areas Jaguars Have an Advantage Over Eagles: Trevor Lawrence and Jalen Hurts
full_text:
JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- The Jacksonville Jaguars will need to be at their very best in Week 5 if they want to keep their winning ways going.
The Jaguars have been able to take advantages of mismatches against opponents in recent weeks, especially in Week 4 against the Cincinnati Bengals. But what advantages should the Jaguars attack when it comes to Week 5 against the Philadelphia Eagles? We break it down below.
This is the one area where I think the Jaguars have a distinct edge over the Eagles. I have believed for a few years now that Trevor Lawrence is the more talented passer than Jalen Hurts, and we have now seen the talent around each passer change enough since then for it to start becoming clearer and clearer. Since Lawrence got the best play-caller of his career in Liam Coen and an improved supporting cast, he has been playing a different sport than Hurts.
As things stand today, Lawrence is No. 8 amongst qualifying quarterbacks in EPA/Play and No. 4 in success rate. Meanwhile, Hurts ranks No. 24 and No. 28 respectively. Hurts has dealt with a bad hand in terms of injuries, but he is coming off several stinkers in a row, while Lawrence just keeps building momentum. For the fifth week in a row, the Jaguars should be entering Sunday with the better quarterback.
The Jaguars' skill players are a major reason they are 3-1right now. The Jaguars have seen all five of their top pass-catchers (Parker Washington, Jakobi Meyers, Brenton Strange, Brian Thomas Jr., Josh Cameron) make big plays, while Bhayshul Tuten and Chris Rodriguez Jr. have led the way for the rushing attack. Compare that to an Eagles offense that is a bit broken right now, and the Jaguars have a big advantage.
While the Jaguars are dealing with some injuries defensively, none of their top-seven skill players have missed practice time this week with injuries. Meanwhile, the Eagles are dealing with injuries to Devonta Smith, Saquon Barkley, Tank Bigsby, Dallas Goedert, and Dontayvion Wicks. The Eagles' playmakers are banged up right now, while the Jaguars' are healthy and ready to produce right away.
Week 5 will be a Green Bay Packers reunion of sorts when the Jaguars' defense share the field with the Eagles' offense. In 2024, Jaguars defensive coordinator Anthony Campanile was the Packers inside linebackers coach/run game coordinator, while Eagles offensive coordinator Sean Mannion was an offensive assistant. Fast forward two seasons, and both coaches are now coordinators who are set to play a game of chess against each other.
“Sean's a great football coach. Great guy," Campanile said Wednesday. "I thought he was an extremely hard worker. We were both in there late hours a lot, he's one of the guys you'd see in there. You know what I mean? He's no stranger to hard work. I think he is a really good football coach, super detailed, really bright. Obviously, anybody that's played quarterback that long in the NFL, you have a really good knowledge of the game, and I think he brings that to the offense.”
For as much mutual respect that there is here, though, it is clear that Campanile's unit has the edge. Both coaches are working through some penalties on their respective sides of the football, but Campanile has his unit absolutely humming right now, while Mannion and the Eagles' offense can barely get into neutral. The Jaguars' defense ranks No. 7 in EPA/Play right now despite giving up plenty of yards, and that is due to their ability to force turnovers and prevent points. Meanwhile, the Eagles' offense ranks No. 29 in EPA/Play and No. 30 in success rate.

title: 5 Winners, 4 Losers From Jaguars' First Month of the Season: Rookie and Veteran Risers
full_text:
JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- The Jacksonville Jaguars have had quite the first month.
For 14 of the 16 quarters of the season, the Jaguars have been a dominant team that has pushed the opposing teams around. Take away the second half against the Broncos, and there are not many teams better than the Jaguars right now.
But which Jaguars have been the most impressive during the first month of the season? We break it down below with this week's winners and losers.
It is hard to think of many bigger winners than Bhayshul Tuten. According to NextGenInsights, Tuten has reached 15+ mph on 19 of his 60 rushes this season, the most of any player. Nearly half of Tuten's rushing yards (49.9%) have come after a missed tackle this season, the highest share of any player (min. 25 rushes). In short, he is creating a ton of explosive plays and generating his own yards. This is something the Jaguars stressed that they needed from the running back position all offseason, and Tuten has given it to them. He has produced big plays all season long, and he should be only getting better.
Everyone expected Travis Hunter to be a stellar cornerback , but this quickly? Hunter already has become one of the top cornerbacks in football after just playing a month of cornerback full-time. He has already taken massive steps compared to last season, too. According to NextGenStats, Hunter has played 175 defensive snaps through four games this season, already more than his total as a rookie in 2025 (154), while playing 16 offensive snaps after 305 last season. Hunter has aligned as the field cornerback on 74.9% of his defensive snaps this season, up from 44.2% in 2025, and logged a career-high 58 coverage snaps against the Bengals in Week 4.
Emmanuel Pregnon has played every single snap for the Jaguars this season, not something easy to do for a rookie joining a team that went 13-4. Pregnon has had his ups and downs, as any rookie offensive lineman will have, but he has stood out each week with his run-blocking ability. Pregnon has been the Jaguars' most impactful rookie to date, and he is the future at the guard position for the Jaguars moving forward.
There were plenty of questions the Jaguars had to face at the linebacker position this offseason, but Ventrell Miller has helped answer all of them. After losing former All-Pro linebacker Devin Lloyd in free agency, the Jaguars had Miller step into the full-time starting linebacker role for the first time in his career, and he has thrived. He has been one of the NFL's best linebackers against the run (if not the very best) and he has been an impactful blitzer. He has made himself some money this season.
6th round rookies do not often make big impacts on winning teams. It is even more uncommon when that rookie plays the position the team is the strongest at, but that is where the Jaguars are with Josh Cameron. The Baylor product has certified himself as the team's No. 4 receiver, caught two touchdowns in four games, and has turned every single one of his catches into a first-down or a touchdown. He has become a home run Day 3 pick very, very quickly.
Brian Thomas Jr. clearly has a ton of talent and value to the Jaguars' offense, but the lack of production through the first month is jarring. He is averaging a little over 25 yards a game, has only seen a heavy dose of targets in one game, and looks more like a piece of the equation on offense than he looks like a true X-Factor for how they attack each week. Thomas is a good player; too good for just over 100 yards through four weeks.
With Caleb Ransaw placed on injured reserve earlier this week, he is now set to miss 21 of his first 25 possible games in the NFL. He did some good things for the Jaguars at the start of the season, especially as a tackler, but he will now be sidelined for at least a month, if not longer. Ransaw has had some really tough breaks at the start of his NFL career, especially considering how excited the Jaguars were about him as a prospect when they drafted him.
Patrick Mekari did not play in the first four games due to the back injury that landed him on injured reverse, and it does not look like there is much reason for the Jaguars to introduce him back into the starting lineup when he is healthy. Pregnon has played well at left guard for a rookie, and Ezra Cleveland has done enough at the right guard spot for the Jaguars to not muddy up the waters. Mekari has of course done nothing wrong, but the Jaguars do not need guard help, which means he is likely an expensive backup once he returns.
While Travis Hunter has been stellar at cornerback, he has been mostly forgotten on the offensive side of the ball. That makes sense for where the Jaguars are with cornerback injuries and with Hunter's high level of play at cornerback, but nobody could say that Hunter having one catch for eight yards through four games was expected. Hunter is playing great football, but it has been mostly one-sided. That does not take away from his value to the team, but it does change expectations.

title: 5 Bold Predictions for Jaguars' London Battle vs. Eagles: Trevor Lawrence Keeps Finding Endzone
full_text:
JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- For the Jacksonville Jaguars to improve to 4-1, they will have to get over the hump against a Philadelphia Eagles team that has had the Jaguars' number in recent years.
The Eagles, of course, are a different team now than when the Jaguars lost road games to them in 2022 and 2024. The Eagles were powerhouses then, while this year's 2-2 Eagles squad seems like it is coming apart at the seams.
“I know that just because you think about—when you're playing an opponent, you naturally just think about the prior games that you've played against them," Jaguars quarterback Trevor Lawrence said Wednesday.
"So yeah, I've thought about that I haven’t beat these guys, and they've had some really good teams and we've had some close ones that we've lost. So just excited for another opportunity, because it's the next game though, not because of all that. Like I said last week, I'm like a broken record with you guys. You prepare every week to go win the game regardless of who it is. You don't want to win it more because it's someone in particular. Yeah, we got to put together a good plan.”
So, how do we see the Jaguars' Week 5 battle with the Eagles playing out? We break it down below.
Trevor Lawrence, for my money, has been the Jaguars' MVP through the first four games of the season. The Jaguars' franchise passer is playing the best football of his career from an accuracy and decision-making standard, and he has put several wow throws on tape in every single game this season. The Eagles have a great defensive scheme and some good players on that side of the ball even with injuries, so they are no pushover.
With that said, I think Lawrence has a stellar day vs. the Eagles that sees him score four touchdowns: three through the air and one on the ground. Over the Jaguars’ last 12 games (Since Week 11 of 2025), Lawrence has completed 225-of-348 passes (64.7%) for 2,852 yards, 27 touchdowns and a passer rating of 107.6 to pair with 221 yards and five scores on the ground. His 32 total scores lead the NFL over that span, and I think he picks up several more this week. This feels like the type of game that Lawrence could take over from the first drive, and it would be a big step to see him continue his momentum.
The Eagles certainly are facing a lot of changes across the offensive line, plus they are down to their third- and fourth-string running backs. Better running games have tried and failed to get something going against the Jaguars on the ground, but each have failed since the start of the 2025 season; I do not see the Eagles offense in its current form being the offense that flips that script. As a result, I think the Jaguars have another stellar performance against the run.
Last week, the Jaguars held the Bengals to 23 rushing yards, the fourth fewest allowed in franchise history in a single game. The Jaguars have gone 21 straight games not allowing a 75-yard rusher, the fourth longest such streak in the last 50 seasons. The Eagles simply are undermanned when it comes to facing an elite Jaguars' run defense.
The surest sign that things are going a bit wayward for the Eagles is the fact that even the tush push is getting stopped lately. The Eagles got stuffed on a key tush push rep against the Los Angeles Rams last week, and I think the Jaguars are well-equipped to stop the most efficient and effective play in football thanks to their strength in the middle of the defense with their front and linebackers Ventrell Miller and Foyesade Oluokun.
The Rams stop the tush push‼️ 📺: FOX/FOX One pic.twitter.com/7siNXhy8D4
I think the Eagles will go to the well a few times against the Jaguars considering that play is like comfort food to them and, right now, they need something they can rely on. But I also think the Jaguars' run defense is made to stop such efforts, and I think the Jaguars get a few wins against the play Sunday.
The Jaguars have simply had a knack for forcing takeaways under Liam Coen and Anthony Campanile. The Jaguars have three red-zone takeaways in 2026 as well, the most in the NFL. No other team has recorded more than one, while the Jaguars have scored an NFL-leading 38 points off taekaways. They force takeaways and they produce once they get the ball, and I think that happens again this week.
With the way the Eagles offense has taken to their new scheme and offensive coordinator Sean Mannion, and with the injuries they are facing across the board, I think this is bound to be a mistake-filled day from Philadelphia's unit and Jalen Hurts. Jacksonville has 13 multiple-takeaway games dating back to Week 1 of last season, and I see No. 14 coming on Sunday.
Arik Armstead was outstanding for the Jaguars in Week 4, and now he will get a chance to do so again with the Eagles on the dockett. The Eagles' days of having a truly elite offensive line seem to be gone, and the departures of Lane Johnson and Cam Jurgens this week, along with GOAT-level offensive line coach Jeff Stoutland this offseason, will play a big role in that. Add in Armstead's momentum, and I think this will be a big week for Armstead.
I would assume the Eagles, like most teams facing the Jaguars, will ditch the run early and proceed to throw a lot of passes. This will give Armstead enough reps against a new-look offensive line that I think he cashes in and records his first two-sack game as a Jaguar. He has heated up with 10 pressures over the last two weeks, and I think he cashes in vs, the Eagles.
