title: Rams Rookie Report Cards After Week 4 (And an Update on the Ones That Got Away)
full_text:
Through four weeks of the NFL season, the Los Angeles Rams haven’t gotten any production out of their rookie class. Ty Simpson has been the emergency third-string quarterback on game days. Despite head coach Sean McVay saying that Max Klare would get more snaps last week with Terrance Ferguson’s injury, he played one . Keagen Trost started the season on injured reserve and CJ Daniels has been inactive on game days. Lastly, Tim Keenan didn’t make the initial 53-man roster.
The Rams have gotten about as little production as a team could get out of a rookie class. In a way, it makes sense. This class was clearly one for the future. The Rams see Ty Simpson as the future after Matthew Stafford. With Colby Parkinson and Davis Allen set to hit free agency next year, Klare will be expected to step up at that time.
Trost was always a depth pick and some insurance if the Rams lose Warren McClendon or one of their two guards next offseason in free agency. Keenan may have been a disappointment on Day 3, but CJ Daniels was at least showing some upside in training camp.
Still, the Rams have gotten some production out of undrafted free agents. Wesley Bailey has been a good rotational player and both Dean Connors and Maximus Pulley have stepped up on special teams.
Given some of the injuries at tight end and wide receiver, it’s fair, to an extent, to question some of the choices the Rams made in the draft. However, given that this was more of a class for the future, it doesn’t seem right to grade this class after four games. With that said, let’s check in on this rookie class and then look at some players that the Rams could have drafted.
During the first four games, Ty Simpson has been the weekly third-string emergency quarterback. Given how he performed in the preseason, an argument can be made that Simpson should have been the backup. However, the Rams seem to value Stetson Bennett’s experience, which will put them in an awkward spot in the case that Stafford does have to miss a game at some point. Simpson had a good preseason and can only do what the coaching staff asks of him, and they seem pleased with his current body of work.
“He’s so conscientious,” said McVay before the season. “I think you really saw his preparation and his comfort of doing the things that he's coached to do, reading with his feet, getting through progressions. I thought that really showed up in the preseason.”
If Simpson ends up as the franchise quarterback, nobody will be questioning this pick in five years. However, given the lack of production and some needs on the roster due to injuries, it’s fair to question it in the moment. Grade: B
The player that many wanted the Rams to take at 13th overall was wide receiver Makai Lemon. Given the Rams’ shift to 13 personnel and the fact that he would have been WR3 at best, Lemon didn’t make sense at that spot. Lemon struggled during the summer with the Philadelphia Eagles and through four games, he has 10 receptions for 65 yards. The Rams’ current third wide receiver, Konata Mumpfield, has six receptions for 112 yards.  Now, Lemon is undoubtedly the better player than Mumpfield, but the early production proves that the Rams were right not to take the USC wide receiver.
Not many expected Rueben Bain Jr. to be available at 13 and when he was there, some thought the Rams might select him. Instead, he went 15th overall to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. Bain looked good in the preseason but has been credited with just two pressures since. Even without Myles Garrett, the Rams are getting more production out of Josaiah Stewart in his place.
Rueben Bain Jr. had 0 sacks, 0 pressures, 0 stops, and just 1 tackle on 41 snaps in his NFL debut It’s always rough for rookies in the trenches, I expect him to improve as the season goes on pic.twitter.com/YUsxMnIYsK
With the projected shift to more 13 personnel, there were some who thought the Rams could take Kenyon Sadiq out of Oregon. Sadiq has 12 receptions for 143 yards and is producing with the New York Jets. Given the injuries to Terrance Ferguson and Colby Parkinson right now, maybe the Rams could use Sadiq. Among tight ends with at least 15 targets, Sadiq ranks fifth in yards per route run.
Unlike Lemon, an argument can be made that the Rams should have taken KC Concepcion. He brought value as a wide receiver and a returner. Right now, the Rams could use a third wide receiver and a punt returner. Concepcion has 17 receptions for 144 yards and four punt returns for 21 yards. He also brings a creative element that the Rams don’t have outside of Nacua.
Browns WR receiving yards so far this season Denzel Boston*         269 KC Concepcion*       138 Jerry Jeudy                   26 Isaiah Bond                  12 *Rookies pic.twitter.com/nICwiNCiQQ
While Denzel Boston went in the second round, it wouldn’t have been unheard of for the Rams to take him at 13 or potentially trade back for him. Boston has 13 receptions for 284 yards and is an early Offensive Rookie of the Year candidate . Like Lemon, he doesn’t have the special teams upside, but at least he’s producing in a Cleveland Browns offense.
If there is a pick to question in the Rams’ draft, it’s the Klare pick. Again, it’s easy to see the logic here . Next offseason, the Rams have a huge need at tight end. Colby Parkinson and Davis Allen are both free agents. Additionally, the future of Tyler Higbee is a bit of an uncertainty.
“I've seen a guy that's maximized a lot of opportunities in practice and done some things on special teams,” said McVay last week. “Got a lot better throughout the course of camp. [He] hasn't taken quite as many reps just because of the top four guys for the most part being available.”
It’s true that there is quite a bit of depth ahead of Klare. At the same time, the Rams had to completely shift their offense back to 11 personnel against the Eagles and Klare only played one offensive snap. A second-round pick should be able to step up in that situation. After watching the preseason, he seemed like he was capable as he finished with 12 receptions and got a lot of playing time. Grade: D
The need for a wide receiver is evident here. This would have been the perfect spot to take one and Williams went 10 picks after Klare. Williams has 12 receptions for 124 yards. He’s been stuck in a Commanders offense without Jayden Daniels, but has stood out in moments and displayed his big-play ability.
Have to love an illegal motion flag being thrown after the WR has caught the ball We Antonio Williams truthers didn’t deserve that pic.twitter.com/xbeBQ3a9E3
Coming into the season, Trost was going to be a depth piece. Unfortunately, an injury in the first preseason game put him on injured reserve . Trost was playing all over the offensive line in training camp and seemed to be someone the Rams were excited about.
“It’s not too big for him. He’s a very mature rookie,” said McVay this week on the Coach McVay show. “Got the ability to play on both the left and right side. Probably a little bit more comfortable on the right, but certainly you see the athleticism, the flexibility to get in and out of right- and-left handed stances. I like what he’s about and think he’s got a bright future for us.” Grade: B
Bell would have been a risk because of his injury history, but he had four receptions for 67 yards last week for the Miami Dolphins against the Kansas City Chiefs. The third round may have been early, but given the Rams’ issues on special teams, they could use someone like Kaden Wetjen at returner. Wetjen had a punt return for a touchdown during the preseason.
Chris Bell showing off his speed 💨 @KCvsMIA on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/tNbGIYPEGf
Daniels had a strong training camp and preseason. It’s partially why Daniels being inactive every week so far has been surprising. Daniels was a standout during training camp and then led the NFL in receptions during the preseason with 15. Unfortunately, Daniels simply may not have special…

title: Raiders vs. Patriots: 3 Key Matchups To Watch
full_text:
The Las Vegas Raiders will travel to the East Coast this weekend for an early kickoff (on the West Coast) against the reigning AFC champion, the New England Patriots.
To say the two teams are vastly different from last season is an understatement, as the Raiders are off to a 3-1 start while the Patriots, head coach Mike Vrabel, and star quarterback Drake Maye are 2-2 and still finding their rhythm. This is the first big road game for head coach Klint Kubiak as the Raiders look to start a tough two-month stretch by going 4-1 in their first five games. Here are the key matchups for Sunday's game in Foxboro.
To the Raiders' credit, their run game has improved, but it remains a below-average part of the offense after four games, ranked in the bottom 10 in the NFL at 93 yards per game. The Raiders are also averaging the fewest yards per carry (3.1) and average 1.4 yards before contact. Offensive coordinator Andrew Janocko said that paying more attention to the details will help improve this area.
"I think we just have to pay attention to our details," Janocko said. "Starting with ourselves, what we're asking of the players, how we're attacking each plan, what we are attacking each game plan. And then, presenting a great plan to the players, allowing them to be detailed so they can go out, play fast, and attack it. That's what we're looking forward to doing."
However, Las Vegas will have a chance to improve in this area against a Patriots defense that allows the fourth-most yards per carry after contact (3.8) and the third-highest missed tackle rate (18.2 percent), according to Next Gen Stats . If there is a game Ashton Jeanty can break out, this could be the opportunity he has been waiting for.
It has been stunning to see how much Drake Maye has struggled early in the season, but a great performance in Buffalo may have the former MVP runner-up back on track, which could be a disaster for most NFL secondaries. This season, Maye is 18th in passing EPA (-9.4), 17th in EPA per dropback (-0.07), and 16th in completion percentage over expected (+0.9%). He will face a Raiders pass defense that is sixth in EPA per pass (-0.12) and has an 8.2 percent sack rate— fifth in football.
The issue will be throwing against rookie cornerback Hezekiah Masses and second-round safety Treydan Stukes, arguably Las Vegas' best-performing defensive backs. The pass rush with Maxx Crosby has been exceptional. If the Raiders can do what the Jacksonville Jaguars did and make life maddening in the pocket and downfield, a win could be in sight.
Who would've thought the Las Vegas Raiders would have the sixth-best passing EPA in the NFL and Kirk Cousins would lead the league in passing touchdowns? Kubiak has done a tremendous job with this offense despite not having a true No. 1 and No. 2 wideout on the roster (unless you count Brock Bowers and Michael Mayer at tight end). This week, they play a stout Patriots secondary.
The Patriots are seventh in EPA per pass allowed (-0.11) and fifth in passing yards per game allowed (189.8). Even with Christian Gonzalez out, players such as Carlton Davis and Charles Woods have been impressive at cornerback, while safeties Craig Woodson and veteran Kevin Byard continue to make plays. This is the week Tre Tucker and Cody White will need to make substantial impacts at wide receiver, along with Bowers on the perimeter.

title: Predicting Raiders Week 5 Starters vs. Patriots: One Notable Change
full_text:
The Las Vegas Raiders will soon head to the East Coast to face the New England Patriots. Las Vegas' Week 5 matchup against the Patriots will be yet another test for Klint Kubiak's young Raiders. Las Vegas' first loss of the season adds even more intrigue to the matchup.
In the first four weeks of the regular season, Las Vegas has shown marked improvement from the 2025 season. However, their sudden surge to a 3-1 record has made 2025 an afterthought. Las Vegas' next four games will determine if it is time to readjust what is expected of them this season.
Las Vegas spent the offseason, training camp, and preseason working through their depth chart. Kubiak and his coaching style let the players' production on the field, which in some cases included positional battles, determine how the depth chart shook out entering the regular season.
Four games into the season, Las Vegas knows where each player on its depth chart and what the plan is if a player gets injured. The Raiders' coaching staff has already had to lean on the depth they have spent months building.
As the Raiders prepare to face the Patriots on Sunday, their depth chart is set, except for a few players. Offensive lineman Jackson Powers-Johnson is expected to return. However, wide receivers Jack Bech and Jalen Nailor will miss Sunday's game with injuries.
Bech was placed on Injured Reserve and will miss at least three more games, including Week 5. Nailor suffered a concussion against the Kansas City Chiefs in Week 4 and has not practiced this week, so he will likely not play against the Patriots. This leaves a sizeable hole at Las Vegas' receiver position.
With Bech and Nailor both out, the Raiders naturally have to look towards another receiver they had high hopes for during the offseason. Second-year wide receiver Dont'e Thornton was placed on Injured Reserve at the end of August, missing the first four games of the season.
The Raiders entered the regular season with questions about their receiving corps. The injuries to Bech and Nailor only add to it. Las Vegas will likely lean on its tight ends again, but Thornton has the potential to make up for lost time and help the Raiders in a time of need.
Las Vegas still has talent at the position, with Tre Tucker still leading the way. However, they'll need much more moving forward. Las Vegas' decision to approach the position by committee will only work if the committee is collectively healthy enough.
The lack of input from the receiver position negatively impacted Las Vegas' offense last week against the Chiefs. The Raiders' offensive coordinator, Andrew Janocko, recently explained what Thornton's return means for Las Vegas' offense.
"Dont'e [Thornton Jr.] brings a lot of talent at that position. He can upgrade us in a lot of different ways. He's a competitor. This guy's trying to get better. So excited to see him get out there and get back into the swing of things. We're excited for him,” Janocko said before Thursday’s practice.
"A lot of good things that he came out and did. [He] attacked the day with a really good mindset. So, it's a constant valuation thing that we can see. How he's getting back in the swing of things, getting his legs back under him and all that, building some chemistry and timing with the quarterbacks."
Raiders quarterback Kirk Cousins noted that although he has missed significant time, he hopes to help the young receiver get back up to speed quickly. Las Vegas desperately needs Thornton and others, such as Malik Benson and Dareke Young, to step up.
“He was able to be out there in OTAs, and it's been hard to get him in the mix as much since. So, it's been a while. It would be good to get him back out there and get him playing and reacclimating. But he's a great teammate. He's a great person. He's worked really hard. He stayed patient, had a great attitude, and was the kind of guy you really pull for,” Cousins said earlier this week.

title: How Raiders' Upcoming Stretch Will Reveal True Potential
full_text:
Through their first few practices ahead of their Week 5 matchup against the New England Patriots, the Las Vegas Raiders have seemed to approach things with the same attitude they did before their first loss of the season. Las Vegas didn't get too high amid their 3-0 start.
That has made their loss to the Kansas City Chiefs in Week 4 just another game in the first quarter of the season. The Raiders plan to apply what they learned from the always-talented Chiefs and move forward as a better unit throughout the season.
The Chiefs kicked off a stretch of games for Las Vegas that will solidify what this year's Raiders are and their true potential. Las Vegas will follow Sunday's matchup against the Patriots with matchups against the Buffalo Bills and the Los Angeles Rams. That is a tough four-game stretch for any team.
Las Vegas' 3-1 start is the best start they have had in years. It has given them a little bit of room for error heading into Week 5. However, Klint Kubiak and his coaching staff continue to stress that they plan to take things one day and one game at a time.
New England has an offense and defense that could trouble the Raiders on Sunday. The Patriots are 2-2, but they did beat the Buffalo Bills in Buffalo last week, which confirms just how tough a team they are.
Still, Sunday's matchup against the Patriots is another chance for Las Vegas to confirm their growth.
This season has shown that the Raiders' defense will lead the way on Sunday and beyond. Raiders defensive coordinator Rob Leonard shared his thoughts on where the unit stands ahead of Sunday's matchup against a solid Patriots offense.
“That's what good teams do is stay emotionally and consistent, consistent to the process, no emotional highs. Our team's done a great job, especially defensively on the sideline,” Leonard said.
“I think you can feel that within a game of not riding the highs and knowing that we got to reset in between series. Whether you gave up a score or getting back to it or having a takeaway. The energy is real during a game, and I think our guys have been really consistent, locked in together."
The first few days of practice this week have been productive. Overall, things have been nearly exactly the same as they have been since training camp started. The Raiders' coaching staff plans to keep doing things the same way, regardless of the results on Sunday.
For a team that has seen its fair share of weekly highs and lows in recent seasons, Las Vegas' new staff is establishing a new way of doing things in the locker room. Raiders offensive coordinator Andrew Janocko echoed Leonard's sentiment.
"It's next up, next day mentality. We have another game coming, so you win, you lose. Either way, you got to evaluate the next day. So, when you come back into the office the next day, whether it's a win or lose, you're trying to scrutinize every part of the plan, every technique we use,” Janocko said.
“Whether it's sometimes wins, you can even be more critical. But you want to be uber critical of yourself, uber critical of what you're doing, so you can fix mistakes and build on the stuff you're doing well."
Las Vegas is in a good position heading into the second quarter of their season. However, one way or the other, the next month of games will make or break the Raiders' season. Right now, the Raiders control much of their future with how they play moving forward.
Sunday's loss was eye-opening for the Raiders' new roster and coaching staff. It clearly identified the areas Las Vegas needs to improve that may have been overlooked by some because of their early success. As interesting as their loss to the Chiefs was, their response will be even more telling.
The most important game is always the next one. That couldn't be truer for this Raiders team heading into Week 5.

title: Hondo's Thursday Raiders Musings: A Chance To Flip the Script
full_text:
The Las Vegas Raiders (3-1) are set to invade Boston this weekend to take on the reigning AFC Super Bowl representative, the New England Patriots (2-2)
The rebuilding Raiders have a chance to change the narrative with a win that could propel them into the NFL playoff discussion and make a clear statement that they are ahead of schedule. A win in New England this weekend would flip the script from rebuild to NFL Playoffs instantly.
Each Thursday, I offer you my musings as a beat writer covering this team from the inside, and today is no different.
The biggest criticism of the Raiders' offense this season has been the ability to run the football. The Raiders need to get the run going , and they'll have significantly more opportunity to do so this weekend. Still, NFL teams know running the ball is the foundation of a Klint Kubiak offense. Without a WR1, and with Jalen Nailor being questionable at best, it makes a total commitment to running the ball even harder.
Kubiak won’t back down. Kubiak won’t flinch; if the Patriots want to stack the box, as others have, he will keep pounding the football to keep the Patriots honest.
We have detailed previously that NFL execs have been shocked by the Raiders' tenacity this year, and rightfully so, but going to New England and winning is a simple case of needing more of the same. If a Silver and Black team plays this weekend as they did last, they will win.
It doesn’t change the Raiders' holes, their rebuild-related weak points, or their youth.
A win in New England would show this team is overachieving and that its parts add up to something impressive and ahead of schedule. Make no mistake that a win in New England would be an upset, but don’t fool yourself into thinking this is the Raiders of old.
They aren’t going to the Northeast hoping to win; they expect to.
The Raiders have a gem of an RB1 in Ashton Jeanty, and they know he is the straw that stirs the Raiders' running attack. There is a sense in the building that this weekend could be big for the young man, and getting him back to his Week 1 numbers against the Miami Dolphins would be enormous; Kubiak didn’t hide that.
"Going back to that first game, just as a whole unit, we played better. We were more efficient running the football, and that's something we got to get back to. So, it's something that we're diligent about. We're practicing, and it's players and coaches working together."
This is the NFL, the best of the best, professionals. They know Kubiak’s offense is predicated on running the ball, and they'll stack the box to stop it. But Kubiak, despite defenses selling out to stop the run, won’t give up.
"It's every week, you're always trying to find a way to win, and sometimes guys get more looks than others. But it's a long season, 17-game season, and it takes everybody to win."
He added about facing those boxes stacked, "Yes, it definitely makes it tougher. But that's still part of our job, is to find ways to move it."
Cody White has been outstanding since joining the organization, and Kubiak targeted him, wanted him, and GM John Spytek went and got him. Each week, the Michigan State Spartan is making big plays, which is exactly why Kubiak wanted him.
"Well, I'll just say he's a good football player. He's getting open. He does it right in the run game. He plays on special teams. He's a good football player. Obviously, he came over as a practice squad add and has earned his way onto the active. That's with every player; we want them to earn it."
Kubiak is all about winning; he doesn’t want to hear about a rebuild or anything other than winning. Al Davis would love him for that, and he focuses solely on it.
“But as far as what we're trying to build is, we're just trying to win, trying to win every game, just like every team the NFL is. That is our mindset, just to win. Not to build or rebuild or anything. Just looking at the next game and competing and winning that game."
Drake Maye is coming off a great week, and the Patriots signal caller is a top young prospect in this league. Kubiak knows how good he is, and he is squarely in the Raiders' thinking process.
"Many things. Obviously, started in the Super Bowl last year and had a great game last week. His mobility, his arm strength, his football intelligence, we have a lot of respect for him."
Kubiak talked about what he wants his team to focus on. He has often discussed 17 one-game seasons, and his goal for what he wants on their minds hasn't changed.
"Just focusing on the first quarter of the season, what we've done well, what we need to improve on, and knowing that our opponents are working on our weaknesses all the time. So, there's so many little things on each side of the ball that that we're keying on, and we're trying to be very intentional about improving."
He may not be the starter, or even the backup, but Aidan O’Connell is loved by his teammates, and having him back after dealing with a deeply personal family matter is great for the Silver and Black and for Kubiak, who truly loves and appreciates him.
"It's great. He gave us a great boost when he came back last week. We really missed him, missed his leadership, his maturity, the type of teammate that he is, and obviously the type of player that he is."
Kubiak has an advantage this weekend in that he schemed for the Patriots' defense in the Super Bowl and won. Does that help this weekend? What would you expect him to say?
"Yeah, they were a great defense last season. They're a great defense this season with a lot of talented players, really talented coaching staff. They play hard, and this is a defense that we have a ton of respect for."
Kirk Cousins knows that playing the Patriots in their stadium is no easy task, but he says it has the attention of the entire NFL.
"Got a big challenge this week on the road against the team that was in the Super Bowl last year. It's got the respect of the whole league, tough place to play, so you know it's going to take our best effort, and just got to put together a good Wednesday, and that's where the focus lies."
The Raiders have put the Chiefs loss in the rearview mirror, and they are entirely focused on the Patriots. Cousins made it clear that this is about the next game, and the Raiders are playing for a lot.
"I think we just have so much to be focused on now moving forward that keeps our attention on today, really. The game plan and all that it takes to put together a great Wednesday. So, I think so. But that's what mature teams got to do is be able to respond and look ahead and keep pushing no matter what happens."
Cousins is a 15-year veteran for a reason, and looking each week at stacked boxes to stop the run, he knows it's just another opportunity for the Silver and Black to punish them in other ways.

title: 'Good Football Player.' Raiders' Cody White Making Big Impact
full_text:
The Las Vegas Raiders may have lost this past weekend, but starting the season 3-1 is something no one saw coming.
This team has had a few surprises in their successful start, whether it's the emergence of the Raiders offense and veteran quarterback Kirk Cousins, a defense playing at an impressively high level, or younger players making impact plays on either side of the ball.
One of those surprises has been Cody White, a former Michigan State standout who went undrafted and has bounced between teams. He has spent time with the Pittsburgh Steelers and Seattle Seahawks over the last five seasons, but in Year 6, he has found a unique role as an impact playmaker for the Raiders' offense.
Through the last three games, White has caught five passes on nine targets for 64 yards and three touchdowns. One of his best games came Sunday against the Kansas City Chiefs , when he caught two passes for 36 yards. While White has made most of his impact on special teams, former Seattle Seahawks offensive coordinator and now Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak has become impressed with what White has done on offense.
What exactly has allowed White to capitalize on his opportunities? Kubiak explained that White earned it by moving from the practice squad to the active roster, considering his first three catches in a Raiders uniform were touchdowns.
"Well, I'll just say he's a good football player," Kubiak said. "He's getting open. He does it right in the run game. He plays on special teams. He's a good football player. Obviously, he came over as a practice squad add and has earned his way onto the active [roster]. That's with every player; we want them to earn it."
Kubiak wasn't the only one to sing White's praises; quarterback Kirk Cousins, who leads the NFL in passing touchdowns, thought he had two more chances to help White make an impact in Sunday's loss, clearly kicking himself for it. However, the way Cousins described the seventh-year journeyman's traits stood out.
"If you watch the tape, there's a good two more opportunities that I felt I missed that would have given him a chance to really impact the game," Cousins explained. "So, I was kicking myself for those plays, but the ball just has found him. I don't have a great answer for you."
"I think it's just kind of how the pocket allows me to get through the progression, and the ball finds him, and he's attacked the football. I think that's the trait that I would say has jumped off the tape, whether it was the Chargers touchdown or the goal ball last week, just attacking the football and saying, 'Ball's in the air, that's my ball.'"
Maybe, just maybe, the Michigan State connection is legitimate. Both White and Cousins are program alumni, and the latter said what he saw in East Lansing—wearing No. 7 and attacking the ball as he did in college—still stood out.
"I think probably going back to watching him at Michigan State a little bit as a alumni. Seeing him make plays there in the number seven, and then that play against the Chargers where he attacked the football for a touchdown in tight coverage. I thought those traits surfaced, and he's been doing it since."
You could make the case that White has been the second-most impactful wide receiver on the Raiders roster alongside Tre Tucker. Before you know it, No. 82 could be a key piece of Las Vegas' offense ahead of a daunting eight-game stretch.

title: New Realities Emerging for Raiders After Four Games
full_text:
The Las Vegas Raiders fell to the Kansas City Chiefs this past weekend, but it was a significant outing for the Silver and Black.
Despite starting the season 3-0, many questioned the Raiders' legitimacy because their wins came against the Dolphins, Chargers, and Saints. Week 4 was the first real test Las Vegas went through, and it's safe to say they passed with flying colors. Here's what we learned about the Raiders in their 30-27 loss to the Chiefs .
We're only a fourth of the way through the 2026 NFL season, so this may sound premature, but the Raiders have shown enough to believe this isn't a fluke. Las Vegas dictated terms in the first half and held the Chiefs at bay through the third quarter before Kenneth Walker III ripped off a 76-yard run.
The upcoming stretch - Patriots, Bills, and Rams - will reveal a lot more about the legitimacy of this sentiment. Even if Las Vegas loses two of those three games, it should still be in a favorable spot in the AFC playoff picture. Four teams in the AFC are 0-4, including the Texans, Chargers, Titans, and Dolphins, who you could consider de facto eliminated. The Raiders' roster is more complete than people give it credit for, and a postseason berth is viable.
If you didn't watch this game and just saw that the Chiefs scored 30 points, you would think it was a poor defensive performance. However, that wasn't the case. As mentioned, Las Vegas allowed 10 points in the first half. Additionally, Kansas City's offense relied on a few explosive plays to drive in points.
Outside of those plays, the Chiefs struggled to string together long drives throughout the game. Kansas City also got seven points off a fumbled kickoff return. It's nearly impossible to prevent an opposing team from scoring when it starts with the ball inside the red zone. Not to mention, the Raiders kept Patrick Mahomes in check, as the 31-year-old quarterback completed 15-of-30 passes for 225 yards and two touchdowns, while being sacked twice.
Barring injury, the 38-year-old quarterback is primed to start all 17 games, allowing Fernando Mendoza to redshirt his rookie season. Cousins was forced to throw the ball over 50 times, completing 31-of-52 attempts for 365 yards, two touchdowns, and one interception.
This season, the 15-year veteran has thrown for 1,026 yards, 11 touchdowns, and four interceptions, while completing 64.6 percent of his passes. Las Vegas' rushing attack hasn't even clicked yet. Imagine when Ashton Jeanty finally gets going. This offense could be one of the most well-rounded units when it all comes together.

title: 3 Storylines I'm Watching Most in Raiders Week 5 Matchup
full_text:
The Las Vegas Raiders are back to work after suffering their first loss of the season last Sunday against the Kansas City Chiefs. Las Vegas has no room to dwell on last week, as they now face a strong New England Patriots team that has one of the league's best players under center.
The Patriots pose multiple problems for a Raiders team still coming together in its first season under head coach Klint Kubiak. Las Vegas' first four games were a success, but the season is long.
Las Vegas has begun a tough slate of teams in consecutive weeks. They have earned a little bit of breathing room. However, with games against several of the league's best teams coming up, the Raiders cannot let their guard down, or their 3-1 record can quickly become 3-4.
Many factors will shape how things turn out between the two teams this weekend. Las Vegas' coaching staff needs to have the team well prepared to face a talented Patriots team early on Sunday. Below are the storylines I am watching the most when the Raiders face the Patriots.
The Raiders' defense was near the top of the league in forced turnovers through the first three weeks of the season. Then, Las Vegas played a Chiefs team that entered Week 3 with only two turnovers, ranking near the top of the league. Las Vegas did not force a turnover against the Chiefs.
New England is the opposite. They don't have Patrick Mahomes, and they are tied for the most turnovers in the league. The Patriots are tied with the Los Angeles Chargers for the most turnovers in the league through three games. Las Vegas hopes to have similar success forcing turnovers.
The Raiders will not face Mahomes on Sunday, but Drake Maye is undoubtedly talented. Nearly every defensive back who played extensive minutes against the Chiefs has plays they want back. Sunday against the Patriots is their chance to get back on track.
Mahomes may not be on the field, but every defensive coordinator in the league now has a blueprint of what works. The Raiders' defensive backfield must clean up a few things during this week of practice before heading to the East Coast.
Jeanty is far from healthy. There were plays in the first four games of the season that a healthy Jeanty would have made. Coaches and Jeanty himself will downplay it, as they should.
However, the game of football rarely cares what is said. One look at Jeanty's performances this season will confirm that he is not healthy and may be flat-out uncomfortable on the field. Sure, all teams are dealing with injuries.
Still, few are dealing with an injury that takes away what makes one of their best players special. Luckily, even injured, Jeanty adds value to the Raiders' offense. I will be watching his health, his running burst, and his ability to jump-cut as only a healthy Jeanty can.
Las Vegas' offensive line will do its part , but it created multiple holes for Jeanty that he likely would have attacked better had he been healthy. Las Vegas still has other backs to help with the running back duties. Kirk Cousins explained the challenges Las Vegas has faced running the ball.
“It just becomes a little bit of the math of how many players are down inside the tight end box, and do we have angles, do we have numbers or don't we? And it changes play to play, and even within the play,” Cousins said earlier this week before practice.
“Sometimes they can start with eight in the box and kind of then be bailing out on the snap, or they can start with seven in the box and kind of move down at the snap. So, it's kind of a fluid deal, but teams are always going to be in that cat-and-mouse game a little bit of how you're trying to defend or how you're trying to attack the defense."

title: 3 Matchups That Will Decide Raiders' Week 5 Matchup vs. Patriots
full_text:
Each passing week gives us another look at this year's Las Vegas Raiders and the new direction they are heading in. Las Vegas started the season 3-1, which is better than most would have expected before the season began.
Below are three matchups I believe will determine the Raiders' chances of beating the Patriots on the road this Sunday.
Las Vegas' offense often capitalized on short fields their defense gave up during the first three weeks of the season. The Raiders' loss to the Chiefs exposed the unit's strengths and weaknesses. The same unit that scored 13 points in the first three quarters against the Chiefs scored 14 in the fourth quarter.
This confirms that the Raiders' offensive success has just as much, if not more, to do with executing the proper play call as their opponent's. Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak, who coached against the Patriots in last season's Super Bowl, knows how tough the Patriots' defense is.
“They were a great defense last season. They're a great defense this season with a lot of talented players, really talented coaching staff. They play hard, and this is a defense that we have a ton of respect for,” Kubiak said earlier this week.
So far, the Raiders' offense has continued to gel through the first quarter of the season. Kirk Cousins shared his thoughts on the offense and the team as a whole as they prepare for a Patriots team that is well established after spending years together.
“I think it's been a resilient group . I think our defense has played very well. I think guys are making plays. I think it's probably less learning and more confirming what I learned about them back in the spring or even in training camp,” Cousins said.
“These guys, they want to do it the right way. Football means something to them. They're hardworking, listen well, and it makes it a joy to be the quarterback for a group of guys like that. But you got to go prove it again every week.”
This one will be multifaceted, as the Patriots have a group of underrated but solid wide receivers, similar to the Kansas City Chiefs. New England also has Hunter Henry, a younger, more agile version of Travis Kelce, whom they faced last week.
Teams will likely use their passing attack to open up running lanes against the Raiders' defense. Las Vegas' defense must get back to where it was in the first three weeks of the season, when the unit used sticky coverage and stout run-stopping to make teams one-dimensional.
Entering this season, Las Vegas' need for additional help in its defensive backfield was no secret. Their 3-0 start may have overshadowed that need, but their loss to the Chiefs should have reinforced it. The Raiders' rebuild is just beginning, especially in their defensive backfield.
Teams will attack this position group weekly, especially after the success the Chiefs had last Sunday.
Las Vegas found itself thin at wide receiver against the Chiefs after losing Jalen Nailor to a concussion during the game. With Jack Bech already out with an injury, Las Vegas needs Tre Tucker and others to step up until the unit returns to full strength.

I think that's the trait that I would say has jumped off the tape, whether it was the Chargers touchdown or the goal ball last week, just attacking the football and saying, 'Ball's in the air, that's my ball.'"

title: How Raiders Plan To Bounce Back From First Loss
full_text:
For better or for worse, the Las Vegas Raiders' Week 4 loss to the Kansas City Chiefs essentially confirmed what this year's team will be. After four games, Las Vegas' strengths and weaknesses are becoming clearer. Many of Las Vegas' strengths and weaknesses were on display in each game.
The Raiders jumped out to a 3-0 start to the season behind a stingy defense that forced turnovers better than nearly any team in the league through the first three games. Las Vegas' defense also ranked near the top of the league in sacks during that span.
In a league driven by quarterbacks and offense, Las Vegas' defense has led the way this season. The Raiders' defense has set the table for an opportunistic offense. Through three games, Las Vegas rarely beat itself with backbreaking mistakes.
Nearly all of those things changed against the Chiefs. Las Vegas' defense failed to create any turnovers, which forced the Raiders' offense to work harder than it had all season. The Raiders' offense had to work harder because they faced one of the NFL's best defenses.
Still, Las Vegas fought until the very end, losing to the Chiefs by three points. As the week progresses, the Raiders have returned to the practice field to prepare for their third road game in four weeks. The Raiders are set to face a talented New England Patriots team.
The Patriots are coming off a Super Bowl appearance in 2025-26. They are currently 2-2, with wins over the Pittsburgh Steelers and Buffalo Bills. New England's defense ranks in the top 10 in yards and points allowed per game, allowing among the fewest of any team.
Overall, the Raiders have reason to be just as optimistic and hopeful as they were before their loss to the Chiefs. They are still ahead of schedule for now. Yet things change quickly in the league. Las Vegas' coaching staff must produce a solid week of practice to regain momentum.
Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak is only focused on his team taking care of their end of things ahead of their Week 5 matchup against the Patriots.
"I just worry about us. Not thinking as much about them, other than the game, the team we're playing this week schematically and player-wise,” Kubiak said before Wednesday’s practice.
“But as far as what we're trying to build is, we're just trying to win, trying to win every game, just like every team the NFL is. That is our mindset, just to win. Not to build or rebuild or anything. Just looking at the next game and competing and winning that game."
With the Raiders' first loss of the season highlighting many of the things they struggled with in the first three games, Las Vegas has no room to let their guard down. Each passing week gives upcoming opponents a better idea of what to expect from Las Vegas throughout the rest of the season.
Kubiak's coaching staff has shown the ability to scheme and call plays well. They have shown they can make necessary adjustments that put players in position to succeed, should they execute. However, those abilities begin in practice, as Kirk Cousins noted.
“I think we just have so much to be focused on now moving forward that keeps our attention on today, really. The game plan and all that it takes to put together a great Wednesday. So, I think so. But that's what mature teams got to do is be able to respond and look ahead and keep pushing no matter what happens,” Cousins said before practice on Wednesday.
“It is early, but I think you just go right back to work. I think Monday, we had good workouts, good meetings. Tuesday, a lot of guys are in here doing a myriad of things, and so you just go through your weekly process, your rhythm, your routine. And I think we as a team, we as individuals, have a good process we're going to stick to and trust that that’ll get us ready for what we got to do on Sunday."

title: One Simple Thing Stands Between Raiders Rebuild and NFL Playoffs
full_text:
The Las Vegas Raiders (3-1) will head to New England on Friday to prepare for their Sunday matchup against the Patriots (2-2) in Boston.
In the Raiders' rebuild, there is no question that they are ahead of schedule in wins, but that doesn’t mean they’ve been perfect. They haven’t, and neither has any other NFL team.
The nature of the game is that the other side has players who are paid millions of dollars, and they have a say in your success or failure. I already gave you my winners and losers from last week; this is not the discussion today.
The iconic Green Bay Packers coach, Vince Lombardi, is credited with being the first football coach to tell the hard truth about this glorious game centered around a pigskin-covered oblong ellipsoid: "Football is a game of inches, and inches make the champion."
​Most people remember it from the awesome pregame speech by Al Pacino's character in the legendary movie "Any Given Sunday."
While Pacino said it in a pretend world, quoting Lombardi, who lived it in the real world, the Raiders are learning that to overachieve, they have to find those inches.
Matt Gay has been an exceptional kicker for the Raiders in 2026. On Saturday, he is credited with four made field goals, but he actually had five.
Kubiak took one of his successes off the board after a Chiefs penalty. This article is not directed towards debating Kubiak’s decision, but when the Raiders' subsequent play failed, it was a total of five drives that ended with only three points, or no points.
After the game in which the Raiders only lost by three points, QB Kirk Cousins said it best.
"I think there's a lot to build on. I felt like our defense did just a great job keeping us in the game. We kicked too many field goals, didn't score enough points but our defense's play allowed us to still have a lead, to still be in it for so much of the game, so it's just tough to not finish."
Cousins wasn’t attacking Gay, far from it. He was making it clear that the offense he leads can’t settle for field goals. In a points-driven league, the Raiders need touchdowns.
If any of those four successful field goals had been turned into touchdowns, those four points would have been the difference in a Raiders win, and us discussing today the Raiders being 4-0.
I am not a revisionist. I stand by my takes. As a football nerd, I love and respect how Kubiak is attacking. Cousins does as well, but for the Raiders to go from simply rebuilding to overachieving and becoming an NFL Playoff option, they have to find the end zone at a higher rate.
I agree with Cousins on this, who made it very clear.
"Klint [Kubiak] felt we needed to be aggressive, we needed to be attacking all game long. If you come in here trying to just hang around with a good football team, it may not pan out the way you want. Felt like we needed to attack, just wish there have been, by me, better execution at moments that would have given us that chance to come out on top."
If the Raiders get the upset on Sunday, and they are very capable of it, they have to find the inches. The Patriots are the reigning AFC representative in the Super Bowl, and the Silver and Black can make a definitive statement.
What is the statement? Rebuild or not, they are ahead of schedule, and the NFL Playoffs are now on the map.
If the Raiders find the inches on Sunday, they will have changed the season's narrative. If they don’t, this rebuild is still clearly on the right road.
The playoffs are made up of teams that find the inches. We will learn on Sunday if the Raiders are one of those teams.
I suspect they might be. We'll see if they can find the inches. I believe in Kubiak; the team does, and on Sunday, I think the nation will as well.

title: Projecting When the Dolphins Offense Will Break Out
full_text:
The Miami Dolphins' 0-4 record isn't necessarily shocking given all the roster sacrifices the team made to get its salary cap in order, but maybe the lack of offense wasn't totally expected.
A depressing stat surfaced after the Week 4 loss against the Minnesota Vikings, courtesy of Tim Reynolds from The Associated Press, indicating the Dolphins became the third team since 2004 to fail to score at least 14 points in any of their first four games.
The other two? The 2004 Dolphins and the 2019 Dolphins.
Like the 2026 edition, the 2019 Dolphins were in full rebuilding mode in Brian Flores' first year as head coach, though things were much different with the 2004 team.
The Dolphins were coming off a string of seven consecutive winning seasons, including a 10-6 finish in 2003, but things started going off the rails even before Ricky Williams blindsided the team by deciding to retire on the eve of training camp, with Joel Collier resigning as offensive coordinator in the spring citing exhaustion.
One big difference between the 2026 team and the previous two is that Malik Willis has been the only quarterback to play so far this season, while Jay Fiedler and A.J. Feeley split the first four starts in 2004 and Ryan Fitzpatrick and Josh Rosen did the same in 2019.
While the 2026 Dolphins at least have reached 10 points in each of their four games, the 2019 team reached 10 points twice in the first month that season and had a total of 26 during its 0-4 start, while the 2004 team was held under 10 points in three of its first four games.
Where the 2026 team is way ahead of those other two editions is in taking care of the ball because turnovers were a major problem in 2004 and 2019.
Through four games, the Dolphins have committed five turnovers this season, compared to nine in 2019 and a whopping 14 in 2004. The Dolphins also have been much better on third down, converting at a 38 percent clip this year, compard to 26.8 and 26 percent in those two other seasons.
And while Malik Willis' performance hasn't been good enough so far, the Dolphins still have gotten much better quarterbacking than they did in 2004 or 2019. Willis' passer rating currently stands at 73.0, while the two 2004 QBs were at 48.4 and Fitpatrick and Rosen combined for a 52.5 rating through four games in 2019.
The obvious question, of course, is when will the Dolphins offense reach at least 14 points and/or score more than one touchdown in a game.
The 2019 Dolphins' winless streak to start the season reached seven games before the 5-4 finish, but they did get to 16 points in their fifth game, a 17-16 loss against Washington.
The 2004 Dolphins failed to score at least 14 points through their first six games and were 0-6 before they finally broke out in a 31-14 victory against the St. Louis Rams.
The Dolphins' next game is against a Cincinnati Bengals defense that gave up 22 points against Jacksonville in Week 4 after allowing 30 against the Pittsburgh Steelers the previous Sunday.
So maybe this is the week for Miami. If not, the Dolphins will have to wait at least another two weeks because they have their bye in Week 6 before facing the New York Jets at MetLife Stadium on October 25.
When the streak will end is anybody's guess and it should happen sooner rather than later, and it would have happened against the Minnesota Vikings last Sunday if not for Chris Bell barely stepping out of bounds before catching that long pass from Willis.

title: How Dolphins Head Coach Jeff Hafley Addressed Three Key Problem Areas ... And Our Take On His Takes
full_text:
There are several issues the Miami Dolphins are facing right now, which is to be expected for a team that’s 0-4 and in the early stages of a pretty massive rebuilding project.
Three issues in particular stand out, and that Malik Willis’ performance at quarterback, Austin Jackson’s apparent pass-protection problems, and the defense giving up sizable numbers to opposing tight ends.
Head coach Jeff Hafley was asked all three topics during his pre-practice media session Wednesday, and we decide to examine his comments and offer our take on them.
We don’t need to remind everyone that Hafley and Jon-Eric Sullivan brought Willis from Green Bay because they believed in him, but the results obviously haven’t been good for the offense so far in 2026. Willis clearly is operating with a substandard supporting cast that got that much more mediocre when De’Von Achane tore his ACL, but Willis hasn’t yet done anywhere near enough to convince folks he should be the starting quarterback beyond this season.
Willis is near the bottom among NFL quarterbacks in both passer rating and completion percentage and he’s accounted for only two touchdowns with four turnovers (two fumbles, two picks),
He has twice as many turnovers as touchdowns produced. Is that a concern? We know that Malik is a work in progress. Is that a concern?
“I would say like everything else, like what can we do better, right? We’ve got to look ahead at this point and not behind and we’ve got to improve. And that's with everything that we're doing right now in all three phases with all the coaches and all the players and that's where we're at.”
Our take: Hafley is being very careful not to throw Willis or anybody else under the bus, so he is diverting specific questions about Willis to the entire offense, which is fair in a way because the whole offense is a big-time work in progress. That said, Willis isn’t without blame and there are improvements to be made in all areas, whether it be consistency, accuracy, decision-making, foot work, etc.
The Dolphins are coming off the loss at Minnesota where T.J Hockenson had 13 catches for 119 yards, including the game-clinching third-down before the two-minute warning. Before that, George Kittle had four catches for 80 yards, with a 40-yard reception and a wide open touchdown and Travis Kelce had a 48-yard catch and another wide open touchdown. And in the opener the Dolphins avoided Raiders star Brock Bowers because of an injury, but backup Michael Mayer wound up tying for the team lead with six receptions.
So I asked Hafley on Wednesday what’s been the biggest issue in defending tight ends, and he replied that he doesn’t look at the opponent by position but rather what needs to be done to keep them from scoring and then prioritizing the top threats, to which I followed up asking if he then ever would consider the tight end the player his defense needs to prioritize.
“Absolutely, yeah. If he's the most explosive player and we need to pay attention to that guy, for sure. But just in general, when you look at a team, it's who do we have to stop that can beat us the fastest? And you kind of go down in that order. Or who do we need to protect on our side of the ball that they're going to go after, right? So I think that all kind of balances out as you go. I mean, if you want to look at this week, there's a couple guys that we're going to have to pay very close attention to. You can't pay attention to all of them. So I respect the question, and there's some plays we need to play better on tight ends in situations where we're right there and there's some where they might get a five-yard pass because in zone defense there's a no cover zone that they're dumping the ball off to and you're rallying. There's give and take. Does that make sense?”
Our take: Yes, it makes sense, and there definitely was a pick-your-poison element when facing the 49ers or Chiefs offense because in addition to a star tight end, the 49ers have one of the top running backs in the NFL with Christian McCaffrey and an elite wide receiver with Mike Evans, while Kansas City has the league’s rushing leader with Kenneth Walker and speed galore at wide receiver. Maybe we have more of an issue here with Minnesota and being overly protective of the deep ball against a wide receiver corps that was missing Justin Jefferson. Yes, Jordan Addison is a former first-round pick and Aaron Jones is a solid running back, but wouldn’t it have made more sense to try to make Kyler Murray beat the Dolphins deep. What can’t be helped by scheme are the one-on-one battles the Dolphins lost, for which Jordyn Brooks took responsibility after the game.
The nature of playing tackle in the NFL is that getting beat is impossible to hide, and there was obvious pressure coming from the left side of the defensive formation in the Minnesota game, including the Dolphins’ final third down of the game, the throw down the middle to Chris Bell where Willis was hurried.
This has been a recurring them, but Hafley was quick to point out after earlier games that Jackson was going against stars like Maxx Crosby and Nick Bosa.
The question becomes, at what point does Jackson’s apparent protection issues become a real concern.
“I'm not concerned,” Hafley said. “I think if you really study that tape and watch the tape, you'll see improvement from Austin in that last game as well as the rest of our offensive line. So I am not concerned.”
Our take: Even if Jackson wasn’t constantly beaten in this game, there’s absolutely still room for improvement and having him beat so quickly on a key play late in the game like he was is just disappointing beyond words. That Hafley is backing his veteran is understandable, and the other fact that can’t be overlooked is that it’s not like the Dolphins have great options right now because moving Kadyn Proctor from left guard to right tackle after he’s gotten off a good start doesn’t seem wise at all and there’s a vast experience drop-off to Caedan Wallace or even Chukwueduka Godrick. We understand tackles will get beat from time to time, but at some point Jackson has to pitch a shutout.

title: Dolphins Wednesday Mailbag: How Will the Defense Deal with Mike Gesicki?
full_text:
Part 2 of the post-Vikings game Miami Dolphins On SI mailbag:
Hi Alain, with our problems covering TEs which needs to fixed ASAP, is Kyle Louis a potential solution if he returns and, if so, what is his timeline for return?
Hey Keith, Louis will be eligible to return from IR after the Week 5 game against the Bengals, but we have not gotten a progress report on his recovery from his knee injury, so I don’t know that he’ll be back for the Week 7 game against the Jets after the bye. I would suspect he’ll be given a shot to cover tight ends at some point, but I’d be concerned a bit about his lack of size being a problem there.
Why have the special teams been so awful and will we have to wait until next year to fix the problems?
Look at how the Dolphins have churned the bottom of the roster, which is where all of the special teams units get their players. Then add the inexperience factor with a lot of rookies involved. Then you can see where issues pop up. The group should get better as the season progresses, but it started from a difficult position.
Is the game too fast for Malik Willis ? He seems flustered at times, not seeing open receivers and often off target (inconsistent). Should we still view him like a rookie where the game has not yet slowed down?
Hey Zander, it’s a fair question, but how often is he flustered because there’s pressure and his receivers aren’t getting open? I’m not buying this “game is too fast” narrative, but he’s certainly more inconsistent than ideal with his passes and what’s pretty clear is he often doesn’t set his feet probably and relies too much on his arm strength.
Is it me or did anyone else get an uneasy impression from Malik Willis’ demeanor when the cameras were on him from the sidelines? Wouldn’t you be talking to your WRs and OC and trying to get organized and such, especially right before their last drive w/ 6+ minutes left.
Hey Bubba, yeah, I’m not on board that whole narrative. If there were specific issues that needed to be discussed before a drive, rest assured the offensive coach on the sideline would get with Willis to go over everything.
On the flight home, what was that conversation like between Hafley and the special teams coach?
Hey Jayco, it might have gone something like this, “Hey, Chris (Tabor), make sure you remind Malik (Washington) not to try fielding a punt around the 5-yard line and let’s keep coaching our young players so our kick coverage teams stop leaking, even though I understand you’ve got a lot of fringe NFL players and young guys on that unit.”
Hi Alain, thx for all the hard work. Why it seems that we have the same issues regardless of who's the head coach? Bad offensive line play, defending TE, has been an issue forever. Is it Grier been in charge for so long?
Well, everything this season boils down to the roster not being good enough and not having enough experience, so I guess you could pin that on Grier because of the roster overhaul the new regime deemed necessary.
Have you seen enough from Malik to say he is/isn’t the guy? I think it’s too early to say no, but it’s leaning that way.
You said it right there, it’s way too early for me. We’ve seen flashes here and there with some great off-schedule plays that we haven’t gotten from a Dolphins QB in maybe a decade, but the consistency just hasn’t been there. But the question is whether the consistency is lacking because Willis just isn’t the guy or because the supporting case currently just isn’t good enough and that consistency will show up once it improves.
Hi Alain, I watched the game hoping to see some improvement. On defense I did but one area is still bad. Why can’t this team cover a tight end? The running game was better, but there seems to be a real issue with our passing game. Lack of talent or chemistry? Maybe next week.
Hey Mark, yeah, this doesn’t have anything to do with chemistry. The Dolphins just don’t have that one guy who can cover tight ends one-on-one and they’ve left big holes in their zones at times, and then you’ve had some busted coverages. It’s a combination of several factors, none of them good.
At Monday’s presser Hafley did something I’ve never really seen him do. Perk asked him about a third-and-goal play where Willis had to choice to run for the end zone or make a pass attempt. Perk asked if he made the right choice on that particular play and he said something to the effect of everything happens so fast that it’s Willis’s choice to make. To me it was a deflection. It’s his job as coach to look at every play and make a determination of what the right thing to do is. I looked at play in real time and thought he had a lane and should have ran for the end zone. Even if he doesn’t make it, he would have been stopped very close to the end zone and the Dolphins would have had a choice to go for it on fourth-and-short. I thought Hafley for the first time was copping out. Are we to the point where the coach is excuse-making and deflecting? Do you think Willis should have ran for it ? Also currently Willis has one of the lowest completion percentages in the league; how concerning is that stat?
Hey Dana, first off, I’m on board with Hafley saying Willis has to make that decision because the last thing you want is a QB playing robotically and do you really want a coach publicly second-guessing a player’s decision after the fact? Do you eliminate the possibility that Hafley told Willis privately that if the situation presents itself again he should go for it? It’s very easy for fans and the media alike to look at a replay and decide what a player should have done; it’s not the same thing at full speed. Even if Hafley agreed with you that he should have run, I think we’ve seen he’s not willing to criticize his players publicly and I’m not going to fault him for that. Just like Malik Washington fielding a punt around the 6-yard line seemed like a clear mistake, but Hafley answered a question about the muff without saying that. And the completion percentage stat itself doesn’t bother me because a throw at the line of scrimmage just to get that number up doesn’t accomplish anything (as we saw for most of 2024 and in 2025). I would like to see more success in the passing game, period.
Will Storm Duck replace Jason Marshall in lineup or will Chris Johnson slide inside to the slot more? Seeing some All-22 tape on our receivers getting separation, it seems like Willis is struggling reading the field, with his decision-making, and knowing where to go with the ball in the pre-snap read. Do you believe this is something that can be taught and worth 2-3 years invested?
I wouldn’t assume anything about Duck immediately going into the starting lineup. You got all that about Willis from the All-22? If you’re accurate about your assessments there, no, it’s not worth investing 2-3 years. Or it could be that Willis needs to be more consistent at everything and he needs more help from the offense.
I’m wondering what the answers the Dolphins may try to limit tight ends running roughshod over our defense. I like the growth I've seen so far, but this is going to continue to be an issue until we find a coherent response.
Correct, and the answer isn’t easy and requires improvement in several areas, whether in man or zone coverage.
Hey Alain, after hearing Hafley's press conference last week about getting Greg Dulcich more involved, I was surprised to see that he didn't even get a target. He's probably our most accomplished receiving threat and one would think that he would be a safety blanket for Willis (kinda like Murray to Hockenson was). Hard to believe he can't be schemed up to get open, especially on a designed rollout where the tight end kind of runs a 5-yard out toward the sideline. Tua did in a couple of those a game for us last year and they always seem to work. And I was also disappointed in Willis not reading the field properly, because if you look from the All 22 he had receivers open, yet couldn't pull the trigger or was not…

title: Dolphins Tuesday Mailbag: What's the Biggest Issue with Each Unit?
full_text:
Part 1 of the post-Vikings game Miami Dolphins On SI mailbag:
I’ve been following you for years and you always give us the truth no matter how hard it is to hear sometimes. My question is even though it’s early this draft seems solid; is there a chance we found a GM and possibly coach for the future?
Hey Mark, yeah, the early returns from the 2026 draft have been pretty encouraging that GM Jon-Eric Sullivan can pick good players, though I’d caution against anointing any draft pick a hit just yet. We also don’t know what Sullivan can do in terms of landing big-name free agents because that wasn’t on the agenda this year with the lack of cap space. And the same applies to Jeff Hafley as a head coach, it’s just too early to make a call. Let’s see what the Dolphins look like toward the end of this season.
Bobby Slowik seemed to finally found something on the lone TD drive by rolling Malik out & having him throw on the run. Could this be the game plan moving forward?
Hey Lu, that touchdown drive consisted of just four plays after the bad punt by Minnesota. And only one of those plays was a completion of a rollout and I’m not even sure that was a designed rollout as opposed to Willis moving to his left to avoid pressure up the middle before throwing a dart to Malik Washington. I would like to see more of that, but I get the feeling the Dolphins want to establish a traditional from-the-pocket passing game first (though I could be off the mark with that, which wouldn’t be a first).
We should have had Gordon spell Achane way before he got hurt. Love seeing that dude hit the hole. Great to see the left of the line provide so many gaps. Do you think the right side of the line, cough cough Jackson, finally gets it together at some point this season?
Hey Dean, I sure would hope that Austin Jackson’s game would get better as the weeks go by, and the same goes for Jonah Savaiinaea, who already has made progress, but the fact is the left side always is going to be the strength of the offensive line and I’m not sure it’ll ever be close with the current personnel.
Alain, my fellow Canadian Dolphins fans and I were shocked at the bad look Willis stretched out and disinterested on the bench in 2nd quarter and in the 2nd half? Was he lost in thought?  Did that 1st hit give him a concussion?  Does he not need to be talking and engaged with coaches?  Looking at an iPad?  Where is his leadership and working on plays with the WRs?  Can you ask the question? I have not had a chance to listen or read your latest articles. It was a bad look…if I was the GM or coach I would have sat his butt on the bench.
Hey Jeff, a quarterback looking at an iPad to see what the video is telling him about coverages and what the defense is doing is completely and totally par for the course. There’s really nothing there.
Morning, Alain. This is the 2nd or 3rd game I didn’t notice Jonah. Is he turning the corner?
Hey John, I think it’s actually more accurate to say he’s already turned a corner. Now, nobody is suggesting he’s getting a Pro Bowl or All-Pro nod this season, but he’s clearly a much better offensive lineman than he was as a rookie (admittedly a low bar).
From Jorge Francisco boyd:
Hi Alain, do you think Malik Willis looks into his progressions; how much better would he look with Caleb Douglas playing again; do you think he sees the open receiver all the time or makes poor choices?
Hey Jorge, yes, Malik Willis goes through his progressions, he clearly would be significantly better with Caleb Douglas, the one downfield threat the Dolphins had before he was sidelined with that ankle injury, and no quarterback sees the open receiver all the time and every quarterback sometimes makes poor choices. What Willis has to do is get more consistent in all areas, but he also needs help from his receivers in getting open and the line in giving him more time.
Mike Gesicki over / under 200 yards Sunday?
Ha! We have a comedian in our midst. The former Dolphins tight end may very well be a big factor for the Bengals passing game on Sunday given the injuries to Ja’Marr Chase and Tee Higgins.
Is anything going on with Wright besides he was injured? He doesn’t look good at all.
Hey Jorge, Wright was dealing with injuries last week, so he probably wasn’t at 100 percent in the Minnesota game, but I don’t know that it explains everything because he indeed didn’t look great against the Vikings.
Four part question: 1) Biggest problem for the offense so far? 2) Biggest problem for the defense so far? 3) Biggest problem for the special teams so far? 4) Biggest team-wide problem? This would help to check what they fix the rest of the way.
Hey Erick, will answer those, but it doesn’t mean there are easy fixes. Biggest problem on offense I would say is the lack of dynamic options in the passing game, which makes everything more difficult. Biggest problem on defense is covering tight ends now that the pass rush came to life against Minnesota. Biggest problem on special teams is poor kick coverage. The biggest problem overall is a lack of depth and a lack of experience.
Will Chris Bell eventually cut out the mistakes, step into his potential, and get in the end zone this year? Aka will he become a consistent contributor year 1?
Yes, it’s fair to expect Bell to eliminate the mental mistakes he’s been making and I certainly would expect to get into the end zone at some point, but I’m not sure I would count on him reaching his potential this season as he works his way back from his November 2025 ACL injury and I’d also temper expectations in terms of how much contribution he can provide for the offense.
Hi Alain, why are people saying that Grant can help with the pass rush? That isn't, and never has been, his game. Also, much was made about how bad the Vikings offense is, plus without JJ, but now the Dolphins defense is getting props? Explain it to me like I'm 5, please.
Hey Jason, last things first, the Dolphins could only play the opponent in front of them Sunday, so it’s not their fault the Vikings offense stinks. It doesn’t take away from what overall was a solid performance, but it wasn’t as dominant as it could have been (particularly allowing four first downs on each of the final two drives) and it also shouldn’t be viewed as a sign that the defense has arrived. As for Grant, he’s viewed as being able to help the pass rush from the IDL spot in part because Jordan Phillips and Zeek Biggers offer next to nothing in that department and while it may not be Grant’s game, he’s still better in that area than any DT on the roster not named Zach Sieler. Now, here’s your lollipop.

title: Dolphins Week 5 Power Rankings Roundup: Baby Steps Recognized
full_text:
The Miami Dolphins remained winless following their loss against the Minnesota Vikings, but after their closest call yet this season they're inching their way out of the bottom of the NFL power rankings.
The Dolphins finished just one point behind the Tennessee Titans in our weekly survey of national outlets — Yahoo Sports, Sports Illustrated, ESPN, The Athletic, NFL.com, USA Today, Pro Football Talk, FOX Sports, The Sporting News, CBS Sports — with an average ranking of 31.4 compared to 31.3 for the AFC South team.
The Dolphins did get a ranking as high as 29th, that coming from Nick Shook of NFL.com.
The average ranking position for Miami's Week 5 opponents, the Cincinnati Bengals, was 14.2 after their loss against the Jacksonville Jaguars at Paycor Stadium on Sunday dropped them to 2-2 on the season.
Before we get to our weekly rundown of the Dolphins placement in the rankings with the accompanying commentary, we'll again examine the other winless teams.
The Dolphins were one of five teams that started 0-3 along with the Houston Texans, Titans, Los Angeles Chargers and Tampa Bay Buccaneers, and remarkably (or perhaps not) all five of them lost in Week 4.
In a quick ranking of most disappointing starts among the winless teams, based on preseason expectations, the distinction of ranking at the top there comes down to either Houston, which some analysts had pegged as a legitimate Super Bowl contender, or the Chargers, whose offense was supposed to ignite with former Dolphins head coach Mike McDaniel as their new OC but instead has been a comedy of errors.
We are assured of having no more than four teams without a win after Week 5, barring a tie, because Houston and Tennessee will be facing each other. The Dolphins will be at home against Cincinnati, the Chargers will be at home against Denver, and Tampa Bay is playing the Thursday night game at Dallas.
Los Angeles Chargers — Their offense finally showed signs of life in the second half of their Week 4 loss at Seattle, but they already trailed 27-6 by that point. It was bad enough again Sunday that head coach Jim Harbaugh was asked about McDaniel's job security in the aftermath. Houston Texans — Houston wasted C.J. Stroud's best performance of the season because its vaunted defense couldn't stop Dak Prescott and CeeDee Lamb. Tampa Bay Buccaneers — The Bucs are in a major trouble with QB Baker Mayfield expected to miss a few more games and the current option at quarterback being undrafted rookie Jalon Daniels. Tennessee Titans — The Titans gave the Baltimore Ravens a pretty good game in Week 4, but couldn't overcome mistake like running back Tony Pollard deflecting a shovel pass from Cam Ward into the arms of a defender for an interception. Miami Dolphins — The Dolphins gave themselves a chance to win in the fourth quarter their last two games, and now it's a matter of being able to finish.
The Sporting News (Vinnie Iyer)
Analysis: The Dolphins played with more defensive energy in Minnesota and are trying to do what they can with now Malik Willis and Ollie Gordon II leading the offense. They still are dealing with an overall talent deficiency from week to week.
Analysis: Their offense is so limited right now, which showed up against the Vikings. The defense actually played a solid game and kept them in it.
Analysis: They haven't led for a single minute of any game so far.
FOX Sports (Ralph Vacchiano)
Analysis: Yes, they’re movin’ on up! But don’t get comfy up this high. They still stink. And they’re probably still the worst team in football. But they deserve a reward for pushing an undefeated (though likely overrated) Vikings team to the limit. They only lost by five points (though it would’ve been 12 if Minnesota TE T.J. Hockenson hadn’t slid at the 1 to let the clock run down with two minutes remaining). RB Ollie Gordon did a nice job replacing the injured DeVon Achane (100 yards on 9 carries, albeit 53 on one). But QB Malik Willis is still as bad as many of us thought he’d be.
Analysis: Haters who haven’t watched the Dolphins will call them the worst team in the league. I am not a hater. Miami is on a slow-but-steady track of improvement, showing signs of progress with each week. It's still a low-ceiling offense and the team remains winless, but I see the vision Jeff Hafley has for the Fins.
The Athletic (Chad Graff and Josh Kendall)
Analysis on concern level (not as high as you'd think): Without De’Von Achane, Ollie Gordon ran for 100 yards and a touchdown on nine carries, while the defense looked good against the Vikings. They’re a rebuilding team headed for an ugly record, but there have been some brief moments of hope along the way.
Analysis: Through the first two weeks of the season, the Dolphins looked like they weren't ready to compete. In Weeks 3 and 4, however, their defense pushed a pair of undefeated division leaders to the brink. On Sunday, the Dolphins recorded 17 pressures and four sacks -- their first sacks of the season -- while holding an admittedly struggling Minnesota offense out of the end zone. First-year coach Jeff Hafley said his team is "starting to believe." Rookie linebacker Jacob Rodriguez said the team is close to its first win: "The physicality and the want-to are there. ... We've just got to learn how to win." -- Marcel Louis-Jacques
Pro Football Talk (Mike Florio)
Analysis: Could the first team to go 17-0 go 0-17?
Sports Illustrated (Conor Orr)
Analysis: Until Miami gets a win, this will become a Jacob Rodriguez bot account. I have Rodriguez right there in the Defensive Rookie of the Year conversation.
Yahoo Sports (Frank Schwab)
Analysis: The Dolphins battled at Minnesota, and if they didn't get unlucky on Chris Bell barely stepping out of bounds before catching a long touchdown and getting an illegal touching penalty, maybe they'd have a win. But it's another loss, and Miami's offense is still hard to watch. Unfortunately for Dolphins fans, it's a familiar feeling.
