title: Why Garrett Wilson Has the Right Approach to Jets' Losing Streak (And It's Time to Reward Him)
full_text:
As franchise cornerstones come, the Jets are very fortunate to have Garrett Wilson .
The former 10th overall pick out of Ohio State has had to endure multiple changes at the quarterback position, two head coaching regimes and two different rebuilds. Through it all, he's been a consummate professional and has continued to be the focal point of New York's offense.
Even more impressive, despite the team's 1-3 start, Wilson didn't blame the team's struggles on the coaching staff, but shifted ownership to the players more than anyone else.
“All of it,” Wilson said when asked who deserves most blame on Wednesday. “We are the ones out there on the field playing the game and making each play come to life, or not doing so. I take a lot of pride in just playing my role to make sure everyone’s job in this facility is secure and at an all-time high."
While Wilson remains a true pro and leader on the Jets roster, its not fair for the team around him to go through another losing season. And the wideout's answers about their current standing only highlights the importance of what New York is about to embark on.
The Jets currently sit at 1-3 heading into Sunday's Week 5 action against the Browns .
After a positive Week 1 win over the Titans, the Jets have stumbled in three games against NFC North opponents. With that, Wilson's target shares remain somewhat mixed .
After seeing just seven targets in Week 2's loss to Green Bay, the wideout had a monster Week 3 game against Detroit, in which he recorded 10 catches and a touchdown grab on 13 targets. But in Week 4, the Jets went back to failing to get their star the ball enough, totaling just four targets and three receptions.
That fluctuation in Wilson's production has even left Glenn confused as to how the Jets can maximize their top offensive weapon.
" We have to find a way to try to get (Garrett) the ball," Glenn said. "He's basically one of the engines that get us going. ... We have to figure out a way to get those guys the ball as much as possible."
But again, Wilson remains steadfast in his belief that the team can right the ship. The next test is against the Browns on Sunday, and three of the four upcoming matchups are against teams that were picked to struggle all year: the Browns, Dolphins and Raiders.
Wilson is ready for the Jets to break out of their funk.
At 26 years old, Wilson wants to try to play meaningful football. He's been patient before, but that patience could always run out. At the end of the day, the more the Jets lose, the harder it will be for the team to sell him on whether or not they will be able to turn things around in his career.

title: 4 Jets Suddenly Look More Important in Week 5 as Breece Hall and AD Mitchell's Outlook Worsens
full_text:
Every NFL team is dealing with its fair share of injuries now that we're one month into the 2026 season, and the New York Jets aren't an exception.
The latest wave of injury news heading into a Week 5 showdown with the Cleveland Browns is impacting New York's offense, which is already struggling to score points this season (19.0 ppg, T-24th). And while it's been nice to see tight end Mason Taylor make significant strides toward his return, it's starting to look like the Jets will be without two key offensive pieces against the Browns: star running back Breece Hall and No. 2 wide receiver Adonai Mitchell.
The offensive duo each missed the Week 4 loss to the Chicago Bears. Hall is dealing with a quadriceps injury, while Mitchell's hand issue kept him off the field. Unfortunately, neither Jet is making much progress, as both Hall and Mitchell missed Thursday's practice , according to ESPN 's Rich Cimini, marking their second straight absence this week.
No surprise here, but no sign of Breece Hall and AD Mitchell at practice. Jarvis Brownlee Jr in positional drills. #Jets
Back-to-back missed practices don't create much optimism for a potential Week 5 appearance. Assuming Hall and Mitchell need more time to heal and are inactive against the Browns, the Jets might need to rely on these four players to lead them to a potential win.
How does, arguably, the most important player on the roster become even more important? Well, by the Jets finally treating him consistently like that.
Don't get it twisted: Garrett Wilson is off to a solid start this season, converting 31 targets into 24 receptions for 270 receiving yards and two touchdowns. Staying at this pace puts him on track for a 102-1,148-9 statline in 17 games, which would be career-high marks across the board. The problem is that Wilson's stat line should be better.
Sports Illustrated 's Nick Faria said it best when he wrote, "Wilson needs at least 12-15 targets per game." Over four weeks, Wilson has been the recipient of only one double-digit game, when he saw 13 targets against the Detroit Lions in Week 3.
Unsurprisingly, that produced his best line (10-107-1) of the season. How'd the Jets follow that up? They targeted him just four times in the 11-point loss to the Bears in Week 4, in which they didn't score a touchdown until the fourth quarter.
Considering how poorly their depth WRs have performed, the Jets have every reason to funnel the offense through Wilson if Mitchell and Hall can't play in Week 5.
It isn't Braelon Allen's fault that he didn't see a ton of opportunities last week, but having 14 catches for 59 rushing yards didn't leave much to be excited about. Although Allen is a solid backup, the Jets might benefit from getting more legs involved in the backfield, which means finally giving Isaiah Davis a chance to run with the ball.
Even though he's played 73 snaps this season, only two of those came on offense for Davis, with neither resulting in a carry. His usage (or lack thereof) has been bizarre , especially when the former 2024 fifth-rounder has been productive in his young NFL career. Davis has 410 rushing yards on 73 carries, 261 receiving yards on 30 catches, while scoring three total touchdowns. On top of that, he's done it without fumbling the ball once.
If Hall can't play, the Jets can lighten Allen's load by finally giving Davis some carries. The Browns might be 3-1, but their run defense hasn't been great on the road, allowing the 10th-most rushing yards per game and the 11th-most yards per carry in enemy territory. If that doesn't give enough reason to use Davis, I don't know what will.
Kenyon Sadiq showed Jets fans, coaches, and teammates exactly the player he could be in Week 3 , amassing seven catches for 105 yards and a touchdown in the Motor City. But just like the Jets let Wilson down a week after an offensive explosion, Sadiq went from being a hero to a stat line that reads like a quote from former NBA head coach Sam Mitchell :
Zero touchdowns. Zero receiving yards. Zero receptions.
Sadiq also saw his targets cut in half (eight to four), which was extremely disappointing for anyone hoping to see him build on his potential Offensive Rookie of the Year case. Hopefully, offensive coordinator Frank Reich learned his lesson and plans to use Sadiq more, especially if Mitchell's absence continues to leave a hole in the passing game.
The fact that Taylor will likely make his return could allow the Jets to use Sadiq more as a receiver, potentially creating favorable mismatches. Anything to give Gang Green an offensive edge this weekend will be necessary.
For better or worse, offseason additions like Minkah Fitzpatrick, Dane Belton and Joseph Ossai have had a chance to make early impressions on Jets fans. One offseason arrival who hasn't had a chance to make his regular-season debut is Tim Patrick, whose practice window finally opened on Wednesday (h/t Jets) after missing four games on injured reserve due to a groin strain.
WR Tim Patrick has been designated to return
With so many WR-related injuries impacting the offense, the Jets should be excited to get a veteran like Patrick back. He isn't going to walk onto the field and be the same guy who caught 104 balls for 1,476 yards and 11 TDs with the Denver Broncos in 2020 and 2021, but anything is an improvement for a New York team whose WRs not named Wilson, Mitchell, or Isaiah Williams have combined for only two catches and 33 yards.
Patrick had a modest 15-187-3 line in 16 games with the Jacksonville Jaguars last season, which is far from his best numbers, but beggars can't be choosers at this point. Throw in the fact that he's a solid run blocker, and it's clear how Patrick could help the Jets' shorthanded offense this weekend, assuming he's healthy enough to play.

title: What's Changed (and What Hasn't) About the Jets' Practice Squad 1 Month Into NFL Season
full_text:
New season, same results for the Jets. After an offseason filled with promise and hope for an improved team, Gang Green finds itself in a familiar position after four games: last in the AFC East with a 1-3 record.
While there’s still time for the Jets to turn their season around , things aren’t looking so bright in Gotham. Injuries to both sides of the ball have derailed the team, forcing general manager Darren Mougey to constantly make moves to strengthen the depth.
As a result, the Jets' practice squad has undergone significant changes since it was first announced at the start of September, and this article breaks down all the moving pieces.
With that said, let’s take a look at the practice squad when it was first announced compared to what it looks like today.
Bamba, Banks, Clark, Ekeji, Henderson, Keller, Page, and Womack are the eight players who have been on the practice squad since the beginning of the season. Of the eight, Keller is the only one who's been elevated to the 53-man roster, playing 15 special teams snaps in last week's loss to the Bears.
While Clark hasn’t been elevated, he signed to the active roster following the injury to Minkah Fitzpatrick in Week 1. Clark played 17 snaps on special teams before being released and signed back to the practice squad last week.
If another injury occurs to the linebackers or safeties room, we should expect Clark and Keller to either be elevated or signed to the active roster. For the others, meanwhile, it’s hard to say that they’ll be brought up anytime soon.
Since the Jets have a tight rotation at cornerback, defensive line, and offensive line, there are two reasons for them to see playing time: more injuries or a late-season scenario in which New York is eliminated from playoff contention.
The Jets moved on from Cooper, Hayes, Newman and Zappe. Cooper, Hayes, and Zappe remain free agents, while Newman is on the Patriots' practice squad. New York briefly had John Saunders Jr. on the unit, but released him last week.
Heflin, Levao, Lynn, McClain, Pritchett, Sanders and Wallace have all signed to the active roster. Heflin was called up and has played 24 defensive snaps in two games after David Onyemata was placed on injured reserve . He hasn’t made much of an impact yet, though, leaving Heflin's spot on the active roster uncertain once Onyemata returns.
With numerous injuries to the receivers room, New York signed McClain and Pritchett to bolster New York’s depth at the position. McClain has appeared in 19 offensive snaps over two games, but he hasn’t made the most of his opportunity, as he still hasn't been targeted.
Pritchett hasn’t played on offense, but he was tasked with kick return duties in Week 3 and returned one for 27 yards. If Pritchett wants to stay, he’ll have to step it up, as with Kene Nwangwu back, there isn’t much room for him.
With Grupe unable to instill confidence in the coaching staff, the team rolled with Sanders for the kicking job in Week 1. Converting on seven of his attempts over four games, Sanders has established himself as New York’s starting kicker.
The Jets have added nine players to the practice squad, but only Grupe and Shepard are worth keeping an eye on.
Despite earning a roster spot, Grupe didn’t attempt a single kick for the Jets. Clearly, the Jets weren’t impressed with his play in practice and turned to Sanders, who took advantage of the opportunity.
But stashing Grupe on the practice squad is a bit eye-opening. While you can say it’s for emergency depth, you could argue they did this so that there’s still pressure on Sanders to perform well, or he, too, could end up losing the spot.
Meanwhile, Shepard brings plenty of experience to a receiver corps that has dealt with injuries. So far, he’s played in two games, recording one catch (on two targets) for three yards and converting a two-point attempt.
Once Cooper and Mitchell come back, Shepard will likely stay on the practice squad. But if Isaiah Williams doesn’t build on last week's performance, don’t be surprised if New York calls on Shepard to take some of his reps.
Not everyone is waiting on an injury to create an opportunity. Players like Bamba and Voorhis are developmental projects the team hopes will become contributors down the road.
Ultimately, this Jets practice squad offers a perfect blend of serviceable backups, emergency depth, and developmental players. While the group has changed considerably, it still gives New York options to turn to.

title: 4 Jets' Overreactions Heading Into Week 5 vs. Browns (Including David Bailey Concerns)
full_text:
At 1-3, the Jets are in familiar territory as they hit the quarter-way point of the 2026 NFL season. They enter the month of October in desperate need of victories to prove to their fans that they can play meaningful football when it matters.
As with any slow start to the year, though, fans are no longer willing to give the organization the benefit of the doubt. Some incredible overreactions have even popped up among even the most loyal parts of the fanbase.
While overreactions come with the sport, it's time to debunk some of the most outlandish ones as the Jets head into Week 5's clash with the Browns .
This has nothing to do with David Bailey and more to do with the player who was taken after. During the pre-draft process, the Jets contemplated taking either Bailey or Arvell Reese with the second overall pick. Reese was more of a project and an off-ball linebacker, while Bailey was thought of as the sure-fire pass rusher.
Through four games, though, Reese has been the better performer . The Ohio State phenom leads the league in solo tackles, has an interception and four passes defended. Bailey, meanwhile, has struggled over the last couple of games, but leads the Jets in pressures and has recorded two sacks.
The overreaction here is the most ridiculous of any topic on this list. Four games are not enough to determine how good a rookie will be. Some players take time to develop into stars. Others are stars right away. That doesn't diminish any player.
Bailey will be perfectly fine. It's not fair to think he won't be due to the play of another prospect.
This one is an overreaction, but of all the topics here, it's easily the one most likely to actually take place.
Jets head coach Aaron Glenn needed victories this season in order to prove to the league and organization he was the right man for the job. The talent on the roster has obviously improved, but it hasn't improved enough to mask some of the coaching struggles that Glenn continues to have.
That said, a 1-3 record doesn't doom any season. New York can still win seven or eight games by getting healthy and performing at a high level. Glenn won't lose his job if that happens. Other coaches have gone through a similar slow start in Year 2, only to turn into a winner that same season.
That is what could await the Jets this season. And it doesn't make Glenn a dead man walking (even if more losses could certainly do that).
Over the next few games, the Jets find themselves playing the Browns, Raiders, Patriots, and Dolphins. While the Raiders and Browns have greatly improved to start the year, they are still winnable games on the schedule.
That said, the notion that lighter games on the schedule mean the Jets will be able to get some wins on their tally is a farce. New York will need to play much better than it has over the last several weeks on both sides of the ball.
And while a 4-4 mark at the midway point of the season could certainly be in play, the Jets don't have any easy games. They could end up being 1-7 by that point, too.
In some cases, the Jets' offense has taken positive steps forward. Geno Smith has played well as the team's starting quarterback , and when healthy, the rest of the unit has looked competent.
The problem is that the same issues that have plagued the team for years have re-emerged many times.
The Jets are too inconsistent at getting the ball to Garrett Wilson despite another strong start to the year for the star receiver, and their offensive line hasn't been as consistent as many hoped. Even more alarming, New York's run game ranks fifth-worst in the league with only 84 rushing yards per game.
Getting a better quarterback is only half the battle. New York's scheme and target shares have been very poor to begin the season, and it highlights a group that isn't much better after finishing last in most offensive categories last season.

title: One Thought on All 22 Jets Starters After First Quarter of 2026 Season
full_text:
At the quarter-way point of the NFL season, it's time for teams to finally shake off the rust and determine who they are going to be as a football team .
For the Jets, their 1-3 start seems dismal, but there are certainly positives to look at across the roster. Now that the first four games of the 2026 season are behind us , we'll take a look at one thought from each starting member of the organization as the next phase of the season takes shape and the Jets determine whether they'll actually compete this year.
If you look at the numbers compared to the last few quarterbacks the Jets have had, Geno Smith is on pace to have a top-five season as a passer in franchise history. That isn't saying much, especially after a game in which he failed to pick up a third-down conversion.
Still, the Jets remain high on their signal-caller, especially head coach Aaron Glenn
" I know that he's going to get right back to who he is, and that's completing a high percentage of throws," Glenn said. "I have no concern with that with this player because of  who he is and his career and how he's operated."
Breece Hall has been hurt since the team's Week 3 loss in Detroit, but the team's running game has taken a hit well before that. Hall remains out of practice and is slated to miss Sunday's contest against Cleveland.
Until he returns, it seems like the Jets are comfortable giving Braelon Allen the bulk of the carries.
When he's been given the chance to show it , Garrett Wilson has remained not only New York's best player but also one of the top receivers in the NFL. In fact, he's in the top 15 across the league in receptions, yards, and touchdowns. That even includes the measly four targets he received last week in Chicago.
"It's just because we didn't have as many opportunities," Glenn said. "The more opportunities that we get, you can rest assured Garrett will get his targets."
If New York wants to win this season, Wilson needs at least 12-15 targets per game. That's not hyperbole either. It's the truth.
Like Hall, injuries have derailed what Adonai Mitchell could have been to start the season. He remains an intriguing second receiving option behind Wilson, but an odd finger injury has kept him out of the lineup for the last few weeks.
Time will tell when Mitchell returns, but he's going to be very important in trying to modernize this offense with multiple weapons on the roster.
When healthy and targeted fairly, Kenyon Sadiq has looked like an excellent player for the Jets and a smart pick for the first round. Sadiq has recorded 12 receptions for 143 yards and a touchdown, and even though he didn't record a catch in Sunday's loss to the Bears, he remains a central cog for this offense moving forward.
The injury to Dylan Parham hits the Jets' offensive line hard . Meanwhile, Olu Fashanu has not taken the leap many had hoped to see so far, and Josh Myers has been serviceable but is a low-ceiling player.
Armand Membou and Joe Tippmann have been solid on the right side of the line, but this is a group that will need to play better if the Jets want to improve collectively on offense.
No group has been more disappointing this season than the Jets defensive line. They have multiple draft picks and millions of dollars invested in the group from this offseason, and nothing has really panned out through four games.
From David Bailey to T'Vondre Sweat to Joseph Ossai, the Jets need more from this group moving forward . They can't keep getting all their pressure from blitzes. Good quarterbacks on their upcoming schedule will eat them alive.
Like his counterpart, Jamien Sherwood has struggled to begin the season . His reads are too slow, he overpursues at times, and hasn't made many impactful plays. For a player with an enormous contract for his position, the Auburn product will need to turn up his level of play quickly, or he'll be in danger of being without a team this offseason.
Demario Davis was brought in to help fix the Jets' alignment issues and provide a stable force for the rest of the defense. While New York's unit has improved, Davis has also struggled in his own right. Pro Football Focus ranks him as the 62nd-best linebacker out of 74 players and the seventh-worst at defending the run.
At 37 years old, it's fair to wonder how much Davis has left in the tank. He remains an important face in the organization, but he will need to improve as the season goes on.
Last season, Brandon Stephens was the best player on a bad secondary for New York. This year, he's one of the better performers on a secondary that has become one of the NFL's top units.
Stephens currently ranks as the 14th-best corner in the game on PFF , and his coverage stats rank among the best as well. If he keeps playing like this, it might behoove the Jets to get him some new money this offseason.
Rolling through the list of surprise performers this season is former third-round pick AZ Thomas. The Florida State product has earned and kept his starting role throughout the regular season so far and has competed well against quality receivers.
He's currently the 17th-best cornerback by PFF and certainly looks like an ascending young player the team can rely on moving forward. It would be massive for him to be a hit on the roster.
Minkah Fitzpatrick is a hero for simply being the player who ended the team's 20-game interception drought. He remains a strong off-ball safety with the versatility to play inside the box as well. As he gets healthier as the season progresses, Fitzpatrick will be an important player as the team moves forward with as they try to rack up wins.
No Jets player has had a better start to the season than Dane Belton. The fact that he's willing to play on special teams makes him a player Gang Green should covet for as long as possible , as proven by Glenn's praise for the veteran safety.
Belton is a major part of why this secondary has surprised people and continues to remain a bright spot heading into the next portion of the Jets' season.

title: Another Concerning Streak Is Plaguing the Jets After Ending INT Drought
full_text:
It never seems to end. Just when the Jets end a season-long drought , another glaring trend rears its ugly head.
Is that the mark of a bad football team? Perhaps, but what is clear is that the organization just can't seem to catch a break. Even if the Jets finally ended a 20-game interception drought dating back to the 2024 season with Minkah Fitzpatrick's INT against the Bears in Week 4 (h/t NFL).
Minkah Fitzpatrick gives the Jets their first INT in 636 pass attempts NYJvsCHI on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/CQUCl4JVnt
Despite all the joy that should come from finally recording an interception last week in Chicago (there wasn't much else to celebrate from that game), New York has had to be reminded of another concerning record.
And this time, it focuses on the offensive side of the ball, and an area Gang Green has struggled mightily in over the last two seasons.
Over the last eight games played, the Jets have failed to score a single point in the final four minutes between the first and second halves (h/t ESPN 's Rich Cimini). The streak goes all the way back to the end of the 2025 season, in which the Jets were outscored in games by a combined tally of 134 points.
Here's a chance for the Jets to end another drought -- scoring in the final minutes of a half. Eight straight games without pts in the final 4 minutes of the first/second halves. #Jets
Gang Green Nation 's James Wudi further illustrated how bad New York's two-minute offense has been even before last week's game:
Jets head coach Aaron Glenn was clear in his very first training camp. The final two minutes of each half belong to the head coach. His decision about when to use timeouts or challenges ultimately affects how the rest of the offense looks .
And it isn't exactly a good thing that's where the new Jets' drought lies.
Last season, there was an excuse. Brady Cook, an undrafted free agent, was brought in to see what the team had. He wasn't ready for that role as a starting quarterback, and it showed. This year, the Jets upgraded the quarterback room with Geno Smith, and they still can't seem to figure out the two-minute offense.
Arguably the most frustrating part about it is that there's no clear person at fault. In some games, like the team's failed two-minute drive in Detroit two weeks ago, the offensive line committed penalties when they could ill afford them.
Others, like against the Packers, the coaching staff not having any timeouts available, severely limited the team's options.
No one person is at fault for the team's current drought. But one thing is clear:
If you ask leaders on the Jets roster, the best way to fix their four-minute offense is simple. Grind harder.
"You’ve got to get back to work, and you’ve got to demand it from yourself," Geno Smith said after New York's loss to Chicago. "Got a lot of belief in this team and in this offense as well. We’ve just got to get into a rhythm, create some momentum, and then get rolling.”
But is it just a matter of "working harder?"
The reality is, New York is not talented enough to make up for mental mistakes or bad play calls. The Jets may get there eventually, but the organization is in the next phase of a rebuild, and that comes with coaching needing to be as important as player execution. When one falters, the whole thing collapses, as evidenced by the team's current drought in key moments of the game.
It is fixable, of course, but the only way it does is if the Jets play the kind of "perfect" football in those moments that eliminates all mistakes in the forefront. It's a tall order, but if the team is going to get to where it wants to be, it's how it must be moving forward.

title: What Jets' Wednesday Injury Report Means for Week 5 vs. Browns
full_text:
A 23-12 loss to the Bears was disappointing enough in Week 4 , and now the Jets continue to deal with mounting injuries that have forced multiple players into larger roles earlier than anticipated amid a three-game losing streak.
Even before the uninspiring loss to the Bears ensued in the Windy City, injuries were a major issue plaguing this Jets team. Prior to kickoff last Sunday, nearly half of New York's offensive starters were sidelined due to injuries , and that doesn't even include cornerback Jarvis Brownlee Jr., who is in concussion protocol after colliding with teammate Dane Belton in the loss to Chicago.
With a Week 5 home tilt against the surprising Browns looming on Sunday, it remains to be seen if the Jets will be closer to full strength. ESPN Jets reporter Rich Cimini provided an update on Wednesday that listed Adonai Mitchell, Breece Hall and Dylan Parham as "week-to-week," per head coach Aaron Glenn.
Additionally, Kingsley Enagbare and Mason Taylor "are OK to practice."
AD Mitchell, Breece Hall and Dylan Parham are still week to week, per Glenn. Jarvis Brownlee Jr in the concussion protocol. Kingsley Enagbare and Mason Taylor are OK to practice. #Jets
That is just a fraction of the injuries the Jets continue to deal with, which in turn has allowed several players to see an uptick in snaps and role changes to account for the roster holes.
With an updated injury report to dissect, here is what it could mean for those players and what to monitor in the coming days.
Mitchell suffered a right finger injury during practice and has missed the last two games as a result. However, while he only has nine catches and zero touchdowns so far, Mitchell's 123 receiving yards are still the fourth-most on the team, and his 13.7 yards per reception is the second-most among players who have appeared in at least two games.
After a disastrous showing from the offense and an inconsistent volume for the receivers against Chicago, it was clear once again how vital Mitchell is as the WR2 on the team behind Garrett Wilson. A favorable matchup against the Browns' 23rd-ranked pass defense (235.3 ypg) should present some opportunities on Sunday, even if Mitchell is unable to play again, which may be the case since he is still listed as doubtful.
Hall missed the Week 4 loss to the Bears after suffering a right quad injury against the Lions the week prior. Although an MRI revealed no long-term or major structural damage, Hall's absence has been felt, considering his versatility as a runner (163 yards, one TD) and a receiver (102 yards).
Given his overall importance on the team, getting Hall back on the field as soon as possible is a high priority. That said, it does not sound likely that he will be cleared for Sunday, or at least at full capacity, which should give Braelon Allen another opportunity to impress after accumulating just 59 yards on 14 carries against Chicago and leaving a lot on the table.
Parham, meanwhile, sustained a knee injury in Week 3 and is coming off a full week of not practicing leading up to the Week 4 game against the Bears. While the offensive line has been a letdown so far, Parham has been a consistent bright spot after joining the Jets in the offseason and leaves a massive hole to fill the longer he remains out.
Jordan Meredith is listed behind Parham on the depth chart and filled in for him when he got injured in the Motor City, while Kohl Levao is listed as the backup to Joe Tippmann on the right side of the O-line. Parham's status remains in doubt, and it could be more of the same for Gang Green up front if they cannot impose their will more in the trenches.
The 25-year-old leads the Jets with 110 slot snaps , per Pro Football Focus , and ranks inside the top 20 among all CBs in tackling (82.6) and coverage (74.0). Being without him would certainly be difficult to overcome, which makes his incidental collision with Belton even harder to deal with after going into concussion protocol, per Cimini.
Jarvis Brownlee Jr. left the game after this play, a collision with teammate Dane Belton. Brownlee now in concussion protocol. One of those days for the #Jets . pic.twitter.com/kd0B4282Ay
Brownlee must clear the NFL's five-stage concussion protocol to return to action, which makes it unlikely that he will play on Sunday. He still could, but there is a good chance that rookie D'Angelo Ponds could be staring at a bigger role with the Jets in light of the injury, after coming in and playing a career-high 18 snaps in Week 4.
Ponds possesses the run-defense skills and the versatility to play in the slot and on the perimeter. Still, Brownlee's potential absence could prove costly for a unit that made some key plays last Sunday, only to have disciplinary issues come back to bite them .
The Jets took a shot on Enagbare when they signed him to a one-year, $9 million deal in the offseason. While that gamble seemed to be paying off through the first two games and he has excelled in pass rush, his season took a turn when he went from a limited participant in practice to inactive for the Week 4 game due to a knee injury.
With the thumbs-up to practice, it sounds like Enagbare is trending toward making his return this week, even though it also seemed that way last week as well. When you think about the struggles that Joseph Ossai continues to have and the lack of impact plays from Will McDonald IV, who finds himself on thin ice , the Jets really need Enagbare on the field to feel like they have a chance up front on Sunday.
Taylor sustained a thumb injury during the Week 2 game against the Packers and has missed each of the last two games. Although the tight end room made a statement with a season-high 164 yards in Week 3, it took a massive step back last week and looked like a shell of itself in a game where nothing seemed to go right on either side of the ball.
Still, Taylor led the team with 44 receptions in his rookie season and could be poised to return to form when he returns to the lineup. As of Wednesday, that seems even more likely as the Jets look to add more bodies on the field and overcome the injury bug that has plagued several key players so far.

title: Why Jets' Looming IR Returns Could Give Offense a Much-Needed Boost
full_text:
The Jets are still working through growing pains as they head into a Week 5 clash with the Browns, with the inconsistent offense being among the top lingering concerns. Gang Green is averaging the ninth-fewest points per game (19.0) and is coming off an uninspiring loss to the Bears, in which they put up only 157 total yards while going 0-for-7 on third downs.
While some offensive struggles can be linked to underperforming players and questionable coaching decisions, it's safe to say the injuries the Jets are dealing with aren't helping either.
The wide receiver and tight end rooms have been depleted, with Mason Taylor, Tim Patrick, Omar Cooper Jr., Arian Smith and Adonai Mitchell all missing time, and even the offensive line had to play last week shorthanded as left guard Dylan Parham missed the loss to the Bears with a knee injury. That's without mentioning star rusher Breece Hall's quadriceps injury , too.
The good news is that, even if it doesn't erase all concerns, offensive help could be on the way for the Jets sooner rather than later. Being four games into the season means players who started the year on injured reserve or the Physically Unable to Perform (PUP) list are eligible to return in Week 5, potentially giving teams like New York reinforcements at positions of need.
Certain defenders (EDGE Tyler Baron and safety VJ Payne) are eligible to return now, but the attention should be on the potential offensive help on the horizon: Patrick and rookie offensive guard Anez Cooper.
Nearing a decade in the NFL, Patrick was signed in the offseason to add depth to the Jets' WR room behind Garrett Wilson and Mitchell. Much to his dismay, the 32-year-old pass-catcher suffered a groin injury at the start of September, landing him on IR before even playing a regular-season game.
Now that his practice window has opened (h/t New York Post 's Brian Costello), it'll be interesting to see how Patrick can help the Jets as Mitchell's hand continues to heal and Cooper remains on IR for at least another game. His preseason wasn't exactly explosive, but Patrick caught both of his targets for 14 yards while playing to a 54.5 run-block grade on Pro Football Focus . That could help an offense averaging the fifth-fewest rushing yards per game (84.0).
The Jets haven't shared how close Cooper is to returning to action, but his eventual insertion into the lineup could help make the offense's life easier.
The 2026 sixth-rounder out of Miami (FL) gave fans plenty of reasons to feel optimistic about his outlook in the preseason, playing to a solid 67.9 run-block grade (and 64.1 for overall offense) in three appearances, per PFF. Cooper's pass-block grade (45.3) doesn't look ideal on paper, but it's worth noting that a poor effort against the Steelers in the second preseason game likely drove it down, as the rookie blocker earned marks of 85.2 and 81.3 in the opener and finale, respectively.
Ex-Raider Jordan Meredith has been handling lead LG duties with Parham sidelined, but who knows how long that will last. Meredith's run blocking has been decent; however, he's struggled in pass protection, allowing seven pressures (including two sacks) in the last two weeks.
Getting Cooper back will at least give Glenn and offensive coordinator Frank Reich another option to consider, whether Parham misses more time or needs an in-game breather.
Expectations should be tempered no matter what, though, as Patrick and Cooper haven't played in over a month. They'll need time—both in practice and during games—to get back to their old selves. Still, their looming returns are exactly what the Jets need right now, potentially helping create optimism that the season is far from lost.

title: Nate Lynn's Jets Promotion Comes at Perfect Time as Joseph Ossai's Struggles Continue
full_text:
It's been hard to find many positives amid a 1-3 start to the season, but the New York Jets have shown flashes of improvement through the first four weeks. The offense is more reliable with quarterback Geno Smith under center, and the secondary isn't as big of a concern anymore , especially after offseason addition Minkah Fitzpatrick ended the interception drought last week.
That said, being two games below .500 means Gang Green still has improvements to make, with their pass rush among the most pressing concerns.  Sure, they're tied for the 14th-most sacks (nine), but the Jets' pass rush enters Week 5 with the fourth-worst grade (58.3) on Pro Football Focus. On top of that, the unit lost Braiden McGregor, who was placed on injured reserve earlier this week with a season-ending pectoral tear.
Throw in the help that a big free-agent signing like Joseph Ossai hasn't given New York much pass-rushing help, and it's easy to see why general manager Darren Mougey needs to act fast before it's too late.
With no time to waste, the Jets added reinforcements, signing preseason darling Nate Lynn to the 53-man roster on Wednesday .
We've signed Nate Lynn to the active roster and placed Braiden McGregor on injured reserve We've also signed EDGE Nathan Voorhis to the practice squad
Lynn won't single-handedly fix the Jets' pass-rushing issues, but his promotion could be exactly what the unit needs as Ossai's production remains a concern.
The Jets penned Ossai to a three-year, $34.5 million contract in free agency, hoping he'd provide the pass rush with a much-needed boost. The former 2021 third-rounder was arguably being underused by the Bengals, and the Jets hoped a move to Gotham could unlock his full potential as a quarterback-seeking missile.
Instead, Ossai's start with the Jets has been rocky. A foot injury limited his availability throughout the summer, forcing him to miss the first two regular-season games. He eventually made his debut against the Detroit Lions in Week 3 and still hasn't done much, recording zero pressures and a career-low 52.6 pass-rush grade on PFF . He's also missed two of his 11 tackle attempts, giving him a lowly grade of 34.9.
Nonetheless, Ossai still has time to turn things around , but until that happens, his production is a problem. That's why it'd be huge for the Jets if Lynn could make an immediate impact against the Cleveland Browns this weekend.
Glenn & Co. have leaned on a five-man pass rush, featuring Ossai, McGregor, David Bailey, Kingsley Enagbare and Will McDonald IV. But with McGregor's season over, Enagbare missing last week's loss due to a knee injury, and Bailey and McDonald still looking for consistency, there's an opening for someone like Lynn to make some noise.
When McGregor was placed on IR, Lynn was the first potential practice squad promotion candidate that came to mind . The former Lions/Titans EDGE won Jets fans over with a strong preseason performance despite joining the team in mid-August, and now it's time to see whether his exhibition performance was a mirage or a sign of things to come.
Even though he appeared in two preseason games, Lynn made the most of his opportunities, recording five tackles (two solo) and six pressures (three sacks and three hurries) across 58 defensive snaps. His effort earned him an 80.4 PFF pass-rush grade , which actually led all Jets in the preseason.
Lynn isn't guaranteed to make a similar impact in the regular season, but everyone knows anything can happen on any given Sunday. The Browns' offensive line is solid for the most part, but still allowed Deshaun Watson to be sacked 11 times over four games, including a whopping five sacks in Week 1. Cleveland's signal-caller also struggles under heat, owning a 48.5% completion rate, 5.2 yards per attempt, and a 34.2 passing grade when pressured this season , per PFF .
Regardless of how many snaps he sees, Lynn needs to capitalize on every opportunity against the Browns. Despite both teams sporting inverse records, the Jets have a legitimate shot at winning on Sunday, and that starts with the pass rush—from Lynn to underperformers like Ossai—doing their job immediately off the bat.

title: QB In His Corner: Sean Mannion Still Has Jalen Hurts' Endorsement
full_text:
PHILADELPHIA — Jalen Hurts is not backing away from Sean Mannion.
With the Eagles’ offense stuck near the bottom of the league and questions mounting about the first-year coordinator’s scheme, the QB1 described Mannion as “a warrior, a soldier” at his weekly press availability and noted that the current rough stretch is building equity between the duo rather than tearing them apart.
“Obviously these times are where times you get to build with someone and go through things with someone, and I think that builds equity in everything that we do together,” Hurts said. “And so I’m excited to go to bat with him.”
The comments came as Philadelphia sits at 2-2 and searches for an identity four games into Mannion’s stint as offensive coordinator and play-caller.
The Eagles are averaging 18.8 points and about 270 yards a game, ranking near the bottom of the NFL in both categories, with the passing attack especially shaky. They have stalled in consecutive losses: a 27-7 defeat in Chicago followed by a 24-20 home loss to the Rams in which the offense totaled 172 yards and went 0-for-12 on third down.
Hurts has repeatedly framed those subpar performances as execution problems, not schematic ones.
After the Rams game, the QB1 used the phrase “poor execution” repeatedly and declined to pin the failure on Mannion’s plan.
Head coach Nick Sirianni has been more blunt about the public heat, saying of Mannion, “He’s gonna wear a lot of this. There’s no doubt.”
Mannion, hired from the Packers’ quarterbacks room with a background in the McVay-O’Connell-LaFleur tree, has shown no interest in abandoning the offense he was brought in to install.
He said this week the staff still believes in the under-center, outside-zone, play-action structure and intends to “keep leaning into” it.
“We're here and we're implementing something that we absolutely believe in,” said Mannion. “You're always looking, like we've said, throughout this process, to make it as good as it can be and add tweaks and add wrinkles here and there.
“We believe in the things that we've installed and that we've implemented from a fundamental perspective in terms of the structure of our offense. We're going to keep leaning into that and make it as good as it can be. … Really nothing's changed in terms of our outlook on our offense, and our identity and what we want to be offensively. But each week, you're always looking to attack in the best way possible, either by looking at yourself and the things that you can add and tweak or looking at your opponent and what needs to be tailored to that."
Through four games, the Eagles have run play-action at one of the league’s lowest rates and have been inefficient from under center, a gap critics have treated as evidence the new system and the personnel are not yet aligned.
Asked by Eagles On SI how Mannion is handling the adversity, and what he has seen in daily meetings, the quarterback stayed on the relationship, with the “warrior” sentiment.
That posture fits a pattern.
Early in the season, Hurts preached patience and building in-game chemistry with a play-caller working from the booth, something he had not done in the NFL, and about getting “hip-to-hip” with Mannion over time.
Wins over the Commanders and the Titans masked some of the growing pains. The last two games have not.
The Eagles are in London on Sunday to square off with a talented Jacksonville team while looking for the version of the offense they described in the spring.
And they will have to do it with a makeshift offensive line with no Lane Johnson (retired on Tuesday), Cam Jurgens (traded to Baltimore on Wednesday), and perhaps Drew Kendall, who missed practice on Wednesday and Thursday with a knee injury.
Mannion has insisted his core tenets are unwavering even though, all too often, they haven’t shown up on game days. For now, Hurts is still willing to absorb the shrapnel with the young offensive coordinator.
In Philadelphia, that kind of public cover from the quarterback buys time. It does not buy results. If the endorsement from Hurts is pulled and the messaging begins to change, Mannion will have one-and-done concerns to deal with.

title: One Name Stands Out More Than Many Others On Eagles' Lengthy Injury Report
full_text:
You have to dig really deep to find any good news buried under the pile of rubble that is Thursday’s Eagles injury report. But there it is, a couple shovelfuls later – Quinyon Mitchell was a full participant in practice, a day after being limited with the hyperextended knee he suffered in Sunday’s loss to the Rams.
So, beware Trevor Lawrence. The shutdown corner appears on track to play when the Eagles and Jacksonville Jaguars hook up in a game from jolly old London on Sunday.
Let the trumpets sound, if only for a note or two, because the rest is kind of ugly and not very jolly at all, unless you can take solace in the limited practice participation of linebackers Zack Baun (concussion) and Jihaad Campbell (knee), tight end Dallas Goedert (knee), and tackle Fred Johnson (knee). Even here, though, there’s more dirt - receiver Dontayvion Wicks was limited for the first time this week with a hamstring.
With DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and Hollywood Brown (ankle) not practicing yet this week, there’s a chance Jalen Hurts might be without three of his weapons. That would leave him with rookie Makai Lemon and Elijah Moore, who hasn’t even been targeted in the 16 snaps he has received in the two games he has gotten into this season.
Throw another weapon into the mix. Saquon Barkley's hamstring has been slow to heal and he hasn't practiced this week, either.
All of that may not even be the worst news the injury report revealed. That would be Drew Kendall, who missed his second straight practice with a knee injury. Given the bombs that were dropped along the offensive line this week, being without their new center isn’t particularly good news. In fact, it’s terrible news.
Kendall made three starts but could miss a fourth on Sunday. Remember when Jason Kelce made 156 straight starts at center? Yeah, that’s something that won’t be seen in these parts anytime soon. If ever again.
If Kendall can’t play, there’s a chance Jake Majors could make his NFL debut. Majors made 57 starts at center for the University of Texas but went undrafted in 2025. He signed as an undrafted free agent with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, but a wrist injury led to his release. Majors, 24, was signed to Philly’s practice squad last year.
He wouldn’t be the only young face on an Eagles offensive line that is changing daily. Willie Lampkin, 24, could make his first career start, lining up at left guard. Then there is 22-year-old Markel Bell, who is the likely starter at right tackle after Lane Johnson retired on Tuesday. It would be Bell's second start.
The lone stalwarts for Eagles first-year offensive line coach Chris Kuper would be left tackle Jordan Mailata and right guard Tyler Steen.
“Obviously, you want continuity on the line,” said Mailata, “but there are things out of our control, and we can only do with what we're given. It doesn't matter who the guy is next to you; you gotta get ready and prepare for the next week, but learning a new offense and trying to execute that game plan and execute the schemes is one thing, but I've always said this: continuity builds success.”
Continuity went out the window this week.

title: Why Zack Baun's Time With Eagles Could End Sooner Than Later
full_text:
It's not quite a fire sale yet.
But what the Eagles and general manager Howie Roseman have already begun doing is show they won't wait long to see if the 2026 team has any moxie . If their five-year playoff run is coming to a close, you can rest assured the organization will be proactive in its response.
First, it was Lane Johnson retiring on Tuesday . On Wednesday, the Eagles traded center Cam Jurgens to the Ravens in a deal that included a second-round pick in 2028. A team that many picked to be in the playoffs lost two starting offensive linemen in a 24-hour period.
It feels almost unfathomable that the Eagles would consider moving on from any other players on their roster. They are, after all, just 2-2 on the year. They aren't 0-4 or 1-3, but an average 2-2. Sure,  they haven't played well, but this is a roster that notoriously starts seasons slow.
That's what made the Jurgens trade so shocking. It was an immediate move to get younger and healthier along the offensive line.
But what's stopping them from trading away other high-priced talent that may not be available for their next run of dominance? Could Dallas Goedert be next? Riq Woolen? Moro Ojomo?
The Eagles may not be done, and as their gauntlet begins, they have more decisions to make. What happens next with linebacker Zack Baun is one of them.
While Jurgens was the player moved this week, Baun may end up being an unlikely casualty if things continue to go sideways for the organization. The two-time Pro Bowler and All-Pro has been a revelation since arriving in Philadelphia in 2024, working as a key catalyst for the defense to be among the best in the league.
But with a contract that expires at the end of the 2027 season, Baun's time in Philadelphia could end up ending sooner rather than later.
He's 30 years old and will be on the wrong side of 30 over the next few seasons. While it's true that Baun hasn't taken as much of a physical pounding as other career off-ball linebackers, it also doesn't hide the fact that Father Time waits for no one.
If Philadelphia is getting younger on the offensive line, some of its aging starters on defense could end up heading out as well.
Baun, being among the oldest, could be next. That is, if Roseman ends up blowing up the current iteration of the team.
Speaking to reporters after trading Jurgens to Baltimore, Roseman made one thing clear: Philadelphia was not tanking. The Eagles are still pushing for a playoff berth in 2026.
" Nothing has changed in terms of our goals. We're trying to win this year ," Roseman said (h/t The Athletic 's Zach Berman). "You want to have an extended run, and so my job is to look at how we can have sustained success for a long period of time, and you don't get many opportunities to get second-round picks in trades and get flexibility."
In Howie-speak: he's essentially saying that while the Eagles will try to compete for the playoffs this season, they also want to protect themselves for the future.
And if the losing continues, that mindset could shift again. Other aging players could find themselves on new teams.
Baun, despite all the dominance he has brought, may end up being next by default.

title: Eagles Markel Bell Keeps Hearing Lane Johnson's Advice, Excited For Future
full_text:
PHILADELPHIA – Lane Johnson’s words echoed through Markel Bell’s head when he learned he would be starting in the right tackle’s place last Sunday against the Los Angeles Rams.
“One thing that Lane always said was, ‘You can't make the game bigger than it is. You gotta go out there and play your best ball, and if you mess up, let that be a tomorrow problem, and go out there and play the next play,’” said the Eagles' rookie and new right tackle.
Bell did some good and some bad on his debut. Overall, it was solid enough to give hope to his teammates, especially after stepping into the breach in a big spot in a big game when Johnson was unavailable to play and has since retired, effective immediately.
He should get better, and maybe he will be the next Lane Johnson and anchor the right side for 14 years. That’s a lot to ask and probably unfair to do so. Johnson is probably in the top five of the best players to ever don an Eagles uniform.
“I'm very excited for the future,” said Bell. “I mean, I got a lot of faith for myself. I played fair in my first game, just being short notice. I plan to improve each and every game, each and every practice, each and every day.”
It’s going to look different without Johnson out there. He’s missed time due to injury during his career, but you always knew he’d be back. Now, there’s clarity, and he’s not coming back. He won’t soon be forgotten on or off the field.
“He's definitely a big brother to me,” said Bell. “He always poured into me. He always was saying little tidbits on, not even just football, but how to get my body right and staying in the games because it’s longevity that keeps you in the league.”
The one word that could best describe the Eagles when it comes to the offensive tackle position is stability. They’ve had Johnson, Tra Thomas, Jason Peters, and Jon Runyan each make well over 100 starts at tackle for the Eagles. Jordan Mailata will make his 90th start at left tackle on Sunday in London against the Jaguars.
Stability at that position has led to a lot of success for the Eagles since the turn of the century. Maybe Bell can be the next success story.
“Kudos to the rook, man,” said Mailata. “You know, stepping in and stepping up. He'll tell you himself, probably wish he could've done a few things different (in his debut), but that's the beauty about Markele, man.
“He's not afraid of criticism, he's not afraid of hard work. And so, right back on the film work, right back out there on working on stuff that he needs to correct. We have all the faith in the world, because that's just who he is, man.”

title: Making Sense of the Eagles' Offensive Line After Cam Jurgens, Lane Johnson Departures
full_text:
Seventeen years ago, the Philadelphia Eagles were at a crossroads.
Their offensive line, the source of their power in the early 2000's, was aging. William Thomas and Jon Runyan were on the downsides of their careers. Shawn Andrews' career was derailed with injuries, and Jamaal Jackson quickly fell out of favor.
For four straight seasons from 2007-2010, the Eagles did not draft a single offensive lineman in the first three rounds. It ultimately led to the group needing to be completely revamped over the following three seasons.
Does this all sound familiar?
It's happening again to the modern Eagles.
Philadelphia has not drafted a single offensive lineman in the first two rounds of the draft since 2023, three complete draft cycles have come and gone since then. Now, the team has seen their All-Pro right tackle retire and their Pro Bowl center traded away for a second-round pick. Injuries to Landon Dickerson have also left the Eagles in the same boat they were in back in 2010: searching for answers from a group that had lost its power.
As the Eagles prepare for the remainder of the season without both Cam Jurgens and Lane Johnson, how the offensive line looks will be a central question mark going forward.
And Philadelphia has some young prospects to try to develop in real time.
Here is the current projection of how the offensive line will look when the team takes on Jacksonville on Sunday:
LT: Jordan Mailata LG: Willie Lampkin C: Drew Kendall RG: Tyler Steen RT: Markel Bell
Far from the All-Pro greats this franchise has been used to.
There is a positive outlook, though. Kendall, Bell and Lampkin are all in their first couple of seasons in the league. This kind of experience will be so important for them and their development in the future. It will also give Howie Roseman a baseline into understanding how much investment the team will need to make going forward along the offensive line.
If the group plays well, the future may be brighter than anticipated. If they struggle, then more draft assets will go to the group.
That's what happens when you lose two Pro Bowlers and are down a third in a three-week span.
"Nothing has changed in terms of our goals," Roseman said. "We're trying to win this year. From my perspective, just looking at what is the ultimate goal, which is to win the last game of the year. And to have a run like we've had. ... You want to have an extended run. My job is to look at how we can have sustained success for a long period of time."
With the youth movement here in Philadelphia for their offensive line, that will be an indication of what the rest of the year looks like. If the group performs well, the team will continue to compete.
If they don't, it's the fast track towards the offseason.
And an end to this era of Philadelphia football dominance.

title: Howie Roseman Exploits NFL Market Inefficiency With Cam Jurgens Deal
full_text:
PHILADELPHIA - The Eagles dealt two-time Pro Bowl offensive lineman Cam Jurgens, along with  2027 seventh-round pick, to the Baltimore Ravens on Wednesday for a 2027 fifth-round selection and a 2028 second-round pick, a trade Eagles general manager Howie Roseman described as too valuable to pass up even with the optics of moving on from another accomplished trench player a day after Lane Johnson’s retirement.
On paper, Philadelphia is significantly thinner on the offensive line than they were on Monday. Johnson is gone. Landon Dickerson remains on injured reserve with a knee injury and Jurgens, who had been shifted to left guard to cover for Dickerson, is now in the Charm City.
What had been the strength in Philadelphia throughout the Nick Sirianni era is now a question mark, with second-year center Drew Kendall being joined by rookie right tackle Markel Bell and Willie Lampkin, a second-year interior option about to get his first opportunity set to team with the two remaining proven commodities: Jordan Mailata and Tyler Steen.
Despite the look to the outside world, Roseman insisted that the Eagles are not giving up on the season.
“You can’t discount opportunities that you think give you a chance to compete at a high level for a long period of time,” Roseman told reporters.
The well-regarded personnel executive framed the return as more than two picks: moving up from a seventh to a fifth in 2027, adding a 2028 second, while also banking the cash flexibility from Jurgens’ oversized contract, and keeping the ascending Kendall in place at center or guard amounting to significant value.
And yes, the Eagles are playing coy again with Lampkin at least floating the idea he may play center against Jacksonville on Sunday in London, which would push Kendall to left guard.
Jurgens, a natural center and the player the Eagles drafted in 2022 to succeed future Hall of Famer Jason Kelce, struggled mightily at LG.
If he’s not snapping the football, the Eagles were never going to get the best version of Jurgens, and the fact that the organization signed off on the positional move to get Kendall in the lineup at center spoke volumes as to where the organization felt Jurgens was.
The idea that the Eagles would have moved a Pro Bowl-level player they still viewed at his pre-injury standard is specious.
After back issues that required surgery and a 2025 season played through pain, Jurgens had struggled at both center left guard this season, including a rough outing against the Rams before he entered concussion protocol this week.
Kendall, a 2025 legacy fifth-round pick out of Boston College, had taken the center job and, in Roseman’s words, was “doing a nice job.”
Roseman insisted the Eagles were not shopping Jurgens. The Ravens, though, had been looking for a center, and the conversation changed over the last 24 hours.
“We weren’t looking to move Cam,” Roseman said. “Obviously, the Ravens have been looking for a center… Kind of told them wasn’t anything we were looking to do.
“Over the last 24 hours, it got to the point where we felt like it could be a win-win. … Obviously, getting a player who’s been a two-time Pro Bowl center and obviously for us, being able to get the picks we’re able to get, and use that money also to sign players.”
Baltimore’s need was acute. Pro Bowl center Tyler Linderbaum left for the Las Vegas Raiders in free agency. The Ravens signed veteran stopgaps Danny Pinter, Jovaughn Gwyn, and Ethan Pocic; all three are on injured reserve. Rookie first-round guard Vega Ioane had been moved to center.
Ravens general manager Eric DeCosta called Jurgens a player the team had admired since the draft process and “a young foundational piece” under contract through 2029. Jurgens must clear concussion protocol before he can play for the Ravens where he will pilot the offensive line.
As for those pesky optics, Roseman rejected the idea that his team is selling.
Getting a 2028 second-round pick and real cash savings is hard to turn down for an Eagles team heavily leveraged with void years for its plethora of stars. Future selections are routinely discounted in NFL trade markets, a market inefficiency tied to the job insecurity of many general managers that Roseman often exploits.
Roseman’s job security gives him a leg up in thinking about the future. For coaches and players, the horizon is game day. Those clocks are not the same, and this trade is a stark reminder of that.
It’s somewhat surprising that DeCosta, who is also secure, fell into this trap, but multiple injuries at the same position can derail seasons, creating desperation.

title: Recalling The Grit, Fun, And More That Highlighted Cam Jurgens' 4 Years With The Eagles
full_text:
This is what I wrote when Cam Jurgens came to Philadelphia for rookie minicamp just days after the Eagles selected the center out of Nebraska four years ago: “It’s not clear if Cam Jurgens has a little dog Toto, though what the Eagles’ latest second-round draft pick has is tornadoes where he grew up.”
Jurgens grew up in Pickrell, Nebraska, a town of about 2,000 people in a slice of the Midwest known as Tornado Alley. On the night he was drafted in the second round, April 29, 2022, a tornado alert sounded on his cell phone.
Ten minutes later, Howie Roseman called to let him know they were taking him with the 51st overall pick. Just minutes after that, thunder boomed, lightning crackled, and hail fell in chunks. So, it was off to the storm cellar with his family to celebrate him becoming an Eagle underground, because what choice did they have with a tornado spinning around nearby?
Another kind of storm passed through the Eagles’ locker room on Wednesday. A day after Lane Johnson’s stunning retirement, Eagles general manager surprisingly traded Cam Jurgens to the Baltimore Ravens.
On Friday, the Eagles leave for London to try to snap a two-game losing streak when they face the Jacksonville Jaguars. They will do it with an offensive line that was hardly the vision only a month ago, when they had Johnson, Jurgens, Tyler Steen, Landon Dickerson, and Jordan Mailata. Now, they have just two of those – Steen and Mailata.
Jurgens leaves behind a legacy of success, helping the Eagles win a Super Bowl in the 2024 season, his first as the starting center after Jason Kelce retired. He’s a two-time Pro Bowler, and while many Eagles fans may have wanted him benched for his struggles this season at a new position, he should be remembered for the toughness he played with, the pain he played through, and the fun he had during his four-plus seasons.
Jurgens wasn’t supposed to play in the NFC Championship game in 2024, but when Landon Dickerson went down with an injury, Jurgens came in for the second half despite a back that was in no shape to really walk, yet alone bend over to snap the ball and go block.
In the locker room afterward, Jurgens could barely move. He hobbled like an octogenarian who had just had both hips replaced to the seat at his stool and sat upright, patiently enduring questions and rolling his eyes when one hanger-on that season came over to scream at him, ‘We’re. Going. To. The. (Freaking). Super Boooowl.’
Jurgens’ entire upper body turned slowly to face the person yelling, staring blankly at him to the point where the hanger-on simply walked away without acknowledgement from Jurgens, who slowly turned back to face a couple of reporters and rolled his eyes. Presumably, that was one of the few things he could do that night when his body didn’t feel pain.
Jurgens was responsible for a sign that hung above the locker of former Eagles linebacker/fullback and current Chiefs fullback Ben VanSumeren that read, “Beware of Dog.” VanSumeren told me a couple of days earlier that he was a sleepwalker, and his girlfriend told him he sometimes barked like a dog while sleepwalking around the room
Jurgens saw the story, and the next day, he pointed out the sign to me. I laughed and said, "Where did you get that?" He said, “On Amazon.”
Jurgens may never be the player he was before his back surgery following that Super Bowl season, but he always gave everything he had.

title: Instant Grade: Eagles Trade Cam Jurgens to Ravens as Week 5 Begins
full_text:
The first full week of October has been hectic for the Philadelphia Eagles, and it's barely started. Future Hall-of-Fame tackle Lane Johnson's retirement caught a large chunk of Philly fans off guard on Tuesday, leaving a huge hole on the offensive line. As it turns out, the OL-related news didn't stop there.
Less than 24 hours after Johnson announced his retirement, ESPN 's Adam Schefter reported that the Eagles are trading center Cam Jurgens—along with a 2027 seventh-rounder—to the Baltimore Ravens for a fifth-round pick in next year's draft, as well as a second-round selection in 2028.
Trade: Eagles are sending two-time Pro Bowl center Cam Jurgens and a 2027 7th-round pick to the Ravens in exchange for a 2027 5th-round pick and a 2028 2nd-round pick, sources tell ESPN. pic.twitter.com/AaGL3MYqS7
Fans will never forget his contributions and the toll they took on the road to Super Bowl LIX (h/t Bleeding Green's Brandon Lee Gowton). But it's no secret that Jurgens has been largely disappointing since signing a four-year, $68 million extension in 2025.
He wasn't giving the Eagles what they needed at the starting center spot, and moving him to left guard over the last three weeks wasn't enough to keep him in the City of Brotherly Love. His entering concussion protocol to begin the week may have been the last straw.
So, how should Eagles fans feel about the out-of-nowhere trade?
Sometimes, a fresh start is needed when a partnership has clearly run its course. Although some Eagles fans remained optimistic about a turnaround, the first quarter of the season proved that Jurgens isn't a good fit in the o-line's new scheme under new OL coach Chris Kuper, and a fresh start for both sides was needed.
Between his time at left guard and center this season, Jurgens has played to career-worst marks regarding overall offense (38.4), run blocking (50.3), and pass protection (31.7) , according to Pro Football Focus , with all 12 pressures he allowed occurring after he was moved to LG in Week 2. We must give credit where it's due: general manager Howie Roseman pulled the plug on the experiment before it got even worse.
That said, the Eagles' return in the trade is fairly solid. The 2027 fifth-round pick they're getting back is an upgrade over the seventh-rounder heading to the Ravens, while a 2028 second-round selection is pretty good for an overpaid player who's worn out his welcome.
Even though the playoffs aren't out of reach with the Eagles at 2-2, the Jurgens trade could signal that Roseman & Co. are opting for a retool rather than putting all their resources into another potential Super Bowl run this season.
After all, the 2028 NFL Draft is now shaping up to be huge for the Eagles, who now have another second-round pick to go alongside theirs. That's without even mentioning the New England Patriots' first-round selection coming from the A.J. Brown trade, giving Philadelphia another reason to retool its roster before pushing all the chips in for a 2028 title run.
In the meantime, second-year lineman Drew Kendall will get a chance to prove to the Eagles whether he's a viable long-term center option. He hasn't exactly blown anyone away with his performances outside of Week 3 vs. the Bears, playing to grades of 52.9 and 56.9 , respectively, on PFF . He's still young, though, so the best might be yet to come.
With Landon Dickerson still on injured reserve, a lot of left guard snaps will fall on Willie Lampkin's shoulders. The former undrafted free agent has played two offensive snaps this season; however, he earned 85.8 overall and 85.1 run-block grades during Philadelphia's preseason, sparking hope that he can handle more responsibilities until Dickerson returns.
The impact of Jurgens's trade will be felt across the Eagles' interior offensive line. However, if Roseman and head coach Nick Sirianni play their cards right, the out-of-nowhere split could benefit their future championship aspirations in the long run.

title: 3 Eagles on the Trade Block in October
full_text:
It has been a long time since the future of the Philadelphia Eagles has been as clouded as it is right now.
Perhaps that is what happens when a franchise cornerstone retires as a losing streak begins to form. Lane Johnson calling it a career stunned Philadelphia sports fans, but also leaves a massive vacuum for the team moving forward.
And there are still 13 more games left to play in the 2026 season.
With Johnson gone, the Eagles' holes along the offensive line will remain a problem. They are dealing with a plethora of injuries that could derail their season across the board. As the trade deadline draws near, the Eagles are in a rare position.
If their hobbled roster cannot right the ship soon, it might be time for general manager Howie Roseman to trade some talent in order to gain extra draft picks for the future. A true tear-down for a team that, just two years ago, was the most dominant playoff champion in NFL history.
Much of Philadelphia's current core will be safe, but three names in particular could be traded if things don't get better. Let's get to that list now.
For the last two years, it has seemed like the Eagles weren't willing to give a long-term extension to their star tight end, but also didn't have a good backup plan behind him either. With Eli Stowers on injured reserve, it's hard to count on him to fill that role either.
That said, Goedert is on an expiring deal and could be looking for a chance to win another Super Bowl. With other contending offenses in need of tight end help, the Eagles could get quality draft compensation for one of the more complete tight ends in the league.
Remember, the Eagles traded Zach Ertz in 2021 in similar circumstances. The same fate could be coming for Goedert.
Philadelphia has already extended Jordan Davis and Jalen Carter. That leaves former seventh-round pick Moro Ojomo as the odd man out. Ojomo, like Milton Williams before him, is going to command a massive long-term deal in free agency this offseason. It won't be in Philadelphia.
While the Eagles could wait for a third-round compensatory pick, it wouldn't hurt the team if they tried to pry a second-round pick out of a contending team in need of an excellent defensive tackle. Ojomo hasn't recorded a sack this season, but has been doubled more than Carter along the line.
He's an excellent player who could make a contending team very happy.
During the offseason, the Eagles signed Woolen to complete an elite cornerback trio with Quinyon Mitchell and Cooper DeJean. So far, the secondary has been pretty solid through four games despite some late-game hiccups over the last few contests.
On an expiring deal, and looking for a chance to compete for another title, the Eagles could look to get anything from Woolen on the trade market. It would open up a need on the outside opposite Mitchell, but the lure of adding a draft pick will be too much.

title: 3 Free Agents the Eagles Should Call to Help Replace Lane Johnson
full_text:
The Philadelphia Eagles opened the new week looking to rebound from back-to-back losses to the Chicago Bears and Los Angeles Rams, in which they were outscored a combined 51-27. Before Tuesday was even over, Philadelphia had a new problem to navigate heading into Week 5: star right tackle Lane Johnson's NFL retirement .
Eagles fans knew Johnson wouldn't be around forever, but many assumed that the future Pro Football Hall of Famer would at least stick around until the end of the 2026 campaign. Instead, the beloved fan favorite did what was best for him and his family, ultimately walking away from football and the franchise to prioritize his mental health, as made clear in his retirement letter posted on social media .
Third-round rookie tackle Markel Bell made his first NFL start against the Rams last week, and while he was decent, the Eagles should add more depth now that Johnson is no longer an option. The pickings might be slim, but there are at least three free-agent tackles for the Eagles to target as they attempt to navigate a major loss.
Former Pro Bowl tackle Taylor Decker is still a free agent as the fifth week of the season begins. The former 2016 first-round pick has spent all 10 seasons of his career with the Detroit Lions, even signing a three-year extension ahead of the 2024 campaign. That partnership ended in March, though, when Detroit approved Decker's release request, with the ex-Ohio State Buckeye citing that the two sides "could not find common ground."
Even though he hasn't played Week 18 of the 2025 season, rolling the dice on Decker is still worth the effort for the Eagles. It wasn't at the same level as his Pro Bowl performance, but Decker was still solid across 894 offensive snaps with the Lions last season, allowing only two sacks and 33 total pressures en route to a 69.5 pass-block grade on Pro Football Focus . Not even close to Johnson's level, but then again, who would be?
Decker has exclusively played left tackle throughout his pro career, but the Lions occasionally used him on the right side. You can't always teach an old dog new tricks, but maybe Decker would be willing if the potential of challenging for a Super Bowl with Philadelphia is alluring enough. Bell and Fred Johnson (when healthy) can also hold down the fort at RT until Decker gets up to speed.
Throw in the fact that the Eagles had clear interest in Decker leading up to the 2016 draft over a decade ago, and it makes sense in the world to give him a call.
If the Eagles want someone with more RT experience, Jack Conklin could be there guy.
Conklin is another free agent with a solid list of accomplishments, which includes first-team All-Pro appearances in 2016 and 2020. Injuries have limited him to single-digit appearances in three of the five previous seasons, but that doesn't mean the 32-year-old right tackle can't be a decent contributor for head coach Nick Sirianni & Co.
Conklin was a disaster in pass protection last season, but he was actually playable as a run blocker, finishing with a 67.1 run-block grade —a higher mark than he had in two of the three seasons before that. He also allowed only five pressures (one sack) in his last three games after surrendering 19 (three sacks) in his first five, making it clear that he was improving until his season-ending concussion.
Also, there might be some familiarity between Conklin and Sirianni's staff after the Eagles-Browns joint practices during the 2025 preseason. Every small connection counts when teams are desperate for help.
Former 2022 seventh-round pick Thayer Munford Jr. is looking for a fresh start after a whirlwind ride to begin his NFL career. The Ohio State product spent the first three seasons of his career in Las Vegas before bouncing between the Patriots, Browns, and Pats again throughout the 2025 calendar year.
All five of his appearances came in a New England jersey, and though he didn't do enough to stick around, Mundford's performance could land him on Philly's radar. The 27-year-old allowed one pressure (a QB hit) on 40 pass-blocking downs, ending the season with a career-best 75.9 grade on PFF . Was it a smaller-than-usual sample size? Yes, but that gives the Eagles every reason to see what he can do in an expanded role.
With the ability to play both tackle spots and inline tight end, Munford is the kind of Swiss Army knife Sirianni should want to have on his roster.
