title: Steelers Must Make Patrick Queen Trade
full_text:
Of all the Pittsburgh Steelers ' potential trade candidates, one stands out above the rest.
Patrick Queen, for all intents and purposes, has been a disappointment throughout his three seasons with the Steelers. His three-year, $41 million contract that he signed with the team ahead of the 2024 campaign has not aged well, and there's been so signs of improvement for the 27-year-old under new defensive coordinator Patrick Graham either.
As he plays out the final year of that deal, Queen could find himself on the trade block regardless of if Pittsburgh remains in the hunt for a playoff spot or not ahead of the November 10 trade deadline.
Moving him is the obvious right decision for the Steelers, even if it means rebuilding their inside linebacker room to a certain extent in-season once he's gone.
In 2025, Queen was often a liability in coverage while also leading the NFL in missed tackles with 32 (according to Pro Football Focus ), with the next closest player behind him being Devin White at 26.
The hope was that Queen could bounce back and have a strong season in a contract year with a new coaching staff in place, but that simply hasn't been the case up to this point.
A slight positive to take away from his campaign is that his missed tackle rate has dropped down to 12.9 percent from 19.5 percent in 2025 (per SumerSports), though it's not like that's a sparkling mark either.
Queen has also had a few more positives in coverage, such as his red zone interception of Drake Maye against the New England Patriots in Week 2. The consistency in that aspect of his game hasn't followed, however, and his overall body of work also hasn't been impressive.
His run defense has taken a hit too, and that was never more evident then when he was blocked out of the play by rookie wide receiver KC Concepcion on Jaleel McLaughlin's 28-yard rushing touchdown in the Steelers' Week 4 loss to the Cleveland Browns on Thursday Night Football.
Queen has not played at a starting-caliber level for Pittsburgh, and it's shown with how massive the hole is in the middle of the team's defense with how he and Payton Wilson have performed.
Regardless, Queen is a two-time Pro Bowler who's still pretty young and is on an expiring deal while having loads of experience as a big-name player, which is sure to attract some interest from other teams leading up to the trade deadline.
After all, the Dallas Cowboys reportedly discussed a trade for Queen with the Steelers back in March, but those talks ultimately led nowhere.
Is Pittsburgh going to get a haul for Queen if it does decide to move him? No, not even close. His price tag is likely in the range of a sixth-round pick, and perhaps a fifth-rounder is within the realm of possibility.
The greatest return the Steelers could get by trading Queen might just be removing him from their defense, though.

title: Steelers Desperately Missing a Surprising Player
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- The Pittsburgh Steelers are searching for answers in the secondary. Although it's a problem of the franchise's own creation, the defense has no choice but to adapt with an injured and depleted group of defensive backs.
As the Steelers attempt to rectify the situation on defense, one player stands out as the one the defense misses the most. And it's not the one you're probably thinking of.
While it's true that the team needs safety DeShon Elliott back immediately and they don't have a replacement for Joey Porter Jr ., its neither of these top-tier defenders the Steelers miss the most. That honor is saved for current Minnesota Vikings cornerback and perennially underappreciated Steelers corner James Pierre.
James Pierre played six seasons with the Steelers. During his time in Pittsburgh, he played a variety of roles, going from special teams exclusively to a rotational player on the outside, to temporary starter.
That entire time, there was this sense that he could do more. Former head coach Mike Tomlin frequently cited his ability to rise to the occasion when discussing the defensive back. Last season was the biggest glimpse into that potential. Over 14 games in 2025, he started five and was excellent as a cover corner. Targeted 35 times, he allowed just 15 completions while recording an interception and not allowing a single touchdown in coverage. According to data from Pro Football Reference, quarterbacks posted a meager rating of 41.2 while targeting him.
That performance helped earn him a starting role with the Minnesota Vikings for the 2026 season, and he's looked excellent to begin this year. Playing as a primary outside cornerback under defensive coordinator Brian Flores, his aggression and long reach make him Flores's ideal CB1. In just four games, he's already recorded an interception and broken up three passes over the 12 times he's been thrown at.
Losing JPJ was a tough blow, as he's one of the top corners in the game. With a healthy Jamel Dean and the right supporting cast, however, the Steelers could overcome that blow.
But getting the right supporting cast has proved to be an even tougher process than acquiring top-end talent. Pierre is the perfect player in a time like this. He is a starter that comes without the fanfare, and he solidifies the entire depth chart.
As the Steelers try to establish an identity on both sides of the ball, it's players like James Pierre that are missed the most.

title: Steelers Could Get Huge Offensive Boost for Colts Game
full_text:
The Pittsburgh Steelers appear to be inching closer to having a key contributor return on the offensive side of the ball.
On their penultimate injury report ahead of a Week 5 matchup with the Indianapolis Colts, the Steelers listed running back Rico Dowdle (toe) as a limited participant for the second day in a row.
Dowdle did not participate at all the past two weeks after suffering his injury during Pittsburgh's Week 2 loss to the New England Patriots, so it's clear he's making progress.
His availability vs. Indianapolis is still up in the air, and his designation for the game will be revealed on the final report of the week on October 8, though it's a positive sign for the Steelers that he's trending in the right direction from a participation standpoint regardless of if he suits ip against the Colts or not.
Dowdle suffered his injury in the first half of Pittsburgh's bout against the Patriots and was carted to the locker room before later returning in the second half.
The 28-year-old was pulled once again afterwards, however, and has not played since.
While speaking with reporters earlier this week, Dowdle explained how the entire process played out.
"The first time I did it, I came to the sideline and I was like, 'I think my toe broke,'" Dowdle said. "So I went to the tent and it was dislocated and they popped it back in, did the X-rays. Nothing was broken or whatever, but once they popped it back in, I felt good, so I'm like, 'I wanna go back in the game and play.' Dr. [James] Bradley was like, 'No, we're playing on turf, think I'm gonna be done,' because when you get it, you hurt the plate at the bottom or whatever. So I ended up talking him into going back in, and he was like, 'If it pop out again, you've gotta be done,' and it popped out again, so I had to be done."
Dowdle went on to explain that the key in his recovery process is, "letting the tissue heal," so that his toe doesn't keep popping out of place, as he'd have to undergo surgery for a pin to be put in if that were to ever be the case.
Jaylen Warren has more than held up his end of the bargain during Dowdle's two-week absence, posting a combined 302 yards on 40 touches against the Cincinnati Bengals and Cleveland Browns.
Dowdle was still heavily involved in the Steelers' offense when healthy, garnering 19 touches for 65 yards over roughly a game-and-a-half, and that should remain the case once he's back on the field.
Pittsburgh could really use a bounce-back performance across the board against the Colts. It's not a guarantee that Dowdle will suit up in that contest, but if he does, he'll have an opportunity to provide a spark out of the backfield alongside Warren.

title: Officially Germie Bernard Time for Steelers
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- The Pittsburgh Steelers were once again dealt an untimely injury update, as wide receiver Michael Pittman Jr. is now set to miss multiple weeks. In response, the Steelers are mulling over what to do with his roster spot.
After Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy referred to the injury to Pittman as something that could be a multiple weeks-long issue, the team has to decide if they want to place the veteran on Injured Reserve.
Whatever they decide, the Steelers will have to find a way to get receivers open for quarterback Aaron Rodgers. Their pass-catchers have struggled mightily at creating separation, and needing someone to step up, the perfect candidate is already on the roster. Rookie second-round pick Germie Bernard has impressed in limited reps, and now is officially the time to promote him to a larger role in the offense.
Bernard has been a very small piece of the Steelers' offense so far, and it would behoove them to get the former Alabama wide receiver on the field more often. He's played in just 104 offensive snaps through four games, good for 38% of the total offensive plays, according to Pro Football Reference.
In Week 5 against the Indianapolis Colts, the Steelers have to utilize Bernard more, and the numbers suggest they will. According to game data from SumerSports , the Steelers are operating with three wide receivers on the field, also known as 11 personnel, with a high frequency. They are coming out in 11 personnel 63.8% of the time, which ranks 10th amongst all NFL offenses this season.
This evidence suggests the Steelers will rely on three wide receiver sets once again against the Colts, and with Pittman Jr. out, Bernard is the logical next choice for those snaps.
The Steelers might be forced to play and rely on Germie more with Pittman out, but this is a blessing in disguise for the offense. Bernard demonstrated one key ability during his time in college, and that came out once again in the preseason and over his seven receptions to begin his rookie campaign.
That ability is yards after the catch. Not only is he a polished route runner, despite being just 23 years old, he's extremely difficult to bring down. He's a sturdy and incredibly strong runner with the ball in his hands, and can create extra yards in the open field.
The Steelers need someone who can get open. Bernard does that. They need someone who is not easily taken down. Bernard is that player. Needing a spark on offense and with no other options, it is officially Germie Bernard time in Pittsburgh.

title: Steelers Get Good and Bad Injury News With Two Starters
full_text:
The Pittsburgh Steelers received both positive and negative injury news ahead of their Week 5 game against the Indianapolis Colts.
According to Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy, safety DeShon Elliott is set to have his 21-day practice window opened on October 8 while remaining on the reserve/injured list.
McCarthy added that Elliott will initially register as a limited participant in practice.
On the flip side, McCarthy also told reporters that wide receiver Michael Pittman Jr. is slated to miss multiple weeks with his foot injury, which has lingered for most of the season up to this point and has now been aggravated.
McCarthy noted that the team is still evaluating his roster position in light of that news, likely meaning that a stint on IR is a possibility.
Pittman Jr. missed Pittsburgh's Week 2 loss to the New England Patriots as a result of the injury, though he returned in Week 3 vs. the Cincinnati Bengals and also played in Week 4 against the Cleveland Browns.
The veteran was seen with his foot propped up on a scooter in the locker room on October 7, however, which was a sign that his injury situation had worsened.
It's still up in the air as to whether or not Elliott will be activated from IR this week and thus miss just the minimum of four games.
Being active vs. Indianapolis does feel ambitious, though it doesn't appear as though that possibility can be completely ruled out just yet.
The Steelers have a clear need in their secondary, and adding a proven starter like Elliott back into the mix (whenever the time comes) next to Jaquan Brisker at safety would allow the team to further limit Rayshawn Jenkins' playing time while also not putting too much pressure on rookie Robert Spears-Jennings to go out and perform on defense.
As for Pittman Jr., his absence will open up more opportunities for Germie Bernard over the next handful of weeks.
The second-round pick logged 45 snaps against the Patriots when Pittman Jr. was out and played that exact number over the next two weeks combined (per Pro Football Focus ), so he should be in for quite the jump in reps.
DK Metcalf and Roman Wilson would still seem to profile as Pittsburgh's top-two options at the receiver position for the time being, however.

title: Steelers, Lions Trade Makes Sense
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- The Pittsburgh Steelers and Detroit Lions were linked to Joey Porter Jr., but the NFC North team was beat out by their NFC East opponent , the Dallas Cowboys. But maybe they can return to the negotiation table, with another defensive back on their minds to be dealt.
The Lions aren't satisfied with their defense. Fighting for their season to remain alive, they're desperately looking for help, and Pittsburgh has options. Not the star cornerback in Porter Jr. that Detroit was originally looking for, but maybe another name who could satisfy their need to bulk up the room.
ESPN's Jeremy Fowler recently tossed out the idea that the Lions could call the Steelers for veteran cornerback Jalen Ramsey.
"Is it worth calling Pittsburgh for Jalen Ramsey? Not sure he's available, but the Lions' defense seems far from settled," Fowler wrote in his weekly buzz file.
It makes sense for the Steelers to at least consider the idea. Ramsey is only capable of playing the slot in their defense, and defensive coordinator Patrick Graham has made that very clear. He's the "star position" and that's where he'll stay.
He's 31 years old and it's hard to picture a future in Pittsburgh with his contract continuing to rise, which may be the biggest reason the Steelers should consider the possibility of a trade
Ramsey is set to make $19 million in 2027 with over $16 million in dead cap. The year after, he'll make $31 million or have $11 million in dead cap.
If the Steelers can move on from that contract, it's worth the risk. Because it's hard to picture Ramsey finishing his deal in Pittsburgh, and if they're going to lose out on salary cap space after this season, maybe they should see if the option to avoid that this season is on the table.
Plus, they'd likely get a mid-round pick on top of not having to pay him.
Brandin Echols also adds some security. Echols might not be an every-down cornerback in the NFL, but he's capable of playing a bigger role for this defense. Graham was quick to mention how impressive Echols was during his introductory press conference, meaning there has to be some faith he can play a key role in the slot if needed.
It would all depend on how willing Detroit was to make a deal happen. But if they're fine with taking on his contract and giving up something in return, why not make it happen? The Steelers have a replacement and long-term concerns about his contract.
They're willing to move on from bad deals. Why not consider this one?

title: 7 Losers, 5 Winners From First Quarter of Steelers Season
full_text:
The Pittsburgh Steelers ' 2026 season has been a rollercoaster, to say the least.
From the Joey Porter Jr. contract dispute (and trade) to getting embarrassed by the New England Patriots in Week 2, beating the Cincinnati Bengals in a Week 3 thriller and losing on Thursday Night Football to the Cleveland Browns to Week 4, it's been quite the eventful campaign for the Steelers.
At 2-2 entering Week 5, it feels like Pittsburgh's underperformed expectations a bit. There's still plenty of time to turn things around under first-year head coach Mike McCarthy, however.
With that, here are our winners and losers over the opening quarter of the season for the Steelers .
Any rumors of Watt's regression were greatly exaggerated.
After putting up just 7.0 sacks over 14 games during the 2025 campaign, Watt has returned to his typical elite form so far this season.
He's tied for the third-most sacks in the NFL with 4.5, and he's also logged a forced fumble (and recovery) to go with a pick-six against the Atlanta Falcons in Week 1.
Watt remains one of the game's elite run defenders too, and he's one of the early favorites for the AP Defensive Player of the Year Award after his hot start.
After a disappointing second season for the Steelers in which he failed to take any real steps forward, that trend has continued for Wilson in 2026 .
The hope was that playing in Patrick Graham's system would help unlock Wilson's skill set and make him more of an impactful player in the middle of Pittsburgh's defense.
Instead, his missed tackle rate of 18.9 percent is the fifth-worst among linebackers with at least 100 snaps (per SumerSports ), and his yards per coverage snap of 1.62 is the sixth-worst with that same criteria while also allowing a completion percentage of 91.7 percent.
Pittman Jr.'s Steelers debut was promising, as he lead the team with 58 receiving yards in the team's Week 1 win over the Atlanta Falcons, but it's been all downhill from there.
He did not play in Week 2 vs. the New England Patriots due to a foot injury, and he's posted a total of 31 yards on four receptions in the two contests since.
Pittman Jr. is dealing with plantar fasciitis, so he does deserve some grace in that regard. At the same time, Pittsburgh's decision to trade for him and subsequently sign him to a three-year, $59 million extension doesn't look great at the moment.
Warren's always been one of the league's more efficient and elusive running backs, and he's gotten to prove that so far through four weeks.
The 27-year-old has been the best player on the Steelers' offense thus far and single-handedly kept the backfield afloat amidst Rico Dowdle's absence due to a toe injury , posting a combined 302 yards on 40 touches between Weeks 3 and 4.
Warren's 5.6 yards per carry is the fourth-best mark in the league among qualified rushers (per Next Gen Stats ), and he's tied for the sixth-most tackles forced among running backs with 15 (per Pro Football Focus ).
The hype for Samuel Jr. was real after an incredibly strong summer. He immediately earned the opportunity to continue building momentum and prove himself as a starter amidst Joey Porter Jr.'s absence, yet he's fallen short thus far.
Samuel Jr. was benched at the end of Pittsburgh's Week 3 win over the Cincinnati Bengals in favor of Daylen Everette, though the Steelers will have to continue to rely on him after trading Porter Jr. to the Dallas Cowboys.
Among 94 cornerbacks who have logged 100 snaps or more this season, Samuel Jr. ranks No. 83 in yards allowed (202) according to SumerSports while also having allowed two touchdowns.
Rodgers has shown some flashes, particularly against the Falcons and Bengals, though his outings against the Patriots and Browns were rough to say the least.
The 42-year-old has pushed the ball down the field more in Mike McCarthy's offense, which is a positive. He's been inaccurate though, as evidenced by a 57.5 percent completion rate that is the fourth-worst mark among qualified passers (per Next Gen Stats ).
Rodgers' EPA per dropback of -0.22 is also the fourth-worst among qualified passers, and his complete lack of mobility has become even more glaring in 2026, which severely hampers Pittsburgh as a whole.
One of the best centers in the NFL, Frazier is the strongest link on a Steelers offensive line that's been invested into quite heavily by general manager Omar Khan.
Excluding Brock Hoffman, who has only started half of Pittsburgh's contests, Frazier is the only starter along the team's offensive line who hasn't allowed a sack yet while also boasting a miniscule pressure rate of 4.7 percent (per SumerSports ).
Frazier makes all the difference in the world as a run blocker as well, and overall he's one of the more indispensable players across the Steelers' entire roster.
Jenkins' lapses in coverage are quickly making him an untenable option at safety for the Steelers.
From losing Romeo Doubs on a 63-yard reception in Week 2 to seemingly missing his assignment and being responsible for Denzel Boston's 61-yard catch in the second quarter of Week 4, Jenkins has been extremely unreliable on the back-end of Pittsburgh's defense.
He played a season-low 13 defensive snaps in the team's loss to the Browns (per Pro Football Focus ), and he'll be hard-pressed to carve out any sort of role once DeShon Elliott is activated from the reserve/injured list.
Every catch by Washington is much-watch TV.
Very rarely do you see a tight end with his type of size, especially one who is as much of a receiving threat as he is. Washington is a handful to deal with for opposing defenses as a clear mismatch, and he's recorded 119 yards with a touchdown on nine catches this season while continuing to make his mark as an elite blocker too.
Though he's no longer starting at right guard, having been replaced by Hoffman in Week 3, it's still worth highlighting Anderson's shortcomings.
While he did suffer a bone break in his leg against the Patriots, limiting him significantly in what was a poor showing for him, Anderson's pressure rate of 9.3 percent on the year is the seventh-worst among offensive linemen with at least 100 snaps (per SumerSports ).
Benton hasn't played as much nose tackle this season as he has in the past, which was the clear intention of Pittsburgh's new coaching staff as a means of upping his chances to get after the quarterback given his pass rushing skills on the interior of the defensive line.
The Steelers showed their confidence in him by signing the 25-year-old to a four-year extension worth $72 million extension, and yet his 3.9 percent pressure rate is the seventh-worst among 90 qualified defensive linemen (per Next Gen Stats ).
Benton also has yet to record a sack, and it's not like he's thrived against the run either.
He isn't as flashy or productive as Watt, but Highsmith remains such an integral part of Pittsburgh's defense.
The 29-year-old already has three sacks on the year with 12 pressures (per SumerSports) and is a stout run defender as well.

title: Meet Steelers New CB Sean Murphy-Bunting
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- The Pittsburgh Steelers made two additions to their defense ahead of their Week 5 matchup against the Indianapolis Colts. The biggest name of those two is veteran cornerback Sean Murphy-Bunting.
The Steelers claimed Murphy-Bunting off the Tampa Bay Buccaneers practice squad after he missed the entirety of 2025 with an ACL injury. After impressing in training camp and the preseason, he gets the chance to immediately come in and play meaningful snaps with the Pittsburgh defense.
Speaking to the media for the first time since arriving in town, he spoke about what he brings to this depleted secondary ahead of a must-win game.
"My strengths are my knowledge of the game, my versatility, probably my press (coverage)," he said in self-evaluation. "Being able to play the line of scrimmage. Just versatility."
When Murphy-Bunting heard that the Steelers wanted to claim him, it was a huge update. He told reporters that his agent called him with the news and the choice was up to him if he wanted to travel a bit north and suit up for Pittsburgh. For the 29-year-old cornerback with 11 career interceptions, this was the perfect opportunity to show the NFL that he can still be a starting defensive back in this league.
"When I found out, I was obviously excited, you know, just for the opportunity," he told Steelers On SI publisher Noah Strackbein. "Just blessed for the opportunity to just compete and be on a team with this much talent. So, you know, I'm excited for what's to come."
Not only does Murphy-Bunting bring plenty of NFL experience, armed with 82 games under his belt. The former 2019 second-round pick can do a bit of everything in the secondary. Speaking on how he fits into Patrick Graham's defense, he keyed in on the biggest theme this staff has expressed: versatility.
"Being versatile," he said. "I feel like I can play pretty much anywhere."
Historically, that's been very true of his career. He's experienced as both a boundary corner and in the nickel, and he's worked in a variety of schemes, both zone and man-coverage based.
Murphy-Bunting also brings a keen observational eye in the film room. With so much knowledge of the game and experience on the field, he's a vocal participant and leader when it comes to breaking down tape week in and week out. Last year was a particularly challenging one for him, but he persevered and still made himself an asset to his teammates.
"I prided myself on being able to be there for the young guys that we had in that room," he said. "Whether it's the mental part of the game, whether it's knowing how to watch film. Just being an asset to the team."
The Steelers hope he can be an asset in Pittsburgh i mmediately, and they won't wait long to find out. Murphy-Bunting will likely get snaps as soon as Week 5, and the Steelers need good cornerback play desperately to get back on track.

title: Steelers Get Concerning Michael Pittman Jr. Injury News
full_text:
The Pittsburgh Steelers have released their first injury report of the week as they get ready to take on the Indianapolis Colts.
Michael Pittman Jr. (foot) was a limited participant, as was Rico Dowdle (toe) meaning he’s making progress after missing each of the Steelers ’ past two games.
Earlier in the week, Dowdle told reporters that he was, "supposed to be working in a little bit," this week and went into detail on what needs to happen before he can return.
"It's about letting the tissue heal, like the scar underneath so it don't keeping popping out because if it keeps popping out, I'll have to get surgery and put a pin in there," Dowdle said. "It's just about trying to let the tissue come back together... It's painful obviously, 'cause it's like I got knots in the bottom of my feet."
Jamel Dean (ankle) was listed as a non-participant, which doesn’t come as a surprise considering he’s expected to miss several games after going down in Pittsburgh’s Week 4 to the Cleveland Browns.
Jalen Ramsey (wrist) also didn't practice. He broke his wrist in Week 3 against the Cincinnati Bengals and played against the Cleveland Browns in Week 4, though it feels likely to be an ongoing issue.
The Steelers signed Sean Murphy-Bunting and Terell Smith from the practice squads of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers and Washington Commanders, respectively, as a means of supplementing their cornerback room following Dean's injury as well as their trade of Joey Porter Jr. to the Dallas Cowboys.
The Pittsburgh Steelers have an injury development worth watching with Michael Pittman Jr.
On the first day of practice ahead of the Steelers' Week 5 matchup against Pittman Jr.'s former team, the Indianapolis Colts, the veteran wide receiver was seen moving around with his left foot on a scooter.
He has been dealing with a foot injury this season that kept him out of Pittsburgh's Week 2 loss to the New England Patriots.
Pittman Jr. returned in Week 3 against the Cincinnati Bengals and was also active vs. the Cleveland Browns in Week 4. He didn't make much of a splash in either of those contests, though, finishing with a combined 31 yards on four catches.
Plantar fasciitis, which Pittman Jr. is battling through, usually lasts a while and can be a hinderance for a sustained period of time.
As such, it's fair to assume that Pittman Jr. is playing far from 100 percent and thus has been significantly hampered.
It remains to be seen how he progresses or where he stands in his recovery moving forward. Considering the Steelers signed him to a three-year, $59 million extension after acquiring him from the Colts in the offseason, however, the team really needs him to be out and producing there if the offense is going to really get going.

title: Steelers Have Never Needed DeShon Elliott More
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- The Pittsburgh Steelers are 2-2 after their first four games of the 2026 season. Things haven't reached a total sense of panic, but any time you lose to the Cleveland Browns, you have to take a long look in the mirror.
And that's what Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy called for as the team begins their Week 5 preparations. He described the team's need to "clean our own house," highlighting his intention of getting the team back on track before they take on the Indianapolis Colts.
It's a startling, but necessary admission as the Steelers still try to establish an identity under their new head coach. The team needs to face their failures and try to improve before it's too late, but there's also one missing piece.
The Steelers have a huge need in their secondary. They need a starting cornerback to fill the void of Joey Porter Jr.'s departure, but even more pressing is the need a tone-setter on the back end. Which is why this team can't get back on track until safety DeShon Elliott returns to the field.
During McCarthy's weekly press conference, he offered an encouraging update on Elliott. He was placed on the Injured Reserve at the start of the regular season, but came with the designation of a return. Having served the mandatory four weeks on the IR this designation carries, the first assumption is that Elliott's practice window would be opened and he would return some time in the coming three weeks.
McCarthy said that he's progressing once again when he next spoke to reporters, but the real test was whether or not he would participate in practice. Once that happens, it officially opens his practice window before returning. Unfortunately, coach McCarthy shared that he had "nothing to report" regarding Elliott's practice window, according to The Athletic's Mike DeFabo.
Asked if DeShon Elliott’s 21-day window will be open, Mike McCarthy said the safety is getting closer but there’s “nothing to announce.”
And while it's a formality in the recovery process, those 21 days are crucial. If he is going to return in 2026, those days are the true ramp-up period. Should anything go wrong, they could shut him down for the year. Should everything go right, he could be back on the field by their Week 7 game in Paris, France.
Where things currently stand, that Week 7 game feels like a long shot for Elliott to return.
If the Steelers don't get Elliott back before the end of the month and the secondary continues playing like they currently are, it won't matter how good the veteran safety is upon his return. At that point, the Steelers might be 2-5 and staring up at the rest of the AFC North.
Best-case scenario is that Elliott's practice window is opened without the intention of utilizing all 21 days the player will be allotted before the team has to make a decision on his roster status. As McCarthy noted, he's made progress and is nearing a return. Hopefully, with a few practices and time to get into game shape, he is back to making an impact as soon as possible.
In the meantime, the Steelers' defense is in need of a player to change the momentum. Elliott is exactly the player the secondary and the defense needs to right the ship.

title: Seahawks Injury Report Gives Cause for Concern on Both Sides
full_text:
After what looked like a fairly straightforward and clear injury picture for both teams this Sunday, Thursday brought some plot twists. The Seattle Seahawks and San Francisco 49ers will both be sweating out the final reports tomorrow after Thursday exposed some serious issues. So, who is in danger of missing Sunday’s crucial affair?
There were only two DNPs today for the Seahawks, and one of them was Chazz Surratt (calf), so at first it didn't look so bad. But Leonard Williams (ankle) was the other, after practicing some yesterday, which makes one wonder if he’ll be available for this week. Remember, Friday is typically a lighter day, so Thursday tends to be the key practice day.
Zach Charbonnet (knee) and Irv Charles (knee) remained limited on their trek back to the roster. George Holani (ribs) and Nehemiah Pritchett (ankle) are still there too. Joining them are Julian Neal (hamstring) and Ernest Jones IV on a rest day. Not ideal, but the signs are good for them to be at least available against the 49ers.
Tyrice Knight (ankle) graduated to full practice, as did Beau Stephens (knee) and the previously resting Jaxon Smith-Njigba. Patrick O’Connell (thumb) and Ty Okada (hamstring) remained full participants. It’s not bad overall, but Big Cat’s absence looms massive. Hopefully, this is a move to account for a Thursday game the following week.
The alarm bell for the 49ers was Mike Evans (ribs) missing practice, although it seems to be more a question of pain mitigation, and he plans to play. Not that there’s anything good about your top receiver being in so much pain he can’t practice. Nick Bosa (knee, calf), Kyle Juszczyk (knee), Marques Sigle (ankle) and James Thompson (ankle) all remain out too.
Mykel Williams (knee) is still limited and on track to make his season debut. The good news for San Fran, however, is Upton Stout (shoulder) getting in some work, putting him on a decent track to play. A crucial player in their secondary, Stout was one of the big question marks yesterday. The rest is fairly simple.
Dre Greenlaw , Christian McCaffrey , and Trent Williams returned from rest days to practice in full, Kaelon Black (illness) is feeling well enough to get back on the field, and Jaden Dugger (shoulder) and Romello Height (hand) remain at full blast. Expect all of them to play on Sunday. As it turns out, we can’t have a completely drama-free week at practice.

title: 5 Burning Questions on Seahawks Trade Target Tony Pollard
full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks are linked to several veteran running backs on the trade market ahead of next month's deadline.
Among those players is Tennessee Titans veteran Tony Pollard, who has 54 carries for 221 yards and a touchdown through the first four games of the season. Pollard has run for over 1,000 yards in each of the last four years and could be what the Seahawks are looking for.
To learn more about Pollard, we spoke with Tennessee Titans On SI publisher Lane Mills.
Not at all. He's in the final year of his contract. Pollard does what the Titans ask of him, but he looks like the odd man out in the midst of their rebuild. It's seemed like a matter of time that Tennessee parts ways with him for a while now.
Pollard is at his best in a passing offense as an early-down back. He's not someone to throw in on a crucial third or fourth and medium, but he can reliably collect a few yards and sees the field well as a veteran.
In turn, Pollard's biggest weakness is in short-gain scenarios when defenses are expecting the run. He's not as explosive as he used to be, and Brian Daboll has struggled to make good use of him when the offense needs a big pickup. Pollard can't fully be "that guy" anymore.
Pollard is a leader, and embraces his role as a veteran. I spoke to him a few weeks ago about his role in the Titans' backfield. He embraced splitting snaps with Tyjae Spears, and shared some of the advice he passed on to rookie RB Nick Singleton. That kind of positive mindset is hugely undervalued for a player in his position.
Absolutely. Especially with Emanuel Wilson already in place , Pollard would make perfect sense as a complimentary back in Seattle's offense. Something like 10 carries for 40 yards, and he'd shine.

title: Seahawks' Defense on Verge of Greatness After Players-Only Meeting
full_text:
Week 4 against the winless Los Angeles Chargers should’ve been a get-right game for the Seattle Seahawks. While the Seahawks won convincingly 30-23, they shot themselves in the foot to do it . Between the countless penalties and dumb mistakes, it allowed the Chargers to push for a potential game-winning final drive.
​The game was saved thanks to a strip-sack from former Charger and starting edge rusher Uchenna Nwosu. Seattle is preparing for a huge divisional matchup against the San Francisco 49ers (4-0). The Dark Side Defense can’t afford making penalties and dumb mistakes to give the 49ers’ talented offense more chances. The Seahawks’ defensive players are taking every chance they get to improve with a players-only meeting on defense.
​Veteran defensive tackle Jarran Reed told the media that the Seahawks’ defensive leaders called a defensive players-only meeting. The meeting’s purpose was to eliminate plays that could become penalties or anything that could give the 49ers life. Linebacker Ernest Jones IV, defensive tackle Leonard Williams, safety Julian Love and Reed were the ones who called for the meeting.
There are worse reasons for teams to hold player-only meetings. The Seahawks are still one of the top teams in the league despite the ugly loss to the Washington Commanders. Seattle is fifth in the league in points allowed per game (18.3). Its defense is also first in passing yards allowed per game (144.8), total yards allowed per game (246.8) and first in tackles for loss (28).
​10 of the Seahawks’ 14 penalties were on the defense or the special teams’ defending unit . A good portion of those penalties didn’t need to be called by Scott Novak and his officiating crew, who had a questionable performance of judging plays, but the Seahawks can’t give any reasons why they need to be flagged. Edge rusher Derick Hall’s late hit and nickel Nick Emmanwori’s unnecessary roughness are two types of penalties that the defensive leaders want to shed.
​The Seahawks’ Dark Side Defense arguably played some of its worst performances through the first few weeks of the season. Giving up 27 points to the Commanders’ short passing scheme wasn’t good. The Seahawks’ mistakes resulting in penalties weren’t a good substitute either. This player-only meeting should not only bring the defenders more focus, but also more determination to strive for perfection.
​This defense is among the best in the league in nearly all major statistics and they haven’t been fully healthy. There is a great chance that starting free safety Ty Okada will make his first appearance this season after missing four games with a calf injury.
Williams, Love and Jones are playing at a Pro Bowl caliber level . Emmanwori is 100% healthy and is being utilized at every major defensive area of the field. The Seahawks haven’t even seen the best out of cornerback Devon Witherspoon and defensive tackle Byron Murphy II yet.
​Seattle’s defense has to be ready for its toughest test yet. It will face a 49ers offense that is tied for second in the league in points per game (30.5), the offensive line hasn’t given up a sack yet and quarterback Brock Purdy is playing at an MVP level.
The Seahawks will be the toughest test for the 49ers and the game will be in Lumen Field. This game will be a battle of juggernauts and the Seahawks’ player-only meeting might have been their get-right moment.

title: 5 Seahawks RB Predictions for Week 5 vs. 49ers
full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks will employ several running backs for their game against the San Francisco 49ers in Week 5.
With Jadarian Price on injured reserve and Zach Charbonnet still working his way back from a torn ACL, the running back room has had to adapt every week throughout the season. The team signed Robert Henry Jr. off of the Washington Commanders practice squad to join George Holani, Emanuel Wilson and Velus Jones Jr. on the roster.
Here's a look at how each available running back could perform against the Niners.
As someone who is on the physically unable to perform list, Charbonnet is officially eligible to return to the field in Week 5 against the Niners. That doesn't necessarily mean he will be playing, however.
Charbonnet was a limited participant on the injury report this week, which puts his status up in the air for the game. The fact that the Seahawks signed another running back suggests that he may not be ready quite yet to make a return. Given that the team also has a game on Thursday Night Football in Week 6 against the Denver Broncos, the team might be looking to preserve him for that game.
Prediction: Charbonnet is not placed on the 53-man roster
Wilson crushed it as the lead back in the team's Week 4 win against the Los Angeles Chargers. He ran the ball 21 times for 81 yards and a touchdown, while catching three passes for 39 yards and a touchdown. Wilson proved that he can be the top option in the offense, and it is a role he could easily have against the Niners as well.
San Francisco has a much more challenging defensive front than Los Angeles, so there will be a fair set of challenges going into the week. Wilson is currently Seattle's best running back, so the team should be handing the ball to him frequently.
Prediction: Wilson gets 15-20 carries and scores a touchdown.
Like the aforementioned Charbonnet, Holani was on the injury report this week with a rib injury. Holani has consistently been the team's backup running back throughout the season, accruing a couple of carries in each of the team's first four games. In Holani's most effective game this season, he caught five passes for 48 yards against the Washington Commanders in Week 3.
During that game, the Seahawks found themselves trailing for most of the contest. This is likely where Holani fits best, and if he were to have a larger role in the game, it would possibly be because the team is trailing. The Seahawks hope that this isn't the case, but if they were to fall behind against the 49ers, expect Holani to be catching passes out of the backfield.
Prediction: Holani plays, but only gets around five carries for 10-15 yards.
Jones was signed to the active roster after Jaden Price was placed on injured reserve just ahead of the team's Week 4 contest against the Chargers. Jones has been elevated from the practice squad twice already this season, and the team would have only had one more chance to do so. This meant it was time to bring him back onto the active roster.
In three games so far this season, Jones has been mostly a special teams player. He did appear in two snaps on offense, but special teams has been where the team has asked him to perform. This is what he should be expected to do during this matchup as well.
Prediction: Jones gets special teams snaps, but doesn't play on offense.
The Seahawks signed Henry from the Commanders' practice squad earlier in the week, hoping he would give the team some depth. The 2026 undrafted free agent out of UTSA ran the ball 22 times for 105 yards and a touchdown during three games in the preseason. He did not make the team's 53-man roster but was brought back onto the practice squad.
It remains to be seen if Henry will even be active for the game, especially because he does not have much knowledge of the playbook. He's doing the best he can to make himself available, but if he were to be active, he likely won't have a very large role against the 49ers.
Prediction: Henry is inactive for his first game with the Seahawks.

title: Seahawks Offense Still Thriving When Heavy, Struggling When Light
full_text:
The results from the Seattle Seahawks on offense so far this season have been mixed . There’s been some good and some not-so-good. Which is understandable, given that they have a first-time playcaller and played half the games with a backup quarterback. But there’s a clear trend so far, which is similar to the trend established under Klint Kubiak.
A ‘heavy’ offensive set in the NFL is defined by having zero, one or two wide receivers on the field. Basically, you go heavy on the tight ends and backs. And so far, Seattle is clearly performing better from such heavy sets. Naturally, they’re also in these sets more often than most teams, currently 62% of the time, third highest in the league.
Their EPA per play from heavy is 0.07, which is 8th in the league and would be 9th when compared to the entire league on any play. Their success rate is 52.7%, again 8th in the NFL and 2nd (!) overall. And their explosive play rate is 13%, behind only Buffalo and San Francisco. They’re good, sometimes even great, from heavy personnel.
You’d think the Seahawks would be figuring out the wide receiver thing, given they have some pretty great ones. Signing Rashid Shaheed was presumably a big part of that . So far, we haven’t seen it play out. The EPA per play sits at -0.12, 24th in the NFL and hypothetically 29th overall. Three or more wide receivers just isn’t cutting it right now.
The success rate sits at 38.2%, which is 27th, and 29th overall. The 9.6% explosive rate is passable, about 17th, so there’s something salvageable here. But right now, this is one of the main things holding the Seahawks back from really opening up the offense . Hard to go aggressive and pass-happy when you can only put two receivers on the field.
Here’s the thing. Usually, teams go light on third down, or at least obvious passing situations. So this failure to produce from light sets is definitely correlated to Seattle ranking 31st in the league in third down conversions. And if this doesn’t get better, I can only assume the third down issues will persist. And I don’t know if a team that converts 31% of third downs can win it all.
The primary fix I can put forward is to figure out how to beat the blitz. While the overall stats don’t bear out a massive downswing in performance when blitzed, Darnold has been less efficient when defenses bring the heat. Last year, one of the key attributes of Sam Darnold was the ability to punish the blitz with big plays. We’ll need to get back to that.

title: 3 Players the Seahawks Should Trade for From the Philadelphia Eagles
full_text:
A few days ago, the Philadelphia Eagles were 2-1, held a 20-10 lead on the super bowl favorite Los Angeles Rams, and had a 4th and goal from the 2 halfway through the 4th quarter. Now, they’re effectively tapping out on this era. Life comes at you fast. Since they’ve been kind enough to make their intentions so clear, let’s see what the Seattle Seahawks might want.
This is the one I see come up the most from Seahawks fans that want a shot at the carcass of the Eagles. Saquon is one of the defining running backs of this era of the NFL, with over 11,000 yards and an Offensive Player of the Year award to his name. However, he’s turning 30 before Super Bowl LXI, has over 2,300 career touches, and is currently injured.
A bigger issue may be the contract. The Eagles have packed almost all of Barkley’s substantial contract into bonus money and void years, with the bare minimum left in base salary. This means the Eagles will likely have to pay out almost all of his contract even if he’s traded. Which probably means they need significant assets to consider it. No thank you.
The Eagles have been so aggressive with their contracts in recent years that it may be quite some time before they dig themselves out of the mess they find themselves in. So even though Jalyx Hunt is 25 years old and just starting to realize his immense potential on the edge, he might not be part of the next window. Especially in year three of his rookie deal.
Hunt broke out in 2025 with 6.5 sacks and 3 interceptions. If Mike Macdonald sees him as a fit for his defense, this might be an under-the-radar move to make that could shore up the EDGE room now and later. And unlike most players on the Eagles, his contract hasn’t been pumped full of bonus money and void years, so it’s a much more feasible trade.
Another 2025 breakout on the Eagles defense, Ojomo punched in 6 sacks last year. There’s no way the Eagles can afford to extend him after already giving big contracts to Jordan Davis and Jalen Carter. And he’s a free agent in five months, so the Eagles need to either make a move now or hope for a compensatory pick in 2028. But this one is hard to maneuver.
The Seahawks just gave Leonard Williams an extension , and Byron Murphy is next, so they can’t pay Ojomo either. This would be a half-season rental to try to win another super bowl. But then you still have to give Philly more than they’d get in compensatory picks for Ojomo anyway. I don’t see this one coming together. But someone’s probably landing him.

title: How Bad Has Seahawks' Run Game Been This Season?
full_text:
Through Week 4, the Seattle Seahawks are still searching for answers in the run game , which has been the offense's undeniable weak point so far in 2026.
The elephant in the room is that Kenneth Walker III is leading the NFL in rushing yards after he joined the Kansas City Chiefs in free agency this offseason. What’s currently being overblown is the Seahawks’ choice to let Walker leave; the divorce seemed imminent regardless.
What might not be overblown, however, is how much Seattle’s current stable of running backs has been struggling this season.
First, let’s compare the numbers from this season to 2025, with ranks among the NFL.
Rush yards (total): 441 (13th)
Rush yards per game: 110.3 (13th)
Rush yards (total): 2,096 (11th)
Rush yards/game: 123.3 (11th)
Obviously, the sample sizes are different, and these trends could look much different by the end of the season. But the ranks among the NFL at this point in the season are almost certainly not where offensive coordinator Brian Fleury and head coach Mike Macdonald want to be.
The two 2026 figures that stand out the most are yards per attempt and lost fumbles. Seattle already has more fumbles lost by running backs than they did in the entire 2025 season, and they’re currently under four yards per carry as a team.
Most of the other trends are about the same as they were under Klint Kubiak last season. The Seahawks’ run rate has dropped from 49.71% in 2025 (3rd most) to 47.68% this season, a marginal difference. But run rates across the league are up so far in 2026, as last year’s figure would currently rank 7th among all 32 teams.
One slightly concerning element is the Seahawks’ run-block win rate, which is currently at 72% (24th). Seattle’s offensive line ranked eighth at about 73% last season.
So, a few things are at work here: The offensive line has been slightly worse, Fleury isn’t staying quite as committed to the run as Kubiak did, and the running backs have overall been worse at maximizing runs and not turning the football over.
The good news is that all of these things are fixable, even before Zach Charbonnet and Jadarian Price are back healthy. Fleury is still in the feel-out phase of refining what is working and what isn’t, and it falls on the running backs to contribute to that process.
Still, assuming he’s back to 100% upon his return, Charbonnet should be a major boost to Seattle’s run game. He was arguably the better rusher in Kubiak’s system last season, and the current scheme under Fleury is very similar.

title: Seahawks Injury Report Provides Latest on Ty Okada, Leonard Williams, and Much More
full_text:
After a start to the 2026 season that has, in many ways, been defined by injuries , the Seattle Seahawks have gotten a relatively peaceful Wednesday report. There’s still time for things to become messier, but right now it’s looking like a chill week. The 49ers less so, but even they by and large know what they’ll be bringing to bear this weekend already.
It’s not a perfect injury report. But when are things ever perfect in a sport this violent? Patrick O’Connell (thumb) is a new addition to the report this week, but still practiced in full, so it’s hardly worth noting. The full participant that is really exciting, however, is Ty Okada (hamstring), who seems poised to make his first start of the season this weekend for sure.
Zach Charbonnet (knee) and Irv Charles (knee) are both working their way back, and got limited participation today. George Holani (ribs) stayed limited, and Tyrice Knight (ankle), Nehemiah Pritchett (ankle), and Beau Stephens (knee) all got partial work with new injuries. Leonard Williams (ankle) , as Mike indicated earlier today, got limited practice.
Other than Charbonnet and Charles, I’d expect all of these players to be ready to roll on Sunday, with few or no limitations. The only full DNPs today were Jaxon Smith-Njigba getting a rest day and Chazz Surratt (calf). Surratt is notable, since he was limited late last week, but he’s also a pure special teamer so the significance is fairly low.
San Francisco is very banged up right now, although they at least have the benefit of more or less knowing who will be available this week already. Jaden Dugger (shoulder), a part-time linebacker, was a full participant along with edge rusher Romello Height (hand), so their availability is not particularly questionable at this point in time.
Kaelon Black (illness), Mike Evans (ribs), and Mykel Williams (knee) were all limited, but all three are expected to go for various reasons. Williams in particular is interesting, as this would be his first game in close to a year and he just came off IR this week, so while he’s expected to go, you might be looking at 15 or so snaps. Evans played through his injury last week.
The DNP list is long. Nick Bosa (knee, calf), Kyle Juszczyk (knee), Marques Sigle (ankle) and James Thompson (ankle) are all on it, and have all been more or less declared out this week by Kyle Shanahan. Dre Greenlaw , Christian McCaffrey , and Trent Williams also took the day off, but for rest. Only Upton Stout (shoulder) is an unknown going into the week.

title: Seahawks' Locks for 2027 Pro Bowl After a Quarter of Season
full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks (3-1) are experiencing some growing pains in the 2026 NFL season, much like all teams in the league. The Seahawks are still finding their dominance, but are still looking to get better.
Through the first quarter of the season, there is great progress for the team to remain in Super Bowl consideration thanks to their roster and its contributions . There are several Seahawks that should be in consideration for the 2027 Pro Bowl, but there should be three players that should be considered locks.
The league's reigning Offensive Player of the Year is on track to potentially win the award again this season. Outside of former Seahawk and Kansas City Chiefs running back Kenneth Walker III, no skilled position non-quarterback is playing better than JSN . In four games played, JSN caught 32 receptions for 481 yards and a league-high six receptions.
​He had 405 yards and six touchdowns through the first three weeks, which was easily at the top of the league. The only reason he is now third in the league in receiving yards is that Chris Olave is the only weapon for the New Orleans Saints and CeeDee Lamb caught 17 receptions in a bad-defensive game versus the Houston Texans in Week 4.
​Williams showed how crucial he is to the Seahawks' Dark Side Defense with a new contract this past offseason. He continues his path towards a potential Pro Football Hall of Fame career with potentially a third consecutive Pro Bowl bid.
He is one of five defensive tackles this season to account for at-least three sacks. He has also accounted for 13 total tackles and five tackles for loss. Williams is one of the top leaders of the Seahawks' Dark Side Defense that ranks fifth in the league in points allowed per game (18.3).
Love has been one of the most underrated defenders for the Seahawks since arriving in 2023. This season has the potential for Love to be named to his second Pro Bowl in his career after facing multiple injuries last year. Love is playing faster, more aggressively, and smarter.
Through three games played, he has accounted for 14 total tackles, 10 solo tackles, two tackles for loss, four pass breakups and two interceptions. He has a chance to easily surpass his season-high four interceptions set in 2023.
​Other players who could be in contention are middle linebacker Ernest Jones IV, cornerback Devon Witherspoon, slot cornerback Nick Emmanwori, quarterback Sam Darnold and left tackle Charles Cross. Jones has accounted for 41 total tackles, which is the fourth-most in the league. Witherspoon and Emmanwori are two of the best lockdown defenders for the Seahawks, while Emmanwori continues to be utilized in the pass rush as well .
Darnold completed 65.7% of his passes for 547 yards, six touchdowns and three interceptions in only Weeks 3 and 4. Finally, Cross ranks eighth among offensive tackles in overall grade (77.7) and pass-blocking (79.4) by Pro Football Focus .

title: The Seahawks Pass Rush is Elite, and The Numbers Back That Up
full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks have 11 quarterback sacks so far this season, which is actually pretty good. Only six teams have more. It’s also notable that they’ve faced 124 pass attempts, which is tenth in the league. Nevertheless, the narrative so far this season has been that the pass rush isn’t good enough . Do advanced analytics bear that out?
Not if you ask ESPN and their Pass Rush Win Rate. The metric is best known for being used for individual players, but they also have a version that extends to the entire team. According to that stat, the Seahawks are first in the NFL, and first by a good margin. They win at a 69% clip , with second place Minnesota having 64%. That’s pretty definitive.
But that’s not all. Sam Hoppen, a Football Scientist at theScore, recently posted a table compiling various pass rush analytics. The Seahawks were elite or borderline elite in various categories, like Quick Pressure Rate (24.8% - 2nd), Non-Blitz Pressure Rate (42.7% - 5th), and Average Time To Pressure (2.48 - 6th). Most teams would easily trade with us.
That doesn’t mean there’s nothing to critique, of course. There were a few areas where the Seahawks scored closer to above-average, or even just average. Overall Pressure Rate (43.6% - 9th), Unblocked Pressure Rate (10.7% - 13th), Pressure to Sack Rate (16.9% - 14th), and Sack Rate (7.4% - 10th) could all be better. But none of them are bad.
Simply put, there is no reason to believe, at this point in time, anything about the Seahawks rushing the quarterback is bad. There may be issues with their approach, like playing Leonard Williams too many edge snaps and giving players like Derick Hall and DeMarcus Lawrence too big a piece of the pie, but the results have been good to great.
This isn’t me suggesting that the Seahawks should just stand pat. I’m concerned about what this rush might look like at the end of the season, with Lawrence (and potentially Fowler) running on fumes, while Big Cat might not be too far behind. I’d love to acquire a Khalil Mack to lighten the burden , or a YaYa Diaby to be a long-term foundational piece.
But don’t mistake that desire for a belief in the lack of current effectiveness. Seattle is getting to the quarterback, and they’re not having to do anything overly exotic to accomplish it. The proof is in the pudding, no matter which pudding cup you pick.

title: 49ers’ 2025 Draft Class Raises Major Concerns
full_text:
At the quarter mark of the 2026 season, it is always a good time to look back at the rookie draft class and see how they look adjusting to the NFL. However, the 2025 draft class is just as interesting, and their second season should see a strong leap.
Unfortunately for the 49ers, the early returns from the 49ers' 2025 class are more about big questions than players taking leaps, although they do have some progression candidates.
The 49ers' first draft pick was Mykel Williams. He has not taken a snap yet in 2026 after tearing his ACL in Week 9 of his rookie season. Williams is expected to debut in Week 6. Still, over a year and a quarter into his NFL career, he is still a complete unknown.
Alfred Collins got better as his rookie season went. He was expected to jump into a bigger role on a reshuffled defensive line in 2026. However, he tore his Achilles right before Week 1 started. He is an unknown until 2027.
Nick Martin was active for seven games as a rookie and played 15 defensive snaps along with 74 special teams snaps. He has been on the IR in 2026 and has not taken a snap.
Upton Stout is the first 49ers pick to be a hit. He has started for San Francisco the past two seasons and is progressing in the new Raheem Morris defense.
CJ West was a depth option as a rookie, struggled early into Year 2, and then got hurt. He should be back this season but brings plenty of questions.
Jordan Watkins has four catches for 86 yards in his NFL career. Injuries are starting to force him onto the field in his second season.
Jordan James has four rushes for 15 yards and was promptly beaten out by third-round rookie Kaelon Black.
Marques Sigle has been a breakout starter in his second year after getting benched as a rookie.
Kurtis Rourke has been on the practice squad.
Connor Colby has taken a big step forward and looks like a competent left guard after being benched as a rookie.
Then, there is Junior Bergen, who is not on the team.
They found three starters from this draft class, which is not bad. However, the top three picks are major question marks, and four of the picks look like they will not contribute much in the next year or more.

title: 49ers Have 7 Intriguing Trade Options From Division Rival
full_text:
The Arizona Cardinals are 1-3 this season, and with a new coaching staff, the 2026 season is more about rebuilding than competing. While the 4-0 San Francisco 49ers are in their division, the two teams could end up being great trade partners for each other.
On Arizona’s side, they do not want to give a rival their best players. On the flip side, if they turn the picks they get from San Francisco into players who beat them in the future, the trades will be gifts that keep on giving.
If the 49ers and Cardinals come together on a deal, these seven players are worth keeping an eye on.
The Cardinals are starting to realize that the former top five pick needs a change of scenery. While giving the 49ers this type of talent would hurt, he could also end up burning San Francisco as well. The 49ers need a receiver , and Harrison could grow under Mike Evans' wing.
The 49ers are very familiar with Bourne. This would cost a late pick swap or a conditional draft pick. Still, if the 49ers are desperate at receiver, it makes sense.
The Cardinals have said that they do not plan to trade Sweat, who still has a couple of years on his contract. However, the right price could get them to change their stance. Sweat had 12 sacks last year, but just one so far this season.
Browning is in the last year of his contract with the Cardinals. He is in an edge rusher rotation and has four sacks in 27 games since being traded to the Cardinals. Browning fits the scheme of Morris in that he can play off of the ball or put his hand down and rush. He would also not cost much.
Collins is another player with linebacker/edge rusher hybrid ability. He has been with the Cardinals for all six NFL seasons but is in the last year of his deal. Recouping something would be a win .
Stills starts for the Cardinals, but is in the last year of his contract. The team has other young defensive linemen who can take his snaps. He would immediately come in and start for the 49ers next to Osa Odighizuwa.
Billings is a run-defending nose tackle. This is exactly what the 49ers need. If Arizona wants to give a rental to the 49ers for a late-round pick, this is an excellent fit.

title: Mykel Williams Sends Strong Message Ahead of 49ers Return
full_text:
The San Francisco 49ers' former 11th overall pick Mykel Williams tore his ACL once he was starting to get into a groove during his rookie season. Now, Williams is about a week away from returning to the NFL to start his 2026 season.
He told reporters that he is going crazy in anticipation of getting back on the field.
“I’m going crazy; I'm losing my mind,” joked Williams . “Nah, I'm playing, but I'm ready to go. I'm excited to play ball. I miss playing ball. It's been damn near a year since I played, so I just want to get back on the field.”
"I'm going crazy. I'm losing my mind." Do you think Mykel Williams wants to get back on the field? 😅 pic.twitter.com/IPbCBY7lwW
Williams is on the PUP and can return in Week 6. The 49ers already opened his practice window, signaling they expect him to be on the field at the earliest date he can return.
When the 49ers drafted Williams in the 2025 NFL Draft, the expectation was for him to get off to a slow start. He is a younger player with limited experience at Georgia. His upside was high, but his prospect profile signaled a raw player, especially as a pass rusher.
So, it was not a surprise to see that he had just 19 pressures and one sack on 385 total snaps and 245 pass-rush snaps. He did add 12 run stops on 133 run defense snaps. Still, he had three pressures in his last game, and his first sack came in Week 6. He was playing better when he got hurt.
Now, the question is how he will fit into the new defensive scheme. Williams typically played the edge on run downs, then would slide inside on pass-rush downs under Robert Saleh.
However, Raheem Morris runs more five-man fronts, and it could push Williams inside as more of a 5-technique defensive end. Williams being able to slide inside and outside makes rookie linebacker Jaden Dugger more valuable as well.
Dugger has 100 defensive snaps this year, with 48 being on the edge.
So, the 49ers can align Dugger as a third linebacker in 4-3 base looks. Then, they can slide Williams inside, have rookie Romello Height stand up, and slide Dugger down to be their two outside linebackers in a 3-4 look.
Even if Williams is not providing massive production, his value on the field will be seen immediately. The 49ers defense has been strong already, but could be getting much better.

title: 4 Reasons 49ers Will Be Much Better Against Seahawks
full_text:
No team pummeled the San Francisco 49ers more last year than the Seattle Seahawks.
The 49ers stood no chance in their last two matchups against them. It was downright embarrassing, and that could happen again when they square off on Sunday in Week 5 .
However, I don’t think that will be the case. The 49ers will be much better against the Seahawks this time around, and there are four reasons for that. Let’s dive into what those four reasons are.
Without question, the 49ers’ offensive line has been the best unit in the NFL. They proved that last week against the Denver Broncos, who are one of the best defensive fronts in the league.
I fully expect them to hold their own much better against the Seahawks this year. They are easily still the best defensive line in football, but the 49ers’ offensive line is as well.
They won’t be mauled from start to finish as they were in their last two matchups. I’m sure they will have their fits throughout the game, but pure domination should be out of the question.
The last two games against the Seahawks were when the 49ers missed Brandon Aiyuk. No one could separate or carve out a soft spot in Seattle’s defense for Purdy to throw to.
That’s all changed with Mike Evans and George Kittle in the fold. Yes, Evans won’t be fully fit, but he’ll still have a major impact in this game. So will Kittle, even though he played in one of the last two games in a 13-3 loss.
Deebo Samuel will help as well. He’s not going to make an impact as a pure receiver, but his dynamic gives the 49ers an explosive and aggressive ability they didn’t have the last two times.
You can make the case that Purdy is playing better in this four-game stretch than in any stretch of his career. He’s been sharp, even though he did cool off against Denver last week.
Still, it’s hard to deny how comfortable and composed he looks on almost every drop back. He’s also not trying to force chunk plays as often, which has led to him getting pressured a bunch.
The Seahawks will be a big test for Purdy to see how much he’s ascended this year, but Purdy is also the best quarterback Seattle’s defense has faced thus far. It’s going to be an exciting matchup.
There’s no way the Seahawks would’ve been as incredible on offense in the divisional playoff game if the 49ers had Fred Warner out there. His presence alone is all the 49ers needed on defense.
Obviously, having Dre Greenlaw back is sweet, and Nick Bosa would be phenomenal to have back as well, but Warner is the first and foremost important player they need.
It’s not just what he does against the run and pass, but as a leader. He gets his guys situated in the right spot to execute the play call. His impact is second to none, and it will be felt immediately in this game.

title: 49ers’ Kyle Shanahan Details What Makes Seahawks Defense Difficult to Face
full_text:
No other team in the NFL knows how difficult it is to face the Seattle Seahawks' defense more than the San Francisco 49ers .
The last two times the 49ers faced the Seahawks, they were stonewalled on offense. They stood no chance of moving the ball and putting up points against them.
The 49ers only managed a combined nine points in their last two contests with the Seahawks. On Sunday, they’ll face Seattle for the first time this year.
San Francisco will hope to perform much better than the last two times. That’s easier said than done. Seattle’s defense is still as monstrous as it was last year.
The 49ers will have their work cut out for them once again. On Wednesday, Kyle Shanahan was asked what makes the Seahawks’ defense so difficult to face.
“How sound they are, yet still aggressive,” Shanahan said. “When they're aggressive, they're very rarely irresponsible. It's real tough to get big plays on them. I think they've been number one in the league two years in a row in that, whether it's run or pass game.
“They make you work for everything down the field. Then they’ve got a lot of good players out there. When you have to take that many plays to go on a scoring drive, they’ve got a lot of guys that can create some stuff and make some bad stuff happen.”
Shanahan knows all too well that the Seahawks make offenses work for every inch. They’re doing that again this year. The scheme that head coach Mike MacDonald runs is relentless.
He has all of his defenders playing off each other and in unison, which is easier said than done. It also helps to have a ton of talent at his disposal, like safety Nick Emmanwori.
“When you’ve got a guy with that size and length who can run and cover, to not know whether he's a nickelback, a dimeback, truly a linebacker or a defensive end, schematically it causes a lot of issues, just how to target people. Then just the matchup with how he's built lengthwise and how he can run.”
George Kittle will have his battles with Emmanwori on Sunday. It’ll be an exciting one to watch. But the biggest matchup for the 49ers will be against Seattle’s defensive line.
“There's not one guy out there who's not a good player,” said Shanahan. “They roll them, so they play like overachievers because of how hard they go. They play with their hair on fire, but they're definitely more than that because they're very talented.”
The 49ers’ offensive line has been sensational this season, but their biggest test lies in Week 5. Defeating the Seahawks hinges on how they can handle that vaunted defensive front.

title: Two Returning 49ers Faced Skepticism — They’ve Silenced the Doubters
full_text:
San Francisco 49ers head coach Kyle Shanahan has been criticized for sticking with players longer than he should, but two returning 49ers players have done nothing but justify his faith in them.
This offseason, the 49ers made some swift moves in free agency, including the addition of future Hall of Famer Mike Evans.
They also brought back linebacker Dre Greenlaw after one season with the Denver Broncos, before reuniting with Deebo Samuel following Ricky Pearsall’s season-ending surgery.
These two players are 29 and 30, respectively, and, at least on paper, appeared to be well past their best. That’s certainly what I thought heading into this season - and there was good reason for it.
Greenlaw played just eight games in Denver and hadn’t looked like the same player since suffering an Achilles injury in the Super Bowl. Samuel, meanwhile, had quit on the team toward the end of his time in San Francisco and showed signs of regression before departing for the Washington Commanders.
Yet both have returned on one-year prove-it deals and exceeded the expectations of many, myself included. The moves were initially viewed as Shanahan simply being too loyal to two players who appeared to be well past their best. But through the first four games of the season, neither has been incredible, but both have played well enough to prove plenty of people wrong.
Greenlaw has recorded 34 total tackles and 16 solo tackles, with the latter already surpassing his total from Denver last season in half as many games. He recorded a game-high 12 tackles against his former team, and the obvious motivation to prove his worth to his former employer only added fuel to the fire. He has also forced one fumble, so it's a good start to the season.
As for Samuel, he’s been all business so far. From 14 targets, he has 185 receiving yards, while he’s added 74 rushing yards on seven carries, averaging 10.6 yards per carry. Considering the workload he shares with the rest of the 49ers’ offensive weapons, those numbers are pretty good. He’s also scored three touchdowns, not to mention the 80-yard trick touchdown at the start of the game against the Arizona Cardinals.
Both players left, came back, and seemingly realized that the Kyle Shanahan system is one of the best in the league for a reason. Now, they’re both laser-focused on the same goal: bringing another Super Bowl to the City by the Bay.

title: A Closer Look into 49ers Kicker Eddy Piñeiro's Early Season Struggles
full_text:
Winning tends to hide all shortcomings.
And while the San Francisco 49ers have jumped out to a 4-0 start , the early struggles for kicker Eddy Piñeiro have not cost them in the standings but it shows that this season might not be as smooth as his first season in the red and gold.
The 31-year-old has missed two field goals and two extra points through the first four weeks of the 2026 regular season. Piñeiro’s best game came in Week 2 against the Miami Dolphins, where he was perfect in his five extra point attempts.
Both of Piñeiro’s missed field goals have been from beyond 50 yards, a 52-yard miss in Week 1 against the Los Angeles Rams in Melbourne that hit the right upright and a 54-yard kick that was blocked by the Denver Broncos in Week 4.
One of his missed extra points against the Arizona Cardinals in Week 3 also hit the right upright with the other missing to the left.
What made Piñeiro such a weapon last season was his consistency and reliability. He only missed one field goal in 2025, a 64-yard attempt, which hit the crossbar, against the Indianapolis Colts in Week 16 at Lucas Oil Stadium. He also missed five extra points, two of which were blocked.
But in his 16 appearances, both regular season and playoffs, with the 49ers, Piñeiro was perfect in all but five games. Compare that to 2026 and he has missed a kick in three of his first four games.
While kicking for the Carolina Panthers for three seasons, Piñeiro had his worst season in 2023 where he missed a kick in six games. One of those games occurred at Lumen Field, home of the Seattle Seahawks. A 55-yard attempt had the distance but was wide right. It would have given Carolina a lead halfway through the third quarter but it swung the game back in favor of the Seahawks, who ended up with a 37-27 win.
None of Piñeiro’s missed kicks from 2025 led to him being the reason the 49ers lost a game, his only missed kick in a losing effort came in Week 10, a 42-26 loss against the Rams.
Piñeiro (88.82%) still sits third all-time on the NFL field goal percentage list entering Week 5, so it certainly doesn’t mean to sound any alarms or perhaps sign a replacement. But it should be noted that Piñeiro might not be as Dinero as he was in 2025.

title: George Kittle Reflects on Kyle Shanahan's Evolution Through 10 Years as 49ers HC
full_text:
Kyle Shanahan is officially the longest-tenured head coach of the San Francisco 49ers.
Against the Denver Broncos in Week 4, he surpassed the great Bill Walsh, adding another significant milestone to his decade as the San Francisco 49ers' head coach.
In that time, the 49ers have reached two Super Bowls, two NFC Championship Games and the divisional round last season. So close yet so far, but being at the helm of the franchise is a milestone nonetheless.
Tight end George Kittle is one of two players who have been with the 49ers as long as Shanahan. The other is fullback Kyle Juszczyk, who arrived in free agency.
Kittle has been there through thick and thin, from the near-misses in the Super Bowl to the bleak 6-11 2024 season, when it seemed like the end of the road for the team's core.
But over that time, Kittle has seen firsthand how Shanahan has shaped the team's culture and evolved as a coach.
"One, I'm incredibly happy for him. I'm happy for myself that I was drafted to an organization like this with him at the helm," Kittle shared with reporters .
"The way that he conducts himself on a daily basis, the way that he runs team meetings, the way that he holds everybody to the same standard, everything he's done has been pretty consistent.
"He's grown obviously as a coach and he's done some things differently, but ever since day one, he's been really the same guy and I've really appreciated that. Being able to be here for each one. I haven't played in every single game that he's coached, but to be here for all of them, it means a lot.
"It's an honor to go to battle with him every single Sunday. When you have a head coach that one, holds everybody to the same standard but also two, you know how hard he prepares every single week and the hours that he puts in to try to put the best game plan together for us.
"I just feel lucky every single day that he's my head coach."
Kittle and Shanahan have become synonymous with the 49ers. Their tenures have grown together, and without Shanahan, Kittle may never have had the opportunity to surpass Vernon Davis and become the franchise’s all-time leader in touchdowns by a tight end - a milestone he reached against the Broncos.
