title: Why Daron Payne is Emerging as a Potential 49ers Trade Target
full_text:
The San Francisco 49ers' defensive line is thin, and they need to make a trade for someone. While Vita Vea is the name that is mentioned the most in connection with the 49ers, there is another strong option out there in Daron Payne of the Washington Commanders.
The two sides are a good fit for a trade, according to Bradley Locker of PFF .
“With the Commanders already 1-3 and owning only 11% playoff odds, the pending free agent Payne could soon wear another uniform,” wrote Locker. “49ers defensive linemen are dead last in run-defense grade through Week 4.”
The 49ers had trade interest in Payne going back to the 2022 season. Now, they might finally add him to make their playoff push in 2026.
San Francisco almost has to make a move on the defensive line. Alfred Collins is out for the year and not coming back. C.J. West is out for the majority of the season and did not look good before his injury. Rookie UDFA James Thompson has a high ankle sprain.
They are leaning heavily on rookie fourth-round pick Gracen Halton. He has played well but has already left one game with cramping. He is going to hit a rookie wall at some point, and if they keep playing him at this rate, it might come earlier than expected.
The depth is thin, and they can hardly fill out their starters.
Payne has been with the Commanders for the last nine years. The former 13th overall pick has 128 career starts and 37 career sacks. While he has only made one Pro Bowl, he is right on that fringe of being an above-average player who does not get recognized.
Payne is in the last year of his four-year, $90M deal . The 49ers have plenty of cap space to take on the back end of his 2026 cap hit. On the Commanders' side, they are sitting at 1-3, and they are rushing their starting quarterback into the lineup to try to save their season. A loss this week could send them into a selling panic.
Payne is starting to get older, and he is going to command money this offseason. The Commanders would be smart to get any sort of asset to move on from him. So, the two sides coming together does make sense.

title: Grading the Buccaneers' Week 5 Win Against the Dallas Cowboys
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers finally got their first win of the season, and it was in primetime against the Dallas Cowboys.
There was a great level of execution on the defensive and offensive sides of the ball. Let's go over our grades for the Bucs in their 24-16 win.
It was an overall very solid night for Jalon Daniels. He took what the Dallas defense gave him and didn't make any real mistakes, to the tune of 19/25 passing for 189 yards, one touchdown and no turnovers. He had seven carries on the ground for 23 yards.
The running game was the largest reason the Bucs won this matchup and it was by far the best thing the Bucs offense has produced this season.
Bucky Irving finished the day with 23 touches for 175 scrimmage yards and two total touchdowns. Irving also had the eighth-longest run in team history, with a 72-yard run in the contest as well.
Besides a great 64-yard reception where Tez Johnson broke the ankles of Daron Bland, the receiver room still didn't get much going. Offensive coordinator Zac Robinson tried to get Emeka Egbuka and Chris Godwin more involved, as they did combine for nine catches, but it still only went for 75 yards on the evening.
Egbuka did have a 14-yard end-around for a touchdown, which was a nice play, however.
Cade Otton finished the night with three catches for 25 yards and Payne Durham even got involved with a five-yard reception of his own. Still, this group is middling and hasn't done much of note this season.
This might have been the best performance of the Bucs offensive line this season. Now, they do get a good number of points off for penalties, as there were plenty from this group in this game.
However, they did do a fantastic job of opening up lanes in the rushing attack and Daniels' scrambling ability kept him to only getting sacked once.
The defensive line continued to be largely ineffective in this matchup, as Dak Prescott was not sacked once in this game and generally didn't face much pressure unless the team sent a blitz against them.
The Cowboys' run game did well in this matchup as well until they had to move away from it since they were down in the game. Also, Yaya Diaby had an interception in this game, which was fun to watch.
Who would've thought that Alex Anzalone would end up with the game-sealing interception for the Bucs, huh? I give a lot of points for that, and overall the unit did some pretty solid work, all things considered.
Jacob Parrish had an up-and-down night for the Buccaneers. He did finish with four passes defended — however, receiver George Pickens ate with nine catches for 130 yards and a touchdown.
Zyon McCollum was fantastic today in this one, holding CeeDee Lamb to two catches for nine yards in this contest. Also, I thought the safety duo of Tykee Smith and Ifeatu Melifonwu were solid in this game as well.
It was a great day for special teams as Miles Killebrew forced a fumble on Cowboys returner KaVontae Turpin to help the team pull further ahead. Chase McLaughlin made all of his kicks, and Riley Dixon was fine punting the ball as well.

title: The Good, Bad and Ugly From Buccaneers' 24-16 Win Over the Cowboys
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers had their backs against the wall heading to Dallas on a short week to take on the Dallas Cowboys for Thursday Night Football.
Unlike every other game this season, there was finally some good things happening on the field for the Buccaneers, who managed to pull out an impressive 24-16 victory in Dallas.
Let's get right into the good, the bad and the ugly.
Daniels' career night started on the opening drive where, despite some mental lapses, Daniels led the longest drive for the Buccaneers' franchise since Jeff Garcia in 2007. He completed 8/8 passes for 49 yards and a TD on 15 plays in almost an entire quarter.
Daniels is 1-of-2 undrafted rookie quarterbacks since 1991 – and the first since 2013 – to earn a 100.0% completion percentage in a single quarter, while completing seven-or-more passes (also Matt McGloin, third quarter, 12/15/13 vs. Kansas City). https://t.co/vWKcc4ifXq
Daniels was excellent throughout this game. Was he perfect? No. But he did more than enough to put his team in a position to win a road game they absolutely had to have.
Although he looked a little too patient in the pocket early on, Daniels seemed to really settle into a nice rhythm in terms of his pocket poise, timing, and decisions about when to look downfield and when to tuck it and run.
Despite possessing a big arm and the speed to be a dual-threat quarterback, Daniels resisted the temptation to play hero ball and instead played like a seasoned game manager tonight, taking care of the football and controlling the clock, which is exactly what his team needed.
Through the first few weeks of the season, Bucky Irving looked like the team's only true weapon on offense. Tonight, Bucky looked like the team's best weapon, but it felt like he was finally getting some help from his offensive line and offensive coordinator.
The Cowboys' defense has struggled mightily this season, but this is still an NFL defense, and the Bucs made them look like they weren't when they handed it off. Irving looked electric in this game and showed just how dangerous he can be when given some half-decent lanes to run through.
The Bucs totaled a whopping 243 yards rushing in this game while averaging over six yards per carry as a team. Bucky Irving himself rushed for 165 yards on just 21 carries.
The Bucs' defense played a really solid game vs. the Cowboys. Most impressive was the performance of their cornerback room, with Jacob Parrish, Zyon McCollum and Tykee Smith all having a significant impact on the Cowboys' production through the air.
Jacob Parrish has recorded three-plus passes defensed in a game for the first time in his NFL career. Parrish's six passes defensed on the season are tied for the fourth-most across the NFL this season (teammate Zyon McCollum is also tied for 4th).
Had it not been for Todd Bowles' atrocious game management decisions, the Bucs would have likely hit the 30-point plateau for the first time this year. Zac Robinson has had a really rough start to his debut as the Bucs' OC, but he was in a tough spot trying to alter his offensive game plan to suit an undrafted rookie quarterback playing the Dallas Cowboys on the road.
Although Daniels executed, it needs to be acknowledged that Robinson put together a game plan that allowed the dynamic but inexperienced rookie quarterback to perform at his peak so early in his career. Robinson mixed the run with the pass really well on Thursday night, and the Bucs dominated the game on the ground throughout.
It's important to note that although Tristan Wirfs did leave the game with some sort of lower-body injury on two different occasions in the second half, he did return to finish the game.
Still, there's little doubt that Wirfs is the best player on the roster, regardless of position, and if the Buccaneers were to lose him for any period of time, it would be a catastrophic hit to a team that is trying to dig their way out of a very deep hole.
Unsure if it was non-contact or not here. Thought at first he got rolled up on but not really the case. pic.twitter.com/8rPNALXTf2
With 3:47 left in the first half and the game tied 7-7, Todd Bowles' indecision cost the Buccaneers three points. The Bucs were facing a third-and-six from around midfield after a Tristan Wirfs false start penalty set them back. Initially, it appeared as though Bowles might be planning to punt the ball away, but then he changed his mind and sent out the field goal unit so McLaughlin could attempt a 61-yarder.
Unfortunately, it took the Bucs too long to get set up for the kick, and Bowles did not use a timeout to buy his team enough time to recalibrate. Bowles' lack of decisiveness — something that has plagued Bowles throughout his tenure in Tampa Bay as a head coach — directly resulted in a delay-of-game penalty, which took the Buccaneers out of field goal range and ultimately cost them points they desperately needed.
Absolutely unbelievable levels of incompetence lol. A high school coach would be embarrassed to mess that up
With 8:36 left in the game and the Buccaneers leading 24-10, Bowles decided to go for it on fourth-and-goal as opposed to kicking the FG to make it a three-score game. The perplexing decision was one that not only reflects Bowles' lack of familiarity with holding a lead this year, but also contradicts his profile as an overly conservative decision-maker on fourth downs.
Throughout the first four weeks of the season, it could be argued that the Buccaneers lost in large part because of Bowles. On Thursday, they won a crucial road victory despite some terrible game management decisions he made,

title: Overreactions From Buccaneers' Thursday Night Football Win Over Cowboys
full_text:
It took five games, but the Tampa Bay Buccaneers have a win.
The Bucs defeated the Dallas Cowboys on prime time in AT&T Stadium on Thursday Night Football to move to 1-4 on the year. It wasn't the prettiest win, with problems still present and the Cowboys almost coming back, but the Bucs got it done and outplayed the Cowboys to secure the victory 24-16.
It's a win, but there's still room for some overreactions after the game. Here are three of them as the Bucs get ready for a long week off after their Thursday Night Football matchup:
Walker is playing what is technically his rookie season after he tore his ACL in training camp last year, and boy, has he made the most of it. He pressured quarterback Dak Prescott multiple times on Thursday, disrupting the passing game and helping the defense in a big way. He also tipped a ball in coverage that resulted in a Yaya Diaby interception.
Walker is OLB5 on the depth chart behind Rueben Bain Jr., Yaya Diaby, Al-Quadin Muhammad and Anthony Nelson. So far this year, he's been better than all of them, and he needs the snaps to match.
Yes, this Cowboys defense is awful. But quarterback Jalon Daniels has executed fairly well these last two weeks, and he's played better than most expected him to for an undrafted free agent.
The Bucs took a chance on him after the draft and took an even bigger chance on him by making him QB2. Some were skeptical about what he could do as a UDFA, especially now that the Bucs need him to play, but he's done exactly what he needed to do and played about as well as he can over these past two games to prove the Bucs were right to gamble on him. He wasn't perfect — he almost threw a disastrous pick-six — but he has run the offense and got a win out of it.
Eventually, Mayfield will be back. But the Bucs will feel very comfortable with Daniels behind him.
The Bucs had an absolutely brutal night of penalties in the win, with 13 penalties for 87 yards. A good chunk of those were offensive penalties, with everything from holding to false starts plaguing Tampa Bay throughout the night.
The Bucs have no discipline on the offensive side of the ball. When the play is in motion, wideouts and the quarterback end up in various places the Bucs' line doesn't expect them to, and as a result, the team suffers from a good number of penalties every game.
There doesn't seem to be a fix to these issues in sight, even with this win. The Bucs have to be smoother in their entire operation from the ground up to find a way not to go backwards every week.

title: Buccaneers Matchup Against Cowboys Just Got Tougher
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers already have a tough task on Thursday night. They're set to play a red-hot Dallas Cowboys offense on Thursday Night Football on the road, and at 0-4, the Bucs really need a win to give themselves even a drop of hope for the remainder of the year.
Unfortunately for Tampa Bay, that task got a little bit harder for them once the Dallas Cowboys activated a key starter on the Thursday of the game.
Cowboys guard Tyler Smith was questionable on Dallas' injury report as he's been recovering from thumb surgery before the season. Per the NFL's Ian Rapoport, he's set to make his debut against the Bucs on Thursday night.
The #Cowboys are activating All-Pro G Tyler Smith from Injured Reserve to play tonight against the #Bucs . A big lift. One of the NFL's best, Smith had thumb surgery right before the season with hopes of returning as soon as possible. After a full practice Wednesday, he's back. pic.twitter.com/3XQLuAy8R2
Smith was a Second Team All-Pro in 2023 and is a stalwart on the Cowboys' offensive line. A three-time consecutive Pro Bowler dating back to 2023, Smith has been a crucial part of Dallas' offense and signed a four-year, $96 million contract in 2025.
Now that he's back to protect quarterback Dak Prescott, Tampa Bay's pass rush will have to step up on Thursday to get to him through Smith's efforts. That will include players like Calijah Kancey, Tampa Bay's pass-rushing DT, Vita Vea and A'Shawn Robinson to disrupt the middle and halt both the run and the pass against Dallas.
Tampa Bay is getting a player of its own back with Rueben Bain Jr., who missed the last two games due to a groin issue he suffered against the Cleveland Browns. The Bucs have lost safety Antoine Winfield Jr. for the next few weeks due to a rib injury, though, and they're also starting backup quarterback Jalon Daniels with Baker Mayfield recovering from a thumb injury.
The Bucs will play the Cowboys on Thursday night at 8:15. Head coach Todd Bowles will have to do everything he can to get pressure up the middle, and with Smith's return to the team, his job has gotten a bit harder in that regard.

title: 3 Storylines I'm Watching Most in Buccaneers Week 5 Matchup Against Cowboys
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers are limping into a primetime matchup against the Dallas Cowboys on Thursday Night Football.
A 0-4 start hasn't instilled much confidence in this team, and they face yet another tall task in front of them as they search for their first win.
It doesn't seem like the Bucs will have much of a chance in this one, but these are the three storylines we will be watching when they take on the Cowboys in Jerry's World.
This will be Jalon Daniels' second-ever start, and it will come in primetime. The pressure will amp up, and Daniels will not only need to have an excellent game through the air but also on the ground.
Daniels, along with Bucky Irving, Kenny Gainwell and Sean Tucker, must all be at their best. They will have ample opportunities to make plays as Dallas is surrendering 150.3 rushing yards per game (31st in the NFL).
Zac Robinson must lean on his running backs and mobile quarterback in this one if they hope to match Dallas score-for-score, and it would also help with controlling the game clock, keeping the Cowboys' offense off the field and keeping themselves out of third-and-long situations.
It's the first 0-4 start in Tampa Bay since 2013, and head coach Todd Bowles' seat couldn't get much warmer.
It's desperation time for Bowles and the Bucs, so not showing up at all would quite literally be the straw that breaks the camel's back.
Getting blown out on national television would put the Bucs' record at 0-5, which would make it one of the worst starts in franchise history — the first since Tony Dungy's inaugural season back in 1996.
If that does indeed happen, the writing will most definitely be on the wall for Bowles and company.
Dallas boasts one of the best offenses in the league, which is headed by an elite passing game with Dak Prescott, CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens leading the charge.
It was already going to be a massive challenge for a young Bucs' secondary, but that hill got even steeper with Antoine Winfield Jr. being ruled out as he deals with a rib fracture.
While Winfield hasn't been his best, the Bucs will now have to rely on backups to try and help slow down the Cowboys' passing attack. How Tampa Bay and Bowles adapt to the absence of Winfield against Dallas' passing game will be a major defining factor in whether they can keep this game close.

title: Our Buccaneers vs. Cowboys Score Predictions Are In
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers have a big game against the Dallas Cowboys on prime time Thursday night. If they can't get the win on Thursday night football, they'll be starting at 0-5 and, despite it just being October, virtually the death knell to their playoff hopes.
As always, our staff is putting in our predictions for the Thursday Night Football — do we think Todd Bowles will get his team back on track, or will the Bucs drop their fifth straight game?
It’s hard to imagine the Buccaneers turning things around in a short week, especially against the Cowboys.
The Cowboys' offense is a high-flying machine and will test the Bucs’ secondary that is now without Antoine Winfield Jr. Their defense has been a work in progress, however, so the Bucs just might be able to exploit it to put points on the board.
With that being said, they haven’t been able to exploit anyone this season.
I expect much of what we have seen through four weeks once again on TNF.
The Buccaneers get another loss here and fall to 0-5. This is a ship without oars, a plane without wings and a team without direction. Just about nothing is going well for this football team, and I believe it will continue with another loss.
Not only are the Buccaneers 0-4 to start this season, but they're a league-worst 2-11 over their last 13 games dating back to last year. For a team that was expected by many to be a potential contender in the NFC this season, the early returns have been incredibly disappointing. Todd Bowles' Bucs don't just look lost, they look lifeless — and his job is at risk because of it.
The Dallas Cowboys have a talented offense and a vulnerable defense. That being said, I don't believe that Jalon Daniels (in his second NFL start) will be able to take advantage of the Cowboys' defense anywhere close to what Dak Prescott could do to Todd Bowles' defense. Especially on the road.
The biggest questions asked of us this week to the Bucs coaching staff and players were whether they think they can keep up with the points against the Cowboys. That's the big question.
Dak Prescott, CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens showcase the serious power of their offense. But if there's a defense to succeed against, it would be the Cowboys'. Yes, you are still working with an undrafted rookie quarterback, but if you can't show any type of efficiency, it's going to be a long evening on primetime television.
Zac Robinson hasn't shown me that out of nowhere this offense is going to take a big turn, and remember, it is a primetime game — Those don't usually bode well for Todd Bowles and this Bucs team.
The Buccaneers have kept most games "close" so far — they've never actually been in control of any of these close games — but that's going to change on Thursday night. This Cowboys team has the serious means to put up points, and with weapons in the wideout corps and an elite quarterback in Dak Prescott, they certainly will on a Bucs defense that looks better than it is.
Tampa Bay's offense with Jalon Daniels will likely struggle even against a rough Cowboys defense — Joey Porter Jr. will probably add some extra help to a team that really needs it. I think the Bucs get blown out on national television, and it'll be another ember to the fire under Bowles' seat.

title: 3 Things Buccaneers Must Do to Beat the Cowboys on Thursday Night Football
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers have a tough, tough task on Thursday Night Football. They head to AT&T Stadium to face the Dallas Cowboys, and when they do, they'll be hoping to get a win on a quick turnaround for their first victory of the year.
The Cowboys are 2-2, and although they've struggled at times and have a questionable defense, they pose a lot of problems for Tampa Bay. If the Bucs want to win this game, there are a few things they'll simply have to do to will it to victory.
Here are three keys to victory for Tampa Bay on Thursday night:
The Bucs had a pretty hard time running the football in Week 4 against the Green Bay Packers. The Bucs averaged 3.8 yards per carry on designed runs with an EPA/rush of -0.036 and a success rate of 44.0%. Jalon Daniels propped up the brunt of it with 55 yards on the ground, but that's not good enough.
If the Bucs want to help Daniels in his second-ever NFL start, they'll have to do better with the ground game. That might involve finding better ways for running back Kenny Gainwell to get going (Gainwell had less than two yards per carry last week) or using Sean Tucker, who had three carries and a touchdown, a little bit more.
The Bucs might have to beat this Cowboys team in a shootout. They can't do that if they can't get the ground game going.
This Cowboys offense has the talent to annihilate opposing defenses. Their wideout duo of George Pickens and CeeDee Lamb may be the best in the NFL, and tight end Jake Ferguson also gives them some lethal options up the middle. The whole offense is commanded by elite quarterback Dak Prescott, and if the Bucs have any hope of slowing down this offense, it will have to be by getting pressure.
Prescott's EPA/play when pressured is -0.21, per SumerSports, and he's completed 23 of 48 passes for one touchdown, one pick and six sacks. The Bucs need to disrupt Prescott at the line of scrimmage to be able to stop him from finding his skill position weapons because, simply put, they will be open.
Unfortunately, Tampa Bay has a pressure rate of 26.5% — dead last in the NFL. The Bucs are also 25th in the league in sacks, and the Bucs will simply have to get some on Thursday night to have any sort of hope. We'll see what Bowles cooks up.
As it stands, Tampa Bay's air yards per completion of 3.39 yards is the worst in the NFL, and it's even significantly behind the Atlanta Falcons' 4.03 yards in 31st place. The Bucs aren't actually being conservative with their passing game — they're 14th in the league in average depth of target — they just aren't hitting any deep shots whatsoever.
In Week 4 specifically, during Daniels' first start, the Bucs had just 1.53 air yards per completion (31 of 32 teams) and 4.19 ADOT (31 of 32 teams). That number has to be significantly higher if Tampa Bay wants to have any shot of beating Dallas, because if Dallas' offense is going to score, the Bucs will have to keep up.
Throwing passes behind the line of scrimmage won't do that. Tampa Bay has to go long (or at least intermediate!) if it wants to come out of Dallas with a victory Thursday night.

title: Week 5 Injury: Examining Titans’ Chances if Carnell Tate Can’t Play vs. Texans
full_text:
The Tennessee Titans were hit with some concerning news ahead of their Week 5 AFC South matchup against the Houston Texans.
According to ESPN’s Turron Davenport, rookie WR Carnell Tate appears to have tweaked his back during the individual portion of Thursday’s practice.
It’s unclear whether he returned, since media members are only allowed to watch certain parts of practice, but the Titans listed him as ‘limited’ on its official injury report.
The talented rookie is coming off a monster breakout performance against the Baltimore Ravens that saw him reel in nine catches for 145 yards. And those numbers would be inflated even further had some missed opportunities not gotten away from him.
Nonetheless, the former Buckeye has really started to come alive over the last two weeks, essentially becoming the focal point of Tennessee’s offense, totaling 21 targets and 15 grabs for 203 yards over that span.
If Tate can’t go, the Titans’ already lackluster offense could be without their most explosive and consistent weapon in a divisional game they desperately need to win as they try to avoid an 0-5 hole.
Tennessee may need to lean on the ground game spearheaded by RBs Tony Pollard and Tyjae Spears. But without Tate, it will be up to Tennessee’s other group of pass catchers to keep the passing game afloat. This would be a great moment for the Titans to get their money’s worth out of one of their prized free agent acquisitions, WR Wan’Dale Robinson.
The Kentucky product has only caught 16 passes this season, one more than Tennessee’s rookie has over the last two weeks alone. Outside of him second year pass catchers Elic Ayomanor has only contributed in spurts, while WR Chim Dike and TE Gunnar Helm have been non-existent through four games.
Because of this, Titans QB Cam Ward would undoubtedly take the biggest hit should Tate’s injury keep him out of Sunday’s action. The two former top five picks have a budding connection that needs all the reps they can get together.
It would be a real shame if Tate’s sudden back injury prevents them from building off last week’s success. Only time will tell how all this plays out, but for the Titans’ sake, let’s hope they’re just being overly cautious with one of their most important players.
However, this situation definitely bears watching as kickoff draws nearer.

title: The 3 Matchups Titans Have to Win to Beat Texans in Week 5: Can Tennessee Stop C.J. Stroud?
full_text:
The Tennessee Titans are widely doubted against the Houston Texans this Sunday, despite returning from a two-game road stint. Titans fans are used to that song and dance by now.
Tennessee remains in pursuit of their first win, and Week 5 is specifically important due to it being their AFC South debut. For reference, the Titans went 0-6 in the divison last season. It was the first time they hit that low bar since the division's inception in 2002.
To say that the pressure is high for the Titans to find a way this week would be putting it lightly. Here are three matchups Tennessee has to find a way to win in order to come out on top on the scoreboard.
JC Latham has sneakily developed into one of the best RTs in the NFL in his third year with the Titans. He's yet to allow a sack this season, and is finally looking every part of the elite player Tennessee needs him to be.
Facing off against DE Will Anderson Jr., Latham will face his most important matchup of the season - perhaps even of his young career. With RG Fernando Carmona's absence already impacting the o-line, Latham being pitted against a defender like Anderson could make or break Ward's ability to make plays in the pocket.
Latham called the face-off a "battle of respect" as he looks to limit the 4.5-sack defender this coming Sunday. This is Latham's chance to plant his flag in what appears to be real long-term growth.
This is the big one. The Texans may be 0-4, but C.J. Stroud's revenge tour after his four-interception performance in the playoffs last season is very much alive.
Stroud has five touchdowns to zero interceptions this season. He's led the Texans to 30+ points in two of their four games, and has thrown more than 340 yards twice this year. PFF statistics have him in the league's top 10 in overall grade, passing yards (1141), and passing scores.
An expectedly healthy Titans' secondary, which Saleh acknowledged today "hasn't been great" adjusting to his system this season, will have to counter one of the most explosive passing offenses in the NFL.
For an 0-4 team, it simply is no longer a matter of paced development and inch-by-inch progress. If the Titans want to salvage this season as Saleh believes they can, what is arguably their weakest defensive unit will have to play above the line.
With defensive-minded coach DeMeco Ryans taking over play-calling duties on that side of the ball in Week 5, it will be a battle between Saleh and Ryans on the sideline.
Saleh already lost a similar duel to Aaron Glenn and the New York Jets at the beginning of this season. The secondary stopping Stroud is one thing, but with a new play-caller in place for Houston, we'll get to see two specialized defenses in direct comparison.
The head coach dove into what he dubbed a "unique" zone system for Tennessee today, as compared to match or man coverage. It's a compelling conversation that hasn't yet translated to consistent success on the field, even with pivotal veterans like DE Jacob Martin and EDGE Jermaine Johnson finally beginning to show progress under Saleh.
It must translate in Week 5 if the Titans are to pull off what is being perceived as an upset.

title: Titans' Front Office Firings Can't Distract From Franchise's Broken State
full_text:
How long can a rebuild be deemed a rebuild? When does a team trying to reshape things from the ground up transition from a multi-year project to something deeper than that? The Tennessee Titans haven't had a winning season since 2021. Robert Saleh is 0-4 in his first go-around.
Yesterday, it was announced that the Titans were firing three executives in an effort to overhaul the front office. These include: senior VP and chief revenue officer Adam Nuse, VP of creative Charles Jensen, and senior VP of brand marketing Erin Swartz.
The latter spearheaded Tennessee's recent aesthetic rebrand, seemingly leading the team into a new era that fans have long awaited. Now, as a result of that new era being fully implemented, Swartz has been let go alongside two of her colleagues.
We have an address from the organization regarding this sudden move that was issued to the Tennesseean :
“As the Titans prepare for the opening of our new stadium and the future of Titans football, we are making changes to how we lead the business side of the organization. We will hire an Executive Vice President and Chief Business Officer to lead our revenue, marketing, and communications teams. As part of these changes, Adam Nuse, Erin Swartz, and Charles Jensen are leaving the organization. We are grateful for everything they have contributed to the Titans and wish them the best in future endeavors.”
Burke Nihill has been the Titans' president and CEO since 2020. Under Nihill, the franchise has cycled through three head coaches and four general managers. Just about every level of the Titans' organization has undergone a change throughout their half-decade downward spiral.
The lone exception is, of course, Nihill himself. Is this all just a legendary streak of bad luck, or is there something to be said about the person pulling the strings for Tennessee's unending rebuild?
There may not be a direct answer, but something more has to be going south when a team is constantly recycling front office and sideline names to no avail. There's a deeply broken decision-making process in there somewhere, the blame for which can't be deferred forever.
In a leaked internal memo, Nihill tied off this news by saying: "We adapt when it's for the good of the team. I'm confident this structure sets us up to do special things together as a business and as a culture in 2027 and beyond."
Coach Saleh is still extremely early in his tenure, and GM Mike Borgonzi has helped usher in more than a few draft hits since his hiring at the beginning of last year. "The future is bright" is a common sentiment being floated around this 0-4 Titans team.
But how many times have we heard that in the past five years? More importantly, how much longer will fans accept that sentiment before it loses meaning? That is, if fans haven't reached that point already.

title: Experts Picking Texans Over Titans Reveal Exactly How Tennessee Can Win
full_text:
It's become a minor tradition for our coverage of expert picks to report the worst possible news. Yet again, heading into Week 5, the NFL's Preview Picks are 10-0 in favor of the visiting Houston Texans. This is the second straight week that Tennessee doesn't have a single projected win in the preview.
Although, this time around, these picks have one expectation in common. The Texans score between 23-27 points, and the Titans score between 10-17. Six of the 10 picks fall within this fair range. While only two see Tennessee keeping this contest in the single digits, this board of predictions may reveal just how the Titans can find their first win this week.
It's clear that Houston is expected to win by the merits of their offense. C.J. Stroud is coming off his second game of the year throwing more than 340 yards, and the Texans their second game scoring 30 points as a unit. That came in a loss - like Tennessee, Houstin is 0-4.
Now, head coach DeMeco Ryans did just take up defensive play-calling duties to try and improve the Texans' defense. But no matter how you spin it, the offense is what has brought Houston within striking distance this year.
If Robert Saleh can outmatch Ryans and shut Stroud, Nico Collins, David Montgomery and company down, the Titans may actually have a favorable shot at home.
This isn't just a "score more points than the other team" sort of plea. Week 5 could serve as the perfect crossroads for the Titans. Cam Ward just had the best game of his season against the Baltimore Ravens last week, coming on late and feeding rookie Carnell Tate to no end.
Ward still has plenty of room to improve, but he took a few strides that we've been waiting to see. Another (even small) leap from the offense paired with a sturdy defensive showing could mix the right formula to serve the Texans a defeat.
Per PFF, Houston's 109 points allowed is tied for 26th in the NFL. Their 84 points scored are only good for 20th, but the Texans have scored 19 or more in three of their four games. There's a wide gap between offense and defense right now, and it's one Saleh has to try and exploit.
With both teams looking for their first divisional win, and win in general, the stakes will be boiling over in Nashville this Sunday. If Tennessee can keep Stroud's passing game in relative check, perhaps Ward and the offense have had enough time to make good on some of their potential.
Perhaps the Titans can finally grab a victory, even if Robert Saleh's playoff hopes remain in question.

title: How Titans' RT JC Latham Could Make a Decisive Statement Against Texans
full_text:
The Tennessee Titans are set to host the Houston Texans in a Week 5 battle between two winless teams out of the AFC South.
If either team wants even a sliver of hope going forward, they must find a way win this game. Odds of a playoff run aren’t good with a record of 1-4, regardless, but they become almost nonexistent at 0-5. Simply put, Tennessee needs this one badly.
But for that to happen, the Titans will have to do something that seems almost impossible right now — slow down the incredible Texans DE, Will Anderson Jr.
According to Pro Football Focus , Anderson enters Week 5 as the highest-graded defender in the NFL (92.8), receiving grades of 90+ in the run game (92.2) and as a pass rusher (90.2). Needless to say, Titans RT JC Latham will have his hands full on Sunday. Fortunately, it appears he’s both willing and able to take on the challenge this time around.
The former seventh overall pick in the 2024 NFL Draft is undoubtedly playing the best ball of his young career. Latham hasn’t allowed a single sack or quarterback hit over 145 pass-blocking snaps, earning a pass blocking grade of 71.5 — the highest of his career.
. @Titans @Ravens RT, JC Latham  has emerged this year as a lock down consistent player...Focus, consistency; power.  it's all there regardless of opponent. #titanup #BaldysBreakdowns pic.twitter.com/nO1lxMLACN
To take how impressive he’s Latham has been a step further, he’s also left on an island nearly 70% of his pass-blocking snaps, winning over 95% of those reps, both of which are among the highest in the league per PFF .
It appears that Latham's elite ability to anchor that he routinely displayed at Alabama has found its way back into his arsenal. He's also utilizing his natural length more efficiently and to his advantage than he has at any point in his professional career.
As for the run game, that’s an area where Latham has excelled dating back to last year (PFF grade was 71.3). The third-year tackle has natural power and length at his disposal, and when he’s playing with good footwork and hand placement, he’s able to displace defenders at the point of attack with ease.
The Titans’ tackle is also doing a much better job of correctly identifying his assignments pre-snap. Latham has rarely found himself out of position this season, and that’s because he has a genuine understanding of how the defense is trying to attack him on every play.
These developments have undoubtedly been encouraging, but a massive benchmark now awaits the young tackle on Sunday. Arguably the best edge defender in the NFL will be across from him throughout the contest, so we’re going to find out real fast just how much Latham has truly grown.
In previous years, these are the types of matchups that would ultimately expose Latham’s deficiencies. However, he now has the chance to start changing that narrative completely with a great game on Sunday.
A strong performance against an all-around elite defender like Anderson would do wonders for Latham’s budding confidence going forward. This is the type of individual matchup that can validate him as one of the better right tackles in the NFL. It can also quickly become a brutal reality check if not taken seriously.
Someone like Anderson should have his moments; he’s too good not to do so, but if Latham is able to hold is own for the majority of the game, then he’s undoubtedly going to start being discussed in an entirely different tier of tackles than ever before.
More importantly, it’ll give the Titans a real shot to get their offense going as they try to win their first game of the season. Because if Anderson starts to dominate the way he typically does, we'd be in for another very long afternoon in Nashville.

title: Week 5: Analyzing Robert Saleh's Playoff Hopes Heading Into a Must-Win Game vs. Texans
full_text:
The Tennessee Titans find themselves in the depths of the standings at 0-4, but they're not alone in the AFC South. Although Tennessee is winless, they've lost by less than a touchdown across the last three games. On Sunday, the Titans host their interdivisional rival, the winless Houston Texans, in a dire, must-win game.
"I think anything is achievable," head coach Robert Saleh told the media today, per Jim Wyatt. "I feel if we can win one, we can build momentum [towards a playoff push.]"
While the playoffs are improbable, the Titans aren't eliminated from contention. Hope remains alive in Nashville.
The 1992 San Diego Chargers are the only team in NFL history to start 0-4 and make the playoffs . San Diego finished its season with a 11-5 record and beat the Kansas City Chiefs in the Wild Card.
Tennessee and Houston are two of five teams to be winless through four weeks, the first time this has happened since the 2019 season. To sneak into the playoffs, the Titans would likely have to capture the AFC South.
Currently, the Jacksonville Jaguars have the top spot at 3-1; behind them is the 2-2 Indianapolis Colts. The Titans' Week 5 matchup with Houston will be their first AFC South opponent of the season.
"You got to learn how to stop losing first," Saleh said to media on Monday . "When you're trying to figure out how to win football games, you have to figure out how to stop losing. Right now, we're doing things every week (where) we're putting ourselves behind the eight ball."
While any win would make the Titans' season salvageable, Saleh believes that first the team must not beat themselves. According to the numbers, Tennessee isn't all that far off.
The Titans have only lost by a combined 15 points in their last three games. Currently, Tennessee's -28 scoring differential is better than the 2-2 Green Bay Packers.
"Life does not change," Saleh continued. "I know it's a results-oriented business, but the only chance you have to get the results you want is to have a good process on how you approach things... When you get to Sunday you have to play your absolute ass off; that's the only chance to get the result that you want (a win.)"
The Texans were AFC-contender hopefuls coming off a 12-5 campaign last season, behind a juggernaut of a defense. However, Houston has given up more than 20 points in three games this season, including 36 points to Buffalo and 34 to Dallas.
Tennessee's offense has yet to score more than 18 points in a single game this season. On Sunday, they will look to exploit a struggling Houston defense to escape a 0-5 start. Right or wrong, Saleh believes in his message, and that execution is the difference between wins and losses. That's what it will take to finally get a victory.

title: Why the Titans Will Beat the Texans in Week 5, Why They Won't, and a Prediction
full_text:
Week 5 is almost as big a game for the Tennessee Titans' opponent as it is for the Titans themselves. The Houston Texans come to Nashville with an equal 0-4 record, only they've already dropped an AFC South competition to the Indianapolis Colts.
The last remaining drop of optimism for either of these teams could be on the line this coming Sunday. Robert Saleh and his staff should be swinging for the fences to get Tennessee in the victory column here before it's far too late.
As has become a weekly tradition, I'm back with one reason why the Titans will beat the Texans, one reason they won't, as well as my own prediction. We'll start with the (potentially) good news.
In a game that I expect could be decided by an offensive hot streak on either side, the Titans' best chance to come out with a win originates in Carnell Tate. The rookie pass-catcher had the biggest game of his young career in Week 4.
If Tennessee continues to look this way, and Cam Ward gets in a rhythm, perhaps Tate will finally get into the end zone and open things up on that side of the ball. Ward's 222 passing yards against the Ravens last week were a season-high for him, too. The momentum is here.
It helps that the Texans have one of the worst pass defenses in the league through one month of football. FOX Sports has Houston listed down at in the league 28th in that category, having allowed six passing scores and an average of 260 yards per contest.
Saleh's defense has been (mostly) reliable for weeks now. That defense will have to once again somewhat contain an elite offense, but it's more on Brian Daboll's group to catch up now and make the most of their chances.
If they can lean into their budding rookie in Week 5, maybe we'll finally see that unit pull even. Maybe.
This is the flip side of the offensive battle. In spite of their defeat vs. the Dallas Cowboys last week, QB C.J. Stroud and the Texans' offense put up 30 points. That's the second time this season Houston has eclipsed the 30-point mark.
If Tennessee falls behind, it will likely be due to Stroud and his cast of playmakers staying hot. With star WR Nico Collins back from injury, the Texans are primed for another scoring barrage in Week 5. Stroud threw for 347 yards, two scores, and no interceptions against Dallas.
Even given an uptick in offensive production for the Titans, the last thing Tennessee wants to do is get into a shootout with Houston. However, the Texans appear most comfortable with that outcome. Stroud's showing from Week 4 if all the evidence you need.
Ideally, the Titans limit the air attack and make the Texans try and beat them on the ground. That's where my prediction comes in.
Call me optimistic, call me plain old silly, but I have the Titans winning this one. For the conspiracy theorists, it was Week 5 last season that Tennessee secured their first win after an 0-4 start. But the best of the Titans' offense this season suggests they have a real shot here.
The boys in baby blue and white are also returning back home for the first time in two weeks. It's a division rivalry game (the first this year for the Titans) and, simply, Saleh and his team have more to lose. Where the Texans could be barreling toward a reset, Tennessee is clawing to get out of one.
Immediate results matter more right now for the Titans. I'll take that ever-elusive Carnell Tate score, a good enough game from Cam Ward, and, in the end, a tight Tennessee victory.
If things do pan out this way, you can expect the home team to finally break away from their predictable one-man backfield show. You can also expect Stroud to throw for less than 300 yards. If those details stack up, well... we'll see.

title: Titans' Cam Ward Has Less Time to Prove He's "The One" Than You Might Think
full_text:
The journey for every young QB is different. It took Bryce Young the better part of three seasons to settle in with the Carolina Panthers after being thrown into the fire as a first overall pick. Fernando Mendoza, on the other hand, was just taken first by the Las Vegas Raiders to sit and learn behind Kirk Cousins. Cam Ward's scenario with the Tennessee Titans leans toward the former, of course.
Only, Ward may not have the same benefit of time to come into his own. Four games into his sophomore year, the Miami product seems to be battling regression. His accuracy has hardly improved, and looks downfield have become more scarce.
Where other passers have a runway paved for their progression, Ward appears to be falling behind his fellow young playmakers in Tennessee. Quickly, at least as far as I'm concerned, what was "Carnell Tate has to make things easier on Ward" has become "Ward has to make things easier on Tate."
Ward himself said as much in Wednesday's press conference.
Some things were bound to change when Robert Saleh was brought in to replace Brian Callahan. It was Callahan, after all, who was here when Ward was drafted. That's an offensive-minded coach being fitted with weapons that suit his profile.
Tate may have been drafted under Saleh, but EDGE Keldric Faulk and LB Anthony Hill Jr. were, too. To that point, it's unsurprising that the Titans' offense has been the team's weaker side this season. Saleh's defensive play-calling is the closest thing this team has to an identity right now.
The history of QBs picked first overall suggests that their development will come along eventually. In fact, every QB taken first from the 2016 NFL Draft on still has a starting job today, save for the aforementioned Mendoza.
Ward, however, has the worst record of any of those guys through the first 21 games of his career, at 3-18. I'd argue that he has less room for error within the walls of a desperate franchise facing their second straight failed rebuild.
Saleh is far from a surefire failure, that's not a discussion. He's winless through four games, but we haven't really seen what the head coach will do when his back is against the wall and a tough decision has to be made. Ward being benched has already been brought up.
After the Titans' QB threw a game-losing interception to the New York Giants in Week 3, Saleh was asked about the possibility of sitting Ward. Mind you, the Panthers did the same thing in Young's second year before he ultimately found his footing.
Saleh responded with an unceremonious "no," and that was that. Ward did go on to have his best game of the season in Week 4's loss to the Ravens, but that still only amounted to one score, 222 yards, and a pick.
I'm not saying that the Titans should be ready to go ahead and can the guy, but would a second coach be fired with Ward under center before a change is made? I don't think so, especially not if Saleh keeps fielding solid draft picks and defensive improvements.
The further we progress into his second season, the more crucial Ward's own progression becomes. Tennessee can only wait and see for so much longer.

title: Titans Winners and Losers After First Quarter of 2026 NFL Season
full_text:
We're now essentially one quarter into the 2026 NFL season. Objectively, things could not be going any worse under Robert Saleh, at least as far as wins and losses go. The Tennessee Titans are 0-4, and look nearly identical to their despised franchise-reset state from last season.
Yet, there are things for Titans fans to hold out hope for. Between quick rookie developments and late arrivals, multiple players are starting to take leaps toward becoming reliable, even winning pieces for Tennessee.
On the flip side, there are a couple of assets heading in the opposite direction. Here are the biggest winners and losers from the Titans' first four games.
Anthony Hill Jr., the Titans' second-round rookie LB, is third in the NFL in total tackles with 42. He's stepped into a debatable LB room and turned it into one of Tennessee's defensive strengths when he's on the field - now, that's most of the time.
Hill has consistently topped the charts in our rookie power rankings. Before Week 4, Hill held the crown as the NFL's leading tackler. Mind you, he's four games into his professional career.
Say what you will about Saleh's job so far, but the coach clearly has a one-of-one mind for defensive talent and development. Hill is a peak example of that process, and goes down as a huge winner for the Titans so far.
Less excitingly, backup RB Tyjae Spears makes an unfortunate addition to the losers column through four contests.
With Tony Pollard in the final year of his contract and Spears entering this season fully healthy, 2026 appeared like the prime window for Spears to eventually take up lead-back duties. Up to this point, he's been on and off the field, and unreliable even in a secondary role.
Having been questionable with an ankle injury for two straight weeks now, Spears' impact has dwindled down to almost nothing despite playing through it. He's got just 15 carries for 65 yards this year.
In the receiving game, where Spears tends to thrive, just five receptions for 40 yards. Pollard being treated like a workhorse isn't working for the Titans, but Spears hasn't done enough to confidently pose himself as a replacement.
Alongside the aforementioned Hill, Carnell Tate has come on strong in his first NFL campaign. The rookie wide receiver is fresh off a breakout performance that only seems to signal more growth.
Tate went for 145 yards on nine receptions vs. the Baltimore Ravens in Week 4. He leads Tennessee in receptions (22), targets (32) and receiving yards (268). PFF has Tate with the second most contested catches at a 100% rate in the league, at 6/6.
The fourth overall pick has long arrived in an offense that is far from complete. If Cam Ward fully figures it out, Tate could find himself in superstar conversations sooner rather than later.
Speaking of Ward, the second-year signal caller finds himself on the negative side of this list. He's not had a bad season necessarily, but the standard is higher for him than anyone on this team.
Ward has thrown three touchdowns to two interceptions this season. His 63% completion rate thus far shows little improvement to last season, and worries about his footwork and decision-making continue to overshadow the wins.
PFF rankings see Ward in the league's bottom 10 in overall grade, passing yards, and passing scores. His best game came against the Ravens last week, and even that resulted in a loss that saw the Titans playing from behind the entire time.
As young, star-making pieces rise around him, the pressure for Ward to improve with them gets greater. The QB simply isn't there yet, and ringing alarm bells aren't far off if he doesn't find a way to succeed.
Finally, third-year T JC Latham has elevated into truly elite status on the offensive line. After a so-so first two seasons, the Alabama alumni's numbers are now an undeniable marker of his growth.
Latham has an astonishing 0% sack/QB hit rate this season. Saleh said prior to Week 4 that Latham is having a Pro-Bowl worthy season up to this point, and the T only helped his case vs. Baltimore. He might be the best protector on this Titans team right now.
With no sacks allowed through four games and one of the best island (one on one) win rates in the NFL, Latham deserves a spot as a winner here. Ward's life has been made a whole lot easier by Latham, and he's a piece that Tennessee must now prioritize keeping around in the long run.

title: The Titans’ Most Underrated Free-Agent Addition is Turning Heads Despite Tennessee's 0-4 Record
full_text:
The Tennessee Titans were incredibly active during NFL free agency in the spring, with one of their signings being edge rusher Jacob Martin.
Martin, a sixth-round pick in the 2018 NFL Draft by the Seattle Seahawks, has been a journeyman pass rusher for the entirety of his career. The Temple product has had stops with the Seahawks, obviously, the Houston Texans, the New York Jets, the Denver Broncos, the Indianapolis Colts, the Chicago Bears, the Washington Commanders, and now the Titans.
Outside of a three-year stint in Houston from 2019 to 2021, Martin hasn't been able to find a long-term home at the next level. However, he's off to a fantastic start in 2026 and is showing why Tennessee made the right decision inking him to a two-year deal in March.
Through four games, Martin has been one of Tennessee's most productive defenders. He has posted 1.5 sacks, 13 quarterback pressures , two defensive stops, and two tackles for loss so far, and is coming off a five-pressure game with half a sack against the Baltimore Ravens in Week 4 . Martin also recorded seven quarterback pressures and a sack in the Week 2 loss to the Philadelphia Eagles.
Martin has been a bright spot on a Titans defense that has been inconsistent to kick off the year . But the unit hasn't gotten any help from an offense that's been dysfunctional and out of sorts on nearly every drive.
The Titans' addition of Jermaine Johnson was the premier acquisition for the team at edge rusher. However, Martin has slightly outplayed Johnson so far this season, tallying one more pressure and half a sack more, though Johnson has been better in the run game.
Regardless, Martin is making his presence felt on the defensive line, and it's integral that he keeps this level of play up. Tennessee's secondary hasn't been the most reliable, and the group could use a lot of help from the front seven in the pass-rushing department.
The Titans are eyeing their first win of the 2026 season at home against the Houston Texans in Week 5, and Martin is a player who will need to step up for Tennessee to finally break a losing streak that dates back to Week 17 of the 2025 season.

title: Sonny Styles vs Arvell Reese: Which is Better Positioned to Win NFL Defensive Rookie of the Year
full_text:
Sonny Styles and Arvell Reese shared a linebacker room at Ohio State. On Sunday, Oct. 11, the two rookies will meet for the first time as NFC East rivals when the Washington Commanders host the New York Giants at Northwest Stadium. Back in April, these two made NFL Draft history for being part of the first college program to have two linebackers selected in the top 10 of the same draft. The Giants selected Reese with the No. 5 pick, and two picks later, the Commanders selected Styles with the No. 7 pick. When they each chose their NFL numbers, they both picked No. 52. Sunday's game will be the first time the two can be compared on the same grass. Currently, NFL.com's Gennaro Filice ranks Styles first and Reese second among defensive rookies. While that is only one opinion, it's a strong one with some backing. Both were on Ohio State's 2024 national championship team. By 2025, Styles led the Buckeyes with 82 tackles; Reese followed with 69 tackles and 6.5 sacks. At a media event in August of 2025 , Reese specifically credited Styles with helping him understand preparation away from the field, saying, "I have learned a lot from Sonny, and it's more off the field. How you prepare for games, how he prepares practice to practice, and how intentional he is, Sonny is a great person." At that same event, Styles said Reese’s mental development is the place he's grown the most: "I would say mentally, just understanding the game." Styles explained that Reese had always possessed the physical tools, but a better understanding of the game was allowing him to play faster and use them.
Since joining the Commanders , Styles has 20 tackles (two for loss), one sack, one interception, one forced fumble, and two passes defensed. He had eight tackles against Indy this past weekend, one week after becoming the franchise’s first rookie linebacker to record an interception, a forced fumble, and multiple passes defensed in one game. He won NFC Defensive Player of the Week for that performance . Styles's play has put him in the conversation for rookie of the year , even if that conversation was had without words. He has demonstrated several ways to affect the passing game, which strengthens his case beyond his tackle total. PFF agrees, giving him an 85.2 coverage grade through four games, third among 74 qualifying linebackers.
Sonny Styles was EVERYWHERE in Washington’s win over Seattle. 4 TKL, 1 INT, 2 PD, 1 FF, 1 QBH vs Seahawks The rookie came away with his first career interception and forced a fumble against the defending champs. https://t.co/UMG5nOAliR pic.twitter.com/H3zRDCHDxE
Reese hasn't been a slouch himself: in four games, he has 34 tackles (three for loss), four passes defensed, one interception, and two quarterback hits. This past Sunday against Arizona, he had nine tackles, three passes defensed, and his first NFL interception. PFF also credits Reese with 13 defensive stops and just one missed tackle, compared with seven stops and four missed tackles for Styles. That gives Reese an early advantage in tackling production and reliability as both build their cases for Defensive Rookie of the Year. Their overall PFF grades are nearly identical through four games: 77.1 for Reese and 76.9 for Styles. Reese has also played 243 defensive snaps compared with Styles' 219, giving him more opportunities to add to his numbers.
Arvell Reese just gets better every week 9 tackles, 5 stops, 1 INT, 1 pressure, 1 batted pass in week 4 https://t.co/RGJ6tKfoco pic.twitter.com/t0oPdXp2zX
Both players look like problems for the NFC East for several years to come, and right now, I have them in a dead heat. Styles has the stronger coverage grade, a sack, and a forced fumble. Reese has more tackles, more defensive stops, and fewer missed tackles. I can make a Defensive Rookie of the Year case for either one. What's wild is that two guys from the same college, wearing the same number and respecting one another, are now building those cases on opposite sides of an NFC East rivalry. Their first meeting comes Sunday, with all of us watching No. 52 on both defenses for different reasons. title: Commanders Need More From Chig Okonkwo, but the Problem Goes Beyond Him
full_text:
The Washington Commanders, like most 1-3 operations in the first month of the NFL regular season, have produced numerous players and position groups who could contend for the distinction of their roster's most disappointing element.
Even if it entered the season with minimal hype, the offensive line has crumbled about as dramatically as anyone could have imagined, with their two best blockers presently down for the count. Other playmakers like Terry McLaurin and Jacory "Bill" Croskey-Merritt have fluctuated between exciting and inefficient, while someone like Mike Sainristil has completely careened from Washington's secondary rotation, with some of the lowest defensive metrics of anyone league-wide.
#Commanders CB Rasul Douglas' share of defensive snaps: Week 1: 32% Week 2: 43% Week 3: 67% Week 4: 85% Over the same stretch, Mike Sainristil went from 98% to 8%. 📊: NFL Pro | #RaiseHail pic.twitter.com/EJMWLYowfy
Some of those key Commanders have been loud in their letdowns, but Chig Okonkwo deserves a shout of his own, given how little he's factored into the group's equation through four weeks. His lingering hamstring injury has to be mentioned for keeping him out of Washington's Week 2 and 3 matchups- the first absence of his professional career- but 21 yards on four receptions and seven targets just can't go undiscussed.
It's important to note that Okonkwo isn't Zach Ertz , and that's more or less the tight-end archetype that fans have grown to anticipate within their offense.
Okonkwo more closely resembles a big receiver than Ertz, someone who could regularly find openings 10 yards out and nab easy first downs as Jayden Daniels ' go-to checkdown read before he shredded his knee last season. It wasn't exciting, but it required strong footwork and a veteran awareness that was easily taken for granted.
Ertz's replacement, meanwhile, is more likely to try beating coverages with his raw speed, and he's failed to beat the Philadelphia Eagles' or Indianapolis Colts' defenses in two outings. And with Washington’s quarterback situation having changed repeatedly over the last few weeks, that lack of a security blanket has been particularly glaring.
One example of how Chig Okonkwo hasn't gotten it going yet. I assume this is supposed to be a rub route by Diggs but #57 just ... goes around it and Chig is never freed up for a big gain. Instead, just two yards pic.twitter.com/jcuSor5jRc
Again, this is based purely on two games' worth of snaps. Okonkwo will benefit greatly from a more consistent passing game once Daniels returns and McLaurin and Diggs are healthy, because he's likely getting very little help from his positional understudies .
Even if Okonkwo was never a star with the Tennessee Titans, his stable average of 450-560 yards a season sounded pretty nice when the tight end room was left without its pass-catching starter for two games.
For all the good things we can say about John Bates' willingness to stay committed to blocking in an overtasked role, he'll never force a defense's hand when he drifts downfield into open space. That's to say nothing of reserves like Ben Sinnott and Colson Yankoff, who've fallen short of leveraging their respective talents into every-down roles; despite playing eight combined games to Okonkwo's two, they've each failed to eclipse the starter's paltry yardage total of 21.
The Commanders' TE production through four weeks (via @TruMediaSports ): Receptions — 10 (Tied for 31st/last) Targets — 17 (tied for 31st) Yards — 65 (32nd*) Rec. TDs — Zero (one of four teams without a TD) Air yards per target — 2.30 (28th) YAC — 42 (31st)
Prodigies like Brock Bowers and Trey McBride aren't walking through the Commanders' facility anytime soon, and the following draft is still 13 games away. If the team has any hope of getting anything out of its disappointing tight end rotation, it'll come down to freeing Okonkwo up by taking pressure off him with other receiving threats and giving the quarterback enough protection to find him. That means a cleaner pocket for the quarterback, more play-calling and route-running diversions, and ideally, enough health to return as many receiving threats to the starting lineup as possible.
David Blough has passed most of the adaptive tests thrown his way, so consider the Okonkwo dilemma just another schematic puzzle for the new offensive coordinator to solve with his makeshift remains.

title: Jayden Daniels’ Return Could Put Antonio Williams in a Much Bigger Role — Commanders Daily
full_text:
The Washington Commanders face an interesting situation this weekend against one of their oldest and most bitter rivals, the New York Giants. The team is expected to get quarterback Jayden Daniels back just two games after he dislocated his non-throwing elbow in a contact-less situation. Daniels practiced fully for the first time since the injury on Wednesday , the same day Terry McLaurin and Stefon Diggs missed practice with hamstring injuries. McLaurin already missed the London game . The potential of not having Diggs, who leads all receivers with 18 receptions for 170 yards and three touchdowns — and/or McLaurin is nightmare fuel for the weak-hearted. This is where having a dynamic player like Antonio Williams pays off. He can be that guy when and if needed. The great part is, he's already been ramped up, inadvertently, for this very opportunity. Williams has seen his snaps climb from 26 snaps (37%) in Week 1 to 44 snaps (69%) in Week 4, with 49% and 41% snap shares in Weeks 2 & 3, respectively. Over that time, he has 12 receptions for 124 yards and one touchdown. Last week against Indianapolis, he had eight targets and caught three for 21 yards, but an 87-yard touchdown was called back due to penalties. His usage shows he's grown quickly from a complementary rookie to being in on two-thirds of Washington's offensive plays with McLaurin out. Williams' most productive game as a pro came in Week 1 against the Philadelphia Eagles when he was targeted four times and caught four passes for 64 yards and a touchdown. In the three games since (two without Daniels), Williams has caught eight passes for 60 yards without another touchdown.
Antonio Williams (#14) All-22 on 10 routes vs Eagles • 4 recs on 4 tgts • 64 rec yds • 1 TD • 91.0 PFF overall grade (highest graded receiver in the game yesterday) #RaiseHail pic.twitter.com/fGojlpffxz
Back at the end of July, McLaurin saw that Williams had the ability to contribute early on: "He has a good feel for the receiver position, and I think he has a chance to really help us, especially in [OC David] Blough's offense, where guys will be able to move around," McLaurin said. While most think Williams is only a slot receiver, a trip through his game film from Clemson will show you that he played there his last year in college, but he had 317 snaps on the outside during the 2024 season and did well. Blough's offense is supposed to be designed for players to move around, so that should benefit Williams no matter if Diggs and McLaurin can't play or not. "I think he really excels in the slot, and I know he's gonna have a chance to move around, but I think it's just really important, especially when you're a young guy gaining that confidence," McLaurin said. As we all know, more opportunities don't always turn into more production; as against Indy, Williams only had 21 yards on eight targets. But that conversation needs a little context, with the offense having to shift to a rookie quarterback with a different skill set, who the rest of the offense was not completely comfortable with, having not practiced much together, if at all. Then again, the 87-yard play that was negated by the illegal shift/holding penalties is the missing yardage. Daniels' expected return changes the quarterback situation, but doesn't eliminate the challenges facing the receiving corps. The Commanders drafted Williams hoping he could become a meaningful part of Daniels' offense. Depending on how the next two days unfold, they might be asking him to prove that sooner than anyone expected.
